source.title: [Bug] DSpark draft depth 5 (the checkpoint default) corrupts output on SM120 — depths 3, 4, 6, 7 are clean
source.body:
### Checklist

- [x] Searched existing issues. Closest are #32666 (same boundary reported on
      a different backend: depth 5 → 23/24 runs corrupt, depth 3 → 0/607) and
      #32038 / #32183 (accuracy regression + the verifier state rewrite
      window). None of them tests **above** the native block size, which is
      what makes this non-monotonic result new.
- [x] English.

### Summary

On SM120 (4× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, TP=4 + DP attention + EP), DSpark
generations corrupt under real agentic load **at draft depth 5 only**.
Depths 3, 4, 6 and 7 are clean under the identical protocol. Depth 5 is
exactly `dspark_block_size` in the DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 checkpoint config —
i.e. the value you get when `--speculative-dspark-block-size` is omitted, and
therefore the default most people run.

The corruption is not a crash: output degrades into repetition loops
(`` ` for ` for ` for `` …), token salad, and `</think>` leaking into content,
with `finish_reason` normal and no errors in the log.

### The sweep

Every arm uses the same server config (only `--speculative-dspark-block-size`
changes) and the same load; scoring is an output classifier (U+FFFD
replacement chars, punctuation density, single-character spray, repeated
trigrams).

| gamma | verify rows | how set | requests | corruption events |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 4 | explicit | 10,885 (5 cold launches) | **0** |
| 4 | 5 | explicit | 11,040 (5 cold launches) | **0** |
| **5** | **6** | **inferred (flag omitted)** | 2,148 | **10** |
| **5** | **6** | **explicit** | 2,138 | **7** |
| 6 | 7 | explicit | 2,282 | **0** |
| 7 | 8 | explicit | 2,198 | **0** |

Reproduced on v0.5.16 (+ backports listed below) **and** on upstream `main`
@ `211ee642` (2026-08-05), 5/5 cold launches dirty at depth 5 in both.

### Why this is not "depth ≥ N is too deep"

Depths 6 and 7 are wider than 5 and are clean. Both explicit and inferred
depth 5 corrupt, so it is not the config-inference path. That points at
something keyed to the draft head's *native* block size rather than to window
size, capacity, or any bound that grows with depth.

Ruled out by measurement, not argument:

- **c4 compress-state ring capacity** — doubling it (16 → 32 positions)
  changed nothing: 32 events / 10,209 requests, statistically identical to
  the unfixed baseline.
- **Verify window vs compress ratio** — depths 4 and 6 cross the same c4
  boundaries and are clean.
- **NaN logits** — a `sanitize_nan_logits` tripwire ported into the DSpark
  verify path fired **zero** times across every corrupting launch; the
  poisoned logits are finite.
- **#32183** (verifier state rewrite window / `kMaxMTPDraftTokens = 4`) —
  backported and instrumented: `verify_width = 6` demonstrably reaches the
  patched plan kernel, and depth 5 still corrupts. Necessary but not
  sufficient.
- **#32277** (all-sentinel draft row clamp) — backported, no effect here.
- **Attention kernel choice** — forcing the Triton sparse-MLA path instead of
  the padded CUTLASS path produces identical corruption, so the attention
  inputs are already wrong.
- **KV-store padding slot writes** — guarded, no effect.

### Reproduction

Server (the only variable is the block-size flag):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --tp-size 4 --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head --ep-size 4 \
  --trust-remote-code --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --context-length 1048576 \
  --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 --max-running-requests 256 --cuda-graph-max-bs 64 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-attention-mode decode \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --tool-call-parser deepseekv4
  # depth 5 = omit the flag, or --speculative-dspark-block-size 5
  # clean    = --speculative-dspark-block-size 4
```

Load — this part matters, easier tests do not reproduce it:

- **5 cold launches per arm.** The fault is stochastic per server launch; a
  config can pass a full battery on one boot and corrupt on the next.
- **Bursty, not steady.** Two 45-minute steady-concurrency soaks (~8K
  requests) came back clean on a config that then failed 5/5 under bursts.
  We use 4 phases per launch: 3 min @ 4 workers, 3 min @ 20, 2 min @ 2,
  4 min @ 14.
- **Streaming, thinking enabled, tool schemas, multi-turn** —
  `chat_template_kwargs: {thinking: true}`, high reasoning effort, ~20 tools,
  conversations that grow. The batch-shape sweeps at burst transitions are
  what single-shape steady load never exercises.

A 10-minute variant that needs no load generator: boot the same shape with
and without `--speculative-algorithm`, send identical prompts at
`temperature: 0`, and diff. Speculative decoding is distribution-preserving,
so any divergence is a verify-path mis-commit — at depth 5 the spec-on output
is garbage while spec-off is clean.

### Environment

- 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q, 96 GB (GB202, sm_120), PCIe gen5,
  no NVLink; driver 595.71.05, CUDA 13.
- sglang v0.5.16 + backports (#32332, #32167, #31009, #32320, #33098, #32467,
  #32183, #33531, #31017, #32277, plus our #33407 SM120 dispatch fix);
  flashinfer 0.6.15.post1. Also reproduced on `main` @ `211ee642` with the
  same patch set rebased.
- Full recipe, patch set and numbers:
  https://github.com/ombori/deepseek-v4-flash-0731-sglang-4x-rtx-pro-6000

### Notes / possible leads

- #31018 and #31016 report that overriding the native block size used to
  crash graph capture, which may be why depth 5 is rarely left in practice —
  and why the non-monotonic shape has not been noticed.
- The draft confidence/Markov head is keyed to the checkpoint's block size
  rather than the runtime value (`deepseek_v4_dspark.py`), which is the kind
  of asymmetry that could make "requested == native" behave differently from
  every other depth. We have not confirmed this is the mechanism.
- Equivalent framing, in case it is width rather than the native size:
  the broken configuration is exactly `verify_num_draft_tokens = 6`.

Hardware is available and we are happy to run instrumented builds or
candidate patches on it.

source.body:
### Feature request

Hi, we are big fans of the library and the NF4 data-type, so much so that we have been working on [CUDA kernels](https://github.com/HanGuo97/flute) to speed-up inference for NF4-quantized models (and more). We'd love to explore ways we can integrate FLUTE into the `bitsandbytes` library.

### Motivation

I think FLUTE could make two contributions to bitsandbytes:

- An inference-time kernel for NF4-quantized LLM (and more). For example, this could help extend the current GEMV kernel into GEMM (i.e., batched inference).
- A new quantization algorithm that lightly extends bitsandbytes's NF4 into a learned version.

The kernel and algorithm still have room for improvements. For example, it has limited GPU support, and specializes in specific shapes. These are hopefully not hard limits and could be relaxed. As such, we do not expect FLUTE to be the default option. That being said, we thought it'd be great to have FLUTE be an opt-in feature.

### Your contribution

We are happy to submit PRs, though I'm sure there will be some rough edges that we will need some help with.

Hey folks — first off, congratulations on the AMD launch, and thank you for it. Getting Unsloth
onto Radeon is a big deal for those of us who went AMD for the VRAM-per-dollar and then spent a
year watching the good tooling land on CUDA first. We were genuinely excited to try this the day
it dropped.

We have a slightly unusual box — **two Radeon AI PRO R9700s (gfx1201)** — which we think sits
outside your current AMD CI, so hopefully this is useful rather than annoying. We hit a wall, but
we did a fair bit of digging to narrow it down, and we're very happy to keep digging or test
patches if that helps. Short version: **the published RDNA4 prebuilt won't start at all**, and
when we built your fork from source to work around it, we found a second, separate crash in what
looks like the multi-GPU path.

We've tried to make everything below reproducible. Happy to run anything you'd like.

### Our setup

| | |
|---|---|
| GPUs | 2× AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, 32 GB each) + a Ryzen iGPU ~~(excluded via `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES`)~~ **(correction: the iGPU was visible in the Problem 2 runs — that was the cause)** |
| CPU | AMD Ryzen 9 9950X (16C/32T) |
| RAM | 64 GB |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.8.0-124-generic |
| Host ROCm | 7.2.3 |
| amdgpu-dkms | 1:6.16.13.30300300 |
| Install | `curl -fsSL https://unsloth.ai/install.sh \| sh`, as an unprivileged user |
| unsloth | 2026.7.4 |
| torch | 2.10.0+rocm7.2.3 (from `repo.radeon.com/rocm/manylinux/rocm-rel-7.2.3/`) |
| llama.cpp asset | `app-b10069-mix-fb3d4ca-linux-x64-rocm-gfx120X.tar.gz` |
| release | `unslothai/llama.cpp@b10069-mix-fb3d4ca` (tag `b10069`) |
| archive sha256 | `e82239ad779674fd0fedffe0222195fc0b5b27e2cd7a1ef83b2455d7292425c7` — the installer verified this, so it isn't a corrupted download |

### First, the things that went really well

We want to lead with this, because the install experience was mostly excellent and it helps
localise the problem:

- **gfx1201 was detected correctly** even with two discrete GPUs *and* an iGPU in the box. We'd
  half-expected that to be the hard part, and it just worked.
- **PyTorch resolved to our exact host ROCm** — `torch 2.10.0+rocm7.2.3` straight from the Radeon
  repo. That's better than the docs led us to expect (they suggest nothing exists above ROCm 7.2).
- **The vision projector was auto-detected** sitting next to the model, with zero configuration.
  Lovely touch.
- GGUF metadata parsing was spot on — context length, chat template, reasoning and tool-calling
  flags all read correctly.
- The prebuilt **bundles its own ROCm 7.14 runtime**, which nicely decouples it from whatever the
  host happens to have. Smart.
- `--disable-tools` and the Cloudflare-off default both behaved exactly as documented, and the API
  correctly returned `401` without a bearer token. We care about that a lot and it was right.

So this really does look like a problem with one published artifact rather than anything
fundamental.

### Problem 1: the gfx120X prebuilt segfaults immediately

The binary the installer places doesn't run at all — not even `--version`:

```
$ cd ~/.unsloth/llama.cpp
$ export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$HOME/.unsloth/llama.cpp/build/bin
$ ./llama-server --version
Segmentation fault (core dumped)     # exit 139
```

From the kernel log:

```
llama-server[...]: segfault at 100000001 ip 0000000100000001 sp 00007fff1ecd7b78
                   error 14 in llama-server[5d94eac9d000+1000] likely on CPU 0
```

The instruction pointer is `0x100000001` and equals the faulting address, which reads like a jump
through a corrupt or uninitialised function pointer very early in startup — before any model,
ROCm, or GPU work happens. A few things support that reading:

- it fails the same way on `--version` and `--help`, which touch no hardware at all
- VRAM never moves off idle (~57 MiB/card) on any attempt
- the fault address is identical across runs; only the load base changes

Studio's fallback chain retried five times and every attempt died identically:

| attempt | flags | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `--fit off --flash-attn on --split-mode layer` + `--mmproj` | exit -11 |
| 2 | `--fit on` retry | exit -11 |
| 3 | `--flash-attn off` | exit -11 |
| 4 | `--fit on --flash-attn off` | exit -11 |
| 5 | text-only, no `--mmproj` | exit -11 |

One small thing that made debugging harder: the bundle ships **only `llama-server`** — there's no
`llama-cli`, `llama-bench` or `llama-mtmd-cli` to cross-check against. Including those would have
saved us a while.

**To reproduce:** install on any gfx1201 host and run `~/.unsloth/llama.cpp/llama-server --version`.

### Problem 2: building your fork from source fixes that — ~~but reveals a different crash~~ **[diagnosis corrected — the cause was the iGPU]**

To work out whether this was packaging or code, we built the fork ourselves on the same machine:

```
git clone https://github.com/unslothai/llama.cpp.git
HIPCXX="$(hipconfig -l)/clang" HIP_PATH="$(hipconfig -R)" \
  cmake -S . -B build -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1201 \
        -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLLAMA_CURL=ON
cmake --build build --config Release -j 24
```

HEAD was `5ff665dc` (`git describe` → `b10068-mix-fb3d4ca`); the binary self-reports
`version: 9690 (5ff665dc)`. Small note — we couldn't pin the prebuilt's exact ref because
`fb3d4ca` turns out to be part of the *tag name* rather than a commit hash, which took us a moment
to work out.

**The good news:** the source build runs fine (`--version` exits 0) **and it has MTP** —
`--spec-type ... draft-mtp` and `--spec-draft-n-max` are both there. So Problem 1, and the missing
MTP in Problem 3 below, both look like **packaging or build-configuration issues rather than
anything wrong with your code**. That felt like the most useful thing we could tell you.

> ⚠️ **Retracted.** The crash is real; the diagnosis was wrong. Cause: the Ryzen iGPU visible to
> HIP. Context size, `--mmproj`, `-sm tensor`, MTP and AllReduce are all irrelevant. With
> `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` set to the two discrete cards this command loads and serves.

~~**The less good news:** the source build still segfaults on our actual production configuration:~~

```
./llama-server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9310 \
  -m Qwen3.6-27B-UD-Q6_K_XL.gguf --mmproj mmproj-F16.gguf \
  -c 262144 -sm tensor -ngl 999 -fa 1 -np 1 \
  --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 3 --fit off --kv-unified -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0

-> Segmentation fault (core dumped); VRAM never allocated (~57 MiB/card idle)
```

~~The **last line logged before the crash, every single time**:~~

```
W internal AllReduce init failed (n_devices != 2?); falling back to meta-backend butterfly
```

~~We bisected the flags at `-c 4096` and everything loads happily — baseline, `-sm tensor`,~~
~~`--spec-type draft-mtp`, `--mmproj`, and tensor+MTP together — with **zero** AllReduce warnings.~~
~~So it seems to need large context (and in our runs, the vision projector) before it shows up.~~

**Here's the bit we think is most actionable.** We run the *same model, same flags, same two GPUs*
on an upstream-derived **llama.cpp build 9860**, and it prints that *same*
`AllReduce init failed (n_devices != 2?)` warning — and then carries on and serves perfectly
happily at 262144 context with the vision projector loaded, using ~38.9 GiB across the two cards.

> ✅ **Stands.** The warning appears on runs that load and serve normally, so it is not a crash
> indicator on either build.

~~On your fork's build 9690, the same warning is followed by a segfault. So something in that~~
~~multi-GPU AllReduce fallback either regressed, or is being reached in a state the fallback path~~
~~can't cope with.~~

We're very happy to run a debug build, grab a backtrace, or bisect further if that would help —
just say the word.

### Problem 3: the gfx120X prebuilt has no MTP support

On startup Studio logs:

```
llama.cpp prebuilt lacks MTP support (--spec-type mtp/draft-mtp).
Run `unsloth studio update`. MTP GGUFs will load without speculative decoding.
```

Since the source build *does* have MTP, this looks like the same packaging story as Problem 1.
Worth flagging because it matters a lot on this hardware: on our working build, MTP is worth
**1.63–1.79× generation throughput** on code and reasoning workloads, so quietly dropping it is a
big hit — especially for the Qwen3.6 and Gemma 4 families the launch post highlights.

### Problem 4: `unsloth studio update` can't resolve it

The remedy in that warning is a no-op, because `b10069` already *is* the latest published release:

```
existing install detected -- validating update
llama.cpp      prebuilt up to date and validated
               installed release: unslothai/llama.cpp@b10069-mix-fb3d4ca (tag b10069)
```

So as far as we can tell there's currently no supported route to a working RDNA4 install.

### Problem 5: the update path reports the CPU as the GPU

Minor, but confusing while debugging. The **install** path correctly says
`gpu  AMD ROCm (gfx1201)`. The **update** path, same machine, same session, says:

```
GPU: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X 16-Core Processor
```

Looks like the two paths use different detection logic.

### Problem 6: the crash gets misattributed

This one cost us real time, so it might be worth a look. The segfault surfaces as two different
and both incorrect diagnoses:

```
llama-server crashed during startup (exit code -11) with forced --fit off;
the fit estimate was optimistic, retrying once with --fit on so it can offload.
```
```
llama-server could not load this model's vision projector (--mmproj).
The installed llama.cpp build is likely too old for it. Loading text-only for this session
```

with a final user-facing error of *"Vision projector incompatible with this llama.cpp build, and
the text-only retry also failed"* — when really the binary never started. We went looking at our
mmproj file and our VRAM headroom for a while before checking `dmesg`. Since a negative exit code
(`-11` = SIGSEGV) is unambiguous, surfacing it as "the child crashed with SIGSEGV" would point
people at the real problem much faster.

### Problem 7: installing without sudo, non-interactively

Installing as a user with no `sudo` and no TTY:

```
deps           missing: libcurl4-openssl-dev
    WARNING: We require sudo elevated permissions to install: libcurl4-openssl-dev
    Accept? [Y/n] sh: 593: cannot open /dev/tty: No such device or address
sudo: a terminal is required to read the password
curl: (23) Failure writing output to destination
ERROR: Process exited with status 1
```

Two small things bundled together: with no TTY the prompt hard-fails rather than detecting
non-interactive mode and printing what to install; and the build dependencies are required *up
front*, before checking whether a prebuilt exists — even though the whole point of the prebuilts
(per the AMD post) is avoiding local compilation. For CI, containers, or locked-down accounts,
that's a stop for tooling that may never get used.

### Problem 8: the startup reachability probe

On startup, Studio reached out to external probe nodes and had them attempt an **inbound**
connection to the bound port, then logged the machine's public egress IP:

```
Reachability check: http://<PUBLIC-IP-REDACTED>:8090/ is NOT reachable from the public
internet (2/2 probe nodes failed).
```

We understand what it's for and it's a genuinely nice feature for someone trying to share a
Studio. But it's undocumented, happens without asking, and discloses the deployment's public IP
plus the presence of a listening service to a third party. For lab, air-gapped, or
privacy-sensitive deployments that's a surprise. Could it be opt-in, or at least have an env var
to switch it off?

### One more small thing ~~— retracted~~

~~We passed `unsloth run --tensor-parallel` and saw `--split-mode layer` appended to the~~
~~`llama-server` command line rather than tensor split. That may just be the fallback chain degrading~~
~~after the first crash, so treat it as low confidence until the segfault is sorted.~~

> ❌ **Retracted — was my error.** `--tensor-parallel` correctly produces `--split-mode tensor`.
> The original reading came from the last line of Studio's multi-attempt fallback chain rather
> than the first; the last line is a degraded retry. Studio is behaving correctly here.

### Happy to help

We've got **dual R9700 (gfx1201)** hardware, a fully instrumented baseline of the same models on a
working llama.cpp build, and time to spend on this. If a fix or a test build would benefit from
someone running it on real RDNA4 multi-GPU, we're glad to be that someone — debug builds,
backtraces, bisects, before/after numbers, whatever's useful.

Thanks again for the AMD work. Really looking forward to running this properly.
*(We've bundled several things into one issue to keep the story together — the packaging problem,
the source-build crash we found while proving it was packaging, and a few smaller things we noticed
along the way. Very happy to split any of it into separate issues if that's easier for you to
track.)*

source.title: [gfx1151] Silent hard hang under sustained vLLM inference with MES 0x86 — amdgpu hangcheck never fires
source.body:
Follow-up to [ROCm/ROCm#5724](https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/5724) and [ROCm/ROCm#5991](https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/issues/5991). The MES 0x83 page-fault class was resolved for us by upgrading to MES 0x86 (upstream `linux-firmware` tag `20260410`). A **distinct, silent hang** remains on the same node under sustained compute — no page fault, no GPU reset, no MCE, no kernel log. Filing because the fence-ring evidence below narrows it beyond what dmesg shows and may be useful for triage.

## System

| | |
|---|---|
| Machine | Framework Desktop (2025) |
| SoC | AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (Strix Halo) |
| GPU | Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, PCI `0000:c1:00.0` `[1002:1586]` |
| BIOS | 03.04 (2025-11-19), LVFS latest |
| Distro | Ubuntu Questing (25.10 / 26.04-preLTS) |
| Kernel | `7.0.0-070000-generic` (mainline, `#202604122140 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sun Apr 12 22:05:40 UTC 2026`) |
| Kernel cmdline (relevant) | `iommu=pt amdgpu.gttsize=126976 ttm.pages_limit=32505856 amd_iommu=on amdgpu.cwsr_enable=0` |
| `linux-firmware` in use | Ubuntu `20250901` + upstream `20260410` override at `/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/` |
| **MES firmware** | `MES feature version: 1, firmware version: 0x00000086` |

### Container / runtime

- Image: `docker.io/kyuz0/vllm-therock-gfx1151:latest` (built 2026-04-19 21:31 UTC)
- vLLM: `0.19.2rc1.dev14+gf150107ef.d20260419`
- PyTorch: `2.13.0a0+rocm7.13.0a20260419`
- HIP: `7.13.26154`

## Symptom

Running vLLM with `cyankiwi/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-AWQ-4bit` (MoE 35B/3B active, AWQ-4bit, ~20 GiB weights), `--enforce-eager`, `--max-num-seqs 1`, `--max-model-len 262144`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`, vision encoder disabled.

Under sustained prefill load (agentic client sending back-to-back long-context requests), the engine wedges after **20–90 seconds**:

```
Engine 000: Avg prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s,
            Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s,
            Running: 1 reqs, Waiting: 1 reqs,
            GPU KV cache usage: 0.9%
```

From that point:

1. CPU-only services (systemd-cron, sysstat, tailscaled, journald) keep heartbeating for **2–4 minutes**.
2. The whole box then fully freezes. Only a hard reboot recovers it.
3. After reboot: `EXT4-fs (dm-0): orphan cleanup on readonly fs` + `system.journal … corrupted or uncleanly shut down` (hard-hang confirmation).

### What is NOT present in dmesg

- No `amdgpu … page fault`, no `GCVM_L2_PROTECTION_FAULT_STATUS`.
- No `GPU reset` / `device wedged`.
- No MCE / `hardware error` / `machine check`.
- No OOM / `Killed process`.
- No thermal / throttling / `under-voltage` / `brown-out`.
- No panic / Oops / Call Trace.

The **only** kernel tell on the crashing boot is `pcieport 0000:00:08.1: PME: Spurious native interrupt!`, typically 30–60 s after the engine wedges, consistently present across every reproduction on this node.

## Reproduction

1. Kernel ≥ 6.18-rc6 (or mainline as above), `amdgpu.cwsr_enable=0`.
2. Upstream `linux-firmware 20260410` installed to `/lib/firmware/updates/amdgpu/`, MES reports `0x86`.
3. vLLM via `docker.io/kyuz0/vllm-therock-gfx1151:latest`, settings above.
4. Drive concurrent long-context prefill load (~20 k-token prompts, back-to-back).
5. Hang within 20–90 s.

Short conversational requests do **not** trigger it. A ≥10 k-token prefill burst or sustained decode does.

## Fence-ring evidence (new this round)

### How it was collected

A 2-second-cadence sampler of `/sys/kernel/debug/dri/0000:c1:00.0/amdgpu_fence_info` running as a systemd service on the host, log rotated on each service start so the file active at the moment the box freezes survives the reboot.

Sampler (`/usr/local/bin/gpu-fence-sampler.sh`):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Fence-info sampler: 2s cadence, timestamped.
# Rotates on service start so prior-boot data is preserved across crash+reboot.
set -u
LOG=/var/log/gpu-fences.log
if [ -s "$LOG" ]; then
  for i in 4 3 2 1; do
    [ -f "$LOG.$i" ] && mv "$LOG.$i" "$LOG.$((i+1))"
  done
  mv "$LOG" "$LOG.1"
fi
: > "$LOG"
printf '=== boot $(uname -r) start %s ===\n' "$(date -u +%F\ %T)" >> "$LOG"
while true; do
  ts=$(date -u +%H:%M:%S.%3N)
  {
    printf '=== %s ===\n' "$ts"
    cat /sys/kernel/debug/dri/0000:c1:00.0/amdgpu_fence_info
  } >> "$LOG"
  sleep 2
done
```

systemd unit (`/etc/systemd/system/gpu-fence-sampler.service`):

```
[Unit]
Description=amdgpu fence sampler (2s) for hang investigation
After=multi-user.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/gpu-fence-sampler.sh
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5s

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

### MES scheduler ring (`mes_3.0.0`) across the wedge

Projected from one representative crash boot (full log attached below as `gpu-fences.log.2`). Each row is a 2 s sample; columns are `Last signaled fence` / `Last emitted`.

| UTC | mes_3.0.0 sig / em | interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| 15:36:00.409 | `0x3ef` / `0x3ef` | normal advance |
| 15:36:46.633 | `0x559` / `0x559` | first request just submitted |
| 15:36:48.641 | `0x561` / `0x561` | advance |
| 15:36:50.648 | `0x561` / `0x561` | advance |
| **15:36:52.666** | **`0x570`** / **`0x570`** | **last observed advance** |
| 15:36:54.675 | `0x570` / `0x570` | frozen |
| 15:37:08.731 | `0x570` / `0x570` | **vLLM reports first `0.0 tok/s`** (≈16 s after MES last advanced) |
| 15:37:46.907 | `0x570` / `0x570` | first `pcieport … PME: Spurious native interrupt!` fires |
| 15:39:39.403 | `0x570` / `0x570` | CPU-only services still heartbeating |
| 15:41:07.794 | `0x570` / `0x570` | **last sampler read before full box freeze** (4 min 14 s of MES freeze captured) |

Across every post-freeze snapshot:

- `Last signaled fence == Last emitted` — host and device agree the ring is idle; host is *not* queuing new MES work.
- `Last reset = 0x00000000` — amdgpu's GPU reset path is **never** invoked.
- `Last preempted = 0x00000000` — no preemption attempts.

### What this rules in / out

- **Rules in:** amdgpu hangcheck/watchdog never fires for this failure mode — that's the reason the crash is silent in dmesg.
- **Rules in:** MES firmware is not fully dead on the bus — the debugfs node is still readable throughout the 2.5–4 min window, i.e. PCIe config space is alive. But the MES ring is not being driven.
- **Does not resolve:** whether the root cause is in MES firmware itself (wedged on chip) or in the amdgpu MES command path (deadlocked on host). `amdgpu_fence_info` is blind to KFD user-mode compute queues (doorbell-driven), which is where vLLM's actual compute submissions live.
- **Does not resolve:** whether a compute shader is still running on the CUs, or the CUs are idle.

## Ruled out (single-variable probes, all exonerated on this node)

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `TORCH_ROCM_AOTRITON_ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL=1` dropped | still crashed |
| `amdgpu.noretry=1` | still crashed |
| `ATTENTION_BACKEND=ROCM_ATTN` (vs default `TRITON_ATTN`) | still crashed — note `chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:398 Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation`, so this override is a no-op for the AWQ decode path |
| `VLLM_V1_USE_PREFILL_DECODE_ATTENTION=1` | crashed ~40 s |
| `VLLM_USE_TRITON_FLASH_ATTN=0` | crashed ~23 s |
| `VLLM_ROCM_USE_MMAP_FOR_TRITON=0` | crashed (~60 s) |
| BIOS upgrade | already on latest (03.04, 2025-11-19) |
| Thermal / RAM / GTT pressure | all flat at values well below any threshold during the whole repro window |
| PSU sag | inconsistent with symptom — CPU + NVMe + net keep running 2–4 min after GPU wedge; no under-voltage/MCE/throttle events |

## Known workaround (not a fix)

`VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` prevents the hang. The mechanism appears to be that per-step stderr writes throttle the Python submission loop enough that GPU utilisation drops from ~100% to ~70%, which dodges the timing window that triggers the hang. This is consistent with the `pcieport 0000:00:08.1: PME: Spurious native interrupt!` precursor pointing at root-complex bursty-submission stress.

## Questions for AMD

1. Is there a recommended debugfs / sysfs observable for **KFD user-mode compute queue** state that would let us see whether a shader is wedged vs the doorbell path itself? `amdgpu_fence_info` is blind to the actual vLLM compute work.
2. Why does the MES ring freeze while the amdgpu hangcheck never fires? Is the watchdog not armed for MES-ring idleness, or is it armed but the recovery path itself deadlocks before logging?
3. Is the `pcieport 0000:00:08.1: PME: Spurious native interrupt!` signal on Strix Halo (GPU root-complex, `00:08.0`) a known accompanying symptom, and does it point to a specific layer (SMU, PCIe AER, MES)?

---

## Attachments

### `amdgpu_firmware_info` (full)

```

source.title: Int8DynamicActivationInt8WeightConfig noticeably slower than torch.ao's quantize_dynamic()
source.body:
### Description

This isn't so much a regression within torchao itself as it is a regression compared to torch.ao, but when I run for example:

```
pocket-tts generate --voice voice.wav --language english_2026-04 --quantize --device cpu --text "hello world, this is a very long sentence so that the inference will take long enough for us to do some chunking and show that the same performance is repeated. hello world, this is a very long sentence so that the inference will take long enough for us to do some chunking and show that the same performance is repeated."
```

(where voice.wav is simply [this wav](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/chatterbox-multilingual-ONNX/blob/2301da1364e51845d60726654bcd0a85d0e96f02/default_voice.wav) converted to a 16-bit signed integer wav)

With torchao installed (which is automatically detected and used), I get ~5.33x faster than realtime performance. If I don't install or I uninstall torchao so that the fallback to torch.ao is used, I get ~7.17x faster than realtime.

I'm not familiar enough with pytorch, torchao, or even Python for that matter to know where the fault lies.

I did try various things like adding a `module.compile()` after the `quantize_()` call, but that actually made things significantly slower (I guess because there is a lot of recompiling going on or something similar).

I also tried reducing the quantized parts of each layer to see if it was just the attention or just the ffn quantizations that were the problem and removing either did not result in equal or better performance for torchao.

### Before/After numbers

```text
With torchao: ~5.33x faster than realtime
With torch.ao: ~7.17x faster than realtime
```

### Model and quantization config

[pocket-tts](https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts) 2.1.0

[Here](https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts/blob/670e7772607d182929594fdf11540d7565246477/pocket_tts/quantization.py) is the quantization code. As far as I can tell it's using the fbgemm backend to apply Int8DynamicActivationInt8WeightConfig quantization to the attention and ffn parts of flow lm transformer layers.

### Environment

```text
Python 3.12.3 + CPU (tested with: Ryzen 7700X, Xeon Gold 6238)
torch==2.11.0+cpu
torchao==0.17.0
torchaudio==2.11.0+cpu
```

source.title: Merge llama.cpp commit b9fd7ee (remove bit-shuffling) breaking changes to old quantized models
source.body:
llama.cpp recently removed bit-shuffling in some of the quantized file formats to improve performance, this a breaking change which currently doesn't have an upgrade path other then re-quantizing the base models (some users only have the quantized ggml models).

I support any change that makes inference faster as I think we still have a long way to go and don't think we should slow down the pace of improvements for what is still essentially still alpha software. That being said I also don't want to cause too much disruption to existing users who have _working_ setups. I'll create a PR for this change and keep it open for at least the weekend before publishing a new PyPI release with the changes. After that the old version will remain available on PyPI and through the releases so people can keep it pinned.

source.body:
### System Info

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| GPU | NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell |
| GPU compute capability | 12.0 / SM120 |
| GPU memory | 48935 MiB |
| Host driver | 580.126.20 |
| TensorRT-LLM release image | `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc22` |
| Release image digest | `sha256:36d6146dfb19084f7098852991b0da67565cba1e5a9bb5980b1c1a7edae3bf1b` |
| TensorRT-LLM devel image | `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/devel:1.3.0rc22` |
| Devel image digest | `sha256:08fd5ecb9598cc9736fb80585c214984081ae205f284341ad6a1dad21235c572` |
| TensorRT-LLM version in release log | `1.3.0rc22` |
| PyTorch in release log | `2.12.0a0+5aff392`, NVIDIA Release 26.05 |
| CUDA note in release log | CUDA forward compatibility enabled; CUDA 13.2 driver version 595.58.03 with kernel driver 580.126.20 |

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Information

- [x] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [x] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder (such as GLUE/SQuAD, ...)
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

## Summary

I am trying to serve a Gemma NVFP4 vision-language model on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell GPU. The same model can be served and benchmarked successfully with vLLM, but TensorRT-LLM `release:1.3.0rc22` fails during executor warmup before the OpenAI-compatible HTTP server becomes ready.

The main release-image failure is:

```text
RuntimeError: Error in function 'TllmGenFmhaRunner' at
/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/flashinfer/data/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaRunner.cuh:37:
Unsupported architecture
```

I also tried the `devel:1.3.0rc22` image and attempted to build TensorRT-LLM from source for `sm_120`, but could not produce a usable runtime image.
## Model

Local model path:

```text
nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4
```

Model config summary:

```json
{
  "model_type": "gemma4",
  "architectures": ["Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration"],
  "dtype": "bfloat16",
  "quantization_config": {
    "quant_algo": "NVFP4",
    "quant_method": "modelopt",
    "producer": {
      "name": "modelopt",
      "version": "0.43.0rc2.dev91+gc79ebc014"
    },
    "kv_cache_scheme": {
      "dynamic": false,
      "num_bits": 8,
      "type": "float"
    }
  }
}
```

The release image appears to load the NVFP4 weights before failing during warmup. The log repeatedly shows:

```text
[TRT-LLM] [W] [quantize] Inline 'config.json.quantization_config' diverges from 'hf_quant_config.json':
  - group_size: file=16, inline=None
```


### Expected behavior


`trtllm-serve` should start successfully on SM120 and serve the Gemma NVFP4 model, or the documentation should state that this model/GPU/quantization combination is unsupported and provide the recommended image/configuration.
The same model can run through the OpenAI-compatible API with vLLM on the same server. A small vision request benchmark used one inline 1x1 PNG image, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=64`, 64 measured requests per worker setting, and 4 warmup requests excluded from timing.

Results:

| Framework | w1 QPS | w2 QPS | w4 QPS | w8 QPS | Abnormal outputs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| vLLM | 6.37 | 10.77 | 21.73 | 41.51 | 0 |
| TensorRT-LLM | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | 0 |

This suggests the model files are usable and the failure is specific to TensorRT-LLM runtime/configuration/support.


### actual behavior

With `release:1.3.0rc22`

The service fails before becoming ready. The default path enters FlashInfer/TRTLLM-gen FMHA and fails with `Unsupported architecture`:

```text
Model init total -- 21.36s
[TRT-LLM] [W] [_torch] KVCacheV2Scheduler only supports MAX_UTILIZATION for now, got GUARANTEED_NO_EVICT, setting to MAX_UTILIZATION
flashinfer.jit: Fetching .../fmha/trtllm-gen/checksums.txt
flashinfer.jit: File downloaded successfully ...
flashinfer.jit: Fetching .../fmha/trtllm-gen/include/flashInferMetaInfo.h
flashinfer.jit: File downloaded successfully ...
[TRT-LLM] [E] [executor] Failed to initialize executor on rank 0:
Error in function 'TllmGenFmhaRunner' at
/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/flashinfer/data/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaRunner.cuh:37:
Unsupported architecture
```

The full traceback ends with:

```text
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/flashinfer/prefill.py", line 264, in _paged_run
  op.trtllm_paged_attention_context(
File "python/tvm_ffi/cython/function.pxi", line 923, in tvm_ffi.core.Function.__call__
RuntimeError: Error in function 'TllmGenFmhaRunner' at
/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/flashinfer/data/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaRunner.cuh:37:
Unsupported architecture
```

Then the server exits:

```text
[TRT-LLM] [E] [executor] Executor worker died during initialization.
RuntimeError: Executor worker died during initialization
```

## Workarounds Tried

I tried forcing different attention backends and explicit KV cache limits:

```yaml
max_input_len: 2048
attn_backend: VANILLA
kv_cache_config:
  max_tokens: 32768
```

```yaml
max_input_len: 2048
attn_backend: TRTLLM
kv_cache_config:
  max_tokens: 32768
```

The recorded result was that these avoided the first `TllmGenFmhaRunner` failure, but still entered `flashinfer.py` and failed with a metadata mismatch:

```text
swap_paged_kv_indices_for_layer missing on Vanilla/TrtllmAttentionMetadata
```


### additional notes

I also pulled `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/devel:1.3.0rc22`, but it is not a drop-in replacement for the release image:

```text
which trtllm-serve -> not found
python3 importlib.util.find_spec("tensorrt_llm") -> None
bash: line 1: trtllm-serve: command not found
```

The `/workspace` directory in the devel image contained README/tutorial/docker example files, but no TensorRT-LLM source checkout.

## Source Build Attempt From Devel Image

I uploaded a TensorRT-LLM source checkout under:

```text
/root/workspace/test_script/build/TensorRT-LLM
```

The README in the checkout identifies the release as `1.3.0rc22`. I attempted to build for:

```text
--cuda_architectures=120-real
```

Important observations:

```text
-- TensorRT LLM version: 1.3.0rc22
-- CUDA compiler: /usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc
-- The CUDA compiler identification is NVIDIA 13.2.78 with host compiler GNU 13.3.0
-- GPU architectures: 120
-- Excluding SM 80
-- Excluding SM 86
-- Excluding SM 89
-- Excluding SM 90
-- Excluding SM 100
-- Excluding SM 103
-- Excluding SM 100F
```

So CMake did accept SM120 at configure time.

Build attempts:

1. Full `build_wheel.py` with `requirements-dev.txt`: container exited with code 137 during pip dependency installation.
2. Runtime-only requirements: container also exited with code 137 during pip dependency installation.
3. No-requirements build using preinstalled packages plus Conan: reached CMake configure and accepted SM120, but `FetchContent[pybind11]` GitHub clone hung/killed.
4. GitHub mirror/ghproxy: `git ls-remote` worked, but actual `git clone` still exited 137.
5. Minimal URL/tarball build with `BUILD_DEEP_EP=OFF`, `BUILD_DEEP_GEMM=OFF`, `BUILD_FLASH_MLA=OFF`, and pip-installed `nanobind`: nanobind resolved, but CUTLASS tarball download failed:

```text
-- FetchContent[cutlass]: clone start
-- Using src='https://ghproxy.net/https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/archive/v4.4.2.tar.gz'
CMake Error at .../download-cutlass-populate.cmake:163 (message):
  error: downloading 'https://ghproxy.net/https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/archive/v4.4.2.tar.gz' failed
  status_string: "Stream error in the HTTP/2 framing layer"
...
HTTP/2 stream 1 was not closed cleanly: INTERNAL_ERROR (err 2)
...
CMake Error at /usr/local/cmake/share/cmake-4.0/Modules/FetchContent.cmake:1918 (message):
  Build step for cutlass failed: 2
```

No usable TensorRT-LLM image with `trtllm-serve` was produced.
## Questions

1. Is RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell / SM120 officially supported by `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc22` for Gemma NVFP4?
2. Is `TllmGenFmhaRunner ... Unsupported architecture` expected on SM120 in this image, or is this a missing FlashInfer/TRTLLM-gen FMHA cubin/kernel support issue?
3. What is the recommended attention backend and `trtllm-serve` configuration for Gemma NVFP4 on SM120?
4. Is the `swap_paged_kv_indices_for_layer` metadata mismatch with `VANILLA`/`TRTLLM` attention backends a known issue in `1.3.0rc22`?
5. Which image should be used to build and run TensorRT-LLM for SM120 + Gemma NVFP4? Is there a newer internal/nightly image or documented source build path that includes all required dependencies?
6. Are there any required flags for NVFP4 acceleration on Blackwell that are not automatically enabled by `trtllm-serve`?


### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and checked the [documentation](https://nvidia.github.io/TensorRT-LLM/) and [examples](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/tree/main/examples) for answers to frequently asked questions.

source.title: [Bug] Qwen3.6 awq doesn't work with offloading
source.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

I'm trying to run `cyankiwi/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ-4bit` with sglang on 4090 24G. The model contains visual embeddings inside therefore already 23G, but unfortunately I can't choose not to load them, because --language-only requires --encoder-urls, and providing a random url doesn't decrease mem usage at all, therefore I have to use offloading. Then I hit the exception below

  ## Bug Description

  Running `Step-3.5-Flash-FP8` with `--tp 4 --ep 4 --quantization fp8` fails during model loading with a `ValueError` in FP8 block quantization validation. The shared
  expert's `gate_up_proj` (a `MergedColumnParallelLinear`) has an output partition size of 320, which is not divisible by the FP8 block quantization `block_n = 128`.

  ## Reproduction

  ```bash
  python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path Step-3.5-Flash-FP8 \
    --tp 4 \
    --ep 4 \
    --quantization fp8 \
    --trust-remote-code

  Error Traceback

  File "/workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py", line 350, in validate_block_quant_shapes
      raise ValueError(
  ValueError: Weight output_partition_size = 320 is not divisible by weight quantization block_n = 128.

  Full call path:
  Scheduler.__init__ → init_model_worker → TpModelWorker.__init__ → ModelRunner.load_model
  → Step3p5ForCausalLM.__init__ → Step3p5Model.__init__ → make_layers
  → Step3p5DecoderLayer.__init__ → Step3p5MLP.__init__ (share_expert)
  → MergedColumnParallelLinear.__init__ → Fp8LinearMethod.create_weights
  → validate_block_quant_shapes

  Root Cause Analysis

  In step3p5.py, the shared expert MLP is constructed with intermediate_size=config.share_expert_dim (1280 for Step-3.5-Flash). The Step3p5MLP.__init__ does not pass a
  custom tp_size to MergedColumnParallelLinear, so it defaults to the global TP size (4).

  This results in:
  - output_partition_size = 1280 / 4 = 320
  - FP8 block quantization requires output_partition_size % block_n == 0 (i.e., 320 % 128 == 0)
  - FP8 block quantization requires output_partition_size % block_n == 0 (i.e., 320 % 128 == 0)
  - 320 % 128 = 64 ≠ 0 → validation fails

  Suggested Fix

  The shared expert should not be sharded across TP ranks for its column-parallel dimension when the partition size is incompatible with FP8 block quantization. Possible solutions:

  1. Pass tp_size=1 for the shared expert when using EP (expert parallelism), since the shared expert is replicated across EP ranks anyway and its output is combined with the MoE output before
   a single all-reduce.
  2. Pad the partition size to be divisible by block_n in the FP8 quantization layer.
  3. Skip block quantization validation for the shared expert and fall back to per-tensor FP8 quantization for this specific layer.

  Environment

  - SGLang version: v0.5.11
  - Model: Step-3.5-Flash-FP8
  - TP: 4, EP: 4
  - Quantization: fp8 (block quantization, block_n=128)

- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

## Describe the bug

Launching `RedHatAI/Kimi-K2.6-NVFP4` (CompressedTensors W4A4 NVFP4; language model is `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM`) on `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` deterministically crashes during `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA.__init__`, ~37 s after `launch_server` start and before any weight tensors are loaded:

```
File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 1527, in __init__
    and self.fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa.weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1968, in __getattr__
    raise AttributeError(
AttributeError: 'ReplicatedLinear' object has no attribute 'weight'
```

### Root cause

The `use_min_latency_fused_a_gemm` check in `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA.__init__` reads `self.fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa.weight.dtype` directly, guarded only by an AWQ-family allowlist:

```python
self.is_packed_weight = (
    self.has_fused_proj
    and hasattr(self.fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa.quant_method, "quant_config")
    and self.fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa.quant_method.quant_config.get_name()
    in {"awq", "awq_marlin", "moe_wna16"}        # <-- compressed-tensors not listed
)
self.use_min_latency_fused_a_gemm = (
    self.has_fused_proj
    and not self.is_packed_weight                 # True for NVFP4 → falls through
    and self.fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa.weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16   # crashes
    ...
)
```

CompressedTensors NVFP4 builds the `ReplicatedLinear` with `weight_packed` / `weight_scale` / `weight_scale_2` parameters — no top-level `.weight`. Because `"compressed-tensors"` isn't in the allowlist, `is_packed_weight` is `False`, the third `and` clause runs, and `nn.Module.__getattr__` raises.

(Line 1527 in the dev-cu13 image's sglang `0.0.0.dev1+gedb1b3f8f`; the same logic sits at L1349-1364 in current main, commit `cbc2bee547`.)

### Related

Issue #22855 reports the identical traceback with `cyankiwi/GLM-5.1-AWQ-4bit` on H800. PR #23195 attempted a defensive `getattr(..., "weight", None)` fix but was closed unmerged by the author on 2026-05-02 after a downstream `KeyError` was reported. No replacement PR exists.

source.title: discussion: No default backend included
source.body:
**Version:** 0.6.6

## Describe the Bug

No fallback backend is baked into the Jan 0.6.6 build.

This is not good design: it means that the app does not work out of the box; that it cannot run for the first time without an Internet connection (think PCs where Internet traffic is monitored, airgapped machines, live boots, etc.); that corrupt backend downloads don't have a fallback; also for the AppImage build it runs counter to the principle of AppImages being self-contained.

**Proposed fix**: just revert the (unintentional?) change and include a full working llama.cpp backend in the build as was the case before v0.6.6, while keeping the background download of the newest backend version. This would be straightforward and also fix issue #5979 at once with zero effort - the user could immediately start using the app while the latest tested backend, when available, is downloaded in background.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Either install Jan v0.6.6 for the first time using the installer file for any given platform, or run the Linux AppImage, without an Internet connection.
2. Try to run any saved GGUF model. Only the error message _Invalid version/backend format: none. Expected format: \<version\>/\<backend\>_ is displayed.

Marking as bug and not feature as it is a regression from v0.6.5.

## Operating System
- [x] MacOS
- [x] Windows
- [x] Linux

**Describe the bug**
I have a manually installed model (Mistral Instruct 7B, v0.2) and given it a model.json file with a max context length field of 32,768. source.title: [Bug] revert_checkpoint_conversion_mapping crashes with re.error "invalid group reference" on transformers-5.x models
source.body:
### Problem Description

Exporting a quantized model whose HF class defines a `checkpoint_conversion_mapping` (transformers 5.x) via `format="llm_compressor"` raises `re.error: invalid group reference 1` inside `revert_checkpoint_conversion_mapping`.

The function strips regex **capture groups** from the *source* pattern (`re.sub(r"\(.*\)", "", source_pattern)`) but leaves the corresponding **backreferences** (e.g. `\1`) in the *target* pattern. `re.subn(source, target, name)` then fails to compile the replacement template because the referenced group no longer exists.

### Reproduction Steps

```python
from auto_round import AutoRound
ar = AutoRound(model="<any Qwen3.5-MoE checkpoint>", scheme="W4A16")
ar.quantize_and_save(output_dir="out", format="llm_compressor")
```

Qwen3.5/3.6-MoE's transformers conversion mapping is e.g.
`{'^model\.language_model\.(.+)$': 'model.\\1', ...}` — the `(.+)` group is stripped from the source while `\1` remains in the target, triggering the error.

### Environment Information

- auto-round 0.14.1
- transformers 5.10.4
- torch 2.12.0+xpu
- Python 3.12.3

### Error Logs

```
File ".../auto_round/utils/common.py", line 1195, in revert_checkpoint_conversion_mapping
    name, n_replace = re.subn(source_pattern, target_pattern, name)
File ".../re/__init__.py", line 334, in _compile_template
    return _sre.template(pattern, _parser.parse_template(repl, pattern))
re.error: invalid group reference 1 at position 22
```

### Additional Context

- The function is imported into multiple modules (`compressors/base.py`, `compressors/shard_writer.py`). The `shard_writer` path only fires when a `layer_config` excludes some layers (mixed-precision quant), so a **uniform** quant can pass while a **mixed** one fails — worth patching in both call sites' shared helper.
- Suggested fix: keep source/target consistent — either do **not** strip the capture group from the source, or strip the backreference from the target whenever the group is stripped from the source.
- Worked around locally by monkeypatching the function to try the intact pattern first and fall back to stripping both sides.

source.title: [Bug]: cannot quantize models larger than available VRAM using v0.10.0 unless low_gpu_mem_usage = True
source.body:
### Problem Description

With release V0.9.7, I was able to begin quantization of google/gemma-3-27b-it on a 48GB GPU (RTX 6000 Ada) despite the model not fitting entirely into VRAM. Now, the exact same call in v0.10.0 fails when the model is moving to CPU:

```python
2026-02-12 15:00:32 INFO autoround.py L165: using MLLM mode for multimodal model.
Loading weights: 100%|████████████████| 1247/1247 [00:00<00:00, 2167.15it/s, Materializing param=model.vision_tower.vision_model.post_layernorm.weight]
2026-02-12 15:01:03 INFO base.py L486: using torch.bfloat16 for quantization tuning
2026-02-12 15:01:03 WARNING formats.py L154: some layers are skipped quantization (shape not divisible by 32).
2026-02-12 15:01:03 INFO base.py L1739: start to cache block inputs
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/daved/project/code/convert_autoround.py", line 43, in <module>
    ar.quantize_and_save(output_dir = quant_path, format = "auto_round")
  File "/home/daved/miniforge3/envs/autoround/lib/python3.12/site-packages/auto_round/compressors/base.py", line 949, in quantize_and_save
    model, _ = self.quantize()
               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/daved/miniforge3/envs/autoround/lib/python3.12/site-packages/auto_round/compressors/base.py", line 1740, in quantize
    all_inputs = self.try_cache_inter_data_gpucpu(all_first_block_names, self.nsamples, layer_names=layer_names)
                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/daved/miniforge3/envs/autoround/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/utils/_contextlib.py", line 124, in decorate_context
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/home/daved/miniforge3/envs/autoround/lib/python3.12/site-packages/auto_round/compressors/base.py", line 2209, in try_cache_inter_data_gpucpu
    new_max_memory[device] = max_memory[device] * 0.9
                             ~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^
KeyError: 0
```

The error occurs here: https://github.com/intel/auto-round/blob/81c8ee4262dd0094d736545deac0af8a393ecfb7/auto_round/compressors/base.py#L2190

The cause is due to a mismatch between the list of devices here:
https://github.com/intel/auto-round/blob/81c8ee4262dd0094d736545deac0af8a393ecfb7/auto_round/compressors/base.py#L2172

And the max memory produced here: 
https://github.com/intel/auto-round/blob/81c8ee4262dd0094d736545deac0af8a393ecfb7/auto_round/compressors/base.py#L2174

The former includes device 0 for the GPU, whereas the latter only picks up the CPU. Hence, there is no 0 key on the later line:

```python
['cuda:0'] # devices
{'cpu': 143219032064} # max_memory
```

By manually setting `low_gpu_mem_usage` to `True`, this `KeyError` can be avoided, but this is suboptimal since it leads to performance reductions. Note that correcting the max_memory to include the gpu (`'0'`) led to additional (different) errors.

### Reproduction Steps

1. Run this command:
auto-round \
    --model model \
    --scheme "W4A16" \
    --format "auto_round"
2. Where model is any model larger than available VRAM (e.g., google/gemma-3-27b-it for a 48GB GPU)
3. Run as shown
4. See error above

### Environment Information

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04
- Python version: 3.12
- AutoRound version: v0.10.0
- Hardware: RTX 6000 Ada 48GB

```

source.title: [Question]: Anyone else encounter Ollama Starter Example working once, then failing thereafter?
source.body:
### Question Validation

- [X] I have searched both the documentation and discord for an answer.

### Question

I've previously used a RAG system using Ollama x langchain, but decided to try Ollama x llama-index to see if I'd get better results. Started off with the [Ollama Starter Example](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/getting_started/starter_example_local/), **got it to work once, and then thereafter it would always timeout** (despite setting a 10+ min timeout).

**More details:** In these failures, I noticed that **it wouldn't even progress to the embedding phase (where the progress bars load)**, and looking in task manager the **`ollama_llama_server.exe` was consuming a ton of resources but nothing was happening until the timeout**. When it timed out, the error message would mention **`map_httpcore_exceptions` (similar to the logs [here](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/2424))**.

1. **Is it a problem with my machine specs?** I have 16GB RAM and the Starter Tutorial says at least 32GB of RAM is required. If so, why did it work the first time? [Also, others have run it on 16GB machines.](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/2424#issuecomment-1935459956)
2. **Is it a problem specific to llama-index?** I tried to use (through Ollama) the 4-bit quantized mistral and phi3 models, all of which have worked fine (by themselves and in the langchain RAG) on my machine. For example, llama-index has an [in-memory vector store](https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/community/faq/vector_database/); is it possible that it worked the first time, then the in-memory vector store ran out of memory and thus failed on subsequent tries? Or is it a problem specific to the `llama-index-llms-ollama` library; [some say using the Ollama library works](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/2424#issuecomment-1961173682)?
3. **Is it a problem with Ollama itself?** It sounds like some default context window mismatches are causing odd behavior. See [here](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/issues/13106) and [here](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/pull/13139).

Does any of the above give any clues that help diagnose what's going on? I'm not just looking for a fix, but more trying to understand the principles of why llama-index may not be working for me. And if there's some fundamental problem with Ollama x llama-index (that isn't a problem with Ollama x langchain), such that if I want to use llama-index I need to ditch Ollama for OpenAI?

Thanks in advance.

source.body:
MiMo-V2.5 NVFP4 produces degenerate `+` token output on SM12.0a (RTX PRO 6000).
**Repro:**
1. Launch server with `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13-mimo-v2.5` image.
2. Mount `shadowlilac/MiMo-V2.5-NVFP4` at `/models/model`.
3. Run with `--tp 4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass --quantization modelopt_fp4`.
4. Send POST to `/v1/chat/completions` with simple query.
5. Observe output: `{"choices":[{"message":{"content":"++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++"}}]`.
**Env:**
- GPU: 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM 12.0a), Driver 580.x.
- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13-mimo-v2.5` (sha `983cd01bc992`).
- Model: `shadowlilac/MiMo-V2.5-NVFP4` (175GB, NVFP4 W4A4).
- Config: TP=4, PP=1, DP=1.
**Expected:** Coherent text generation matching BF16 behavior.
**Actual:** Output is always `++++++++++…` regardless of backend or `--enable-fp32-lm-head`.

source.body:
# [Bug] `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE runner has no DeepEP fused func registered — blocks EP+NVFP4 on Blackwell ## Summary When running any NVFP4 MoE model with `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm --moe-a2a-backend deepep --ep > 1`, scheduler init crashes immediately with: ``` NotImplementedError: Runner backend MoeRunnerBackend.FLASHINFER_TRTLLM requires a fused func for a2a backend deepep, but none is registered. ``` Raised at [`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/runner.py:71`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/runner.py) inside `MoeRunner.__init__`. This is a hard block on the natural EP+NVFP4 path on Blackwell: `flashinfer_trtllm` is the runner SGLang's own auto-resolution selects on B200/B300 for NVFP4 MoE, but it has no `(runner=FLASHINFER_TRTLLM, a2a=deepep)` entry in the fused-func registry, so any attempt to combine it with DeepEP fails before weight load completes. ## Environment - Hardware: 8× NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, driver 595.58.03, CUDA 13.2 - TP=8, EP=8, `--quantization modelopt_fp4` Reproduced on **two models** × **two images** × **two `deepep_mode` values**, demonstrating the bug is purely a missing `(runner=FLASHINFER_TRTLLM, a2a=deepep)` registry entry — independent of model architecture, sglang version, or DeepEP routing mode. | Model | Architecture | Image | sglang version | `deepep_mode` | |---|---|---|---|---| | `lukealonso/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4` (256 routed experts, `moe_intermediate_size=1536`) | MiniMaxM2 | `lmsysorg/sglang:latest-cu130-runtime` | 0.5.10.post1 (release) | `auto` | | `nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-NVFP4` (256 routed + 1 shared, MLA, `moe_intermediate_size=2048`) | DeepseekV2 | `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` | latest dev | `normal` | ## Reproduction ### Repro 1 — MiniMax M2.7 NVFP4 on the release image ```bash docker run --gpus all --shm-size 32g --ipc=host --ulimit memlock=-1 \ -p 30000:30000 \ lmsysorg/sglang:latest-cu130-runtime \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path lukealonso/MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4 \ --tp 8 --ep 8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --moe-a2a-backend deepep \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \ --deepep-mode auto \ --disable-radix-cache \ --context-length 16384 ``` ### Repro 2 — DeepSeek R1 NVFP4 on the dev image ```bash docker run --gpus all --shm-size 32g --ipc=host --ulimit memlock=-1 \ -p 30000:30000 \ lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path nvidia/DeepSeek-R1-NVFP4 \ --tp 8 --ep 8 \ --trust-remote-code \ --quantization modelopt_fp4 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --attention-backend trtllm_mla \ --moe-a2a-backend deepep \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \ --deepep-mode normal \ --disable-radix-cache \ --context-length 16384 ``` Both crash at scheduler init before weight load completes — same error message, same `MoeRunner.__init__` raise site, just with line numbers shifted between sglang versions. ## Full tracebacks
Repro 1: MiniMax-M2.7-NVFP4 on `latest-cu130-runtime` (sglang 0.5.10.post1) ``` [2026-04-16 04:18:09 TP5 EP5] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last): File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3600, in run_scheduler_process scheduler = Scheduler( File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 385, in __init__ self.init_model_worker() File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 632, in init_model_worker self.init_tp_model_worker() File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 600, in init_tp_model_worker self.tp_worker = TpModelWorker(**worker_kwargs) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py", line 261, in __init__ self._init_model_runner() File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py", line 344, in _init_model_runner self._model_runner = ModelRunner(...) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 427, in __init__ self.initialize(pre_model_load_memory) File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 507, in initialize self.load_model() File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 1159, in load_model self.model = self.loader.load_model(...) EP+NVFP4 is effectively dead-ended on current SGLang. Worth fixing this issue and #21602 together so EP+NVFP4 has at least one working path. ## Suggested resolution Either of: 1. **Register a DeepEP fused func for `flashinfer_trtllm`** — most aligned with how SGLang's own auto-resolution selects this runner on Blackwell. 2. **Migrate `deep_gemm`'s DeepEP path** off the deprecated forward and onto a non-deprecated equivalent, so `deep_gemm + deepep` becomes the working pair. Path #1 looks more natural since `flashinfer_trtllm` is the production runner upstream is already steering people toward on B200/B300. ## Additional context - We've reproduced this across multiple SGLang images (`latest-cu130-runtime`, `dev`, `dev-cu13`) — the missing registration is on `main`, not container-specific. - Full attempt matrix (8 configurations across 2 models): happy to share if useful. - We have a downstream patch for the modelopt loader EP-slice issue (essentially equivalent to #23531) that gets us past weight load — but inference still fails because of this runner-registry gap.

source.title: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ fails to load with KeyError: experts.w2_weight
source.body:
## Title

Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ fails to load with KeyError: experts.w2_weight

---

## Environment

- GPU: A100 40GB
- CUDA: 12.9
- Docker image: lmsysorg/sglang:Qwen3.5-35B-A3B
- Single GPU
- Model format: AWQ (safetensors, 9 shards)

---

## Model

Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ  Model path: `/data/llm/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ`  The same model works correctly with vLLM.
```bash
docker stop Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ && docker rm Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ
docker run -d --net=host \
--name Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ \
-e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
--runtime=nvidia \
--shm-size 32g \
-e TZ=Asia/Shanghai \
--ipc=host \
-v /data/llm/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ:/data/llm/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ \
vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-a572baff5e5fde4aa3fb92961de04eb043dc5cf4 \
/data/llm/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ \
--tensor-parallel-size 1 \
--reasoning-parser qwen3 \
--enable-auto-tool-choice \
--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
--served-model-name Saga \
--port 8001 \
--max-model-len 65536 \
--enable-prefix-caching \
--generation-config vllm \
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'
```
---

## Command

```bash
docker run -d --net=host \
--name Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ \
-e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
--runtime=nvidia \
--shm-size 32g \
-e TZ=Asia/Shanghai \
--ipc=host \
-v /data/llm/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ:/data/llm/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ \
lmsysorg/sglang:Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
--model-path /data/llm/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-AWQ \
--host 0.0.0.0 \
--port 8001 \
--served-model-name Saga \
--reasoning-parser qwen3 \
--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder
```

---

## Error

During model loading:

```
KeyError: 'model.layers.0.mlp.experts.w2_weight'
```

The error happens inside `model.load_weights()`.

---

## Expected Behavior

The model should load successfully, since it works with vLLM.

---

## Question

Does SGLang support Qwen3.5-35B-A3B AWQ (MoE) format?

Is this a weight format mismatch issue?

source.title: bug: GPU not utilized with manually loaded models
source.body:
**Describe the bug**
With manually loaded models, e.g (https://huggingface.co/TheBloke/OpenHermes-2.5-Mistral-7B-GGUF), the GPU is not used and all inference is performed on CPU.

Of course, without a proper CUDA toolkit and Nvidia GPU this can happen, but even with these properly completed (and displaying versions in settings.json) this bug appears to occur

**Steps to reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
(Using Jan nightly v0.4.3-141)
1. Download OpenHermes GGUF (or any other GGUF quantized model)
2. Install it into the models directory under a folder
3. Run Jan to generate the model.json
4. Load the model as usual, including ensuring that it is set to use GPU
5. When loading model, no VRAM is occupied, and when inferencing no GPU is used.

**Expected behavior**
That GPU should be utilized, much like with models downloaded directly

**Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your issue.

**Environment details**
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Jan Version: Nightly v0.4.3-141
- Processor: Ryzen 5 7600x
- RAM: 64GB
- GPU: Nvidia 3080TI 12GB
- CUDA Toolkit: 12.3
- NVIDA Driver: 546.12

source.title: Issue: Can I load THUDM/chatglm-6b?
source.body:
I've been searching for a large-context LLM with a relatively low parameter count suitable for local execution on multiple T4 GPUs or a single A100. My primary goal is to summarize extensive financial reports. While I came across FinGPT v1, it seems it isn't hosted on HuggingFace.

However, I did find chatglm-6b, which serves as the foundation for FinGPT v1. This model is accessible on HuggingFace, but I'm facing issues loading it.

Here's a snippet that successfully loads and uses the model outside Langchain:

```
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

model_name = "THUDM/chatglm2-6b"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, trust_remote_code=True)

# model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name, trust_remote_code=True).cuda()

# 按需修改，目前只支持 4/8 bit 量化
# model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("THUDM/chatglm2-6b", trust_remote_code=True).quantize(4).cuda()

import torch

has_cuda = torch.cuda.is_available()
# has_cuda = False  # force cpu

if has_cuda:
    #model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("THUDM/chatglm2-6b-int4",trust_remote_code=True).half().cuda()  # 3.92
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("THUDM/chatglm2-6b", trust_remote_code=True).quantize(4).cuda()
else:
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("THUDM/chatglm2-6b-int4",trust_remote_code=True).half()  # float()

response, history = model.chat(tokenizer, f"Summarize this in a few words: {a}", history=[])

```

But, when I try the following, to use in Langchain:

```
from langchain.llms import HuggingFacePipeline

llm = HuggingFacePipeline.from_model_id(
    model_id="THUDM/chatglm-6b",
    task="text-generation",
    model_kwargs={"temperature": 0, "max_length": 64},
)
```

I encounter this error:

```
ValueError: Tokenizer class ChatGLMTokenizer does not exist or is not currently imported.
```

From what I gather, the ChatGLM model cannot be passed directly to HuggingFace's pipeline. While the Langchain documentation does mention using ChatGLM as a local model, it seems to primarily focus on using it via an API endpoint:

```
endpoint_url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"

# direct access endpoint in a proxied environment
# os.environ['NO_PROXY'] = '127.0.0.1'

llm = ChatGLM(
    endpoint_url=endpoint_url,
    max_token=80000,
    history=[["我将从美国到中国来旅游，出行前希望了解中国的城市", "欢迎问我任何问题。"]],
    top_p=0.9,
    model_kwargs={"sample_model_args": False},
)
```

Would anyone have insights on how to correctly load ChatGLM for tasks within Langchain?

source.title: Ternary-Bonsai-27B Q2 produces gibberish; Ternary-Bonsai-8B Q2 works on same host/build
source.body:
## Summary

Ternary-Bonsai-**27B** GGUF (`Q2_0` g128 and `Q2_g64`) loads and runs at a non-trivial tok/s, but decoded output is gibberish (symbol/digit noise).

On the **same machine** and **same class of Prism llama.cpp builds**:

- Ternary-Bonsai-**8B** `Q2_0` answers correctly
- Bonsai-**27B** `Q1_0` (1-bit) answers correctly

So this does **not** look like a generic “GPU/CPU cannot run ternary” failure; it appears specific to **27B ternary**.

## Environment

- OS: Linux (Ubuntu 24.04-class)
- GPU: NVIDIA Tesla P40, compute capability **sm_61**, 24 GB VRAM
- CPU: KVM guest **without SSE4.2 / AVX / POPCNT** (prebuilt Prism CUDA binaries crash with `Illegal instruction`; we build from source)
- CUDA toolkit: **12.8** (`nvcc` 12.8.93)
- Note (probably unrelated): NVIDIA kernel module **580.126.20** vs userland NVML **580.173** (`nvidia-smi` fails; CUDA still enumerates the P40; 1-bit and 8B ternary work)

### llama.cpp builds used

Both built from source with:

```bash
cmake -B build \
  -DGGML_CUDA=ON \
  -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=61 \
  -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF \
  -DGGML_AVX=OFF -DGGML_AVX2=OFF \
  -DGGML_FMA=OFF -DGGML_F16C=OFF -DGGML_BMI2=OFF -DGGML_SSE42=OFF \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=/usr/local/cuda-12.8/bin/nvcc
cmake --build build -j"$(nproc)" --target llama-cli
```

| Tree | Branch | Commit | Role in repro |
|------|--------|--------|----------------|
| A | `prism` | `62061f9` | Loads demo `*-Q2_0.gguf` (g128). 8B OK, 27B gibberish |
| B | `pr/q2_0-cuda` | `87ff025` | Rejects 27B g128 layout; loads `*-Q2_g64.gguf` but 27B still gibberish |

Clone examples:

```bash
git clone --depth 1 -b prism https://github.com/PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp.git llama-prism
# expect 62061f9 (or pin: git checkout 62061f9)

git clone --depth 1 -b pr/q2_0-cuda https://github.com/PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp.git llama-prism-q2
# expect 87ff025
```

## Models (public HF, anonymous download)

| File | Hugging Face repo | Size (bytes) | Result |
|------|-------------------|-------------:|--------|
| `Ternary-Bonsai-27B-Q2_0.gguf` | https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-gguf | 7165121600 | **gibberish** (~19 t/s decode) on tree A |
| `Ternary-Bonsai-27B-Q2_g64.gguf` | same | 7585330240 | **gibberish** (~19 t/s) on tree B |
| `Ternary-Bonsai-8B-Q2_0.gguf` | https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-8B-gguf | 2182184672 | **OK** on tree A |
| `Bonsai-27B-Q1_0.gguf` | https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Bonsai-27B-gguf | 3803452480 | **OK** on stock ggml-org/llama.cpp CUDA sm_61 and on Prism builds |

27B `Q2_0` local size matched HF `x-linked-size`.  
Tree B + 27B `Q2_0` g128 fails to load:

```text
gguf_init_from_reader: tensor 'output_norm.weight' has offset 337715200, expected 357580800
```

Also tried 27B ternary with `-ngl 0` (CPU only): still gibberish (slower).

## Minimal repro commands

```bash
# --- BAD: 27B ternary (tree A / prism @ 62061f9) ---
./build/bin/llama-cli \
  -m Ternary-Bonsai-27B-Q2_0.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -fa on -c 2048 -n 64 \
  --temp 0.5 --top-p 0.85 --top-k 20 \
  -st --reasoning off \
  -p "What is the capital of France? One word only." \
  --no-display-prompt

# --- GOOD control: 8B ternary (same binary, same flags) ---
./build/bin/llama-cli \
  -m Ternary-Bonsai-8B-Q2_0.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -fa on -c 2048 -n 64 \
  --temp 0.5 --top-p 0.85 --top-k 20 \
  -st --reasoning off \
  -p "What is the capital of France? One word only." \
  --no-display-prompt

# --- BAD: 27B ternary g64 (tree B / pr/q2_0-cuda @ 87ff025) ---
./build/bin/llama-cli \
  -m Ternary-Bonsai-27B-Q2_g64.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -fa on -c 2048 -n 64 \
  --temp 0.5 --top-p 0.85 --top-k 20 \
  -st --reasoning off \
  -p "What is the capital of France? One word only." \
  --no-display-prompt
```

## Actual outputs (verbatim-style)

**27B ternary Q2_0 (bad):**
```text
> What is the capital of France? One word only.
4.!-.4%$33"-3*.""""%1+,.32%1,)!4.+$""""$*%)*01"42$
[ Prompt: ~67 t/s | Generation: ~19 t/s ]
```

Other 27B runs look similar (noise; sometimes after `[Start thinking]`).

**8B ternary Q2_0 (good):**
```text
> What is the capital of France? One word only.
Paris.
[ Prompt: ~192 t/s | Generation: ~77 t/s ]
```

**27B 1-bit Q1_0 (good, for contrast):** coherent answers (e.g. capital of France; `17*19` → `323`). `llama-bench` tg128 ≈ 21.9 t/s on this GPU.

## Expected

27B ternary should produce coherent text with the matching GGUF + documented runtime (similar usability to 8B ternary on the correct file/branch pair).

## Questions

1. Exact supported matrix for **Ternary-Bonsai-27B** on CUDA: which GGUF filename + which branch/commit (or release binary)?
2. Is there a known **27B-only** packing / arch issue vs 8B?
3. Should `pr/q2_0-cuda` reject g128 by design, and is g64 expected to be quality-equivalent for 27B?

We can re-test a fixed GGUF or a pointed commit quickly.

Thanks!

source.title: Bug report — Qwen3-Next hybrid cache silently fails - Prompt cache silently broken for Qwen3-Next (hybrid Gated-DeltaNet + SWA Gated-Attention) — recomputes every turn
source.body:
## Summary

The `PromptCache` in `mlx-lm` does not correctly persist state for Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B (hybrid architecture: 36 Gated-Attention layers with SWA + 12 Gated-DeltaNet recurrent layers + MoE routing). Cache hit-rate appears ~0 on multi-turn workloads: every repeat of the exact same prompt triggers a full prefill. No error is raised — the cache silently recomputes.

By contrast, the same model served via `llama.cpp`'s `llama-server` (post PR #19408, merged Feb 2026) achieves correct cache reuse with 40×+ speedup on warm turns.

## Environment

- Mac Studio M4 Ultra, 128 GB unified memory, macOS 25.3
- `mlx-lm` served via LM Studio (MLX backend, build from 2026-04)
- Model: `qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct-mlx@8bit` (80.8 GiB)
- Test harness: direct streaming HTTP POST to `/v1/chat/completions`, measuring TTFT

## Expected behavior

On a repeat of the exact same prompt within the loaded model's lifetime, TTFT should drop from cold (~70 s for 60K tokens) to hit (~1–2 s).

## Actual behavior

TTFT stays at cold levels for every turn. There is no speedup from cache reuse.

### Numbers — cold TTFT (no cache needed — first turn)

| Input size | TTFT |
|---|---|
| 12K | 12.4 s |
| 30K | 28.7 s |
| 60K | 71.6 s |

### Numbers — "hot" TTFT (same prompt, repeated) — should be 1–2 s

| Input size | TTFT observed |
|---|---|
| 12K | ~12 s — no change from cold |
| 30K | ~28 s — no change from cold |
| 60K | ~70 s — no change from cold |

### Comparison — same model, llama.cpp backend (cache works)

| Input size | Cold TTFT | Hot TTFT | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 60K | 54 s | **1.0 s** | **54×** |
| 120K | 250 s | **~1.2 s** | ~208× |

Config: `--swa-full --ctx-checkpoints 128 --checkpoint-every-n-tokens 4096 --slot-prompt-similarity 0.3`

## Reproduction

1. Load `qwen3-next-80b-a3b-instruct-mlx@8bit` in LM Studio (or `mlx-lm` directly)
2. Send a ~10K token prompt via `/v1/chat/completions`, record TTFT
3. Send the exact same prompt again, record TTFT
4. Observe: both TTFTs are similar (both cold) — cache is not hit

## Root cause hypothesis

`PromptCache` appears to be designed for pure transformer layers (list of K, V per layer). Qwen3-Next has 12 Gated-DeltaNet layers that hold **recurrent state**, not K/V. When the cache "restores" a prior prompt, those 12 layers presumably reset to zero state, so the effective model output is wrong → the server falls back to recomputing the full prompt.

Related: the SWA (sliding-window attention) layers may also need special handling around window boundaries that the current cache class doesn't implement.

## Reference implementation

`llama.cpp` PR #19408 (merged Feb 2026) added hybrid-architecture checkpoint save/restore. The key additions:
- Per-layer polymorphic cache entry type (K/V for attention, recurrent state for Mamba/DeltaNet)
- Position-indexed checkpoints (`--checkpoint-every-n-tokens`)
- Prefix-match restore that replays only new tokens

A Python port of the same logic into `mlx-lm` should be feasible in ~1–2 engineer-weeks.

## Impact

Qwen3-Next is a 2025 flagship MoE release and a primary target for local agentic workloads (3.9B active of 80B total — fits comfortably on 128 GB consumer machines). Multi-turn / conversational / tool-calling workloads lose the primary performance lever (prefix-cache reuse).

Until this is fixed, users running Qwen3-Next on Apple silicon are better served by the `llama.cpp` GGUF path, even though MLX cold prefill is ~15 % faster. The cache deficit dominates after turn 2.

## Related

- Existing issue: `mlx-lm#980` (speculative decoding breaks prompt cache — similar cache-path fragility)
- Upstream reference: `ggml-org/llama.cpp#19408`
