source.title: [Bug]  CPU OffloaderV2 with DeepEP fails when local expert count is not in copy_to_gpu_no_ce supported sizes
source.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Environment

- Model: GLM-5.2 FP8
- `n_routed_experts=256`
- `--ep-size 16`
- DeepEP normal mode
- CPU OffloaderV2:

```bash
--offload-group-size 4 \
--offload-num-in-group 1 \
--offload-prefetch-step 1
```

## Problem

Enabling CPU OffloaderV2 causes Prefill warmup to fail with:

```
RuntimeError: unexpected N
```

The failure occurs in:

```
sglang.srt.layers.moe.moe_runner.deep_gemm
    -> copy_list_to_gpu_no_ce()
    -> sgl_kernel.copy_to_gpu_no_ce()
```

Relevant code:

```python
if get_offloader().forbid_copy_engine_usage:
    num_recv_tokens_per_expert_gpu = copy_list_to_gpu_no_ce(
        num_recv_tokens_per_expert
    )
```

When CPU OffloaderV2 is enabled, `forbid_copy_engine_usage` is `true`, so this path is taken unconditionally.

## Root Cause

`num_recv_tokens_per_expert` is a small `int32` control vector produced after DeepEP dispatch. It contains the number of received tokens for every local expert and is used by `ep_scatter()` / grouped GEMM to compute per-expert offsets and work sizes.

For this configuration:

```
global routed experts: 256
EP size:               16
local experts/rank:    16
```

Therefore, the control vector has:

```
N = 16
```

However, the installed `sgl_kernel.copy_to_gpu_no_ce` only provides fixed-size specializations for:

```
N = 32, 64, 72
```

```cpp
void copy_to_gpu_no_ce(const at::Tensor& input, at::Tensor& output) {
  int N = static_cast<int>(input.numel());
  if (N == 72) {
    copy_to_gpu_no_ce_impl<72>(input, output);
  } else if (N == 64) {
    copy_to_gpu_no_ce_impl<64>(input, output);
  } else if (N == 32) {
    copy_to_gpu_no_ce_impl<32>(input, output);
  } else {
    TORCH_CHECK(false, "unexpected N");
  }
}
```

It does not support `N=16`, which causes:

```
RuntimeError: unexpected N
```

This is not an invalid DeepEP output.

`N=16` is the expected local expert count for:

```
256 experts / EP16
```

## Expected Behavior

CPU OffloaderV2 should work with DeepEP for arbitrary valid local expert counts, including `N=16`.

## Actual Behavior

The service fails during model warmup / first Prefill forward:

```
File "sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/deep_gemm.py", line ...
    num_recv_tokens_per_expert_gpu = copy_list_to_gpu_no_ce(...)

File "sgl_kernel/elementwise.py", line 420
    torch.ops.sgl_kernel.copy_to_gpu_no_ce(input, output)

RuntimeError: unexpected N
```

## Suggested Fix

Avoid calling the fixed-shape kernel unconditionally.

### Option A: Add a generic fallback

```python
if len(num_recv_tokens_per_expert) in SUPPORTED_NO_CE_SIZES:
    use copy_to_gpu_no_ce(...)
else:
    use pinned CPU tensor.cuda(non_blocking=True)
```

### Option B: Fallback permanently after unsupported size

Catch the unsupported-size error once and permanently fall back to the regular pinned-memory H2D path for the process.

### Option C: Add an `N=16` specialization

Add a dedicated `N=16` implementation to `copy_to_gpu_no_ce`.

Option A/B is more robust because future models may use different expert counts and EP configurations.

## Workaround

Use the normal pinned-memory H2D copy path for unsupported `N`.

This does not change:

- DeepEP routing
- token counts
- expert offsets
- grouped GEMM semantics

It only disables the `copy_to_gpu_no_ce` optimization for this small control vector.

### Reproduction

## Cross-machine CP Note

This reproduction intentionally enables experimental cross-machine context
parallelism:

```bash
export SGLANG_ALLOW_CROSS_MACHINE_CP=1
```

By default, SGLang rejects cross-machine CP when `tp_size > 8`. The current
source gates this configuration behind `SGLANG_ALLOW_CROSS_MACHINE_CP`, rather
than enabling it silently.

The failure in this issue is independent of that experimental CP gate:

- Cross-machine TP16/CP16 distributed initialization succeeds.
- Mooncake RDMA initialization succeeds.
- Model weights load successfully.
- The failure occurs later, during the first Prefill warmup forward in:
  `copy_to_gpu_no_ce(num_recv_tokens_per_expert)`.

- The same cross-machine CP16 configuration starts successfully when
  OffloaderV2 is disabled.


## Full Command

```bash
export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=bond0
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=bond0
export NCCL_IB_HCA=mlx5_3,mlx5_4,mlx5_5,mlx5_6,mlx5_8,mlx5_9,mlx5_10,mlx5_11
export NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX=2

export SGLANG_ALLOW_CROSS_MACHINE_CP=1
export SGLANG_RUN_ID=glm52-prefill-offload-v2

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \

  --mem-fraction-static 0.82 \

  --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake \
  --disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_bond_0 \
  --enable-prefill-cp \
  --cp-strategy interleave \

  --deepep-mode normal \

source.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 HiSparse crashes/wedges with multiple long-context requests
source.body:
## Summary

DeepSeek-V4 / DSv4 HiSparse can boot, allocate the hierarchical sparse KV pools, and serve one near-max-context request, but it crashes or wedges when multiple long-context requests are active. The failure is not CUDA graph capture and not GPU OOM; the concrete traceback points at DSv4 HiSparse full-token-location -> compressed-C4-location translation.

This was observed on a downstream branch used for SM120/B12X serving, but the failure is in the SGLang DSv4 HiSparse memory-pool path (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py` / `hisparse_memory_pool.py`), so I am filing it here for upstream visibility.

## Tested profile

Hardware / serving shape:

- 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell / SM120, TP=4
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`
- Context cap: `363264`
- Speculative decoding: off
- KV dtype: `fp8_e4m3`
- Chunked prefill: `8192`

Relevant launch flags:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --attention-backend dsv4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --enable-hisparse \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --hisparse-config '{"top_k":512,"device_buffer_size":4096,"host_to_device_ratio":8}' \
  --max-running-requests 16 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 16 \
  --cuda-graph-bs 1 2 4 8 16 \
  --context-length 363264
```

The downstream run also used SM120/B12X kernels for DSv4 attention/MoE/GEMM, but HiSparse initialization and the crash are in the SGLang DSv4 HiSparse pool/coordinator path.

## Startup succeeds

The server starts, initializes DSv4 HiSparse, allocates host KV, and captures CUDA graphs:

```text
HiSparse c4 host-to-device ratio = 8
DSV4 pool sizes: full=3014912, swa=301312, c4=94216, c128=23554, c4_state=18832, c128_state=301312
Initialize DeepSeekV4TokenToKVPool with max_num_reqs=16 swa_size=301312 c4_size=94216 c4_logical_size=753728 c128_size=23554 c4_state_pool_size=18832 c128_state_pool_size=301312
Allocating 9.24 GB host memory for hierarchical KV cache.
Capture cuda graph bs [1, 2, 4, 8, 16]
Capture cuda graph end ... avail mem=9.08 GB
```

So this is not a graph-capture failure.

## Repro workload

A simple synthetic long-context request is enough. For this tokenizer, `"x " * N` is approximately `N+1` tokens.

```python
import concurrent.futures, json, time, urllib.request

URL = "http://127.0.0.1:5076/generate"
C = 4
N = 100000
OUT = 8
base = "x " * N

def one(i):
    payload = {
        "text": f"Request {i}. Continue briefly after this long filler.\n" + base,
        "sampling_params": {
            "temperature": 0,
            "max_new_tokens": OUT,
            "ignore_eos": True,
        },
    }
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        URL,
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    t = time.time()
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800) as r:
        return i, time.time() - t, r.status, r.read().decode()[:200]

with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=C) as ex:
    for fut in concurrent.futures.as_completed([ex.submit(one, i) for i in range(C)]):
        print(fut.result())
```

## Observed pass/fail matrix

| Workload | Result |
|---|---|
| `1 x 360k` input tokens, 1-8 decode tokens | PASS |
| `2 x 360k` concurrent | FAIL: first request completes, second returns HTTP 500 / rank crash |
| `2 x 300k` | FAIL/wedge after first request; `/health` times out |
| `2 x 100k` | PASS, ~44s wall, 0 retractions |
| `3 x 100k` | PASS, ~60s wall, 0 retractions |
| `4 x 100k` | FAIL: all requests return HTTP 500 |

This suggests the issue is not simply context length or total memory. A single near-cap request works, and three 100k requests work, but the fourth long active request reliably trips the HiSparse path.

## Failure signature

For `4 x 100k`, the scheduler crashes after the long prefills complete and multiple requests are active:

```text
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 7168, ... #running-req: 3, #pending-token: 0
Scheduler hit an exception:
  File ".../sglang/srt/mem_cache/hisparse_memory_pool.py", line ..., in translate_loc_to_hisparse_device
    self.translate_loc_from_full_to_compressed(full_indices)
  File ".../sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py", line 206, in translate_loc_from_full_to_compressed
    compressed_indices = full_indices[mask] // self.compress_ratio
                         ~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

The process then tears down and clients receive 500s:

```text
SIGQUIT received. It usually means one child failed.
INFO: 127.0.0.1:38596 - "POST /generate HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
```

For `2 x 300k`, it can wedge instead of immediately throwing the traceback: one request completes, the next hangs, and `/health` times out. The container is not OOM-killed.

## Why this looks like a DSv4 HiSparse location-mapping/lifecycle bug

- CUDA graph capture succeeds before requests.
- Not GPU OOM: `OOMKilled=false`; there is still HBM headroom.
- Single near-max request succeeds.
- Failure appears when several long requests are active and the stack translates full-token locations into compressed C4 / HiSparse device-buffer locations.
- The concrete failing line is in DSv4 full-to-compressed translation: `deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py:206`.

Areas that look relevant:

- `sglang/srt/mem_cache/deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`
- `sglang/srt/mem_cache/hisparse_memory_pool.py`
- `sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py`
- request lifecycle cleanup/reuse for:
  - `req_to_device_buffer`
  - `req_to_host_pool`
  - `req_device_buffer_tokens`
  - `req_device_buffer_token_locs`
  - `raw_indices_buffer`
  - full-token locs passed into `translate_loc_to_hisparse_device`

The suspicion is stale/corrupted full-token locations or masks when several long requests have active C4 HiSparse device buffers and one request is already running while another finishes prefill.

source.title: [Bug] [Hisparse] Hisparse CPU Memory Allocation Checker
source.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

I'd like to report a severe CPU memory allocation bug in the v0.5.10 feature Hisparse(DSA CPU-offload decoding) 

During Hisparse, for each new token generated, it is backed-up in CPU, causing additional CPU memory usage. This is different from non-Hisparse methods as they do not back-up newly generated kv-cache on CPU unless a sequence is retracted.

However, the memory pool system still uses the non-Hisparse checking method that accepts the request if input_length+a small number< CPU memory. 

So when the CPU memory pool is about to become full and the generation length is long, there may be CPU overflow as decode length increases. 

 

### Reproduction

Though the overflow may happen at any setting with rare chance, a way to increase the chance of reproducing it is to 


1: Use a DSA model(Deepseek-V3.2-Speciale/GLM-5.1) and PD disaggregation, set up a small ``host_to_device_ratio`` in ``hisparse-config``, for example, ``--hisparse-config "{'top_k':2048,'device_buffer_size':4096,'host_to_device_ratio':1}"`` 

2: Prepare long hard prompts that require the model to think a lot of tokens.(input is better at 50-100k range, generation shall be more than 4k each)

3: Arrange a lot of prefill servers and only one decode server to give larger pressure to the decoding side.

The decode server is likely to crash due to short of CPU memory because of the bug described.






### Environment

sglang-0.5.10

source.title: [Bug] GLM-5.1-FP8 on H200x8 with TP=8 + EAGLE speculative decoding fails CUDA graph capture: Unsupported h_q: 8 in flash_mla_with_kvcache (NSA backend)
source.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

When launching `GLM-5.1-FP8` on 8x H200 with TP=8 and EAGLE speculative decoding enabled, the scheduler crashes during CUDA graph capture inside the NSA attention backend. The underlying `sgl_kernel.fwd_kvcache_mla` op rejects the head count with:

```
RuntimeError: Unsupported h_q: 8
```

This happens at startup during `init_device_graphs()` → `CudaGraphRunner.capture()`, and the server never finishes booting.

With TP=8, the model has `128 / 8 = 16` query heads per rank. With `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4` the EAGLE verify path effectively requests `h_q = num_draft_tokens * heads_per_token / something` that ends up as **8** when entering `flash_mla_with_kvcache` via the NSA backend's `_forward_flashmla_kv` path. The FlashMLA kernel only supports a fixed set of `h_q` values (typically 16/32/64/128) and rejects 8.

The "possible solutions" printed in the error (lower `--mem-fraction-static`, lower `--cuda-graph-max-bs`, disable torch compile, disable CUDA graph) are unrelated to the real cause — this is a kernel-shape support issue, not OOM.


### Reproduction

`docker-compose.yml`:

```yaml
services:
  glm5.1_worker:
    image: lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.10
    container_name: glm5_worker_node1
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: "host"
    shm_size: "512g"
    ipc: host
    runtime: nvidia
    privileged: true
    cap_add:
      - IPC_LOCK
    ulimits:
      memlock:
        soft: -1
        hard: -1
    environment:
      - SGLANG_DG_CACHE_DIR=/dg_cache
      - SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
    volumes:
      - /data3/models/GLM-5.1-FP8:/models/GLM-5.1-FP8:ro
      - ./dg_cache:/dg_cache
    command: >
      python -m sglang.launch_server
      --model-path /models/GLM-5.1-FP8
      --served-model-name glm-5.1
      --host 0.0.0.0
      --port 8000
      --tp 8
      --reasoning-parser glm45
      --tool-call-parser glm47
      --speculative-algorithm EAGLE
      --speculative-num-steps 3
      --speculative-eagle-topk 1
      --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
      --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
      --mem-fraction-static 0.77
      --max-prefill-tokens 32768
      --max-running-requests 32
      --enable-metrics
      --enable-cache-report
      --page-size 1
      --enable-hierarchical-cache
      --hicache-size 180
```

  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/nsa_backend.py", line 1426, in forward_extend

source.title: [Bug] HiCache loadback 后 GLM-5.2 EAGLE acceptance 静默坍塌
source.body:
## 问题

GLM-5.2 开启 HiCache 后，经长请求填充和 KV 驱逐，EAGLE acceptance
length 从 `4.487` 降至 `1.589`，acceptance rate 从 `69.9%` 降至
`11.7%`；调用 `flush_cache` 后恢复至 `4.331 / 67.0%`。

服务全程正常，无 OOM、retract、KV-full、CUDA error、Traceback 或重启，
因此这是一个静默性能退化。

## 环境

- SGLang `v0.5.15.post1`
- GLM-5.2 W4AFP8，KV FP8 E4M3
- 单节点 8xH20，TP8，DSA attention
- EAGLE：`num_steps=5 / topk=1 / draft_tokens=6`
- HiCache：ratio 3、`write_through_selective`、kernel I/O、无 L3 backend

关键参数：

```bash
--speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
--speculative-num-steps 5 \
--speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
--speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
--enable-hierarchical-cache \
--hicache-ratio 3 \
--hicache-write-policy write_through_selective \
--hicache-io-backend kernel
```

## 复现

所有请求 c1 串行执行，每条请求前确认 `num_running_reqs=0`：

1. `POST /flush_cache?timeout=30`。
2. temperature=0 重放固定的 24 条 Agent 请求，记录逐请求 speculative
   metrics 和完整 response。
3. 发送 12 条无关长请求，每条输入 111k–175k token、只生成 1 token，
   制造 cache 填充和驱逐。
4. 重放相同 24 条请求。
5. 再次 flush 并重放。

加权 accept length 的计算为：

```python
sum(completion_tokens) / sum(spec_verify_ct)
```

## 结果

| 部署 | baseline | cache fill 后 | refush 后 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 开启 HiCache，temperature=0 | 4.487 | **1.589** | 4.331 |
| 关闭 HiCache，temperature=0 | 4.438 | **4.386** | 4.353 |
| 关闭 HiCache，temperature=1 | 4.068 | **4.113** | - |

关键证据：

- HiCache fill 后 18/24 请求发生 host loadback，共 509,376 token；
  flush 后 loadback 归零，acceptance 恢复。
- 有 5 条请求在三个阶段生成了相同的归一化 response，但 acceptance
  仍从 `5.1–5.6` 降至 `1.4–1.6`，再恢复到 `5.1–5.6`。
- 关闭 HiCache 后，同等长请求/KV 驱逐压力下没有复现退化。

## 预期

HiCache eviction/loadback 不应在 target response 不变的情况下，让
EAGLE acceptance 从约 `5.5` 降至约 `1.5`。

## 当前判断

黑盒对照已将必要部署差异收敛到 **HiCache × EAGLE/MTP**，排除了
effort、temperature、response 内容/长度和单纯设备 KV 驱逐作为充分原因。

精确版本源码审计和上游同类 issue 已进一步定位根因：

**HiCache 会同步 target KV、target DSA indexer 和 draft KV，但漏掉 draft
DSA indexer。**

GLM-5.2 的 MTP draft 使用 `DSATokenToKVPool`。该 pool 继承
`MLATokenToKVPool`，除 latent KV 外还持有
`index_k_with_scale_buffer`。`v0.5.15.post1` 的
`maybe_register_hicache_draft()` 没有显式处理 `DSATokenToKVPool`，因此
DSA draft 会命中普通 MLA 分支：

```python
if isinstance(pool, MHATokenToKVPool):
    ...
elif isinstance(pool, MLATokenToKVPool):
    draft_host_pool = MLATokenToKVPoolHost(pool, **kw)
```

最终只创建并搬运普通 draft KV host pool，draft
`index_k_with_scale_buffer` 没有 host pool，也没有参与 HiCache write/load。

L2 回载后，draft KV 已恢复，但 draft sparse attention 使用的 indexer key
仍是旧值或空值。draft 会提出大量错误候选，target verify 再将其拒绝，因此
表现为：

- target response 仍然正确，甚至可以与 baseline 完全相同；
- acceptance length 大幅下降；
- MTP 只剩 draft/verify 开销，性能可能低于 no-MTP；
- flush 后重新执行 fresh prefill，draft KV 和 indexer 一起重建，acceptance
  随之恢复。

部分退化请求当次显示 `host=0` 也不矛盾：它们可以命中此前已经从 L2
回载、并留在 L1 的不完整节点，当次不需要再次发生 host loadback。

## 精确源码版本

线上镜像：

```text
spxix-test.tencentcloudcr.com/model/sglang:20260720.0945-fa30f13
```

镜像构建脚本固定的上游基座为：

```text
lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.15.post1
sha256:00c53fe4c31bf22d7b37537f28bbdfd924c02de13cdfb4bff7378c9c34d75ab2
```

`../sglang` 中该 tag 对应 commit：

```text
0b3bb0cbe31873994c9f989fddfe2f87ca839fdd
```

因此以上判断来自线上精确版本，而非依据较新的 main 推测。

## 相关 issue

### 完全同根因的报告

- [#28895: DSA model (GLM5.1) with L3 HiCache show lower MTP acceptance
  after cache hits](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/28895)

该 issue 明确指出 DSA draft 的 `index_k_with_scale_buffer` 没有随 draft KV
恢复。其 acceptance length 在 cache restore 后从 `2.98` 降至 `1.75`，
TPOT 从 `107.62ms` 增至 `164.74ms`，与本次 GLM-5.2 L2 结果是同一故障
签名。

### 修复 PR

- [#28896: Support DSA draft indexer restore in
  HiCache](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28896)
  - 第一版 DSA 专项修复，同时覆盖 L2/L3；
  - 上游测试中修复后 restore 前后 acceptance 均为 `2.96`；
  - 当前仍 open，且不能直接合入。
- [#30393: Add HiCache draft sidecar pool support for
  MTP/EAGLE](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30393)
  - 后续通用方案，把 `DRAFT`、`DRAFT_INDEXER` 和 `DRAFT_SWA` 建模为
    sidecar pools；
  - DeepSeek-V3.2 测试中，修复前 replay acceptance
    `3.527 → 2.550`，修复后 `3.617 → 3.608`；
  - 当前仍 open、未合入 main，CI 尚未全绿。

已合入的 [#21125](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21125) 只解决了
target loadback 时 draft KV 完全没有同步的第一层问题，没有覆盖
DSA/SWA 等 draft auxiliary pools。

[KV cache roadmap #21846](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21846)
仍把 `MTP × HiCache` 标为未完成，并同时链接 #21125 和 #30393。

截至 2026-07-23，线上 `v0.5.15.post1` 和当日 upstream main
`a25164bda355250015c0ba6d8821f0d4b37abe7d` 都没有完整
`DRAFT_INDEXER` 修复。因此仅升级到当日 main 不能解决问题。

以下两个旧 issue 是可见 crash，并非本次直接同根因：

- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/12477
- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22359

## 临时规避与修复验收

修复合入并完成实机验证前，稳定组合为：

- 需要 MTP：关闭 HiCache；
- 需要 HiCache 容量：关闭 MTP；
- 不把 HiCache + MTP 作为业务稳定配置。

推荐基于精确 tag `v0.5.15.post1` backport draft DSA indexer sidecar，再重跑
同一闭环：

```text
flush → replay → long-prompt fill → replay → flush → replay
```

通过条件是 fill 后 acceptance 不再显著下降，再补 temperature=1 和真实业务
轨迹 soak。

修复预计新增约 `0.21GB/rank` 的 draft indexer pinned host pool，TP8 合计
约 `1.7GB`。节点已知在 HiCache ratio3.5 附近触及累计 pinned-memory
边界，因此 patched image 需要重新执行启动和长稳门禁。

原始请求包含非公开 Agent trace，未附在 issue 中；如维护者需要，可另行
提供脱敏 replay corpus。

source.title: moe_kernels.py, stage-2 reduce path: small SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK silently corrupts output (gsm8k=0) at low concurrency
source.body:
## Summary

On the MoRI expert-parallel backend, a small `SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` **silently corrupts decode output** — the model still generates fluent-looking tokens (speculative acceptance length stays high), but the content is semantically wrong and gsm8k drops to **0.00**. The value is forwarded to MoRI's `max_num_inp_token_per_rank` with no minimum/validation, so configs that legitimately produce a small per-rank dispatch buffer (low concurrency × dp-attention × MTP) hit it with no error or warning.

This is a silent correctness bug: nothing crashes, throughput even looks marginally *better*, so it is easy to ship a broken Pareto point.

## Environment

- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.12.post1-rocm720-mi35x` (sglang v0.5.12.post1)
- HW: AMD MI355X (CDNA, warpSize 64)
- Model: DeepSeek-R1 (FP4), prefill/decode disaggregated
- Decode parallelism: TP8 / EP8 / **dp-attention** / **MTP (num-draft-tokens=4)**
- Backends: `--moe-a2a-backend mori --disaggregation-transfer-backend mori --deepep-mode normal`

## Symptom

At decode concurrency 64 with TP8 + MTP3, the per-rank dispatch buffer works out to `64/8 * 4 = 32` tokens. The server starts, warms up, benchmarks at full speed, and produces grammatical output — but gsm8k = 0. Raising the buffer fixes it.

## Reproduction / evidence (shmoo of the env var, same config)

| `SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK` | gsm8k (strict) | output tok/s | run |
|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | **0.0000** | 6312 | https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/26913235190 |
| 64 (= warpSize) | **0.0000** | 6324 | https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/26919517564 |
| 256 | **0.9424** | 6219 | https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/26920499507 |

(Run links are internal CI; the relevant log excerpts are inline below.) All three runs generate identical token volume — 640 requests, 589,927 generated tokens — so the numbers are directly comparable. Note the corrupt runs are ~1.5% *faster* (less real work), which is why this slips through perf-only validation.

Eval log (256, correct):
```
[MoRI floor] DISPATCH_TOKENS=32 < floor 256; clamping to 256
Decode env: SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=256
PASS: gsm8k exact_match,strict-match = 0.9424 (>= 0.85)
```

## This is not the LL vs non-LL kernel switch

`get_ep_dispatch_configs()` selects `InterNodeV1LL` vs `InterNodeV1` by comparing the dispatch size to `SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_INTER_KERNEL_SWITCH_THRESHOLD` (default 256). In the failing run that threshold was set to 16, and the decode log confirms:

```
[DP+EP override] Decode: ... DISPATCH_TOKENS=8, ... INTER_KERNEL_SWITCH=16
```

Since `32 > 16`, the **non-LL `InterNodeV1`** kernel is selected — and it still corrupts. So the bug is the per-rank buffer size itself, not the kernel variant.

## Where it originates in sglang

In `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/moriep.py` (v0.5.12):

- The value is read with a default of 4096 and **no lower bound**:
  ```python
  self.num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank = get_int_env_var(
      "SGLANG_MORI_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK", 4096)
  ```
- It is passed straight through to MoRI as `max_num_inp_token_per_rank=num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank`.
- There is already a `if num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank < 128:` branch that swaps the launch config (`warp_num_per_block`), so small dispatch sizes are clearly known to be special — but that branch does **not** prevent the corruption at 32/64.

## ~~Likely mechanism (hypothesis — root cause is in MoRI)~~ — **CORRECTED, see below**

~~The MoRI dispatch kernel writes received tokens into warpSize-aligned slots: `destTokId = flagSlotId * warpSize + laneId`, into a per-PE region whose stride is `max_num_inp_token_per_rank`. When that region is smaller than warpSize (64), or smaller than the routing fan-in a rank can receive from all peers, the writes go out of bounds. Empirically warpSize (64) is necessary but not sufficient; ≥256 is needed for this config. Filed in parallel against ROCm/mori: `src/ops/dispatch_combine/internode_v1.cpp` (`DispatchInterNodeSend` / `DispatchIntraNodeBlock`). https://github.com/ROCm/mori/issues/356~~

> ### UPDATE, corrected root cause (not MoRI issue)
>
> The MoRI hypothesis is wrong, and `ROCm/mori#356` was closed as not-a-MoRI-issue. No out-of-bounds write in the dispatch kernel is involved.
>
> The actual root cause is prob in AITER's FlyDSL MoE stage-2 reduce path (`aiter/ops/flydsl/moe_kernels.py`), confirmed by @billishyahao:
>
> - The reduce intermediate is allocated with `torch.empty` (**uninitialized**).
> - In EP, gemm2 writes only valid local-expert slots; masked (non-local) slots are never written.
> - `torch.sum` over `topk` then folds those uninitialized slots in → NaN/garbage → corrupt-but-fluent output.
> - Only the **M≈1024 tuning bucket** selects this reduce kernel; other buckets use a zero-init atomic accumulate, which is why M=1032/2048 were fine and only specific low-concurrency points corrupt.
>
> **Fixed in [ROCm/aiter#3377](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/3377)** (masked gather `valid = expert_mask[topk_ids] != 0` + EP tuned-key `topk -= is_ep`), pulled into SGLang via **#27555** (AITER commit bump `6740fb7` → `7a8ff7d`).
>
> **Not fully resolved:** with the fix applied, conc64 passes but **conc32 and conc16 still fail** ([run](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/27225030090)) — the sub-1024 M-buckets likely need the same masked-reduce treatment. Keeping this open until those are covered.

## Requested fix

1. In `moriep.py`, **enforce or validate a minimum** for `num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank` (and/or emit a clear warning) instead of silently forwarding a too-small value.
2. Revisit the `< 128` launch-config branch — it does not make small buffers correct.
3. Coordinate the actual kernel-level fix with ROCm/mori (sizing from fan-in, or asserting a minimum).

At minimum, a silent correctness failure should become a loud one.

source.title: [Feature] Native SM120 (Blackwell) support for flash_mla_sparse_fwd (DeepSeek-V4 sparse-attention prefill)
source.body:
### Describe the feature / gap

`DeepseekV4AttnBackend._forward_prefill_sparse()` (`sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py`) routes DeepSeek-V4 sparse-attention prefill through `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` (from `sgl_kernel.flash_mla`). This kernel unconditionally raises:

```
RuntimeError: Sparse Attention Forward Kernel is only supported on SM90a and SM100f architectures.
```

on any other compute capability, including **SM120 (Blackwell, e.g. RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q)**. Since PR #29775 ("[DeepSeek V4] Enable FlashMLA sparse prefill by default", merged into `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` as of v0.5.15.post1) flipped `SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL`'s default from `False` to `True`, this now fires unconditionally for DeepSeek-V4 on SM120 hardware — the model cannot serve any request through the default `dsv4` attention backend without the workaround below.

This is a **feature request for native SM120 support**, not a duplicate of #29900. #29900 documents the identical error text but strictly as a *test-suite gating gap* (`test_flashmla.py` needs a compute-capability skip so the 20 already-expected-unsupported failures don't drown out real bugs) — it explicitly does not ask for SM120 support to be implemented, only for the test to skip cleanly. This issue asks for the underlying capability itself.

### Environment

- GPU: 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM120), 97,887 MiB each
- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` resolving to sglang v0.5.15.post1
- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `--attention-backend dsv4`, `--tp-size 2`

### Evidence an SM120-compatible code path is already partially plausible

The **decode-path** kernel (`flash_mla_with_kvcache`) already has an SM120 branch (`flash_mla_with_kvcache_sm120`, added in sglang v0.5.13 via PR #24692), reachable via `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=triton`. Setting `SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL=0` (to opt back out of the sparse-prefill default) together with `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=triton` avoids the unsupported sparse-prefill kernel entirely and routes decode through the existing Triton SM120 fallback — this combination, plus `--mem-fraction-static` tuned to ~0.98 (headroom for the Triton autotune scratch buffer) and `--disable-cuda-graph`/`--skip-server-warmup`, lets DeepSeek-V4-Flash serve real inference requests end-to-end on SM120 today. We verified this empirically with two successful `POST /v1/chat/completions` requests returning valid completions end-to-end.

This confirms an SM120-compatible execution path already exists for the decode side of FlashMLA — it seems plausible the same Triton (or an equivalent) approach could be extended/hardened to cover the sparse-*prefill* kernel (`flash_mla_sparse_fwd`) as well, rather than requiring every SM120 user to discover and apply this env-var combination themselves.

Precedent that SM120-dispatch PRs are accepted for adjacent kernels: PR #28125 ("feat(moe): add SM120/SM121 dispatch for fp8_blockwise_scaled_grouped_mm"), referenced from #29900's `test_fp8_blockwise_moe.py` findings.

### Request

Either:
1. Add native SM120 support to `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` (mirroring the existing `flash_mla_with_kvcache_sm120` decode-path support), or
2. If native support isn't planned near-term, document `SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL=0` + `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=triton` as an official, supported fallback for SM120 users running DeepSeek-V4 so it isn't discovered ad hoc.

Related: #29900 (test-gate gap for the same error, not a fix request), #29897, PR #28125 (SM120 dispatch precedent for a different kernel).

source.title: [Bug] Qwen3.6-27B (hybrid GDN) + AWQ degenerates on few-shot / multi-turn prompts at temperature 0; same checkpoint is clean on vLLM
source.body:
## Describe the bug

QuantTrio/Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ served on sglang 0.5.14 (awq_marlin selected at load) produces degenerate output on multi-turn few-shot prompts at temperature 0: repetition loops, mixed scripts, percent-encoded fragments, spurious `</think>` tags. A 6-shot multiple-choice prompt that should answer with one letter instead runs to the 512-token cap on 8 of 9 probes (mean 435 completion tokens).

Sample (6-shot MC, "What is 2+2? A. 3 B. 4 C. 5 D. 6", temperature 0):

```
- **A. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 6, 9, 10, 1, 2, 3, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1, ...
```

The same checkpoint on vLLM 0.21 answers these prompts with 1-2 tokens, correctly.

## Isolation performed

| variable | result |
|---|---|
| chat template | exonerated: offline `apply_chat_template` output byte-identical to a known-good checkpoint's; the correctly rendered string degenerates identically via `/v1/completions` |
| dtype | not the cause: bfloat16 and all-float16 (with `SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE=float16`, see #31719) both degenerate |
| radix cache | not the cause: `--disable-radix-cache` unchanged |
| awq_marlin alone | works elsewhere: a non-GDN AWQ model (Seed-OSS-arch 36B) on the same install serves multi-turn cleanly |
| engine | vLLM 0.21, same artifact, same prompts: clean |

Remaining suspects are the `qwen3_5` GDN implementation (for example the fused GDN projection path under `sglang/jit_kernel/triton/gdn_fused_proj`) or its interaction with awq_marlin activations. I can run further ablations on request; single-GPU consumer hardware, so tensor-parallel variants are out of reach.

## Reproduction

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path QuantTrio/Qwen3.6-27B-AWQ --dtype bfloat16
# then send a 6-shot multiple-choice chat completion, temperature 0, max_tokens 512.
# Plain single-turn prompts answer fine; few-shot/multi-turn degenerates, as does
# single-turn under an instruction-style system prompt.
```

Probe script with verdict output available; happy to attach.

## Environment

sglang 0.5.14, torch 2.11.0+cu130, flashinfer 0.6.12, driver 595.71.05, CUDA 13.3, RTX 5090 32 GB (sm_120), single GPU.

source.title: [Bug] GlmMoeDsa (GLM-5.2) FP4 + EAGLE: illegal memory access in flashinfer_trtllm bf16 batched-GEMM (nextn draft MoE); triton nextn default is HIP-gated after #30137
source.body:
## Summary
Serving `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, TP4/TP8, B200 & B300, `modelopt_fp4`, kv `fp8_e4m3`) with EAGLE (`--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6`) crashes with `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access` under real production traffic (~10 min to crash per replica at ~1 req/s; ~226k req/day fleet). Disabling speculation (no other change) → zero crashes.

## Root cause evidence
Exception-state CUDA coredump (CUDA_ENABLE_COREDUMP_ON_EXCEPTION) captured the faulting kernel:
```
CUDA Exception: Device Unknown Exception (30)
Bmm_Bfloat16_Bfloat16Bfloat16_Fp32_t128x8x128u2_..._dynB_sm100f  grid (48,8,1)
```
This is a flashinfer TRTLLM batched-GEMM cubin (flashinfer_cubin `batched_gemm-*/Bmm_Bfloat16...dynB`), used by the **flashinfer_trtllm MoE runner for the bf16 nextn/EAGLE draft layer** of the FP4 checkpoint. The kernel family is the sibling of the padding/TMA-OOB issue reported in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3722 (E2m1 swiGlu dynB variant).

## Fix validated in production
`--speculative-moe-runner-backend triton --speculative-moe-a2a-backend none`. Controlled A/B on synchronized-mirrored production traffic (identical requests to both arms, 8xB200 each): **control (flashinfer_trtllm spec-MoE) crashed 5× in 5h; triton arm: 0 restarts in 5h.** Since deployed to production: 24h+ crash-free with healthy speculation (accept len 3.19, accept rate 0.44) and 2.5-2.8× TPOT improvement on real data vs no-spec.

## The config gap
Legacy `server_args.py` applied exactly this default for DeepseekV3-arch FP4 checkpoints ("Use triton fused moe by default for bf16 nextn layer") with **no platform gate**, but `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` was not covered — so GLM-5.2 landed on the broken path by default.
After yesterday's config-pipeline refactor (#30137), `_DEEPSEEK_FAMILY_ARCHS` now includes GlmMoeDsa (good), **but the whole default is now gated `if not is_hip(): return {}`** (arg_groups/overrides.py ~L1199) — i.e. CUDA users of DeepseekV3/V32/Kimi/GLM FP4 + EAGLE no longer get the protective default at all, and fall through to speculative_moe_runner_backend = moe_runner_backend = flashinfer_trtllm → the crashing bf16 dynB bmm path.

PR removing the gate: incoming. Happy to provide coredumps/repro details.

source.title: DSv4 topk_v2 fused-cluster kernel crashes on B300/SM100 with DP-attn + DeepEP
source.body:
## Summary

`topk_transform_512_v2` (the v2 indexer top-k kernel introduced in #23882 and made default in #25406) crashes on **B300 / SM100** when **DP-attention + DeepEP** are enabled, surfacing as `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`. Reproduces deterministically across `lmsysorg/sglang:deepseek-v4-b300-dev`, `:nightly-dev-cu13-20260509-9ee83034`, and `:nightly-dev-cu13-20260517-229cadec`.

## Root cause

`topk_fused_transform` is annotated `__cluster_dims__(1, kClusterSize=8, 1)` via `FUSED_COMBINE_KERNEL`, but its SMALL (`seq_len <= Small::kMax1PassLength`) and TRIVIAL (`seq_len <= K`) branches let 7 of every 8 cluster blocks `return` immediately **without ever calling `cluster.sync()`**:

```cpp
if (seq_len <= K) {
    if (cluster_rank != 0) return;   // 7 blocks exit with no cluster op
    impl::trivial_transform(transform, seq_len, K);
} else if (seq_len <= Small::kMax1PassLength) {
    if (cluster_rank != 0) return;   // 7 blocks exit with no cluster op
    Small::run(...);
    Small::transform(transform);
} else {
    /* large path -- uses cluster ops correctly */
}
```

On SM90 (Hopper) and on SM100 at TP=4/DP=4 this is tolerated. On SM100 at TP=8/DP=8 (where the fused 1-stage path is taken because `batch_size_per_rank=4 <= kNumClusters=15`), the cluster scheduler / PDL state machine trips and CUDA reports `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` at the next sync point — typically CUDA graph replay or a downstream `deep_gemm.fp8_gemm_nt` call, which makes the failure look like an unrelated GEMM/attention crash.

## Reproducer

- Hardware: 8× B300 SXM6 (single host, NVLink only — no IB)
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`
- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260517-229cadec`
- Server flags:
  ```
  --tp 8 --dp-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --moe-a2a-backend deepep \
  --max-running-requests 768 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \
  --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 --cuda-graph-max-bs 512 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --disable-flashinfer-autotune
  ```
- Env: `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=1` (the default since #25406), `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_FIX_MEGA_MOE_MEMORY=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_FIX_NEXTN_MEGA_MOE=1`, `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=4096`, `SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=0`, plus W4A4 (`SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_FP4_ACTS=1 SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_MXF4_KIND=1`)
- Workload: `random ISL=8192 OSL=1024 conc=32 num_prompts=320 warmup_requests=64`

Crash fires ~10 s into decode. With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` + `--disable-cuda-graph` the sync stack pinpoints the kernel:
```
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/indexer.py", line 429, in forward_c4_indexer
    topk_transform_512_v2(...)
File ".../sglang/jit_kernel/deepseek_v4.py", line 381, in topk_transform_512_v2
    module.topk_transform(...)
tvm.error.InternalError: Runtime check failed at
.../sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/deepseek_v4/topk_v2.cuh:473:
CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

## Why CI didn't catch it

`test/registered/dsv4/test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp4_megamoe_b200.py` (added in #25052) covers TP=4/DP=4 on B200 with DSv4-Flash. The TP=8/DP=8 + DSv4-Pro + B300 configuration is uncovered.

## Workaround

`export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=0` — falls back to the v1 kernel (`topk_transform_512`) at `indexer.py:438`. No measurable performance impact at conc=32 (within 0.5% in our measurements).

## Proposed fix

Restructure the SMALL and TRIVIAL branches so all 8 cluster blocks reach `cooperative_groups::this_cluster().sync()` before exit. PR: <PR_URL_PLACEHOLDER>.

The fix preserves the v2 fast path on all architectures. The added cluster barrier is a hardware-fast operation (tens of ns) and is essentially free — the 7 dummy ranks were already pinned to the cluster's SM allotment whether they early-returned or sat at the barrier (CUDA can't reclaim cluster SM slots block-by-block; the cluster releases only after all blocks exit).

Validated on the same reproducer: with `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=1` + the patch applied, the same conc=32 workload completes cleanly at 958.5 tok/s/gpu (vs 963.7 with the `TOPK_V2=0` workaround — well within run-to-run noise).

## Affected revisions

- Bug present since #23882 (DSv4 introduction, kernel was opt-in via `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=False`).
- Surfaces by default since #25406 (merged 2026-05-16) which flipped `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2` default from `False` to `True`.

source.title: [Bug]: Negative CUDA graph memory estimation (-35 GiB) with MTP speculative decoding leads to severe KV cache over-allocation and OOM
source.body:
### Your current environment

Bug Summary
When running Qwen3.6-35B with MTP speculative decoding (method: mtp) on a 128 GB Unified Memory system (NVIDIA GB10 Blackwell), vLLM incorrectly calculates the CUDA graph memory as a massive negative value (-35.69 GiB). This causes the memory profiler to artificially inflate the available KV cache pool. At a standard --gpu-memory-utilization of 0.8, this leads to an immediate OOM. Lowering the utilization to 0.55 acts as a workaround, but still allocates a suspicious 72 GiB KV cache.

Environment:

GPU: NVIDIA DGX Spark GB10 (128 GB Unified Memory)

CUDA Version: 13.2.0

vLLM Version: 0.22.1rc1.dev23+g6bdabbad5.d20260531

Model: RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 (KV-Cache dtype: fp8)

Command Line Arguments:

```
Bash
python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 \
  --max-model-len 131072 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.55 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'
```
Relevant Log Output:

```
Plaintext
(EngineCore pid=257) WARNING 06-06 16:17:06 [compilation.py:1407] CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE is not supported with spec-decode for attention backend FlashInferBackend... setting cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE
(EngineCore pid=257) INFO 06-06 16:17:06 [gpu_model_runner.py:6283] Profiling CUDA graph memory: PIECEWISE=51 (largest=512)
(EngineCore pid=257) INFO 06-06 16:17:13 [gpu_model_runner.py:6369] Estimated CUDA graph memory: -35.69 GiB total
(EngineCore pid=257) INFO 06-06 16:17:14 [gpu_worker.py:469] Available KV cache memory: 72.44 GiB
```
Expected Behavior:
The CUDA graph memory profiling should return a positive value, properly subtracting from the total available GPU memory instead of causing an underflow/negative estimation that inflates the KV cache block allocator.

Load a >30B parameter model using fp8 kv-cache.

Enable chunked prefill.

Observe the Estimated CUDA graph memory in the startup logs.

source.title: GSM8K accuracy regression: nightly (0.26.1rc1.dev77) drops ~5% vs latest (0.26.0) on GLM-5.2-FP8 P/D
source.body:
## Summary

GSM8K accuracy drops ~5 percentage points when moving from `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` (v0.26.0) to `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` on the same cluster, same config, same benchmark command.

## GSM8K Results

### Setup

- **Benchmark**: [GSM8K](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/gsm8k) (grade school math, 1319 test examples)
- **Evaluator**: `lm_eval` v0.4.x, `local-chat-completions` model type
- **Few-shot**: 5-shot (`fewshot_as_multiturn=True`, default for chat completions)
- **Thinking**: Disabled (`enable_thinking: false` via `chat_template_kwargs`)
- **Sampling**: Greedy (`temperature=0.0`, `do_sample=False`)
- **Stop tokens**: `['Question:', '</s>', '<|im_end|>']`
- **Tokenizer**: HuggingFace backend

### Raw results

**`vllm/vllm-openai:latest`** (v0.26.0, commit [`ffd46bfab`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ffd46bfab2128bb84146050e98b51a617c6575ab)):

```
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9447|±  |0.0063|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.9386|±  |0.0066|
```

Tested across concurrency 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384 — all consistently ~94.5%.

**`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`** (0.26.1rc1.dev77, commit [`6f91edf96`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/6f91edf96d3f3272945809c04702380053bff4de)):

```
|Tasks|Version|     Filter     |n-shot|  Metric   |   |Value |   |Stderr|
|-----|------:|----------------|-----:|-----------|---|-----:|---|-----:|
|gsm8k|      3|flexible-extract|     5|exact_match|↑  |0.8931|±  |0.0085|
|     |       |strict-match    |     5|exact_match|↑  |0.8855|±  |0.0088|
```

At 512 concurrency. 377 commits between the two versions.

### Regression summary

| Metric | latest (0.26.0) | nightly (0.26.1rc1.dev77) | Delta |
|--------|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| flexible-extract | 94.47% ± 0.63 | 89.31% ± 0.85 | **−5.16%** |
| strict-match | 93.86% ± 0.66 | 88.55% ± 0.88 | **−5.31%** |

### Null content warnings

The nightly run produced 3 instances of this warning (not seen on `latest`):

```
WARNING  [models.api_models:546] API returned null content. Content filled with
`LMEVAL_MODEL_NONE_ANSWER_PLACEHOLDER = `. Check reasoning_content field or generation limits.
```

These empty completions count as incorrect answers and partially contribute to the score drop.

### Benchmark command

```bash
lm_eval \
  --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args "model=zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8,base_url=http://localhost:8081/v1/chat/completions,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,num_concurrent=512,timeout=120" \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --apply_chat_template \
  --gen_kwargs '{"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}'
```

Accessed via `kubectl port-forward svc/llm-d-inference-gateway-istio 8081:80`.

## Hardware & Topology

- **GPU**: 8× NVIDIA H100 SXM per node
- **Prefill**: 1 replica × 4 nodes (32 GPUs total, expert-parallel across nodes)
- **Decode**: 1 replica × 4 nodes (32 GPUs total, expert-parallel across nodes)
- **Orchestration**: LeaderWorkerSet (LWS) on Kubernetes, P/D disaggregation with NixlConnector

## Prefill vllm serve command

```bash
vllm serve \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
  --port 8000 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --disable-access-log-for-endpoints=/health,/metrics \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --data-parallel-multi-port-external-lb \
  --data-parallel-supervisor-port=8208 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 32 \
  --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --data-parallel-address ${LWS_LEADER_ADDRESS} \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 5555 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
  --data-parallel-start-rank $START_RANK \
  --kv_transfer_config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector",
                          "kv_role":"kv_both",
                          "kv_load_failure_policy":"fail",
                          "kv_connector_extra_config":{
                              "connectors":[
                              {"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"},
                              {"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both",
                               "kv_connector_extra_config":{
                                 "spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec",
                                 "cpu_bytes_to_use":107374182400,
                                 "eviction_policy":"lru"
                            }}]
                            }}' \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput
```

### Prefill environment variables

```

ENABLE_KV_OFFLOADING=1
KV_OFFLOAD_CPU_BYTES=107374182400

## Decode vllm serve command

### Decode environment variables

### Decode sidecar (routing-proxy)

  --port=8000

  --enable-prefiller-sampling
```

## Notes

- The **only** change between the two runs was the image tag (`latest` → `nightly`). All YAMLs, env vars, hardware, namespace, and benchmark command were identical.
- `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1` was enabled — no NaN logit warnings appeared in either run, so this is not a NaN issue.
- Model: [zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8) — MoE with 256 experts, uses FlashMLA + DeepEP.

incidents.observed_failure: Inference does not crash or produce NaNs, but V dequantization and direct XQA output are severely wrong until only the V-scale layout is changed from swizzled to linear; the report describes silent model degradation.
incidents.baseline_or_control: K round trips at about 0.095 relative L2 while current V is about 0.762–0.788; linearizing V scales restores about 0.095. Direct XQA matches a deliberately wrong-scale reference at about 0.0021 and, after linearization, matches the correct reference at about 0.0021. Contiguous copies change output by exactly zero.
incidents.resolution: A rebuilt writer that uses linear V scales on SM120 is reported to restore V error to the K level and correct direct-XQA comparisons; the issue remains open and no merged upstream fix is supplied.
missing_information: upstream merge or release containing the correction
incidents.mechanism: reshape_and_cache_nvfp4_kernel unconditionally applies the SM100 trtllm-gen 4×4 swizzle to V block scales, while the SM120 FlashInfer XQA consumer reads V scales linearly and performs no de-swizzle; values are therefore read in the wrong order.

source.title: [Bug]: NVFP4 KV writes V block scales in the SM100 trtllm-gen swizzle unconditionally, silently corrupting the SM120 FlashInfer XQA route
source.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```
GPU:        NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (32,607 MiB), compute capability 12.0 (SM120)
Driver:     610.62, CUDA 13.0
Host:       Windows + WSL2
vLLM:       v0.25.1 (upstream commit 752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34)
FlashInfer: 0.6.15.post1
PyTorch:    2.11.0+cu130
Power cap:  575 W (default), persistence enabled
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`reshape_and_cache_nvfp4_kernel` writes **K** block scales linearly but writes **V** block scales in the 4×4 swizzle required by the SM100 `trtllm-gen` MHA kernel — **unconditionally, for every architecture**.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/csrc/libtorch_stable/nvfp4_kv_cache_kernels.cu#L155-L173

```cpp
      // Write block scale to scale cache.
      // K (kv==0): linear layout (no swizzle).
      // V (kv==1): swizzled layout for SM100 trtllm-gen MHA kernel.
      if (sf_out_ptr != nullptr) {
        int scale_idx = group_in_head;
        uint8_t* __restrict__ scale_dst;
        if (kv == 0) {
          ...
        } else {
          int swizzled_offset =
              swizzle_scale_offset(block_offset, scale_idx, scale_dim);
```

On SM120 the NVFP4 KV route (FA2 prefill + FlashInfer **XQA** decode, discussed in #49011) consumes K and V scale tensors through **ordinary NHD tensor strides**. The XQA wrapper takes `[pages, page_size, kv_heads, head_dim/16]` scale tensors and passes the real page/token/head strides straight through; the XQA CUDA code contains **no V-scale de-swizzle**. FlashInfer's own paged-NVFP4 quantizer documents its V-scale swizzle as being *for `trtllm-gen` MHA* — that layout is not the XQA layout.

So the SM120 route wires a **swizzled producer to a linear consumer**. Every tensor has the correct shape, dtype and alignment, no kernel errors, no NaNs — the values are simply read in the wrong order. The result is a silently degraded model rather than a crash.

This is separate from #43562 (trtllm-gen FP4 FMHA has no sm_120 build). It sits *below* the read-side view work in #49011 / #44851 — those fix which kernels get selected and how the views are bound; this is the layout the data was written in to begin with.

---

### Evidence

All probes are model-free: deterministic BF16 inputs written through the installed `reshape_and_cache_flash` binding, then independently unpacked and dequantized.

**1. Synthetic round trip.** Normal NVFP4 loss in this exercise is ≈0.095 relative L2 (what K shows). V is far outside that, and linearizing *only* the V scales restores it:

| KV heads / Q heads | K rel-L2 | V rel-L2 (current) | V rel-L2 (scales linearized) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 / 8 | 0.0952 | **0.7625** | 0.0953 |
| 2 / 16 | 0.0954 | **0.7615** | 0.0949 |
| 4 / 24 | 0.0948 | **0.7876** | 0.0957 |
| 8 / 48 | 0.0946 | **0.7649** | 0.0953 |

No NaN/Inf. Per-head matching selected the identity mapping in all cases; no head swap.

**2. Direct XQA.** Two pages, page size 16, non-trivial block table `[1, 0]`, sequence length 23 — so page metadata and indexing are exercised too:

| KV heads / Q heads | current vs correct ref | current vs *deliberately wrong-scale* ref | linear-V vs correct ref |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 / 8 | 0.8222 | **0.00211** | 0.00213 |
| 2 / 16 | 0.7861 | **0.00218** | 0.00219 |
| 4 / 24 | 0.7769 | **0.00216** | 0.00216 |
| 8 / 48 | 0.7453 | **0.00214** | 0.00212 |

XQA reproduces almost exactly a reference that *deliberately applies the current wrong V-scale order*. That isolates the failure to the layout contract, ahead of the XQA math kernel.

**3. Not a striding/contiguity artifact.** Copying the four split views into explicit contiguous buffers changed direct-XQA output by **exactly zero** for every head count. Changing only V scale values from swizzled to linear corrected it. Adding copies does not help.

**4. It is not two-KV-head specific.** Both 2 and 4 KV heads fail the same structural test and both recover when V scales are linear. A checkpoint that appeared healthy on this route was not evidence the layout was valid — it was less likely to expose the corruption on the prompts being run.

---

### Correction to an earlier characterization of mine

I want this on the record because I stated it publicly and it was wrong.

In my first write-up (comment on #49011, and a downstream discussion thread) I described the V write as **destructive** — "V stored only the first four source scales replicated across groups of four; twelve of sixteen values lost at write time." **That is incorrect.** It was an artifact of inspecting only token row 0.

The 4×4 transform is a **lossless bijection** jointly across token and scale-group coordinates — the other source scale groups are present, in destination token rows 1–3:

```
dest_token = (src_token // 4) * 4 + src_scale // (num_scales // 4)
dest_scale = (src_scale % (num_scales // 4)) * 4 + src_token % 4
```

Confirmation: the full 16-token × 16-scale plane contains all 15 representable distinct FP8 values from the structured probe (the nominal 13th and 14th both round to 2.25). Applying the joint inverse restores V stored-order relative L2 from **0.588793 → 0.026317**, *exactly* matching K.

The practical consequence is unchanged — SM120 reads V scales in the wrong order and the model degrades — but "information is destroyed at write time" and "information is permuted into a layout this consumer doesn't undo" are different bugs with different fixes, and only the second one is real. I'd rather correct it here than have a reviewer inherit the wrong mental model.

---

### Proposed fix

Keep the swizzle where its consumer needs it, and write linear V scales where the consumer reads linearly. Compile-time, no runtime cost, K unchanged:

```cpp
#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && \
    (__CUDA_ARCH__ == 1200 || __CUDA_ARCH__ == 1210)
        constexpr bool swizzle_v_scale = false;
#else
        constexpr bool swizzle_v_scale = true;
#endif
        if (kv == 0 || !swizzle_v_scale) {
          // linear
        } else {
          // existing TRT-LLM swizzle
        }
```

After rebuilding the corrected writer, stored V relative L2 is 0.026317 for both 2 and 4 KV heads — exactly matching K — and applying the *old* inverse transform now damages it to 0.592983, i.e. the layout really did flip. Integrated re-validation across KV heads 1/2/4/8:

| KV heads | K rel-L2 | patched V rel-L2 | XQA vs ref | strided vs contiguous |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.09517 | 0.09530 | 0.002135 | 0 |
| 2 | 0.09542 | 0.09493 | 0.002194 | 0 |
| 4 | 0.09478 | 0.09568 | 0.002159 | 0 |
| 8 | 0.09457 | 0.09533 | 0.002121 | 0 |

I'll follow up with a PR referencing this issue. It also tightens the kernel tests, which currently pass with a loose elementwise tolerance that this class of layout error slips straight through — they should assert the expected layout per capability and carry a relative-L2 regression guard.

### End-to-end effect

150-scenario agentic/quality benchmark suites on a Qwen3.6-derived 27B NVFP4 checkpoint over the SM120 NVFP4-KV route, thinking-on, two draws per arm.

The **matched** comparison — same night, same image, same 131,072 context / 8 GiB pinned KV / 6 sequences, changing only `--kv-cache-dtype`:

| KV dtype (post-fix writer) | draws | mean |
|---|---|--:|
| FP8 E4M3 (control) | 121, 122 | 121.5 / 150 |
| **NVFP4** | 121, 124 | **122.5 / 150** |

Post-fix, FP4 KV lands on top of its FP8 control rather than below it.

For context — and I'll flag the confound rather than hide it — the same checkpoint on the **pre-fix** writer scored a 116/150 mean (232/300 at `--repeat 2`). That run used a 262,144 context envelope rather than 131,072, so it is *not* a matched arm and I won't claim the delta as a clean measurement. What it does indicate is direction: pre-fix, this route sat below its own FP8 control and read as ordinary quantization cost.

The wider point for anyone triaging this: the defect was silently costing quality on a configuration that passed every smoke test, needle-in-a-haystack retrieval to 246K tokens, and 1h40m of continuous load without a single error. There is no failure signature to grep for.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I have made sure to search the existing issues and this is not a duplicate. This is distinct from #43562 (missing sm_120 trtllm-gen FMHA build) and sits below the read-side routing work in #49011 / #44851.

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

source.title: [Bug]: TP=2 spec-decode (qwen3_next_mtp / DFlash) on Qwen3.6 hybrid GDN crashes at gpu_model_runner.py:1927 num_accepted_tokens_event.synchronize() (cudaErrorIllegalAddress)
source.body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM: `0.19.2rc1.dev226+g53b9640fb` (built off PR #40898 head — DFlash + SWA support)
- GPU: 2× NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada Generation (sm_89, 48 GB each, no NVLink, P2P over PCIe)
- Driver: 580.126.09 / CUDA 13.0
- OS: Ubuntu, Linux 6.8.0-110-generic
- Python 3.12
- NCCL env: `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=0 NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1`

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Enabling speculative decoding (tested both `qwen3_next_mtp` and `DFlash` methods) on a hybrid-GDN Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model with **TP=2** causes a hard crash on the very first chat completion request. The error is `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`, with the stack landing at `self.num_accepted_tokens_event.synchronize()` in `gpu_model_runner.py:1927`. Both TP0 and TP1 workers raise the same error, and the NCCL ProcessGroup watchdog thread subsequently terminates with the same illegal address exception.

Note: GDN prefill backend was auto-selected as **Triton/FLA** (not FlashInfer) in this build at the time of the crash, so this appears distinct from the FlashInfer-GDN line of bugs in #37729 and #37035, despite affecting the same model family.

### Reproduction

Launch:

```bash
vllm serve QuantTrio/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-AWQ \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-model-len 65536 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --port 8080 \
  --served-model-name qwen3.6-uncensored \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --attention-backend flash_attn \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_next_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'
```

Also tested with `--speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash","num_speculative_tokens":15}'` — same crash at the same line.

Server starts cleanly (`Application startup complete`), but **any** chat completion request triggers the crash immediately.

### Stack trace

```
(Worker_TP1) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:962] WorkerProc hit an exception.
(Worker_TP1) ERROR   File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 3496, in synchronize_input_prep
(Worker_TP1) ERROR     yield
(Worker_TP1) ERROR   File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 3875, in execute_model
(Worker_TP1) ERROR     logits_indices, spec_decode_metadata = self._prepare_inputs(
(Worker_TP1) ERROR   File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 1927, in _prepare_inputs
(Worker_TP1) ERROR     self.num_accepted_tokens_event.synchronize()
(Worker_TP1) ERROR torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
  File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 3498, in synchronize_input_prep
    self.prepare_inputs_event.record()
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered

[rank0]:[E ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp:2119] [PG ID 2 PG GUID 3 Rank 0] Process group watchdog thread terminated with exception: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

### Test matrix

| spec method      | TP | num_spec_tokens | cudagraph_mode | GDN backend     | result          |
|------------------|----|-----------------|----------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| qwen3_next_mtp   | 2  | 1               | full           | triton (auto)   | CRASH           |
| qwen3_next_mtp   | 2  | 2               | full           | triton (auto)   | CRASH           |
| qwen3_next_mtp   | 2  | 2               | piecewise      | triton (auto)   | CRASH           |
| qwen3_next_mtp   | 2  | 2               | none (eager)   | triton (auto)   | CRASH           |
| dflash           | 2  | 15              | full           | triton (auto)   | CRASH (same line) |

Neither `cudagraph_mode`, `num_speculative_tokens`, nor the choice of spec method affects the crash.

### What I observed at TP=1 (NOT a confirmed workaround)

Under a different configuration — an NVFP4-quantized variant of the same model family, TP=1, qwen3_next_mtp with `num_speculative_tokens=2`, and explicit `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` — no crash occurred. However, too many variables changed simultaneously (TP, model, quantization, context length, gpu_memory_utilization) to call TP=1 a confirmed workaround.

Side note: in that TP=1 test, qwen3_next_mtp acceptance rate was 0% (2021 drafts, 0 accepted), but this appears to be a separate issue likely caused by the abliterated/distilled MTP head, and is unrelated to the crash discussed here.

### Related issues

- #37729 — V1 engine silent deadlock under concurrent load, root-caused to the FlashInfer GDN prefill kernel. Different surface from this bug (deadlock vs hard crash), and our crash occurred with Triton GDN, not FlashInfer GDN — but same model family.
- #37035 — `gdn_attn.py:237` OOB at `num_speculative_tokens>=5` (FlashInfer GDN kernel). Different crash location and different threshold for spec-tokens.
- #37750 — Closed PR that attempted to fix #37729 by adding a `device=` parameter to `torch.Event(...)` calls, including `num_accepted_tokens_event`. The fix turned out not to address the root cause and was not merged, but the same event object is the one crashing here.

### Hypothesis (unverified)

`num_accepted_tokens_event` requires cross-rank coordination at TP>1. The fact that this event is the crash point — and that #37750 specifically called out its `torch.Event(device=...)` initialization as suspect — suggests a multi-rank event lifetime or ordering bug in the spec-decode preparation path. A fruitful place to look might be how spec-decode metadata is broadcast across ranks via the multiproc executor before this first `synchronize()` call, and whether the event's device-side state can be invalidated between `record()` and `synchronize()` under TP>1.

### Workaround currently in production

Disabled `--speculative-config` entirely. Pure-decode runs cleanly at 174 tok/s short / 141 tok/s long on this hardware.

source.title: [Bug]: GLM-5.2-NVFP4 produces garbled/incorrect output and hits NotImplementedError in forward_mha on GB10 (SM121a) with FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120
source.body:
## Environment
- Hardware: 6× NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121a — compute_121a), switchless ring topology, dual-rail 200G RoCE (NCCL over RDMA, patched NCCL for topology-aware routing)
- vLLM: v0.26.0
- flashinfer-python / flashinfer-cubin: 0.6.14 / 0.6.14 (confirmed matched, installed via flashinfer.ai/whl since flashinfer-cubin==0.6.14 was not yet on PyPI at time of testing)
- Model: `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (resolved local checkpoint, 432.90 GiB total)
- Parallelism: Pipeline Parallel = 6 (one node per stage), Tensor Parallel = 1, native `mp` distributed executor (not Ray)
- Flags: `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --moe-backend marlin --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75`
- Attention backend selected automatically: `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` (only candidate listed — no fallback available)
- MoE backend forced to `marlin` (see rationale below)



### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Summary

After working around several unrelated infrastructure issues (documented
below for context, since they may affect others trying GLM-5.2 on GB10
clusters), the model **loads and serves successfully** (`Application
startup complete`), but:

1. **Generated output is garbled/nonsensical** on the very first request,
   even for a trivial prompt (`"Merhaba, kendini tanıtır mısın?"`).
2. **A later request crashes the engine** with `NotImplementedError` in
   `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py:1040` (`forward_mha`), apparently
   because a different request (longer prompt / different batch shape)
   takes a prefill code path that isn't implemented for this attention
   backend, whereas earlier requests silently used the `forward_mqa`
   (decode) path.

This appears consistent with the known, still-open issues:
- #49421 (GLM-5.2 NVFP4 support on SM120 — open)
- #49026 (flashinfer `sparse_mla_sm120` livelocks on GB10, adding
  `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` as fallback — open)
- #46726 (sparse-MLA indexer error with GLM-5.2 NVFP4 on SM120 — open)
- #48054 (DeepSeek-V4 sparse-SWA decode passes flashinfer 0.6.14-only
  kwargs while pin is 0.6.13 — open; we hit and resolved the version
  mismatch symptom described here by installing matched 0.6.14/0.6.14
  from flashinfer.ai/whl, but this did **not** fix the garbled output)

We're filing this because our repro is on a 6-node **PP=6** RDMA setup
(rather than the single/multi-GPU SM120 workstation setups in the issues
above), and confirms the garbled-output symptom persists **even with
fully matched flashinfer-python/flashinfer-cubin versions**, which may
help narrow down whether the root cause is in the `sparse_mla_sm120`
kernel itself (as #49026 suggests) rather than a version-mismatch
artifact.

## Reproduction

```bash
# All 6 nodes: flashinfer-python==0.6.14, flashinfer-cubin==0.6.14 (matched)
vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 6 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --nnodes 6 --node-rank <N> \
  --master-addr <addr> --master-port 29501 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --moe-backend marlin \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 \
  --trust-remote-code
```

First request:
```bash
curl http://localhost:7001/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "GLM", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Merhaba, kendini tanıtır mısın?"}], "max_tokens": 100}'
```

Output (garbled, `finish_reason: length`):
```
"...,Y27 <ahan yaar ya fab25) zhouff232 DK58 ... Yokluz, ben50 a önemli
işçilik effectink7 ... da çokonaisu kelumeliyediğ gibi gibi uzunluk d
dahaveya ... fundasyon veya .. kansilityeri için oluşmuaz1ır Kamını..27
bk ..."
```

A subsequent request (different prompt/length) crashes the engine:
```
File "vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/mla_attention.py", line 785, in forward_impl
    self.impl.forward_mha(
File "vllm/v1/attention/backend.py", line 1040, in forward_mha
    raise NotImplementedError
NotImplementedError
```
followed by `EngineDeadError` and full server shutdown.

## Notes on ruling out other causes

- **KV cache memory sizing**: initially hit `ValueError: No available
  memory for the cache blocks` at `--gpu-memory-utilization=0.6`;
  resolved by raising to `0.75` (`Available KV cache memory: 21.18 GiB`).
  Not related to the garbled output.
- **MoE JIT compile storm**: the default `auto` MoE backend selects
  `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS`, which JIT-compiles CUTLASS grouped-GEMM kernels
  for the GB10-specific `compute_121a` arch (no precompiled cubin ships
  for this variant) — with 6 nodes compiling simultaneously, host RAM is
  exhausted and all nodes become unresponsive (not even ping). Forcing
  `--moe-backend marlin` avoids this entirely. Unrelated to the garbled
  decode output (MLA attention backend, not MoE).
- **flashinfer-python/flashinfer-cubin version mismatch**: initially hit
  `RuntimeError: flashinfer-cubin version (0.6.13) does not match
  flashinfer version (0.6.14)`. We resolved this properly (not via
  `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK`) by installing matched 0.6.14/0.6.14
  from `https://flashinfer.ai/whl` (not yet on PyPI at time of testing).
  **The garbled output persisted identically** after this fix, suggesting
  the root cause is not the version mismatch itself.
- **Swap/host-memory thrashing**: separately, we found that leaving swap
  enabled on these nodes causes CUDA/NCCL timing-sensitive steps to stall
  under memory pressure, manifesting as full node hangs (not even SSH/ping
  responsive) rather than clean errors. `swapoff -a` on all nodes converts
  hangs into clean, diagnosable errors — this is what allowed us to reach
  the actual `NotImplementedError` traceback above instead of a hang.

## Question for maintainers

Given #49026 proposes adding `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` (Triton) as a fallback
specifically because `sparse_mla_sm120` livelocks on GB10 — is it
possible the "livelock" also manifests as silent numerical corruption
(rather than an outright hang) in some code paths, which would explain
our garbled-but-completing output? Is there a way to force the
`FLASHMLA_SPARSE`/Triton path today (pre-merge) via an env var or CLI
flag, to test whether it resolves both the garbled output and the
`forward_mha` `NotImplementedError` on our setup?

Happy to test any patches/flags on our 6-node GB10 ring if useful for
validating a fix.

source.body:
### Your current environment

 **Model**: `DeepSeek v4 flash
- CUDA version: 13.0
- GPU model: H100*8
- OS: `Ubuntu 20.04 LTS`
- Container runtime: Docker  deepseekv4 cu130

### 🐛 Describe the bug

## vLLM fails to run DeepSeek-V4 with CUDA launch failure

When trying to serve **DeepSeek-V4** using vLLM, the worker process crashes immediately with a `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` error. The stack trace points to `synchronize_input_prep` in `gpu_model_runner.py`, and the process hangs before any requests are processed.

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1.  Run the following vLLM command to serve DeepSeek-V4:
    ```bash
    docker run --runtime=nvidia --gpus all \
    --name deepseek-v4 \
    -v /mnt/data/modelscope/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash:/model \
    --env CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
    --env VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 \
    -p 8025:8000 \
    --ipc=host \
    --shm-size=32g \
    vllm/vllm-openai:deepseekv4-cu130 \
    --model /model \
    --served-model-name deepseek-v4 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
    --max-num-seqs 8 \
    --max-model-len auto \
    --block-size 256 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --enable-chunked-prefill \
    --enable-expert-parallel \
    --enable-prefix-caching \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager
    ```
2.  The server starts but immediately throws the following error and hangs:
    ```
    File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 3492, in synchronize_input_prep
        self.prepare_inputs_event.synchronize()
    torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: unspecified launch failure
    Search for 'cudaErrorLaunchFailure' in https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html for more information.
    CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
    For debugging consider passing CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
    Compile with `TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA` to enable device-side assertions.

    prompt throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Avg generation throughput: 0.0 tokens/s, Running: 2 reqs, Waiting: 0 reqs, GPU KV cache usage: 1.8%, Prefix cach...
    broadcast block found in 60 seconds. This typically happens when some processes are hanging or doing some time-consuming work
    ``
### Additional context
- The error occurs even with minimal inference requests; GPU utilization and memory usage are low at the time of the crash.
- I have tried setting `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` and `TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA`, but the issue persists.
