source.title: [Bug]: PCP (#46570) broken for non-compress models (GLM-5.2, compress_ratio=1) — multiple crash paths
source.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text - vLLM version: `v0.23.1rc1.dev1327+gf25953cc5` (Jul 21 nightly, includes merged #46570) - Model: `GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (256 routed experts, hidden=6144, kv_lora_rank=512, `compress_ratio=1`) - Hardware: 8×H200 (141GB), `kv-cache-dtype: fp8_ds_mla`, `attention-backend: FLASHMLA_SPARSE` - Config: `TP=4, PCP=2, DCP=2, EP=8, MTP-5` - Speculative: `method=mtp, num_speculative_tokens=5` ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug PCP (#46570) does not work with GLM-5.2-NVFP4 (`compress_ratio=1` path). Multiple asserts/crashes occur when running `TP=4, PCP=2, DCP=2` on 8×H200. All paths were tested on nightly `v0.23.1rc1.dev1327+gf25953cc5` (post-merge #46570). ## Bug 1: Cudagraph warmup crashes with `assert 0 <= num_decode_tokens <= local_num_tokens` **Severity**: blocks startup without `--enforce-eager` **File**: `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/pcp.py:19` **Context**: `_gather_prefill_cache_inputs()` called during `_dummy_run()` → `_warmup_and_capture()` ``` sparse_attn_indexer.py:388 → maybe_gather_indexer_k() → pcp.py:19 assert fails ``` **Root cause**: During cudagraph warmup, `_dummy_run()` creates a dummy `InputBatch` via `InputBatch.make_dummy()` without PCP partitioning. The `attn_metadata_narrowed.num_decode_tokens` is the global decode token count, but `k` is truncated to PCP-local size. The value comparison fails. **Workaround**: `--enforce-eager` ## Bug 2: `sparse_attn_indexer.py` incorrectly divides `num_tokens` by `pcp_world_size` when `compress_ratio=1` **Severity**: blocks all inference with PCP (eager or cudagraph) **File**: `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py:380-384` ```python num_tokens = slot_mapping.shape[0] if use_pcp: num_tokens //= get_pcp_group().world_size # ← Wrong when compress_ratio=1 if k is not None: k = k[:num_tokens] ``` **Root cause**: When `compress_ratio == 1`, `slot_mapping` is **not** all-gathered across PCP — it stays local (`size = local_num_tokens`). But the division by `pcp_world_size` assumes the slot_mapping was gathered (as done for `compress_ratio > 1` in `indexer.py:843-846`). This truncates `k` to `local_num_tokens / pcp_world_size`, making it too small. The fix should conditionally divide only when the slot_mapping was actually gathered, e.g.: ```python if use_pcp and k is not None and slot_mapping.shape[0] > k.shape[0]: num_tokens //= get_pcp_group().world_size ``` ## Bug 3: `split_decodes_and_prefills()` asserts `is_prefilling is not None` in MTP drafter path **Severity**: blocks all inference with MTP + PCP (first non-startup forward) **File**: `vllm/v1/attention/backends/utils.py:624` ``` llm_base_proposer.py:999 build_per_group_and_layer_attn_metadata → indexer.py build_for_drafting() → build() → split_decodes_and_prefills(treat_short_extends_as_decodes=False) → assert common_attn_metadata.is_prefilling is not None ``` **Root cause**: PCP mode sets `treat_short_extends_as_decodes=False` which requires `is_prefilling` to be present in `CommonAttentionMetadata`. However, the MTP drafter's metadata builder path (`build_for_drafting()` → `build(fast_build=True)`) does not set `is_prefilling` — it's only set by `DefaultModelState.prepare_inputs()` during the main model forward. **Fix**: Gracefully handle `None`: ```python if not treat_short_extends_as_decodes: if common_attn_metadata.is_prefilling is not None: is_prefill |= common_attn_metadata.is_prefilling ``` ## Bug 4: `_gather_prefill_cache_inputs()` assumes slot_mapping is all-gathered **Severity**: blocks actual inference (after fixing Bug 2 & 3) **File**: `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/pcp.py:30,38` ```python gathered_slot_mapping = slot_mapping[: pcp_size * local_num_tokens] # line 30 ... rank_slot_mappings = gathered_slot_mapping.view(pcp_size, local_num_tokens) # line 38 ``` **Root cause**: This function assumes the caller already all-gathered the slot_mapping across PCP (`size = pcp_size * local_num_tokens`). For `compress_ratio > 1`, the indexer does this gathering. For `compress_ratio == 1` (GLM-5.2), it doesn't. When the function all-gathers the local slot_mapping internally, the sizes don't match — because in the MLA KV cache path (`maybe_gather_mla_latent_cache_inputs`), `slot_mapping.shape[0]` (e.g., 20) is **not equal** to `local_num_tokens` (e.g., 24). The indexer KV write path's slot mapping may exclude some tokens (e.g., indexer-only tokens with no MLA cache write), creating a size mismatch that `all_gather` cannot compensate for. ## Bug 5 (cascading from Bug 4): MLA KV cache update path slot_mapping size mismatch **Severity**: blocks MLA attention after fixing Bugs 1-4 **File**: `vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/pcp.py:41` ``` RuntimeError: shape '[2, 24]' is invalid for input of size 40 ``` **Root cause**: `maybe_gather_mla_latent_cache_inputs` calls `_gather_prefill_cache_inputs` with `slot_mapping` from `FlashMLASparseMetadata`. The `slot_mapping` for MLA KV writes has `size ≠ local_num_tokens`, unlike the indexer path where they match. When PCP all-gathers this mismatched-size tensor, the result doesn't align with `pcp_size * local_num_tokens` needed for the `view` call. ## Root cause summary PCP (#46570) was designed and tested exclusively with models using `compress_ratio > 1` (DeepSeek V4 variants). The compressed path includes slot_mapping all-gather logic at the metadata builder level (`indexer.py`), which the non-compressed path (`compress_ratio = 1`, used by GLM-5.2) lacks. Several downstream consumers (`sparse_attn_indexer.py`, `pcp.py`, `utils.py`) implicitly depend on this gathering having been done. ## Desired behavior PCP should work for all MLA models, regardless of `compress_ratio`, without requiring `--enforce-eager`. The slot_mapping all-gather should happen in the metadata builder for both paths, and all downstream code should handle the gathered/local distinction correctly. ## Reproduction ```bash # Start server vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \ --decode-context-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla \ --max-model-len 1048576 \ --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 5}' \ --enforce-eager \ --trust-remote-code # Send any request → crash at Bug 2 ``` ## Related - PR #46570: [Core] Add MRV2 virtual-batch PCP for MLA - All benchmarks in #46570 used `--enforce-eager` and did not test `compress_ratio=1` models CC: @LucasWilkinson @MatthewBonanni ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

source.title: [Bug]: Eagle 2/3 acceptance length regression over time
source.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
See below
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

# Problem

Speculative decoding acceptance length (AL) smoothly and monotonically regresses over time when serving models with Eagle/Eagle3 draft models in vLLM 0.17.1. AL never recovers — only a full service restart resets it to the initial high value. The degradation correlates with traffic volume per prompt type — only high-volume prompt types are affected.

# Setup

* vLLM 0.17.1, v1 engine, async scheduling enabled
* 4x H200 GPUs (564GB total), gpu_memory_utilization=0.9 (all models executed with TP=4)
* Model ~250GB, leaving ~257GB for KV cache (~5M tokens capacity, ~312K blocks at block_size=16)
* KV cache dtype: GPT OSS 120B - BF16 (auto), ~50KB per token, other models uses FP8
* Block size: 16
* Prefix caching enabled
* Traffic: ~10-20 RPS
* ~60 different prompt types, average ~30K tokens each
* Per type: ~27K tokens cacheable (unique to that type), ~3K tokens unique per request
* First 4K tokens shared across all types, remaining 23K unique per type
* Traffic distribution: 5 types occupy ~50% of traffic, other 55 types share the rest
* Average OSL: 40 tokens

# Observations

1. Model A (BF16 weights and KV, Eagle2, 4 draft tokens, batch_size=2): AL starts at ~3.07, smoothly regresses to ~2.8 over hours. Only 2-3 highest-volume types affected.
2. Model A (BF16 weights and KV, Eagle3, 4 draft tokens, batch_size=2): AL starts at ~3.07, smoothly regresses to ~2.8 over hours. Only 2-3 highest-volume types affected.
3. Model B (FP8 weights&activation&KV cache, Eagle3, 5 draft tokens, batch_size=4): AL starts at ~4.5, smoothly regresses to ~2.8. All high-volume types affected, low-volume types unimpacted.
4. Model B (FP8 weights&activation&KV cache, Eagle3, 5 draft tokens, batch_size=2): AL starts at ~4.2, regresses to ~3.8. Reducing speculation length to lower values does NOT change the regression behavior.
5. Model C (FP8 weights&activation&KV cache, Eagle3, 5 draft tokens, batch_size=2) with vLLM: AL starts at ~3.9, regresses to ~3.5 vs with TRT-LLM: AL is stable and does not regress.
6. Restart resets AL immediately to the initial high value, regardless of current traffic level.
7. TRT-LLM: slight AL regression at peak traffic but recovers during low traffic. vLLM only regresses, never recovers.
8. Both Eagle2 and Eagle3 shows regression of AL over time.
9. TTFT and prefix cache hit rate appear stable.
10. Running Model B with newer vLLM version 0.19.1 does not fix the problem, regression is still observed.


# Relevant GitHub Issues/PRs

* Issue #14649: "EAGLE / MTP Doesn't Overwrite Approximated Hidden States / KV Cache" — describes the fundamental problem. Unfixed in v0, but v1's first pass mechanism largely addresses it (small residual gap).
* PR #14990: "Enhance EAGLE Architecture with Proper RMS Norms" — merged Mar 2025, adds proper norm handling to Eagle model.
* PR #16370: "[V1][Spec Decode] KV cache slots for eagle heads" — merged, shows v1 gap is small in offline benchmarks (2.43 vs 2.48 for 5 spec tokens on Llama 3.1 8B).
* PR #14464: "EAGLE output norm bug" — merged, fixes return x + residual, None vs return x, residual in Eagle model.
* PR #29845: "Simplified alternative padded-speculation acceptance rate fix" — merged, adds num_rejected_tokens_gpu adjustment to seq_lens before sequential drafting loop.

# Experiments we are running now (will be updated with new observations)
- Disabling prefix caching
- Disabling async scheduling
- Run with batch size=1

source.title: [Bug]: MiniMax M3 Triton path misinterprets token-major top-k buffer
source.body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM: v0.25.1 and current `main`
- Model: MiniMax-M3-MXFP8
- Hardware: 8x NVIDIA A100 (SM80)
- Tensor parallel size: 8

### Model Input Dumps

No model input dump is required to reproduce the layout mismatch. It occurs when the MiniMax M3 Triton indexer receives the model's persistent top-k output buffer.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The NVIDIA MiniMax M3 model allocates `topk_indices_buffer` in token-major `[T, H, K]` layout for the MSA path. The common Triton indexer and sparse-attention paths still slice that buffer as if it were head-major `[H, T, K]`.

During inference this reaches `minimax_m3_index_topk` / `_topk_index_kernel` with incorrect shape and strides and eventually fails with:

```text
RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

The failure occurs in the call chain:

```text
minimax_m3/nvidia/model.py
  -> common/indexer.py
  -> common/ops/index_topk.py
  -> _topk_index_kernel
```

The proposed fix keeps one token-major persistent layout across NVIDIA and AMD and passes transposed head-major views at the Triton write/read boundaries. No Triton kernel algorithm is changed.

A100 validation after applying the fix:

- Model initializes successfully.
- 100/100 long-context benchmark requests complete successfully.
- LMCache registers all 117 MiniMax M3 KV tensors and inference remains stable.

The A100 Triton path has been tested. SM100 MSA and ROCm require CI or maintainer hardware validation.

incidents.optimization: FP8
incidents.runtime_hardware: vLLM v0.17.1; four-rank NCCL execution is shown in the log
incidents.complaint_or_finding: Inference with the FP8 Qwen3.5 model terminated after an asynchronous CUDA illegal-memory-access error.
incidents.observed_failure: After a chat-completions request returned HTTP 200, WorkerAsyncOutputCopy failed while synchronizing async_copy_ready_event; the NCCL watchdog then terminated with the same CUDA illegal-memory-access error and the model stopped.
incidents.resolution: The issue was closed as not planned; no source-supplied fix or mitigation is present.
missing_information: whether the failure reproduces without speculative decoding
incidents.discriminating_test: Repeat the same request with the FP8 checkpoint in another runtime and with a non-FP8 checkpoint under the same vLLM launch configuration; this separates representation damage from runtime or launch corruption.

incidents.optimization: FP8; FP4; FP8 weight-only quantization; Marlin; CUTLASS MoE
incidents.runtime_hardware: Cross-platform discussion covering CUDA, ROCm, XPU, CPU/TPU, and OOT devices; examples include gfx90a, gfx942, gfx950, B200/B300, RTX PRO 6000, and RTX 5090
incidents.complaint_or_finding: The RFC reports that CUDA-style numeric device-capability checks cannot reliably represent cross-platform FP8/FP4 and weight-only-quantization support.
incidents.observed_failure: According to the proposal, XPU capability checks return None and make feature gates false; ROCm architectures are artificially mapped to CUDA-like numbers with different low-bit semantics; and NVIDIA devices can share or split capability numbers despite different FP8/FP4 support, causing gates to miss supported devices or admit unsupported ones.
incidents.baseline_or_control: The source explicitly contrasts CUDA (9,0), where Hopper has FP8 and TMA, with ROCm-mapped (9,0), where gfx90a lacks FP8; it also contrasts RTX PRO 6000 and RTX 5090, both reported as (12,0) but described as having different FP8/FP4 support.
incidents.resolution: The source proposes replacing numeric comparisons with explicit feature queries, while retaining platform-specific kernel dispatch where appropriate; no implemented resolution is supplied.
missing_information: runtime reproductions of the claimed gate failures
incidents.mechanism: The proposal attributes the failures to using CUDA SM-style numeric capability values as proxies for actual low-bit hardware features across platforms and SKU tiers.
incidents.discriminating_test: On the same device and low-bit weights, bypass only the numeric capability gate and directly probe or run the relevant FP8/FP4 kernel; success after bypass identifies gate/config handling rather than damaged weights.

source.title: [RFC]: Unified Device Capability Abstraction for Cross-Platform Feature Detection
source.body:
### Motivation.

This is an AI-generated proposal, there may be some error. appreciate if you can point out. 

## 1. Problem Summary

As raised by @tjtanaa in [#39158](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39158), the current `has_device_capability(int)` / `is_device_capability_family(int)` API is **fundamentally CUDA-centric** and does **not** translate correctly to ROCm or XPU.

### 1.1 Problem A: `device_capability` is inherently a CUDA concept

`torch.cuda.get_device_capability()` returns `(major, minor)` tied to NVIDIA's SM (Streaming Multiprocessor) versioning. **ROCm and XPU have completely different hardware models** — any mapping to CUDA-style numbers is artificial and lossy:

| Platform | Capability Model | How it works |
|----------|-----------------|--------------|
| **CUDA** | SM version `(major, minor)` e.g. `(8,9)`, `(9,0)`, `(10,0)` | Native `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()` |
| **ROCm** | GCN arch string (e.g. `gfx942`) → **artificially mapped** to `(major, minor)` | Semantic mismatch: `gfx90a` maps to `(9,0)` but has NO FP8, while CUDA's `(9,0)` = Hopper = has FP8 |
| **XPU** | No capability model → always returns `None` → all checks = `False` | All feature gates broken |
| **CPU/TPU** | No capability model → returns `None` | N/A |
| **OOT** | No capability model → returns `None` | N/A |

### 1.2 Problem B: Same CUDA generation, different capability numbers across SKU tiers

Even within NVIDIA's own ecosystem, **the same architecture generation has different compute capability numbers** depending on the product tier (server / workstation / client):

| Platform | Device | Compute Capability | Data Types Supported |
|----------|--------|-------------------|---------------------|
| **Server** | B200 / B300 | `(10, 0)` / `(10, 3)` | bf16 / fp8 / fp4 |
| **Workstation** | RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell | `(12, 0)` | bf16 / fp8 / fp4 |
| **Client** | RTX 5090 | `(12, 0)` | bf16 only |

This is particularly problematic because:

1. **Same generation, different numbers**: B200 (`10,0`) and RTX PRO 6000 (`12,0`) are both Blackwell, both support FP8/FP4, but have completely different capability numbers. Code using `is_device_capability_family(100)` to gate Blackwell features will **miss** RTX PRO 6000.

2. **Same number, different features**: RTX PRO 6000 and RTX 5090 both report `(12,0)`, but RTX PRO supports FP8/FP4 while consumer RTX 5090 does **not**. Code using `has_device_capability(120)` to gate FP8 would be **wrong** on RTX 5090.

3. **Maintenance burden**: Every new GPU SKU tier requires auditing all numeric capability checks. The current codebase already handles `is_device_capability_family(100)` and `is_device_capability_family(120)` separately (e.g., in `cutlass_moe.py`), and this will only get worse.

### 1.3 Problem C: Cross-platform semantic mismatch

The same numeric value means **completely different things** on different platforms:

| Capability Value | CUDA Meaning | ROCm Meaning |
|-----------------|--------------|--------------|
| `(9, 0)` | Hopper (H100/H200) — FP8 ✅, TMA ✅ | MI200 (gfx90a) — FP8 ❌, BF16 only |
| `(9, 4)` | N/A | MI300 (gfx942) — FP8 ✅ (FNUZ) |
| `(9, 5)` | N/A | MI355 (gfx950) — FP8 ✅, FP4 ✅ |
| `(12, 0)` | Blackwell consumer (RTX 5090) — BF16 only | RDNA4 (gfx1201) — BF16 only |

### 1.4 Scope observation: where capability checks are used

Most usage of `has_device_capability` / `get_device_capability` falls into:

| Location | Usage Pattern | Notes |
|----------|--------------|-------|
| **tests/** and **benchmarks/** | Test skip / gating | ~60% of call sites. vLLM CI always uses NVIDIA server GPUs, so numeric checks "happen to work" but are not correct for community contributors on consumer/workstation GPUs |
| **Kernel selection code** (`model_executor/layers/`) | Dispatch to optimal kernel implementation | ~30%. Inherently platform-specific (CUTLASS, Marlin, etc.) |
| **Config / runtime** (`vllm/config/`, `vllm/v1/`) | Feature availability checks | ~10%. Should be cross-platform |

This distribution suggests the migration can be prioritized: **fix tests/config first** (highest cross-platform impact), then gradually migrate kernel dispatch code.

---

## 2. Analysis of Current Codebase

### 2.1 How capability is actually used (282 call sites)

Analyzing all `has_device_capability` / `is_device_capability*` call sites across the codebase, they fall into **three distinct categories**:

#### Category A: Testing for a *hardware feature* (~60%)

```python
# "Does this device support FP8?"
current_platform.has_device_capability(89)   # Actually means: supports_fp8()

# "Does this device support BF16?"
current_platform.has_device_capability(80)   # Actually means: supports_bf16()

# "Does this device support TMA / warp-group MMA?" 
current_platform.has_device_capability(90)   # Actually means: supports_hopper_features()

# "Does this device support Blackwell features (FP4, TMA v2)?"
current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)  # Actually means: supports_blackwell_features()
```

These should be **feature queries**, not numeric comparisons.

#### Category B: Selecting a *kernel implementation* (~30%)

```python
# "Use CUTLASS 3.x path for SM90+"
if current_platform.has_device_capability(90): use_cutlass3()

# "Use Blackwell-specific GEMM kernel"
if current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100): use_blackwell_gemm()

# "Use CUTLASS MoE for Blackwell server OR workstation"
if p.is_device_capability_family(100) or p.is_device_capability_family(120): ...
```

These are CUDA-kernel-specific dispatch decisions. They are inherently platform-specific and **do not need** cross-platform abstraction — they are always guarded behind `is_cuda()` check already. However, even here the Blackwell SKU split causes issues (see Section 1.2).

#### Category C: FP8 weight-only quantization fallback (~10%)

```python
# fbgemm_fp8.py — Marlin WOQ fallback for non-FP8 hardware
self.use_marlin = not current_platform.has_device_capability(89)

# marlin.py — FP8 Marlin works on SM ≥ 7.5 (Turing+)
def is_fp8_marlin_supported():
    return current_platform.has_device_capability(75)
```

This pattern reveals that **FP8 "support" is not binary** — there are two distinct levels:
- **Native FP8 compute**: Hardware tensor cores that natively compute in FP8 (SM ≥ 89 on CUDA, gfx942/gfx950 on ROCm)
- **FP8 weight-only quantization (WOQ)**: Kernels like Marlin that can load FP8-quantized weights and dequantize them to FP16/BF16 for compute (works on SM ≥ 75 on CUDA, i.e., Turing+)

The current `supports_fp8()` doesn't distinguish between these, which leads to suboptimal decisions. For example, `FBGEMMFp8Config` uses `has_device_capability(89)` to decide whether to use native FP8 compute vs Marlin fallback, but this is incorrect on RTX 5090 (`(12,0)`) which has `has_device_capability(89)` = True but may not actually have native FP8 tensor cores for all operations.

### 2.2 Existing feature-level APIs (the right pattern)

The codebase already has the correct abstraction for some features:

```python
# vllm/platforms/interface.py — base class
Platform.supports_fp8()    → bool   # ✅ Cross-platform
Platform.supports_mx()     → bool   # ✅ Cross-platform
Platform.support_deep_gemm() → bool # ✅ Cross-platform
Platform.fp8_dtype()       → dtype  # ✅ Cross-platform
Platform.is_fp8_fnuz()     → bool   # ✅ Cross-platform
```

Each platform overrides these with the correct implementation:
- **CUDA**: `supports_fp8() → has_device_capability(89)`
- **ROCm**: `supports_fp8() → "gfx94" in arch or "gfx95" in arch or "gfx12" in arch`
- **XPU**: inherits `False` (or could override when XPU gains FP8)

**This is the pattern that should be expanded** — but with finer granularity (see Section 3).

### 2.3 Missing feature-level APIs

| Feature | How it's checked today | Missing `Platform` method |
|---------|----------------------|--------------------------|
| BF16 support | `has_device_capability(80)` (CUDA-only) | `supports_bf16()` |
| FP8 native compute vs WOQ | Implicit: `has_device_capability(89)` vs `has_device_capability(75)` | `supports_fp8_native()` / `supports_fp8_woq()` |
| FP4 / NVFP4 | C++ `cutlass_scaled_mm_supports_fp4()` (CUDA-only) | `supports_fp4()` |
| Hopper features (TMA, wgmma) | `has_device_capability(90)` | `supports_tma()` or architecture family check |
| Blackwell features | `is_device_capability_family(100)` — misses SM 12.0 workstation | `supports_blackwell_features()` |
| Flash attention FP8 | `has_device_capability(89)` | Covered by `supports_fp8_native()` |
| CUTLASS GEMM dispatch | `has_device_capability(75/80/89/90/100)` | Platform-specific, keep as-is |

---



### Proposed Change.

## 3. Proposal: Two-Layer Capability Model

### Layer 1: Feature-Based Queries (Cross-Platform) — **PRIMARY**

Expand the existing `Platform` base class with **semantic feature queries** that each platform implements correctly:

```python
# vllm/platforms/interface.py

class Platform:
    # === Existing (keep) ===
    def supports_fp8(cls) -> bool: ...      # keep for backward compat, alias to supports_fp8_native()
    def supports_mx(cls) -> bool: ...
    def support_deep_gemm(cls) -> bool: ...
    
    # === New feature queries ===
    
    @classmethod
    def supports_bf16(cls) -> bool:
        """Returns whether the current platform supports BF16 compute."""
        return False
    
    @classmethod
    def supports_fp8_native(cls) -> bool:
        """Returns whether the current platform has native FP8 tensor core compute.
        
        This means the hardware can natively perform matrix multiplication in FP8
        (e.g., NVIDIA SM ≥ 89 Ada/Hopper/Blackwell server, AMD gfx942/gfx950).
        Used for: native FP8 GEMM, FP8 KV cache, FP8 attention.
        """
        return False

    @classmethod
    def supports_fp8_woq(cls) -> bool:
        """Returns whether the platform supports FP8 weight-only quantization.
        
        This means kernels like Marlin can load FP8-quantized weights and 
        dequantize them to FP16/BF16 for compute. Works on significantly older
        hardware than native FP8 (e.g., NVIDIA SM ≥ 75 Turing+).
        Used for: Marlin FP8, fbgemm FP8 fallback path.
        """
        return False

    @classmethod
    def supports_fp4(cls) -> bool:
        """Returns whether the current platform supports FP4 quantization 
        (native compute or equivalent)."""
        return False

    @classmethod
    def supports_tma(cls) -> bool:
        """Returns whether the current platform supports 
        Tensor Memory Accelerator (or equivalent async copy engine)."""
        return False

    @classmethod
    def supports_fp8_kv_cache(cls) -> bool:
        """Returns whether the current platform supports FP8 KV cache."""
        return cls.supports_fp8_native()

    @classmethod
    def get_architecture_family(cls) -> str:
        """Returns human-readable architecture family name.
        
        Examples: 'hopper', 'blackwell', 'blackwell_consumer','cdna3', 
                  'rdna4', 'ponte_vecchio', 'unknown'
        """
        return "unknown"
```

### Why split FP8 into native vs WOQ?

The current `supports_fp8()` is ambiguous. In the codebase today:

```python
# fbgemm_fp8.py — decides whether to use native FP8 or Marlin fallback
self.use_marlin = not current_platform.has_device_capability(89)

# marlin_utils_fp8.py — Marlin FP8 works on much older hardware
def is_fp8_marlin_supported():
    return current_platform.has_device_capability(75)  # Turing+!
```

With the split:

```python
# fbgemm_fp8.py — clear intent
self.use_marlin = not current_platform.supports_fp8_native()

# marlin_utils_fp8.py — explicit WOQ check
def is_fp8_marlin_supported():
    return current_platform.supports_fp8_woq()
```

This distinction matters for:
- **Testing**: A test for native FP8 GEMM should use `@requires_feature("fp8_native")`, while a test for Marlin FP8 WOQ should use `@requires_feature("fp8_woq")`
- **Consumer GPUs**: RTX 5090 (`SM 12.0`) may support FP8 WOQ via Marlin but not native FP8 tensor core compute
- **ROCm**: MI200 (gfx90a) has no FP8 at all, MI300 (gfx942) has native FP8-FNUZ, different Marlin support

### Layer 2: Numeric Capability (Platform-Specific) — **KEEP BUT DEPRECATE for cross-platform use**

Keep `has_device_capability()` / `is_device_capability()` / `is_device_capability_family()` **as-is** for platform-specific kernel dispatch, but:

1. **Document** that these are CUDA/ROCm-specific and must always be guarded by `is_cuda()` / `is_rocm()`.
2. **Deprecation warning** in tests when used without platform guard (enforce via lint rule).
3. XPU/CPU/TPU continue to return `None` / `False` — this is correct behavior.
4. **For kernel dispatch**: These remain the correct API when selecting between CUDA-specific kernel implementations (e.g., CUTLASS 2.x vs 3.x). Such code is inherently platform-specific and doesn't need cross-platform abstraction.

---

## 5. Migration Plan

### Phase 0: Add feature methods to Platform (this RFC)

| Task | Effort |
|------|--------|
| Add `supports_bf16()`, `supports_fp8_native()`, `supports_fp8_woq()`, `supports_fp4()`, `supports_tma()`, `supports_wgmma()`, `get_architecture_family()`, `get_device_tier()` to base `Platform` | Small |
| Implement in `CudaPlatformBase`, `RocmPlatform`, `XPUPlatform` | Small |
| Keep `supports_fp8()` as backward-compat alias → `supports_fp8_native()` | Trivial |
| Add `requires_feature()` to `tests/utils.py` | Small |

### Phase 1: Convert feature-gated capability checks in vllm/ source

Convert ~60% of `has_device_capability` calls that are actually feature checks:

```python
# Before
if current_platform.has_device_capability(89):
    # FP8 native path
elif current_platform.has_device_capability(75):
    # FP8 Marlin WOQ fallback

# After  
if current_platform.supports_fp8_native():
    # FP8 native path
elif current_platform.supports_fp8_woq():
    # FP8 Marlin WOQ fallback
```

**Priority conversion targets** (most impactful):
- `has_device_capability(89)` → `supports_fp8_native()` (~15 sites in vllm/)
- `has_device_capability(75)` for Marlin → `supports_fp8_woq()` (~3 sites)
- `has_device_capability(80)` → `supports_bf16()` (~8 sites)
- `is_device_capability_family(100)` → `supports_fp4()` or architecture check (~20 sites)
- `not has_device_capability(89)` for `use_marlin` → `not supports_fp8_native() and supports_fp8_woq()` (~5 sites)

### Phase 2: Convert test skip patterns

Integrate with the test skip RFC (#39158) to migrate test files:

```python
# Before (CUDA-only, broken on ROCm, wrong on consumer GPUs)
@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.has_device_capability(89), reason="need fp8")

# After (cross-platform, correct on all SKUs)
@requires_feature("fp8_native")
```

**Note**: Since vLLM CI always uses NVIDIA server GPUs, the migration can be incremental — existing tests won't break, but new tests should use the feature-based API.

### Phase 3: Lint enforcement

Add pre-commit hook to warn on new `has_device_capability` usage in test files without a `is_cuda()` / `is_rocm()` guard.

---



### Feedback Period.

1-2 weeks.

### CC List.

@tjtanaa 

### Any Other Things.

## 6. Comprehensive Device Capability Reference

### 6.1 NVIDIA CUDA — `torch.cuda.get_device_capability()`

#### Server / Data Center GPUs

| Device | Compute Capability | Architecture | BF16 | FP8 Native | FP4 | TMA |

| GB300 / B300 | `(10, 3)` | Blackwell | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| GB200 / B200 | `(10, 0)` | Blackwell | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| H100 / H200 | `(9, 0)` | Hopper | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ |
| L4 / L40 / L40S | `(8, 9)` | Ada Lovelace | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| A40 / A10 / A16 / A2 | `(8, 6)` | Ampere | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| A100 | `(8, 0)` | Ampere | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| T4 | `(7, 5)` | Turing | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| V100 | `(7, 0)` | Volta | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

#### Workstation / Pro GPUs

| Device | Compute Capability | Architecture | BF16 | FP8 Native | FP4 | TMA |
|--------|-------------------|--------------|------|------------|-----|-----|
| RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell | `(12, 0)` | Blackwell (consumer SM) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅* |
| RTX 6000 Ada | `(8, 9)` | Ada Lovelace | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| RTX A6000 / A5000 / A4000 | `(8, 6)` | Ampere | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Quadro RTX | `(7, 5)` | Turing | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

#### Consumer / GeForce GPUs

| Device | Compute Capability | Architecture | BF16 | FP8 Native | FP4 | TMA |
|--------|-------------------|--------------|------|------------|-----|-----|
| RTX 5090/5080/5070/5060/5050 | `(12, 0)` | Blackwell (consumer SM) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌* |
| RTX 4090/4080/4070/4060 | `(8, 9)` | Ada Lovelace | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| RTX 3090/3080/3070/3060/3050 | `(8, 6)` | Ampere | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| RTX 2080/2070/2060, Titan RTX | `(7, 5)` | Turing | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

> **Key insight**: RTX PRO 6000 and RTX 5090 both report `(12, 0)`, but RTX PRO supports FP8/FP4 while consumer RTX 5090 does not. **Capability number alone is insufficient for feature detection on SM 12.0.**

### 6.2 AMD ROCm — GCN Architecture → Mapped Capability

| Device | GCN Arch | Mapped Capability | Architecture | BF16 | FP8 Native | FP4 |
|--------|----------|------------------|--------------|------|------------|-----|
| MI4xx (future) | gfx1250 | TBD | CDNA next | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| MI355 | gfx950 | `(9, 5)` | CDNA4 | ✅ | ✅ (OCP+FNUZ) | ✅ |
| MI300/MI325 | gfx942 | `(9, 4)` | CDNA3 | ✅ | ✅ (FNUZ) | ❌ |
| MI200 | gfx90a | `(9, 0)` | CDNA2 | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Radeon (RDNA4) | gfx12xx | `(12, 0)` | RDNA4 | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| Radeon (RDNA3) | gfx11xx | `(11, x)` | RDNA3 | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |

> **Key insight**: ROCm's `(9, 0)` = MI200 (NO FP8) vs CUDA's `(9, 0)` = Hopper (HAS FP8). The same number has opposite meanings.

### 6.3 Feature to Capability Mapping — Why Numeric Checks Fail

| Feature | CUDA Numeric Gate | Why It Fails |
|---------|------------------|--------------|
| FP8 Native | `has_device_capability(89)` | ❌ RTX 5090 is `(12,0)` ≥ `(8,9)` but has no native FP8. ROCm MI200 maps to `(9,0)` ≥ `(8,9)` but has no FP8. |
| FP4 | `is_device_capability_family(100)` | ❌ Misses RTX PRO 6000 at `(12,0)`. |
| BF16 | `has_device_capability(80)` | ⚠️ Works for CUDA server/workstation, but returns `None` on XPU (which does support BF16). |
| Blackwell features | `is_device_capability_family(100)` | ❌ Misses workstation Blackwell at `(12,0)`. Includes some non-Blackwell if future families reuse. |

Start the vLLM(0.17.1) server with the zai-org/GLM-4.7-FP8 model and the following speculative decoding configuration: ``` vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-FP8 \ --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --speculative-config.method mtp \ --speculative-config.num_speculative_tokens 1 \ --tool-call-parser glm47 \ --reasoning-parser glm45 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --async-scheduling \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --performance-mode throughput ``` Start benchmark with: ``` vllm bench serve \ --model zai-org/GLM-4.7-FP8 \ --port 8000 \ --save-result \ --save-detailed \ --backend=vllm \ --dataset-name custom \ --dataset-path SOME_DATASET \ --disable-shuffle \ --metric-percentiles "50,90,95,99" \ --percentile-metrics "ttft,tpot,e2el" \ --result-dir "./vllm_bench_results/" \ --request-rate 1 ``` 2. Send a request to the server. 3. The server will suddenly crash with a CUDA error during request processing.

source.title: [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 produces garbage output + CUDA illegal memory access on Hopper (sm90) via Marlin FP4-MoE
source.body:
### Summary

Serving **MiniMax-M3-NVFP4** on **Hopper GPUs (H100 / H200, sm90)** loads and starts the server, but the FP4-MoE forward pass is broken in two independent ways:

1. **Incoherent output** — every request returns garbage (null bytes / repeated-token soup) instead of real text, even at concurrency 1.
2. **CUDA illegal memory access** — the engine crashes at concurrency ≈ 8 inside `fused_marlin_moe`, killing the worker (`EngineDeadError`).

Both reproduce on the **v0.25.1 release** and on the current **nightly**. On Hopper the NVFP4-MoE selector falls back to **MARLIN** (the FlashInfer FP4 backends are Blackwell/SM100-only), and the Marlin FP4-MoE path is where both failures originate.

### Environment

- vLLM **v0.25.1** (also reproduced on a current nightly)
- GPU: **NVIDIA H200** and **H100** (Hopper, sm90)
- Model: `MiniMax-M3-NVFP4` (ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint; `hidden_act="swigluoai"`, `swiglu_limit` set)
- Selected backend (log): `Using 'MARLIN' NvFp4 MoE backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHINFER_TRTLLM', 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS', 'MARLIN']`

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
vllm serve MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --trust-remote-code
```

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "MiniMax-M3-NVFP4",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}],
  "temperature": 0, "max_tokens": 64 }'
```

**At concurrency 1:** the completion is garbage — e.g. 64× ``, or repeated-token soup like `" |,,,, | |,Cut,, Ta,,…"` — never "Paris". The same corruption appears via `/v1/completions` (no chat template), so the defect is in the forward pass, not templating.

**At concurrency ≈ 8:**

```
CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
  ... vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/marlin_moe.py
  ... vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/utils/marlin_utils.py
EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
```

### Expected behavior

M3-NVFP4 serves coherent output on Hopper and remains stable across concurrency (no illegal memory access).

### Root cause

Hopper has no native FP4, so a clamped NVFP4-MoE model (M3 sets `swiglu_limit`) is routed to the **Marlin** weight-only path (enabled for non-Blackwell by #45836). That path has two independent defects for M3:

1. **Garbage output** — the Marlin MoE adapter substitutes plain-SiLU defaults instead of forwarding the model's **`swigluoai` activation parameters (alpha / beta / clamp)**. With the wrong activation the MoE output is numerically meaningless.
2. **Illegal memory access** — gated NVFP4/FP8 MoE whose **`moe_intermediate_size` is not aligned** to the Marlin kernel tile pads incorrectly, producing an out-of-bounds access under load (surfaces at concurrency ≈ 8).

The Marlin epilogue additionally mis-indexes per-row top-k weights (#48895) — the shared kernel-level defect — and M3's tile geometry is what turns it into an out-of-bounds access.

### The fix — two open PRs

Two independent fixes are needed; each addresses one symptom, and **both** are required (one alone is insufficient):

| PR | Resolves | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **#48929** | the **garbage output** | Forwards M3's `swigluoai` activation parameters (alpha / beta / clamp) to the Marlin MoE adapter, instead of substituting plain-SiLU defaults |
| **#48624** | the **illegal memory access** | Pads the gated-MoE intermediate when `moe_intermediate_size` isn't aligned to the Marlin kernel tile |

Both target `main` and are currently open. Applying both over v0.25.1 makes M3 serve coherently (correct "Paris"; correct Rayleigh-scattering explanation) and pass concurrency 8 with no illegal-memory-access, on the same MARLIN backend.

### Related

- **#48895** — Marlin `moe_wna16_marlin_gemm` mis-indexes per-row top-k weights (shared kernel-level defect)
- **#45836** — enabled Marlin-with-clamp on non-Blackwell (merged v0.24.0), which opened this path without the correctness/alignment fixes above

source.title: [Bug]:CUDA illegal instruction during decode (V1 Engine + NVFP4) on aarch64 (NVIDIA GB10)
source.body:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text # I couldn't run collect_env.py easily due to the crash, but here is my exact environment based on nvidia-smi and the docker image logs: - OS: Linux (aarch64) - GPU: NVIDIA GB10 (Grace Blackwell) - CUDA Version: 13.0 - Driver Version: 580.126.09 - vLLM Version: v0.19.1rc1.dev203+g0f3ce4c74 - Docker Image: vllm/vllm-openai:cu130-nightly-aarch64
### 🐛 Describe the bug 🐛 Describe the bug When running an NVFP4 quantized MoE model (qwen3.5-35b-a3b-nvfp4) on an ARM64 server equipped with an NVIDIA GB10 (Grace Blackwell) GPU (which natively supports NVFP4), the vLLM V1 engine crashes with a torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered. The prefill phase successfully processes tokens (in my case, processing 57,260 prompt tokens with an 84% prefix cache hit rate), but the engine crashes specifically during the decode phase (around output token 45) inside GPUModelRunner.get_output(). Since the Blackwell hardware natively supports NVFP4 instructions, this strongly suggests a JIT compilation bug (torch.compile / Inductor) or CUDA graph issue generating invalid PTX/SASS instructions for aarch64 under the V1 Engine. Workaround: Appending --enforce-eager to the docker run command bypasses the crash entirely, which further confirms it is a compilation issue rather than a hardware limitation. To Reproduce Run the following command on a GB10 (aarch64) node: Bash docker run --runtime nvidia --gpus all \ -v /home/admin/models:/workspace/models \ -p 8081:8000 \ --ipc=host \ vllm/vllm-openai:cu130-nightly-aarch64 \ --model /workspace/models/qwen3.5-35b-a3b-nvfp4 \ --served-model-name qwen3.5-35b \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --max-model-len 131072 \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --enable-prefix-caching \ --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --reasoning-parser qwen3 \ --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml \ --enable-auto-tool-choice source.title: [Bug]: #48036 auto-enables sequence-parallel MoE on TP+EP without DP — −19% throughput, −24% KV cache, and no way to opt out
source.body:
### Summary

#48036 removed `and self.data_parallel_size > 1` from `ParallelConfig.use_sequence_parallel_moe` (`vllm/config/parallel.py`). As a side effect, sequence-parallel MoE is now auto-enabled on **every** EP + TP deployment that has no data parallelism (`dp=1`) — a configuration it was previously never applied to.

On our TP=4 / EP / dp=1 setup this is a sizeable regression in both throughput and KV-cache capacity, and there is currently **no way to turn it off** short of switching `all2all_backend` away from the default `allgather_reducescatter`, which changes the expert-exchange mechanism entirely.

### Measurements

GLM-5.2-NVFP4 (MoE, `glm_moe_dsa`) on 4×H200, TP=4, `--enable-expert-parallel`, dp=1, DCP=4, MTP=1, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.945`, CPU KV offload on. The **only** difference between the two rows is whether `use_sequence_parallel_moe` returns True — same image, same commit, same flags:

| | GPU KV cache | N=1 | N=8 | N=32 (aggregate) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-MoE **off** (pre-#48036 behavior) | **1,032,448 tok** | **75 tok/s** | **407 tok/s** | **931 tok/s** |
| SP-MoE **on** (current `main`) | 784,300 tok | 61 tok/s | 353 tok/s | 875 tok/s |
| delta | **−24%** | **−19%** | **−13%** | **−6%** |

Method: 2 warm-up requests, then 3×N=1, 2×N=8, 2×N=32; 256 output tokens, `ignore_eos`, throughput = `completion_tokens / wall`. MTP acceptance length was identical (1.85–1.87) in both, so speculative decoding is not a factor.

The KV-cache loss is the more painful half for us: it directly cuts how many long sessions fit on the GPU.

### Why this configuration is not exotic

Serving one large MoE model on a single node with TP + EP and no data parallelism is a common single-replica setup — the model does not fit on one GPU, so TP is mandatory, and EP is the natural choice for the expert layers. Before #48036 such deployments simply never took the SP-MoE path; now they all do, silently, on upgrade.

### Ask

Two things would help:

1. **An explicit switch.** `use_sequence_parallel_moe` is a derived property with no override. A tri-state config (`auto` = today's heuristic, plus explicit `on`/`off`) would let deployments opt out without patching `parallel.py` or changing `all2all_backend`. Happy to send a PR for this.
2. **A second look at the heuristic itself** for the `dp=1` case: if SP-MoE reliably loses on TP-only + EP (our numbers suggest it does, at least for this model class), the auto-enable condition may want the `dp > 1` guard back, with #48036's `all_gather` fix retained (that fix is correct and orthogonal — it is what makes SP-MoE + MTP produce correct output at all).

We are currently carrying a local patch that restores the `dp > 1` guard, which is what the "SP-MoE off" row above measures.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to run the A/B and draft this report; the numbers are from real runs on our hardware.

### 🐛 Describe the bug Summary When running Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 on vLLM v0.11.2, the engine crashes with: torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered deep_gemm::DGException: Assertion error: error == CUDA_SUCCESS or error == CUDA_ERROR_DEINITIALIZED This happens even when using the recommended workaround: --compilation-config {"cudagraph_mode": "PIECEWISE"} The crash occurs during generation (sample_tokens) with long sequences (~5400 tokens total). The process dies, and the API server returns EngineDeadError. This appears related but not identical to issue #28835, as the problem persists with PIECEWISE and with the FP8 variant of Qwen3-Next-80B. Environment vLLM version: v0.11.2 (vllm/vllm-openai:v0.11.2 Docker image) Model: Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 GPU: NVIDIA H200 (CUDA 12.8 / 12.9) Driver: NVIDIA-SMI 580.95.05 Setup: single GPU (tensor_parallel_size=1) Docker Compose command: command: - --model - Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8 - --served-model-name - Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B - --gpu-memory-utilization - "0.9" - --enable-auto-tool-choice - --tool-call-parser - hermes - --compilation-config - '{"cudagraph_mode": "PIECEWISE"}' Reproduction Steps Start vLLM with configuration above. Send a chat completion request with a long prompt (> 4500–5000 tokens) or a streaming request that produces > 1000 generated tokens. After several steps of generation, the engine crashes with an illegal memory access. Observed in real usage with: num_computed_tokens=[5457, 245] Expected Behavior vLLM should generate tokens without triggering CUDA illegal memory access, or at minimum fail gracefully without killing the engine. Actual Behavior Crash logs: torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered File ... gpu_model_runner.py line 5101: self.transfer_event.synchronize() Then: deep_gemm::DGException: Assertion error: error == CUDA_SUCCESS or error == CUDA_ERROR_DEINITIALIZED Finally: vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue The whole engine dies and must be restarted. Full stacktrace available upon request. Notes / Observations cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE does not prevent the crash. The pattern is consistent with behavior described in #28835 for inputs > 5k tokens. However: #28835 concerns the BF16 variant and long-context corruption (!!!!!), while this report concerns the FP8 variant and causes a fatal illegal memory access. The crash occurs inside: gpu_model_runner._to_list() CUDA event synchronization sometimes followed by DeepGEMM teardown errors. This might indicate: a FP8 kernel issue, or incorrect tensor shapes / offsets under long-sequence decode, or a memory lifetime problem between torch.compile + DeepGEMM + Qwen3-Next custom blocks. Questions Is this a known issue for the FP8 variant of Qwen3-Next-80B? Is there a recommended workaround besides disabling FP8? Should long-sequence (>5k tokens) support be considered unstable for this model in FP8? ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

incidents.complaint_or_finding: MXFP4 models on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell SM120 still select the Marlin fallback kernel.
incidents.observed_failure: The runtime falls back to the Marlin kernel rather than using the expected MXFP4 path.
incidents.discriminating_test: Run the same MXFP4 checkpoint and prompt on SM120 in vLLM and another MXFP4-capable runtime, recording the selected kernel; a vLLM-only fallback isolates runtime support rather than checkpoint damage.

source.title: [Bug]: disable_flashinfer_q_quantization + fp8 KV + spec decode silently corrupts sliding-window models on SM100 (trtllm-gen); BF16-Q paths also mis-apply q/k/v scales
source.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM nightly `0.23.1rc1.dev843+g04adc8843` (relevant code identical on current `main`), flashinfer-python 0.6.14 (latest) + flashinfer-cubin 0.6.13, torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13, 1× NVIDIA B200 (SM100).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Combination:** `--attention-backend FLASHINFER` + `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` + `--attention-config '{"disable_flashinfer_q_quantization": true}'` (BF16 query) + speculative decoding, on SM100, serving a **sliding-window** model (gemma-4-31B, 50/60 layers SWA window 1024).

**Symptom:** silently corrupted output — sporadic wrong tokens and short repetition loops in otherwise coherent generations, e.g. on a temp-0 summarization request:

> "...a Saga breaks a transaction into a sequence of a sequence of a sequence of local transactions..."
> "#### This implementation analysis of the an this Python API Gateway reveals several critical..."

With deeper speculation (k=64 suffix decoding) the same combination degenerates into full runaway repetition.

Attribution matrix (all temp-0, same prompts, gemma-4-31B NVFP4 + MTP `num_speculative_tokens=7`):

| config | output |
|---|---|
| fp8-Q (flag off), spec on | clean |
| bf16-Q (flag on), **no spec** | clean |
| bf16-Q (flag on), spec on, `-O3` cudagraphs | corrupted |
| bf16-Q (flag on), spec on, `--enforce-eager` | corrupted (not a cudagraph issue) |

**Root cause (kernel level):** flashinfer's trtllm-gen spec-as-decode kernel (`trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache`, `q_len_per_req=8`) with BF16-Q + FP8-KV mis-computes sliding-window attention once `seq_len > window` at certain seq_len/page alignments — errors up to ~1.8 confined to single (query-row, head) pairs, while FP8-Q / no-window / q_len≤4 controls on identical inputs are clean. Standalone repro + characterization filed at flashinfer-ai/flashinfer: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3864. vLLM routes spec-decode verify onto exactly this kernel when the flag is set (`use_trtllm_attention` forces trtllm for decode when `has_spec`), so the flag currently turns a supported-looking configuration into silent corruption for any SWA model.

Suggested action until the kernel is fixed: reject or warn on `disable_flashinfer_q_quantization=True` + quantized KV + speculative decoding + sliding-window layers on SM100.

### Secondary (independent) issue: q/k/v scales mis-applied on the BF16-Q paths

While reproducing this we found the BF16-Q scale bookkeeping in `vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py` is wrong whenever the checkpoint carries calibrated attention scales (inert for the common `_q_scale = _k_scale = _v_scale = 1.0` case, which is why it does not show up in the repro above):

1. `FlashInferImpl.forward` computes
   ```python
   self.bmm1_scale = self.scale
   if is_quantized_kv_cache(self.kv_cache_dtype):
       self.bmm1_scale *= layer._q_scale_float * layer._k_scale_float
   ```
   unconditionally — `_q_scale_float` is applied even when `disable_flashinfer_q_quantization` keeps Q in BF16 (no quantization happened, so there is nothing to de-scale). The XQA helper right above it (`get_xqa_bmm1_scale`) already implements the correct conditional ("only include q_scale when the decode query is actually FP8") — but it is only used for the XQA decode path, not for trtllm-gen decode or trtllm prefill.

2. The BF16-Q + FP8-KV trtllm **prefill** path dequantizes the KV cache into a BF16 mock cache using `layer._k_scale` / `layer._v_scale` (`trtllm_prefill_attn_kvfp8_dequant`) and then still passes `bmm1_scale = sm_scale * q_scale * k_scale` and `bmm2_scale = v_scale` to `trtllm_batch_context_with_kv_cache` — k/v scales get applied twice (and q_scale once too many) for calibrated checkpoints.

### Repro (serve level)

```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-NVFP4 \
  --served-model-name gemma-4-31b \
  --attention-backend FLASHINFER \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"google/gemma-4-31B-it-assistant","method":"mtp","quantization":"fp8","num_speculative_tokens":7}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}' \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 1536 --enforce-eager \
  --attention-config '{"disable_flashinfer_q_quantization": true}'
```

then send any ~1k-token chat completion at temperature 0 and generate a few hundred tokens (the corruption needs `seq_len` to run past the 1024-token sliding window; short prompts stay clean). Drop the `--attention-config` line → clean output; drop the `--speculative-config` line (keeping the flag) → clean output.

### Your current environment


- vLLM version: v0.19.0 (also reproduced on `vllm/vllm-openai:gemma4-x86_64-cu130`)
- GPU: 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96GB GDDR7, SM 12.0)
- OS: Linux 5.15.0-171-generic
- CUDA: 13.0
- Python: 3.12
- Docker image: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.19.0-x86_64-cu130-ubuntu2404` (with `transformers>=5.5.0` installed for Gemma 4 support)

## Model

`google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (Mixture-of-Experts, 25.2B total params, 3.8B active, 128 experts with 8 active per token)

## Command

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --quantization fp8 \
  --max-model-len 25600 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --trust-remote-code
```

GPUs assigned: 2 GPUs (device IDs 6 and 7).



### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

Gemma 4 MoE model crashes at runtime when `--data-parallel-size` is set to anything greater than 1. The model loads weights successfully, captures CUDA graphs, and starts API servers — but fails on the **first inference request** with an `AssertionError` inside the expert-parallel all-gather communication path.

This was also reproduced with `--quantization mxfp4` (which crashes earlier during weight loading) and `--quantization fp8` (crashes on first request after successful load).

**DP=1 works perfectly.** The issue is specific to DP > 1 with MoE models.

Dense models (e.g., `google/gemma-4-E4B-it`, `google/gemma-4-31B-it`) work fine with DP > 1.

## Error traceback

### Phase 1: Weight loading (with `--quantization mxfp4`)

When using `--quantization mxfp4`, the crash occurs during weight loading:

```
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/layer.py", line 1073, in weight_loader
    dim2 = loaded_weight.shape[2]
IndexError: tuple index out of range
```

This is covered by existing issues #35329 and #35324.

### Phase 2: Runtime crash (with `--quantization fp8`)

With `fp8`, weights load successfully and CUDA graphs are captured. The crash occurs on the first inference request:

```
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/cuda_communicator.py", in _all_gather_single
AssertionError: 1 != 36
```

The all-gather operation in the MoE expert dispatch expects a tensor dimension matching `sizes[rank]` (36 tokens) but receives 1. This suggests the MoE dispatch layer is incorrectly routing through expert-parallelism communication paths when running under data parallelism, causing a tensor shape mismatch between DP workers.

## Root cause analysis

The MoE fused expert layer appears to assume that multiple GPUs = expert parallelism (EP), triggering inter-GPU all-gather operations for expert routing. Under data parallelism, each GPU should run an independent full copy of the MoE model with no cross-GPU expert communication. The DP workers seem to be initializing with EP-style communication, leading to the shape assertion failure.

## Workaround

Run separate container instances, each with `--data-parallel-size 1` on its own GPU, with an external load balancer (e.g., Caddy, nginx) distributing requests round-robin across them. This provides effective data parallelism without triggering the MoE dispatch bug.

## Related issues

- #18567 — Single-node data parallel crash (general DP crash, not MoE-specific)
- #35329 — `quantization="mxfp4"` produces incorrect results for MoE at TP=1
- #35324 — FusedMoE.weight_loader MXFP4 crashes on standard HF MoE checkpoints
- #33014 — LoRA loading fails with Fused MoE when DP > 1

### Your current environment


- vLLM version: v0.19.0
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96GB GDDR7, SM 12.0)
- OS: Linux 5.15.0-171-generic
- CUDA: 13.0
- Python: 3.12
- Docker image: `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.19.0-x86_64-cu130-ubuntu2404` (with `transformers>=5.5.0`)

## Model

`google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (MoE, 128 experts, 8 active per token)

## Command

```bash
vllm serve google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it \
  --data-parallel-size 1 \
  --quantization mxfp4 \
  --max-model-len 25600 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --trust-remote-code
```


### 🐛 Describe the bug

Runtime MXFP4 quantization (`--quantization mxfp4`) crashes during weight loading for the Gemma 4 MoE model, even with `--data-parallel-size 1`. The fused MoE weight loader at `layer.py:1073` attempts to access `loaded_weight.shape[2]`, but the weight tensor is 2D, not 3D, causing an `IndexError`.

This is effectively the same class of bug as #35329 and #35324, but specifically reproduced with `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (Gemma 4 MoE). Filing separately because:

1. Those issues focus on other MoE architectures (DeepSeek, Qwen, Mixtral).
2. Gemma 4 MoE is a new model with a unique expert architecture (128 experts, 8 active) that may require specific attention in the weight loader.
3. The `mxfp4` quantization method is the recommended replacement for the deprecated `petit_nvfp4`, so it's critical that it works with newly released MoE models.

## Error traceback

```
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/layer.py", line 1073, in weight_loader
    dim2 = loaded_weight.shape[2]
IndexError: tuple index out of range
```

The weight tensor loaded from the Gemma 4 MoE checkpoint is 2D `(out_features, in_features)`, but the MXFP4 branch of `weight_loader` expects a 3D tensor `(num_experts, out_features, in_features)`. The MXFP4 quantization path doesn't reshape the weights before accessing the expert dimension.

## Expected behavior

`--quantization mxfp4` should correctly quantize Gemma 4 MoE weights at load time, producing a functional model with FP4 weights and FP16/BF16 compute.

## Actual behavior

Crash during weight loading with `IndexError: tuple index out of range`.

## Impact

There is currently **no working FP4 runtime quantization path for Gemma 4 MoE** in vLLM:

| Method | Status |
|---|---|
| `nvfp4` | Removed (unknown method error) |
| `petit_nvfp4` | Deprecated, crashes with deprecation error |
| `mxfp4` | Crashes during weight loading (this bug) |
| `fp8` | Works (2x compression, not 4x) |

For memory-bandwidth-limited hardware (e.g., GDDR7-based Blackwell RTX), FP4 quantization provides significant throughput improvements over FP8. The inability to use any FP4 quantization with the MoE model is a meaningful limitation.

## Workaround

Use `--quantization fp8` as a fallback. This provides 2x bandwidth savings over BF16 instead of the 4x that FP4 would offer.

For pre-quantized FP4, the **dense** model `nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4` with `--quantization modelopt` works correctly. However, there is no pre-quantized FP4 checkpoint available for the MoE variant that loads successfully with vLLM.

## Related issues

- #35329 — `quantization="mxfp4"` produces incorrect results / hangs for MoE models at TP=1
- #35324 — FusedMoE.weight_loader MXFP4 branch crashes on standard HuggingFace MoE checkpoints

source.body:
### Environment

- **vLLM Version**: 0.16.0rc2.dev559+g4bf19f9bf
- **CUDA**: 13.0
- **GPU**: NVIDIA B200 / DGX Spark (SM121)
- **Model**: openai/gpt-oss-120b

**Server command:**
```bash
vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-120b \
  --quantization mxfp4 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --max-model-len 2048 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.70 \
  --max-num-seqs 2 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --load-format fastsafetensors
```

---

### 🐛 Bug Description

When serving `openai/gpt-oss-120b` with MXFP4 quantization on a **single SM121 GPU** (NVIDIA B200 / DGX Spark), all chat completions return `content: null` and `reasoning: null` despite `completion_tokens` showing that tokens were generated.

**Request:**
```python
client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-oss-120b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2+2?"}],
    max_tokens=512,
)
```

**Response:**
```json
{
  "choices": [{
    "message": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": null,
      "reasoning": null,
      "tool_calls": []
    },
    "finish_reason": "length"
  }],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 74,
    "completion_tokens": 512,
    "total_tokens": 586
  }
}
```

512 tokens were generated but none surfaced as content or reasoning.

---

### Root Cause

**The Harmony prompt rendered for `gpt-oss-120b` ends with:**
```
<|start|>assistant        (tokens: 200006, 173781)
```

The model must generate `<|channel|>` (token **200005**) as its first completion token to begin a valid Harmony channel header (`<|channel|>analysis<|message|>...`).

**Instead, on SM121 with MXFP4 + Marlin fallback, the model generates token `181886` = `'farbe'` (German: "color") — a completely wrong non-Harmony text token.**

Verified via `return_token_ids: true`:
```json
"prompt_token_ids": [..., 200006, 173781],
"token_ids":        [181886, 87, 314, ...]
```

Decoded: `'farbex = 0.5\nWe need to produce the next token...'`

The Harmony `StreamableParser` immediately raises `HarmonyError` on token 181886 because it expects `<|start|>` (200006) or `<|channel|>` (200005), not a regular text token. The parser returns an empty result → `reasoning: null`, `content: null`.

**Server log evidence (before HarmonyError fix):**
```
HarmonyError during output parsing, returning partial result:
  Unexpected token 63248 while expecting start token 200006
```

---

### Why This Happens

SM121 (Blackwell) does **not** have native hardware FP4 support. The vLLM server logs confirm:

```
WARNING: Your GPU does not have native support for FP4 computation but FP4
quantization is being used. Weight-only FP4 compression will be used
leveraging the Marlin kernel. This may degrade performance for compute-heavy
workloads.
```

The `csrc/quantization/gptq_marlin/` directory contains only SM80-targeted kernels:
```
sm80_kernel_bfloat16_fe2m1f_bfloat16.cu
sm80_kernel_bfloat16_fe4m3fn_bfloat16.cu
...
```

No SM121-specific Marlin kernels exist. The SM80 Marlin MXFP4 kernel running on SM121 produces incorrect logits for the first assistant token, causing the model to sample a garbage text token instead of the Harmony control token `<|channel|>`.

---

### Relationship to Existing Issues

- **#31422** ([Bug]: SM120/SM100: gpt-oss gibberish with tp=2) — related but different: that issue is TP=2 + prefix caching. This bug reproduces on **single GPU, tp=1**, with prefix caching enabled or disabled.

---

### Secondary Bug: System Message Causes Hallucinated Reasoning

A second bug causes the model to produce hallucinated/off-topic reasoning when a **system message** is included in the request. With the broken prompt, the model sometimes generates tokens in the `analysis` channel, but the content is completely wrong (e.g., discussing Codeforces problems when asked "What is 2+2?", or outputting Russian/Unicode characters).

**Root cause:** `_make_request_with_harmony` was passing system-role messages directly to `parse_chat_inputs_to_harmony_messages`, which does not handle the `system` role in Harmony encoding format. The raw system tokens corrupt the Harmony token sequence, misdirecting the model's reasoning.

This is fixed in the linked PR.

---

### Steps to Reproduce

1. SM121 GPU (NVIDIA B200/DGX Spark)
2. Start vLLM with `openai/gpt-oss-120b --quantization mxfp4`
3. Send any chat completion request
4. Observe: `content: null`, `reasoning: null`, `finish_reason: length`
5. Enable `return_token_ids: true` — first completion token is not `200005` (`<|channel|>`)

---

### Expected Behavior

First completion token should be `200005` (`<|channel|>`), followed by valid Harmony channel content, producing non-null `reasoning` and/or `content`.

---

### Proposed Fix

Add SM121-targeted Marlin MXFP4 kernels in `csrc/quantization/gptq_marlin/` or route SM121 through FlashInfer's native MXFP4 path (if supported) rather than the SM80 Marlin fallback.

---

### Workaround

Remove `--quantization mxfp4` and use `--dtype bfloat16` (unquantized). This avoids the Marlin kernel entirely. Note: 120B model in bfloat16 requires ~240 GB VRAM.

source.title: [Performance]: [Fused MoE] BLOCK_SIZE_K=128 decode default causes large slowdown on Volta/V100
source.body:
### Proposal to improve performance

I am filing this as a performance discussion rather than a bug report because V100 / `sm_70` is not a primary target for current vLLM wheels. The useful upstream part is a measured fused-MoE default/config finding that affects the V100-relevant vLLM line.

The focus is vLLM 0.19, because that is the last broadly practical vLLM line for Tesla V100 users. I also verified the same fused-MoE default shape in my 0.21 source-build path, but I am not asking vLLM to restore V100 wheel support here.

Summary:

1. **Finding**
   - On Tesla V100 / Volta (`sm_70`), the fused-MoE decode/small-M path using `BLOCK_SIZE_K=128` is much slower than expected.
   - The practical symptom is that FP16/BF16 sparse MoE decode can become slower than dense models of similar class.
   - This is not the hardware limit itself; it is a bad fallback/default for Volta.

2. **Measured fix**
   - For small-M decode on Volta, changing the MoE tile to `BLOCK_SIZE_K=64` removes the pathology.
   - In my A/B tests, output remained bit-identical.
   - This is a speed/config fix, not an approximation.

3. **Suggested upstream path**
   - If vLLM is willing to accept V100 config data, I can provide tuned config JSONs for Tesla V100.
   - I am not proposing an sm_70 support-policy change.
   - If heuristic code for sm_70 is not in scope, the data/config contribution may still be useful.

The main question for maintainers:

Would vLLM accept V100 fused-MoE config JSONs / performance data for the 0.19-era Volta path, or is this better kept as external documentation only?

### Report of performance regression

Environment:

- Hardware: 8x NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB
- Architecture: Volta / `sm_70`
- Main vLLM focus: vLLM 0.19.x, because this is the last broadly practical V100 line
- Also checked: vLLM 0.21 source-build path on CUDA 12.6
- Toolchain: CUDA 12.6 / cu126 source builds
- Serving mode: cudagraph decode

Observed symptom:

On V100, FP16/BF16 MoE decode with the stock fused-MoE default can be slower than dense models of similar class. This is backwards for sparse MoE decode, where only a small active subset of experts should move per token.

Measured examples on the same 8x V100 box:

| Model | Stock FP16 MoE | Patched/tuned MoE | Improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, C1 | ~15.6 tok/s | ~65.9 tok/s | ~4.2x |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, C8 aggregate | ~24.9 tok/s | ~173.9 tok/s | ~7.0x aggregate |
| Gemma-4-26B-A4B, C1 | ~10.9 tok/s | ~43.7 tok/s | ~4.0x |
| Gemma-4-26B-A4B, C8 aggregate | ~28.3 tok/s | ~155.9 tok/s | ~5.5x aggregate |

Root-cause summary:

- The initial suspect was `num_stages`, because Volta lacks `cp.async`.
- Sweeping `num_stages` did not explain the slowdown.
- The real lever was `BLOCK_SIZE_K`.
- The decode/small-M path using `BLOCK_SIZE_K=128` spills badly on Volta.
- `BLOCK_SIZE_K=64` removes the pathology.
- The A/B output was bit-identical in the tested cases.

Scope:

- FP16/BF16 fused-MoE decode.
- Small-M / decode regime.
- Volta / V100 evidence only.
- Does not affect dense models.
- Does not depend on my custom FP8 plugin.
- Not an MTP/speculative decoding result.

Reference write-up / evidence:

- https://github.com/KumphanartDansiri/v100-vllm-2026
- Chapter 2 documents this finding.
- The companion implementation/results repo is here:
  https://github.com/KumphanartDansiri/vllm-fp8-w8a16-sm70

### Misc discussion on performance

I am intentionally framing this narrowly.

I understand that current vLLM wheels do not target V100 / `sm_70`, and I am not asking for a policy reversal in this issue. The reason I am reporting it upstream is that vLLM 0.19 remains an important practical line for V100 users, and the fused-MoE default/config issue is large enough that it can make sparse MoE look incorrectly bad on Volta.

The possible outcomes I see are:

1. vLLM accepts Tesla V100 fused-MoE config JSONs as data.
2. vLLM decides this should remain external documentation because V100 is out of current support scope.
3. Maintainers suggest a better place or format for this finding.

If option 1 is acceptable, I can prepare a focused PR with only config data / documentation, avoiding any broad sm_70 support-policy change.

### Your current environment (if you think it is necessary)

Not a live-install bug report, so I did not run collect_env.py here.

The relevant measured environments are:

Hardware:
- 8x NVIDIA Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB
- Volta / sm_70
- NVLink box

Software / build context:
- vLLM 0.19.x source build as the primary V100-relevant line
- vLLM 0.21 source-build path also checked on CUDA 12.6
- CUDA 12.6 / cu126 torch path
- CUDAGraph decode serving setup

Models used in the MoE A/B:
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
- Gemma-4-26B-A4B

Reference repos:
- Write-up / benchmark matrix:
  https://github.com/KumphanartDansiri/v100-vllm-2026
- Companion code/results repo:
  https://github.com/KumphanartDansiri/vllm-fp8-w8a16-sm70

Notes:
- This is not a request to restore V100 wheel support.
- This is not related to my custom FP8 kernels.
- I can provide config JSONs or a smaller reproducer if maintainers think this is useful.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

source.title: CUDA device-side assert with nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 + MTP on nightly f91fb2f
source.body:
## Summary

`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-f91fb2fcf3f100d46baf4db2e5d86fa5596b276b` crashes with a CUDA device-side assert while serving the official NVIDIA `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` model with MTP/spec decoding enabled.

The same local model files were hash-checked against the official Hugging Face repo revision and safetensors LFS SHA256 values.

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, 32 GB VRAM
- NVIDIA driver reported by `nvidia-smi`: 610.47
- OS: WSL2 Ubuntu 24.04
- Kernel: `6.6.114.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`
- Docker: `Docker version 29.5.2, build 79eb04c`
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-f91fb2fcf3f100d46baf4db2e5d86fa5596b276b`
- vLLM: `0.22.1rc1.dev55+gf91fb2fcf`
- Torch: `2.11.0+cu130`
- Transformers: `5.9.0`

## Model

HF model:

`nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`

Repo revision from local Hugging Face metadata and HF API:

`6c7f09d4036e97393f82e9f9ecd1a5c35ca5ee92`

Local safetensors hashes matched official HF LFS hashes:

| File | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| `model-00001-of-00003.safetensors` | `07141c2db92e47bc08777132cd1a0323faf300eab3a7d7c111bc2bf075fda050` |
| `model-00002-of-00003.safetensors` | `6dea9c759a0f941cf9e1cc1501216b0e107966a66c90425050e212efbd053f02` |
| `model-00003-of-00003.safetensors` | `9758875fc55e49561165f4a44342b654c123c3e25c6811b34abb83553fb1a164` |
| `model.safetensors.index.json` | `d67403a4e9793c0ba8a136baf14b3b76ec7b32c822267978084895e07ebd8a3e` |

## Serving configuration

Profile line used locally:

```text
backend=vllm-docker image=vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-f91fb2fcf3f100d46baf4db2e5d86fa5596b276b port=8082 ctx=131072 kv=fp8 gpu=0.94 max_num_seqs=1 max_num_batched_tokens=8192 spec=mtp:3 vision=on chunked_prefill=on prefix_caching=on expert_parallel=on reasoning_parser=qwen3 tool_parser=qwen3_xml thinking=on preserve_thinking=on temp=0.6 top_p=0.95 alias=qwen35-nvidia-nvfp4-sci-thinking
```

Equivalent notable vLLM arguments:

```text
--model /model
--trust-remote-code
--max-model-len 131072
--quantization modelopt
--kv-cache-dtype fp8
--gpu-memory-utilization 0.94
--max-num-seqs 1
--max-num-batched-tokens 8192
--enable-chunked-prefill
--enable-prefix-caching
--enable-expert-parallel
--reasoning-parser qwen3
--enable-auto-tool-choice
--tool-call-parser qwen3_xml
--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":true,"preserve_thinking":true}'
--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"moe_backend":"triton"}'
```

## Failure

During generation, the engine crashes with:

```text
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

Relevant stack excerpt:

```text
(EngineCore pid=264) ERROR [core.py:1188] EngineCore encountered a fatal error.
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 4041, in execute_model
    self.synchronize_input_prep(),
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 3709, in synchronize_input_prep
    self.prepare_inputs_event.synchronize()
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
For debugging consider passing CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
Compile with `TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA` to enable device-side assertions.
```

After that, `AsyncLLM output_handler` fails with `EngineDeadError`, and shutdown also hits the same CUDA assert during cleanup:

```text
vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError: EngineCore encountered an issue.
...
model_runner.shutdown()
...
torch.accelerator.synchronize()
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

## Expected behavior

The engine should either complete generation or return a non-fatal request-level error. A single request should not kill the EngineCore with a CUDA device-side assert.

## Notes

- This was observed after switching from `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.22.0` to the nightly image above.
- Because the assert is asynchronous, I cannot prove the originating kernel from this stack alone.
- The high-risk interaction appears to be Qwen35 NVFP4 + MTP/spec decoding + fp8 KV on Blackwell/RTX 5090.
- I have not yet reduced this to a minimal repro with `spec=off` vs `spec=mtp:3`.

incidents.complaint_or_finding: Under matched vLLM serving benchmarks on eight H200 GPUs, DeepSeek-V3.2 is reported to have worse throughput, TTFT, and TPOT than DeepSeek-V3.1.
incidents.observed_failure: The supplied result charts report slower DeepSeek-V3.2 throughput, time to first token, and time per output token across tested input lengths and request rates.
incidents.baseline_or_control: DeepSeek-V3.1 served with the same script structure, tensor-parallel size 8, memory settings, random dataset, 1,024-token outputs, input lengths from 256 to 16,384, request rates 1/4/8/16, and 100 prompts.
incidents.resolution: The issue was closed as not planned; no fix is supplied.
missing_information: Whether either checkpoint used quantization or another compressed representation
incidents.discriminating_test: Benchmark the same DeepSeek-V3.2 checkpoint, prompts, lengths, and decoding settings in vLLM and a reference runtime; a vLLM-only slowdown indicates runtime/config behavior, while a cross-runtime slowdown points to the model or representation.

source.title: [Performance]: Deepseek-V4 Support and Optimization on ROCm Backend
source.body:
## Motivation

This issue tracks the end-to-end enablement and optimization checklist for **DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm backend**.

DeepSeek-V4 includes multiple critical blocks (mHC/HCA/CSA/MoE/MTP), and ROCm readiness depends on both model-side kernels and system-side runtime behavior.

We’re launching a joint effort to optimize DeepSeek V4 on the ROCm backend—please feel free to take on any task, and we’d love to hear more optimization ideas.

## Purpose

- [ ] Track DeepSeek-V4 functionality and performance readiness on ROCm backend.
- [ ] Keep module-level optimization items visible and actionable.
- [ ] Align acceptance criteria for release and production readiness.

---

## Recipe 

- [ ] Recipe: `vLLM Recipe: DeepSeek-V4 on AMD (ROCm) Usage Guide - vLLM Recipes` https://github.com/vllm-project/recipes/pull/433

## General Checklist

### 1) Functionality / Bugfix / Feature

- [x] [Functionality] Base PR has been merged for functionality/accuracy readiness on MI35x for DeepSeek-V4-Pro and DeepSeek-V4-Flash. <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/40871>
- [ ] [Functionality] DeepSeek-V4-Flash Base FP8 enablement PR: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41136>
- [ ] [Functionality] MI30x support PR: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41451>
- [ ] [Bugfix] Enable cross-node TP=16 FP8 serving for DeepSeek-V4: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41312>
- [ ] [Feature][WIP] Enable KV offload for DeepSeek-V4: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41352>
- [ ] [Feature][WIP] Compressed tensors support for DSV4: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41276>
- [x] [Bugfix] Fix accuracy issue with high concurrency: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42810>

---

## Performance Checklist

### 1) High-Level Performance/Feature

- [x] Full graph support for Decode path. Piecewise graph capture support for Prefill path. <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42604>  <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41601>
- [ ] Support MTP 

### 2) Kernel Fusion

#### Element-wise Fusion
- [x] Avoid redundant dtype conversion: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41374>
- [x] Fuse norm and router for lower latency: <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41263>
- [ ] Silu and Mul is implemented with [`torch native`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/activation.py#L173)
- [ ] inv_rope is implemented with [`torch native`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py#L872)

#### CSA

- [ ] Make the sparse MLA indexer optimization for Deepseek-V4, now the sparse attention indexder is [`pytorch native implementation`](<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py#L592>).
- [ ] Replace torch native sparse MLA path with Triton kernel (<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41136>). Another single kernel (<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41812>)
- [ ] Enable CSA multi-stream execution in Decode (`default stream` + `indexer stream`) to overlap indexer and main attention paths, aligned with the DeepSeek-V4 blog design.

#### mHC
- [x] Now the MHC on ROCm is pytorch native implementation ([`mhc_pre`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py#L237)， [`mhc_post`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/mhc.py#L451)), need to integrate [`AITER MHC kernel`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/blob/main/csrc/include/mhc.h) https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/41946

#### MoE
- [ ] AITER FlyDSL MoE integration when it's ready ([`MoE Kernel`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2951/changes))
