source.title: [Bug]: ROCm MI300X FP8 KV cache MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 accuracy issues
source.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Key environment details</summary>

```text
GPU              : 8x AMD Instinct MI300X (gfx942)
Image            : vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:minimax-m3
vLLM             : 0.22.1rc1.dev490+g4a560dd8d
Model            : MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8
Model dtype      : torch.bfloat16
Quantization     : mxfp8
Attention backend: TRITON_ATTN
Parallelism      : TP=8, expert parallelism enabled
KV cache         : fp8 (broken) / auto-BF16 (working)
Prefix caching   : disabled
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Summary

On ROCm/MI300X, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` starts successfully with
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, and requests return HTTP 200, but generated output is
severely corrupted.

vLLM also reports that calibrated FP8 attention scales are unavailable and
uses `1.0`:

```text
Using uncalibrated q_scale 1.0 and/or prob_scale 1.0 with fp8 attention.
This may cause accuracy issues. Please make sure q/prob scaling factors are
available in the fp8 checkpoint.
```

That warning was initially suspected, but it is not the cause of this failure.
The failure is a dtype mismatch in the MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention path.

This is not a small accuracy regression. GSM8K strict accuracy drops from
`0.9666` with the default BF16 KV cache to `0.0099` with FP8 KV cache.
Outputs contain unrelated problem fragments, incorrect arithmetic, and
repetition that often continues to the generation limit.

Removing only `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` restores normal output and accuracy.

This appears related to #45533, but the failure mode is different: #45533
reports startup failure, while this configuration starts and serves normally
but silently returns incorrect output.

### Root cause

On ROCm gfx942, `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` is
`torch.float8_e4m3fnuz`. The MiniMax-M3 sparse backend instead hardcodes
`torch.float8_e4m3fn` when it reinterprets the byte-backed KV cache:

```python
self.kv_cache_fp8_dtype = (
    torch.float8_e5m2
    if "e5m2" in kv_cache_dtype
    else torch.float8_e4m3fn
)
```

The prefill and decode wrappers also classify only `float8_e4m3fn` and
`float8_e5m2` as FP8, omitting `float8_e4m3fnuz`.

FN and FNUZ do not have the same encoding. Interpreting gfx942 FNUZ KV-cache
bytes as FN changes the represented values before sparse attention consumes
them. A direct MI300X kernel comparison measured:

| KV interpretation | Relative L2 error | Cosine similarity | Output norm ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Correct FNUZ | 0.0387 | 0.9993 | 0.999x |
| Current FN hardcode | 3.227 | 0.8748 | 4.066x |

The fix is to use `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` for E4M3 KV caches and treat
`torch.float8_e4m3fnuz` as FP8 in both sparse-attention wrappers.

### Fix validation

We hot-patched those two Python modules into the same container image and ran
the complete 1,319-sample GSM8K evaluation again. No image rebuild or other
server/configuration change was made.

| KV-cache configuration | Strict match | Flexible extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| FP8 KV, unpatched | 0.0099 | 0.0296 |
| FP8 KV, patched | 0.9575 | 0.9568 |
| BF16 KV reference | 0.9666 | 0.9659 |

The patched run completed all 1,319 requests with HTTP 200 and no server
errors. This recovers the expected accuracy while retaining FP8 KV cache.

### Reproduction

Start the server:

```bash
vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \
  --port 8888 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --block-size 128 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 9472 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --enforce-eager \
  --tool-call-parser minimax_m3 \
  --reasoning-parser minimax_m3 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

Send a deterministic request:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8888/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8",
    "temperature": 0,
    "max_tokens": 2048,
    "messages": [{
      "role": "user",
      "content": "Question: Janet'\''s ducks lay 16 eggs per day. She eats three for breakfast and uses four for muffins. She sells the remainder for $2 each. How much does she make per day? End your response with: #### [number]"
    }]
  }'
```

### Observed behavior

Expected answer: `#### 18`

Output with FP8 KV cache:

```text
Janet's ducks lay 16 eggs per day, so she will lay 16 x 7 = 112 eggs...
Therefore ... 112 - 21 = 91 eggs per day.
#### 91
Answer: 91
answer: 91
answer: 1 / 2 = 91
answer: 1 / 2 = 91
...
```

The response repeats until the generation limit.

Other examples from the same GSM8K run:

#### Example 2

Prompt:

```text
A robe takes 2 bolts of blue fiber and half that much white fiber.
How many bolts in total does it take?
```

Expected: `#### 3`

Observed:

```text
思维140 - 32 = 108 green bars.
After the loss, Corey had 108 + 32 = 140 green bars.
#### 140
Answer: 140 green apples.
Answer: 140 gold apple.
Answer: 140 gold apple.
...
```

#### Example 3

Prompt:

```text
James runs 3 sprints, 3 times a week, at 60 meters per sprint.
How many meters does he run per week?
```

Expected: `#### 540`

Observed:

```text
He runs 3 x 3 = 6 sprints per week.
He runs 6 x 60 = 360
#### 360
Question: 3/8 of his money to his father...
...
```

#### Example 4

Prompt:

```text
One glass costs $5, but every second glass costs 60% of the price.
How much do 16 glasses cost?
```

Expected: `#### 64`

Observed:

```text
<think>
...
3N + 6 = -147
N = -51
N + (N + 2) + (N + 4) = -147
N + (N + 2) + (N + 4) = -147
...
```

### Accuracy comparison

Full GSM8K, 5-shot, temperature 0:

| KV-cache configuration | Strict match | Flexible extract |
|---|---:|---:|
| `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` | 0.0099 | 0.0296 |
| Default (`kv_cache_dtype=auto`, BF16) | 0.9666 | 0.9659 |

Failed FP8-KV run:

https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/27482907707

Passing run after removing FP8 KV cache:

https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/27485772194

### Workaround

Remove:

```text
--kv-cache-dtype fp8
```

The engine then uses:

```text
dtype=torch.bfloat16
kv_cache_dtype=auto
```

No other server arguments were changed. The same image, model, attention
backend, parallelism, prompts, and evaluation configuration then pass GSM8K.

### Expected behavior

The MiniMax-M3 sparse-attention backend should interpret E4M3 KV-cache bytes
using the platform FP8 dtype. On gfx942, that is
`torch.float8_e4m3fnuz`; on platforms using standard E4M3, it remains
`torch.float8_e4m3fn`.

source.title: [Bug][FP8] ScaledMMLinearKernel rejects valid non-contiguous batched activations
source.body:
## Summary

`ScaledMMLinearKernel.apply_weights()` flattens activations with:

```python
x_2d = x.view(-1, x.shape[-1])
```

This assumes every valid higher-dimensional linear activation is view-compatible. That assumption is not part of the linear-layer input contract and fails for valid non-contiguous 3D sequence slices produced during batched inference. BF16 `F.linear` and other quantized linear paths accept the same input layout.

## Concrete trigger: batched Qwen-Image

Qwen-Image computes joint text/image attention and then splits the output into two streams:

```python
joint_hidden_states = joint_hidden_states.flatten(2, 3)
txt_attn_output = joint_hidden_states[:, :seq_len_txt, :]
img_attn_output = joint_hidden_states[:, seq_len_txt:, :]

img_attn_output = self.to_out(img_attn_output)
txt_attn_output = self.to_add_out(txt_attn_output)
```

For batch size greater than one, each slice is a valid non-contiguous tensor. Its logical shape is `[B, S, H]`, but the batch stride still includes the removed tokens from the other stream. It therefore cannot be represented as `[B * S, H]` by `view()` without copying.

A minimal representation of the layout is:

```python
full = torch.randn(2, 8, hidden_size, device="cuda")
x = full[:, 3:, :]
assert not x.is_contiguous()
x.view(-1, hidden_size)  # RuntimeError
x.reshape(-1, hidden_size)  # valid; copies only when required
```

This explains why the bug is usually hidden with batch size 1 and appears once multiple requests are executed in the same model forward.

## Historical path

- vLLM #9812 introduced `view(-1, K)` while adding support for FP8 linear inputs with more than two dimensions. It handled contiguous higher-dimensional inputs, but did not add coverage for non-contiguous 3D inputs.
- vLLM #21961 added non-contiguous FP8 quantization support. Its tests cover a 2D tensor with padded row stride, but the outer `ScaledMMLinearKernel.view()` still rejects non-view-compatible 3D sequence slices before quantization is reached.
- vllm-project/vllm-omni#830 added the Qwen-Image joint-attention output split shown above. This is a valid operation and works with BF16 linear layers.
- vllm-project/vllm-omni#2913 enabled ModelOpt FP8 diffusion checkpoints, exposing the sliced activation to the ScaledMM FP8 path. Its validation used client concurrency without actual multi-request batched model forwards, so the batch-size-dependent failure was not detected.
- vllm-project/vllm-omni#4155 added an Omni-side workaround that makes non-contiguous ScaledMM inputs contiguous before calling vLLM.

## Root cause

The deeper problem is not merely one incorrect use of `view()`. The ScaledMM linear abstraction does not clearly separate a **logical linear input** from the **physical 2D matrix required by the underlying GEMM**.

A linear layer logically accepts an activation shaped `[..., K]` and produces `[..., N]`. The leading dimensions may be arbitrary, and a valid linear input is not required to be contiguous or directly flattenable. In contrast, the underlying scaled GEMM consumes a physical 2D matrix shaped `[M, K]`.

The ScaledMM wrapper owns the boundary between these two contracts:

```text
valid logical activation [..., K]
        -> normalize/materialize when required
physical GEMM input [M, K]
        -> scaled GEMM
logical output [..., N]
```

Using `view(-1, K)` leaks the physical GEMM layout requirement through the linear-layer interface. It silently adds an undocumented requirement that all leading dimensions must be directly mergeable in the existing storage. Qwen-Image joint-attention slices violate that storage-layout assumption while remaining completely valid linear inputs.

This abstraction issue applies to both `ScaledMMLinearKernel` and `BlockScaledMMLinearKernel`, because both wrappers perform the same logical-to-physical conversion and currently use the same `view(-1, K)` assumption. Fixing only one would leave sibling ScaledMM linear implementations with inconsistent input contracts.

The producer of the non-contiguous activation is not doing anything invalid.

## Proposed fix and regression coverage

1. Replace `view(-1, x.shape[-1])` with `reshape(-1, x.shape[-1])` in `ScaledMMLinearKernel`, as proposed by #37620. `reshape()` remains zero-copy when the input is view-compatible and materializes a contiguous matrix only when required.
2. Add a kernel-level regression test using a non-contiguous 3D sequence slice and verify its output matches the same input after `.contiguous()`.
3. Audit `BlockScaledMMLinearKernel`, which currently contains the same `x.view(-1, x.shape[-1])` assumption.
4. Validate that contiguous inputs retain the existing fast path and that the Omni workaround can be removed after the fixed vLLM version is adopted.

## Current status

- Omni workaround: vllm-project/vllm-omni#4155
- Reproduced with batched Qwen-Image ModelOpt FP8 serving.

source.title: Vulkan/AMD RX 6900 XT: inference produces garbage tokens between b9370 and b9389
source.body:
### Summary

Inference produces garbage tokens (mixed-script gibberish across Korean / Japanese / Cyrillic / CJK) on AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT via Vulkan backend in build **b9389**. Rolling back to **b9370** with the **exact same model, args, and chat template** restores correct output. Model loads cleanly in both builds, so the regression is in inference, not loading.

### Environment

- **OS**: macOS 26.5 (build 25F71), Darwin x86_64
- **CPU**: 2x Intel(R) Xeon(R) E5-2680 v4 (16 threads used)
- **GPU**: AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT (16368 MiB) on Vulkan0; secondary RX 590 on Vulkan1 (not used: `--device Vulkan0 -sm none -mg 0`)
- **Vulkan loader**: libvulkan 1.4.350 (MoltenVK ICD, `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/usr/local/etc/vulkan/icd.d/MoltenVK_icd.json`)
- **glslc**: shaderc v2026.2, glslang 11.1.0-1366-gf0bd0257, SPIR-V target 1.0
- **Model**: `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-IQ4_XS.gguf` (Gemma 4 26B-A4B-it, IQ4_XS quant)
- **Chat template**: `models/templates/google-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it.jinja` (passed via `--chat-template-file`)

### llama.cpp versions tested

| Build | SHA | Result |
|-------|-----|--------|
| `b9370` | `aa50b2c2a` | OK |
| `b9389` | `30af6e2b9` | Garbage tokens |

### Build flags (identical for both)

```bash
cmake -B build-vulkan-bXXXX \
  -DGGML_VULKAN=ON \
  -DGGML_BLAS=ON -DGGML_BLAS_VENDOR=Apple \
  -DGGML_ACCELERATE=ON \
  -DGGML_CUDA=OFF -DGGML_HIP=OFF -DGGML_METAL=OFF \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build-vulkan-bXXXX --target llama-server -j16
```

The b9389 configure logs `GL_NV_cooperative_matrix_decode_vector not supported by glslc`, so that path is disabled. `GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix`, `GL_NV_cooperative_matrix2`, `GL_EXT_integer_dot_product`, `GL_EXT_bfloat16` are compiled in.

### Reproduction

Launch command (identical between the two builds, only `bXXXX` changes):

```bash
./build-vulkan-bXXXX/bin/llama-server \
  -m gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-IQ4_XS.gguf \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \
  -c 16384 -t 16 -tb 16 -ngl all \
  --device Vulkan0 -sm none -mg 0 --op-offload --kv-offload --kv-unified \
  --mlock -fa on -rea off -ctk q4_0 -ctv q8_0 --no-warmup -np 1 \
  --jinja --chat-template-file models/templates/google-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it.jinja
```

Then send a trivial chat request:

```bash
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"what is your current working folder?"}]}'
```

### Expected (b9370)

A coherent natural-language reply.

### Actual (b9389)

Server returns HTTP 500 with:

```
Failed to parse input at pos 13: -D_0 (Saric até... <multi-script gibberish>
```

The 500 is the server's tool-call parser rejecting the model output, but the underlying issue is the model emitting non-coherent token streams. The same model loaded successfully (warnings about `<|tool_response>` and `</s>` token control types appear identically in both builds and are unrelated).

### Candidate commits in the range

Only 3 Vulkan commits separate b9370 and b9389:

- `48e7078e` — vulkan: fast path for walsh-hadamard transform (#23687) — **prime suspect**, the PR itself disables this path on Intel due to a segfault, may have a latent issue on AMD RDNA2
- `7c48fb81` — vulkan: fix wrong index variable in inner loop (#23665)
- `91eb8f4f` — vulkan: Fix memory logger unsafe iterator access (#23667) — least likely to affect inference output

Happy to bisect these three on request and report which exact commit introduces the regression.

### Workaround

Staying on b9370.

source.title: Eval bug: GLM 5.x crashes/gibberish with high ubatch and long prompts
source.body:
### Name and Version

$ ./build/bin/llama-server --version
version: 9311 (11ee2ddec)
built with IntelLLVM 2026.0.0 for Linux x86_64

But also happens with current clean upstream master

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA, CPU, SYCL, Vulkan

### Hardware

- Threadripper, 512GB RAM.
- RTX Pro 6000 WS Blackwell (96GB)
- RTX 3090 (24GB)
- Intel B60 (24GB)

### Models

GLM 5.1

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

This issue has been around for months but I've never managed to track it down.
GLM 5.x (tested 5.1 but should apply to at least 5.0 as well) will crash when fed a very long context cold.
If this context naturally builds up/gets added in pieces, no problem. It only crashes when receiving ~120k+ new tokens in one go.

I have this tracked down and "solved" on my end, but it is AI slop I don't understand and thus in no state for me to PR.

Codex describes the identified cause as:

> GLM 5.1 currently runs through a dense MLA attention path instead of its intended GLM-DSA sparse/indexer attention. On cold very-large prefill, the dense KQ mask scales with KV length * microbatch size and can exceed backend/indexing limits, causing downstream invalid results/crashes; hot long-context generation avoids this because each step has a tiny microbatch.

And its applied workaround:

> Added a GLM-DSA-specific cap on prefill n_ubatch so the dense fallback KQ mask stays below the oversized-mask/backend-indexing danger zone.
> I used a signed 32-bit byte-offset ceiling: keep the dense KQ mask under INT32_MAX bytes, about 2  GiB.
> Since the mask is float, that means roughly: 
> `n_kv * n_ubatch < INT32_MAX / sizeof(float)`
> or about 536M mask elements. 

Which in practice means it dynamically scales down ubatch per batch as needed on long prompts. Comes at a speed penalty by virtue of smaller ubatches but fully prevents the problem for me.


Launch command:
```
./build/bin/llama-server -m /mnt/sda1/models/GLM-5.1-GGUF/GLM-5.1-UD-Q4_K_XL-00001-of-00011.gguf --keep -1 --offline --no-context-shift --flash-attn on --jinja --temp 1 --kv-unified --backend-sampling --parallel 1 --fit off --threads 64 -dev CUDA0,CUDA1,Vulkan1 --tensor-split 1,0,0 --n-gpu-layers 9999 -ot (?:^|\.)blk\.(?:[8-9])\..*ffn_(gate|up|down)_exps\.=CUDA1,(?:^|\.)blk\.(?:1[0-1])\..*ffn_(gate|up|down)_exps\.=Vulkan1,(?:^|\.)blk\.(?:(?:1[2-9]|2[0-9]|3[0-9]|4[0-9]|5[0-9]|6[0-9]|7[0-8]))\..*ffn_(gate|up|down)_exps\.=CPU --batch-size 16384 --ubatch-size 16384 --port 8124
```


Notably, it only crashes with backend sampling enabled. Without, it slowly outputs endless question marks instead.

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

### Relevant log output

<details>
<summary>Logs</summary>
Unfortunately none at hand. But the trace is fairly useless anyway, just leads to backend sampling producing/consuming an invalid token ID and crashing. Nothing without backend sampling.

source.title: Vulkan: turbo3 KV produces garbage output, turbo4/SET_ROWS crashes, MTP crashes on AMD RDNA 3.5 (TurboQuant fork)
source.body:
## Bug Report: Vulkan backend issues on AMD RDNA 3.5 (Radeon 8060S)

### Environment
- **OS**: Windows 11 (10.0.26200), x64
- **GPU**: AMD Radeon 8060S (RDNA 3.5, gfx1151)
- **Build**: VS 2022 MSVC, CMake 4.3.2, Ninja
- **Branch**: feature/turboquant-kv-cache (commit 2e81dc5)
- **Vulkan SDK**: 1.4.341.1
- **Model**: Gemma-4-26B-A4B-It Q4_K_XL (Unsloth Dynamic Quant, 15.9 GB GGUF)
- **GPU memory**: 96 GB VRAM (UMA/shared)

### Build config
Two builds tested:
1. **Without coopmat2**: `-DGGML_VULKAN=ON -DGGML_VULKAN_USE_COOPMAT2=OFF`
2. **With coopmat2**: `-DGGML_VULKAN=ON -DGGML_VULKAN_USE_COOPMAT2=ON`

### Bug 1: turbo3 KV cache produces garbage output on SWA models

**Status**: Confirmed on both builds (with and without coopmat2)

Launch command:
```bash
llama-server -m gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -c 131072 --no-mmap -fa on \
  -ctk turbo3 -ctv turbo3 --jinja \
  --port 8087 --parallel 1 -ub 512 --host 0.0.0.0
```

**Expected**: Valid text output (like with `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0`)
**Actual**: Complete gibberish output — random characters, mixed scripts, no coherent text:
```json
{"content": "- траDetہ道ingmetic لط Procmem ownสูOS way으로ly Junk way로로나 way-로로로로 way-eeitononfeit way way than으로ly than than own way own than own than owntole pot than-eGraen"}
```

**KV cache info**:
- Non-SWA: 131072 cells, 5 layers, K(turbo3): 250 MiB, V(turbo3): 250 MiB = 500 MiB total
- SWA: 1536 cells, 25 layers, K(turbo3): 29.30 MiB, V(turbo3): 29.30 MiB = 58.59 MiB total
- Total KV: ~559 MiB (vs ~1520 MiB with q8_0 — 2.7x compression reported)

**Comparison**: Same model with `-ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0` produces valid output at 50.2 t/s.

**Note**: Gemma 4 uses Sliding Window Attention (SWA) with a hybrid pattern (alternating 5 SWA layers + 1 non-SWA layer). This may be relevant to the turbo3 Vulkan shader bug.

### Bug 2: turbo4 KV cache crashes on startup

**Status**: Confirmed on both builds

Launch command:
```bash
llama-server -m gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -c 131072 --no-mmap -fa on \
  -ctk turbo4 -ctv turbo4 --jinja \
  --port 8087 --parallel 1 -ub 512 --host 0.0.0.0
```

**Error**:
```
ggml-backend.cpp:898: pre-allocated tensor (cache_k_l0 (view)) in a buffer (Vulkan0) that cannot run the operation (SET_ROWS)
```

This confirms the README table: Vulkan SET_ROWS is required for turbo4 KV but not yet implemented/functioning.

### Bug 3: MTP speculative decoding crashes after first inference

**Status**: Confirmed on both builds (with and without coopmat2)

Launch command:
```bash
llama-server -m gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --mtp-head gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-assistant-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --spec-type mtp --draft-block-size 3 \
  -ngl 99 -ngld 99 -c 131072 --no-mmap -fa on \
  -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --jinja \
  --port 8087 --parallel 1 -ub 512 --host 0.0.0.0
```

**Behavior**: Server loads successfully, MTP assistant loaded and initialized. On first inference request, the server process crashes (exits). No error message — just termination.

**MTP assistant model**: `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-assistant-Q4_K_M.gguf` (325 MB, from AtomicChat HuggingFace collection)

**KV cache info with MTP**:
- Non-SWA: 131072 cells, 5 layers, K(q8_0): 680 MiB, V(q8_0): 680 MiB = 1360 MiB
- SWA: 1536 cells, 25 layers, K(q8_0): 79.69 MiB, V(q8_0): 79.69 MiB = 159.38 MiB
- Assistant: 419.71M params, 4 layers, GPU: 82 MiB + CPU: 213 MiB

### Additional context

- **Without coopmat2**: regular inference speed was 49.8 t/s (Gemma 4 26B-A4B Q4_K_XL, Vulkan)
- **With coopmat2**: regular inference speed dropped to ~49 t/s — coopmat2 adds overhead on RDNA 3.5 without real coopmat2 hardware support
- On AMD RDNA 3.5 (Radeon 8060S), KHR_cooperative_matrix (v1) is supported but NV_cooperative_matrix2 (coopmat2) is NOT. Coopmat2 shaders add software overhead.
- **ZLUDA v6 + TheRock SDK (ROCm 7.13)** are installed but Vulkan is the only functional backend for this GPU on Windows

### Working configuration (baseline)

```bash
llama-server -m gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -c 131072 --no-mmap -fa on \
  -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --jinja \
  --port 8087 --parallel 1 -ub 512 --host 0.0.0.0
```
Result: **50.2 t/s decode, 223 t/s prompt, valid output** ✅

### Summary

| Feature | Vulkan Status | AMD RDNA 3.5 |
|---------|--------------|---------------|
| Base inference (q8_0 KV) | ✅ Works | 50.2 t/s |
| turbo3 KV | ❌ Garbage output | SWA shader bug |
| turbo4 KV | ❌ Crash | SET_ROWS not supported |
| MTP spec decoding | ❌ Crash after inference | Vulkan MTP bug |
| TQ4_1S weights | ⚠️ Not tested | Likely needs SET_ROWS |

The Vulkan turbo3 KV shader appears to produce incorrect WHT rotation or attention computation for models with Sliding Window Attention (Gemma 4 uses a hybrid SWA pattern). The MTP crash suggests the Vulkan graph doesn't handle the MTP speculative decode path correctly on this hardware.

source.title: Eval bug: NextN (PR #22673) Vulkan path produces ~0.7% accept rate + garbled output on RDNA3+RADV, while HIP/ROCm works correctly (81%)
source.body:
## Context

This is a finding from testing PR #22673 (NextN/MTP support) as bundled in the downstream fork [`AtomicBot-ai/atomic-llama-cpp-turboquant`](https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-llama-cpp-turboquant) at HEAD `0a635dc` (PR #14 in that fork rebases on top of this PR). The fork's issue tracker is disabled, so I'm cross-posting here since the NextN implementation under review is the relevant venue. cc @am17an

Headline: **NextN draft on the Vulkan backend produces ~0.7% acceptance and garbled output on RDNA3+RADV, while the HIP/ROCm backend on the same hardware achieves 81% acceptance + the expected +35.7% tg gain** (matching the M4 Max +36% extrapolation in the fork's NEXTN.md). The bug appears localized to the Vulkan execution of the NextN draft graph; the rest of the Vulkan backend works correctly for this model when `--spec-type` is omitted.

## Name and Version

```
$ ~/llm/bin-atomic/llama-server --version
version: 1 (0a635dc)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64
```

build_info from server log: `b1-0a635dc`

## Operating systems

- Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8.0-111-generic)

## GGML backends

- **Vulkan** (broken)
- **HIP** (works — reference comparison in this report)

## Hardware

- 2x AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (RDNA3, gfx1100)
- Mesa 25.2.8 (RADV NAVI31)
- Vulkan 1.3.275 headers (libvulkan.so.1.3.275)
- ROCm 6.4.0 (hipcc, gfx1100)
- AMD Ryzen 9 7900 (12 cores) + 64 GB DDR5

## Models

- `AtomicChat/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UDT-MTP-GGUF` — `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UDT-Q4_K_XL_MTP.gguf`
- HF lfs oid: `56aeaf6a72cb2a538a7356941fe2983cff7c5efe91cac866336f33d144913cd8`
- Total size: 22,187,497,792 B (≈20.7 GiB)
- Architecture: `qwen35moe`, `nextn_predict_layers=1`, block_count=41 (40 main + 1 NextN)
- HF: https://huggingface.co/AtomicChat/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UDT-MTP-GGUF
- Also reproduced with `unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-GGUF` — `UD-Q4_K_M` (sha256 `0b21525e972670ed59e1812e170b27c26355381f0656ecc4e25617ece7dac58b`, 22.66 GB) to rule out the UDT-mask hypothesis.

## Problem description & steps to reproduce

### Summary

With the same UDT GGUF and same `--spec-type nextn` invocation pattern (shared-model path, target == draft), the **Vulkan backend** produces a NextN draft acceptance rate of ~0.7% and garbled multilingual token output, while the **HIP/ROCm backend** on the same hardware produces 81% acceptance with coherent output and the expected +36% throughput uplift over the NextN-OFF baseline.

NextN initialization succeeds on both backends (`NextN draft: shared-model path (target qwen35moe, no second mmap; nextn_predict_layers=1)` followed by `NextN draft context registered` and `speculative decoding context initialized`). The difference is in the per-token draft prediction signal.

### Reproduction — Vulkan (broken)

Build:

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/AtomicBot-ai/atomic-llama-cpp-turboquant
cd atomic-llama-cpp-turboquant
cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DGGML_VULKAN=ON \
  -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_TOOLS=ON
cmake --build build --config Release -j 8 -- llama-server
```

Run:

```bash
./build/bin/llama-server \
  --model /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UDT-Q4_K_XL_MTP.gguf \
  --model-draft /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UDT-Q4_K_XL_MTP.gguf \
  --spec-type nextn --draft-max 2 --draft-min 1 \
  -c 8192 -ngl 99 -ngld 99 -fa on \
  -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -ctkd q8_0 -ctvd q8_0 \
  --device Vulkan0 --device-draft Vulkan0 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8089 \
  --parallel 1 -np 1 --cont-batching \
  --no-mmap --mlock \
  --temp 0.6 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 20 --min-p 0 \
  --jinja --log-timestamps --log-prefix --metrics --slots
```

Send a chat completion:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8089/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "model":"qwen3.6",
  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Explain in two sentences what speculative decoding is."}],
  "max_tokens":200,"temperature":0.6
}'
```

Observed (Vulkan, `--draft-max 2`):

```
draft acceptance rate = 0.00673 (    2 accepted /   297 generated)
statistics nextn: #calls(b,g,a) = 1 296 1, #gen drafts = 296, #acc drafts = 1, #gen tokens = 297, #acc tokens = 2,
  dur(b,g,a) = 116.794, 799.380, 0.003 ms
HTTP 500: Failed to parse input at pos 514: safezoneش beh again álla  Ristorante **:** dicip ...
  [multilingual garbled token soup, ~290 more tokens of similar gibberish]
```

Observed (Vulkan, `--draft-max 1`) — same pattern, rules out chain-length:

```
draft acceptance rate = 0.00680 (    1 accepted /   147 generated)
statistics nextn: #calls(b,g,a) = 1 147 1, #gen drafts = 147, #acc drafts = 1, #gen tokens = 147, #acc tokens = 1
HTTP 500: Failed to parse input at pos 22: <think>\nHere's a cogsayicer Potr}@ACHINEAsyncResulthazi spasuceToPoint xákti...
```

### Reproduction — HIP (works, reference)

Build:

```bash
export PATH=/opt/rocm/bin:$PATH
cmake -B build-hip -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGGML_HIP_ROCWMMA_FATTN=ON \
  -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1100 \
  -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/opt/rocm/llvm/bin/clang++ \
  -DLLAMA_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_EXAMPLES=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_TOOLS=ON
cmake --build build-hip --config Release -j 8 -- llama-server
```

Run (same args except `--device ROCm0 --device-draft ROCm0`):

```bash
./build-hip/bin/llama-server \
  --model /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UDT-Q4_K_XL_MTP.gguf \
  --model-draft /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UDT-Q4_K_XL_MTP.gguf \
  --spec-type nextn --draft-max 2 --draft-min 1 \
  -c 8192 -ngl 99 -ngld 99 -fa on \
  -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -ctkd q8_0 -ctvd q8_0 \
  --device ROCm0 --device-draft ROCm0 \
  ...
```

Observed (HIP, `--draft-max 2`) — correct behavior:

```
draft acceptance rate = 0.81212 (  134 accepted /   165 generated)
statistics nextn: #calls(b,g,a) = 1 164 133, #gen drafts = 164, #acc drafts = 1, #gen tokens = 165, #acc tokens = 134,
  dur(b,g,a) = 66.062, 340.060, 0.259 ms
HTTP 200: {"choices":[{"finish_reason":"length", ..., "reasoning_content":"Here's a thinking process: ..."}],
  "timings":{"predicted_n":300,"predicted_ms":2910.654,"predicted_per_second":103.07, ...}}
```

### Summary table

| Backend | Build dir | Model | NextN | tg t/s | Accept rate | Output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vulkan | `build/` | UDT Q4_K_XL | OFF | 118.6 | n/a | coherent |
| Vulkan | `build/` | UDT Q4_K_XL | ON (draft-max 2) | n/a (500) | **0.67%** (2/297) | garbled |
| Vulkan | `build/` | UDT Q4_K_XL | ON (draft-max 1) | n/a (500) | **0.68%** (1/147) | garbled |
| Vulkan | `build/` (with sync patch) | UDT Q4_K_XL | ON (draft-max 2) | n/a (500) | **1.01%** (3/296) | garbled |
| Vulkan | `build/` (`GGML_VK_DISABLE_ASYNC=1`) | UDT Q4_K_XL | ON (draft-max 2) | n/a (500) | **0.67%** (2/297) | garbled |
| Vulkan | `build/` | unsloth UD-Q4_K_M | ON (draft-max 2) | n/a (500) | **1.01%** (2/197) | garbled |
| HIP | `build-hip/` | UDT Q4_K_XL | OFF | 76.0 | n/a | coherent |
| HIP | `build-hip/` | UDT Q4_K_XL | ON (draft-max 2) | **103.1** | **81.21%** (134/165) | **coherent, +35.7% vs OFF** |

The +35.7% HIP gain matches the M4 Max +36% extrapolation in README §0 / NEXTN.md §7, confirming the NextN implementation itself is correct end-to-end — the bug is localized to the Vulkan backend's NextN draft execution path. The model GGUF (UDT mask vs upstream unsloth UD) does not matter — both reproduce identically on Vulkan.

### Hypotheses (in order of likelihood)

Localizing to the Vulkan backend, the most likely culprits are:

- **H1 (most likely after experiment)**: Vulkan kernels for the NextN draft graph (`llm_build_qwen35moe_nextn` and adjacent kernels for the NextN-specific tensors `model.layers[n_main + i].nextn.*`) produce numerically incorrect outputs on RADV, so the draft logits are uncorrelated with the target's. The fact that we get ~0.67-0.68% rather than uniform-random (1/152K vocab ≈ 6.5e-6) suggests *some* correlated signal but degraded — possibly only a subset of NextN tensors are mis-computed on Vulkan.
- **H2 (RULED OUT by experiment)**: `t_h_pre_norm` extraction or the `embd_pre_norm` CPU buffer transfer being async-racey on Vulkan. See "Patch attempt" below — explicit `ggml_backend_sched_synchronize(sched.get())` after the get_async at `src/llama-context.cpp:1666` and `:2111` did not fix the bug; `GGML_VK_DISABLE_ASYNC=1` (which routes all transfers through synchronous path) also did not fix it. Therefore the bug is in actual GPU compute, not buffer transfer / sync.
- **H3**: `cparams.nextn_draft = true` + `kv_only_nextn = true` override in `llama_context` ctor is mis-honored on Vulkan, leaving the draft KV cache uninitialized/wrong-sized.

H1 is most consistent with "draft engages, accept very low" plus "target output is also garbled" — if the Vulkan-computed `t_h_pre_norm` tensor (or any NextN-graph tensor) has numerically wrong values, both the draft predictions and the target's sampled tokens (which read back from the same buffer) would suffer.

### Patch attempt (ruled out async transfer race)

Diff applied (then reverted) for the experiment:

```diff
--- a/src/llama-context.cpp
+++ b/src/llama-context.cpp
@@ -1666,6 +1666,8 @@
         ggml_backend_tensor_get_async(backend_h, t_h_pre_norm, embd_pre_norm.data, 0, n_tokens * n_embd_h * sizeof(float));
+        ggml_backend_sched_synchronize(sched.get());
     }
@@ -2111,6 +2113,8 @@
                 ggml_backend_tensor_get_async(backend_h, t_h_pre_norm, embd_h_out, 0, n_outputs * n_embd_h * sizeof(float));
+                ggml_backend_sched_synchronize(sched.get());
             }
```

Result with patch (Vulkan, draft-max 2): `accept rate = 0.01014 (3/296)`. Marginally different from unpatched 0.67% but still essentially random — output still garbled, HTTP 500.

Result with `GGML_VK_DISABLE_ASYNC=1` env var (which sets `vk_backend->iface.get_tensor_async = nullptr` and routes through sync `get_tensor`): `accept rate = 0.00673 (2/297)` — identical to unpatched. Total smoke time 36 s (vs 4 s with async), confirming the env var works as expected (slower sync transfers). Same garbled output, same HTTP 500.

Both experiments rule out the buffer-transfer race hypothesis. The bug must be in the actual Vulkan compute graph for NextN-related tensors.

### Notes

- The Vulkan backend itself is **not broken in general** — the same build produces correct, fast inference (118.6 t/s) when `--spec-type` is omitted on the same GGUF + same device. Only the NextN draft path is affected.
- `--draft-max 1` reproduces the failure with identical accept rate (0.68%), confirming the chain length is not the cause.
- Both AtomicChat UDT and the upstream `unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-GGUF` reproduce identically on Vulkan, so the UDT mask (NextN pinned to Q8_0, attn Q/K lifted to Q6_K) is not the cause.
- Happy to provide full server logs, GGUF metadata dump, or run additional measurements you want. GLSL extension presence at build time: `GL_KHR_cooperative_matrix supported`, `GL_NV_cooperative_matrix2 not supported`, `GL_EXT_integer_dot_product not supported`, `GL_EXT_bfloat16 not supported`.

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

### Command line

```shell

    -m ~/models/bartowski/Qwen_Qwen3-14B-GGUF/Qwen_Qwen3-14B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
    -ngl 99 \
    -fa 0,1
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

It used to be that the metal backend was much slower than the Vulkan backend on Intel Macs. I did some testing with with the latest versions and I'm happy to report that the metal backend is now faster than the Vulkan backend on my Intel Mac. Prompt processing is significantly faster with metal and token output is slightly faster. This is all with flash attention disabled.

With flash attention enabled, prompt processing is unaffected but token output speed is super slow:

source.body:
### Name and Version

```
$llama-cli --version

```


### Operating systems

### GGML backends

Vulkan

### Hardware

Snapdragon 8Gen2, Adreno 740 GPU

### Models

Qwen3.5 2B Q4_K, Q2_K

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

### Situation
I am working with an "unusual" setup (Android 15). I'm looking to either fix performance regressions or fix output corruption in Qwen3.5.

* **Background:** I previously used [chraac's llama.cpp fork](https://github.com/chraac/llama.cpp) for Hexagon backend support.

* **Steps to reproduce:**

    * **Hexagon Backend:** 
     - wanted Qwen 3.5 support.
     - rebased the fork onto the full qwen35 support PR [#19468](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/19468).
     - Qwen 3.5 2B (Q2_K_S) successfully processed a "hey" input once, but subsequently I was unable to reproduce this behavior and it was outputting gibberish at ~1-3 tk/s. Other models function correctly, though Hexagon remains just a slow backend.
     - Decided to try vulkan instead.
 

    * **Vulkan (Rebase):**
    * also produced gibberish (not chinese) but at a much higher rate of 20–30 tk/s, which is also true for other models.
    - llama-cli with -ngl 0 has correct output, and other models (LFM2.5, llama3.2, qwen2.5) run correctly.
    - git clone latest master (March 13th, 2026).

    * **Vulkan (Master - March 13, 2026):** 
    - clean build from the latest master validated that Qwen 3.5 output is correct. However, generation speed has regressed to 6–10 tk/s—slower than CPU performance and significantly worse than my custom build. Reading is also a lot worse.
  
    * **Back to Rebase branch:**
    - traced and merged dependency commits in `qwen35.cpp` up to `add GATED_DELTA_NET op (#19504)`, including the Vulkan Gated Delta Net commit.
    - still has output corruption.
   
#### Debugging 
    * Verified that `llama-cli` with `-ngl 0` (CPU only) produces correct output for Qwen3.5 in all builds after rebase.
    * Confirmed that other models across various quantizations run correctly on the custom build.
    * Attempted common fixes from similar Mac/Multi-GPU issues (e.g., `ggml f16` flags, disabling `flash_attn`), but with no improvement to the output.

**Summary**
While the Qwen3.5 corrupted output issue with Vulkan backend appears resolved in latest master (at least on Adreno GPUs), there's a significant performance regression compared to my custom rebase. Does anyone know which specific commits—beyond the ones I’ve cited—actually fixed the Qwen 3.5 corrupted generation on the Vulkan backend?
The performance regression in master isn't worth at all to run it.

I am hesitant to open a new issue, if this is a known duplicate do point me at the right one. 
I found similar issues opened by multi-gpu and Mac users, but nothing this specific for me to polute in those issues.

source.body:
### Name and Version

$ ./llama-server --version
version: 8363 (ceef6b523)
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

RTX 3090 24GB (Ampere, SM 8.6)

### Models

GLM-4.7-Flash (deepseek2 architecture), Q4_K_M quantization.
tested three separate GGUF providers to rule out conversion issues:
- https://huggingface.co/bartowski/zai-org_GLM-4.7-Flash-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- https://huggingface.co/unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-GGUF (Q4_K_M)
- https://huggingface.co/ngxson/GLM-4.7-Flash-GGUF (Q4_K_M)

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

GLM-4.7-Flash produces a static logit distribution on CUDA. he same output tokens regardless of input or position. CPU inference on the same GGUF returns correct results. the key diagnostic seems to be that with `temperature=0` and `logprobs=true`, every single position returns the same top-3 tokens:
```
pos 1: selected=id:30 '?'  top: [(103257,'有时候'), (103248,'成为了'), (103249,'武器')]
pos 2: selected=id:30 '?'  top: [(103257,'有时候'), (103248,'成为了'), (103249,'武器')]
pos 3: selected=id:30 '?'  top: [(103257,'有时候'), (103248,'成为了'), (103249,'武器')]
```
nothing about the input appears to change the output distribution.

**to reproduce:**

```bash
# GPU -- broken output
llama-server -m GLM-4.7-Flash-Q4_K_M.gguf --port 8012 \
  --ctx-size 4096 --n-gpu-layers 99 --flash-attn off

curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8012/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 7 times 13?"}],"max_tokens":10,"temperature":0,"logprobs":true,"top_logprobs":3}'
# -> "??????????" every time, static top_logprobs

# CPU -- correct output
llama-server -m GLM-4.7-Flash-Q4_K_M.gguf --port 8012 \
  --ctx-size 4096 --n-gpu-layers 0

# same curl -> "91"
```

things tried: 
- flash attention: tested with `--flash-attn off`, same result
- gating function: startup confirms `expert_gating_func = sigmoid` (correct for GLM)
- sampling: tested temp 0, min-p 0.01, repeat-penalty 1.0
- model file: three independent GGUF sources all reproduce
- GPU hardware: Qwen3-30B-A3B (standard MoE, not deepseek2) runs perfectly at 152 t/s on the same card
- quantization: different quants produce different garbage tokens but the same static-logit pattern

the model generates tokens at ~96 t/s on GPU (fast, but wrong). prompt eval looks normal. the compute graph runs, it just produces constant logits.

different GGUF providers produce different degenerate tokens (bartowski: `?`, unsloth: `{n;;`, ollama blob: multilingual gibberish)

### First Bad Commit

haven't been able to bisect this fully. tested b8323 and b8363, both broken. the model might have never worked correctly on CUDA Ampere via llama-server -- I was previously running it through Ollama which may have been silently falling back to CPU.

### Relevant log output

<details>

source.title: SYCL: Qwen3.5 produces gibberish and crashes on Intel Arc A770
source.body:
I am trying to run [Jackrong/Qwen3.5-9B-Claude-4.6-Opus-Reasoning-Distilled-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/Jackrong/Qwen3.5-9B-Claude-4.6-Opus-Reasoning-Distilled-GGUF) (Q4_K_M) on an Intel Arc A770 using the SYCL backend.

**On the latest release (b8277),** the model fails to start with `llama-server` unless Flash Attention is explicitly disabled (`-fa 0`). Without this flag, slot initialization hangs indefinitely.

**After building from master** (which includes the fix from #20283), the situation improves. The model starts and produces some good answers. However, without that merged PR, the output is pure gibberish and repetition loops — for example, endlessly repeating "The question asks: Let me analyze this question carefully."

**The remaining problem:** Even with the latest master build and `-fa 0`, the server becomes unstable after a few successful responses. It starts producing gibberish again — sometimes unicode garbage mixed with random multilingual text fragments, returning HTTP 500 errors. Once this happens, subsequent requests also fail until the server is restarted.

The server log shows:
```
ched_reserve: reserving ...
sched_reserve: Flash Attention was auto, set to enabled
sched_reserve: layer 0 is assigned to device SYCL0 but the fused Gated Delta Net tensor is assigned to device CPU (usually due to missing support)
sched_reserve: fused Gated Delta Net not supported, set to disabled
```

This suggests the fused Gated Delta Net kernel is not implemented for the SYCL backend, and the fallback path is unreliable.

Related issue: #20321

**Hardware:** Intel Arc A770 16GB
**OS:** Linux (Ubuntu)
**Backend:** SYCL

### Name and Version

commit 0988accf824e817d0e3db55c05f5f2954fbfe505

### GGML backends

SYCL

### Hardware

Intel Arc A770 
Intel Arc A380

### Models

unsloth Qwen3.5 9b q8
unsloth Qwen3.5 2b q8

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Title: Second interaction hangs / generates gibberish after commit 0988acc ([SYCL] Add Q8_0 reorder optimization)

Description
After commit 0988accf824e817d0e3db55c05f5f2954fbfe505 ([SYCL] Add Q8_0 reorder optimization), I see a performance improvement for the first completion (≈17 t/s → ≈25 t/s) but the second interaction hangs in an endless loop or produces gibberish output.

Reproduction steps
1. Build from tip including commit 0988accf824e.
2. Run either:
   - cli mode, or
   - server mode
3. Use model: qwen3.5 9b q8_0 on Intel Arc A770 (16 GB) and qwen3.5 2b q8_0 on Intel Arc A380 (6 GB).
4. Request a completion once — first completion returns correctly and with improved throughput.
5. Make a second interaction (another prompt / follow-up completion). The second interaction either:
   - enters an endless loop (nothing generated), or
   - generates gibberish output.

What I tested / observed
- i test older commits with rebuilding all, commit (ggml web gpu) works as intended
- First completion works correctly and is faster (17 t/s → 25 t/s).
- Second interaction consistently fails (endless loop or gibberish).
- Reproduced in both cli and server modes.
- Tested with "thinking on" and "thinking off".
- Collected logs for all combinations; I cleaned logs to reduce the endless-loop spam and marked the point where the endless loop occurs.
- Behavior observed on two GPU configurations:
  - Intel Arc A770 (16 GB), model qwen3.5 9b q8_0
  - Intel Arc A380 (6 GB), model qwen3.5 2b q8_0

Attached logs
- Cleaned logs for:
  - cli thinking on
  - cli thinking off
  - server thinking on
  - server thinking off
- In each log I marked where the endless loop begins.

Expected behavior
- Second and subsequent interactions should behave the same as the first: produce coherent output and not hang.

Actual behavior
- Second interaction either loops forever (no output produced) or emits gibberish tokens.

Notes / hypotheses
- The regression started with commit 0988accf824e (SYCL Q8_0 reorder optimization).
- The optimization likely changes the memory layout or reorders quantized data for Q8_0. Possible issues:
  - buffer/stride mismatch on subsequent inference calls,
  - state (KV cache or related buffers) not being reset or handled correctly after the first run,
  - thread-safety or synchronization problem in SYCL kernel(s) during repeated runs,
  - an indexing or pointer error when reusing reordered buffers for a second inference,
  - an uninitialized memory path exposed only on the second run.
- Problem reproduces on two different Arc GPUs and both 2b/9b Q8_0 models, suggesting the problem is implementation-level rather than model-specific.

What I’ve tried
- Running cli and server variants.
- Toggling thinking on/off.
- Captured and cleaned logs; marked the loop point.
- Compared first vs second run behavior to confirm regression point is after commit 0988accf8.

Request / help wanted
- Guidance on how to debug SYCL Q8_0 reorder interactions and where to look for root cause.
- If maintainers can point to likely files/functions affected by the reorder (quantization/reorder kernels, buffer init, KV cache handling, inference loop, or reuse of device buffers), that would help.
- If you can review the attached cleaned logs and point out where the kernel, synchronization, or buffer misuse is visible, I’m happy to try fixes and open a PR.
- Any hints about typical pitfalls in SYCL device buffer reuse, kernel ordering, or memory lifetime that cause first-run OK but second-run failure.

Relevant info
- Commit: 0988accf824e817d0e3db55c05f5f2954fbfe505
- Hardware:
  - Intel Arc A770, 16 GB
  - Intel Arc A380, 6 GB
- Models:
  - qwen3.5 9b q8_0
  - qwen3.5 2b q8_0
- Logs: (attached cleaned logs covering cli/server × thinking on/off; loop points marked)

Suggested immediate debugging steps I can run if you point me to the right area
- Add validation checks after reorder kernels to confirm data layout/strides match expectations.
- Zero or reinitialize KV cache and device buffers between runs to check if reuse is the issue.
- Run with SYCL debug/env options to enable sync or stricter validation, if available.
- Insert checksums/hash of reordered buffers after the first and before the second run to detect corruption.
- Add debug prints in the inference loop to locate where output generation stalls.

If helpful, I can attach the cleaned logs here and run any suggested debug builds or tests. I'm new to contributing; any pointers about which files to inspect first would be appreciated.

0988accf824e817d0e3db55c05f5f2954fbfe505

source.title: Misc. bug: dual-GPU inference produces gibberish on asymmetric PCIe topology, while single-GPU works and older build b7728 works correctly
source.body:
### NOTE about related issue

I am aware of issue #20052. I do not cite it as proof of a llama.cpp bug, only as a similar symptom on a comparable asymmetric non-P2P topology. In that case, the final conclusion was hardware-induced corruption via a marginal riser cable, not a llama.cpp software defect.

### Summary

I am seeing a regression in dual-GPU inference on llama.cpp.

On the same machine, with the same GPUs, same model, and same physical topology:

- older build `b7728` works correctly on 2 GPUs
- newer build `b8783-e21cdc11a` produces gibberish or hangs/stalls during generation on 2 GPUs
- single-GPU works on both builds

This looks like a regression in the multi-GPU execution path between `b7728` and `b8783`.

### Hardware

- Host OS: Debian Linux
- GPUs:
  - 2 x NVIDIA RTX 4000 SFF Ada Generation
  - compute capability 8.9
  - 20 GB VRAM each
- Driver:
  - NVIDIA driver 595.58.03
- PCIe topology:
  - GPU0 in motherboard x16 slot
  - GPU1 connected through a riser in an x4 slot

Important detail: this asymmetric topology is not inherently broken, because `b7728` works correctly on 2 GPUs on the exact same machine and same setup.

### Model

- `ggml-org/gpt-oss-20b-GGUF`
- file: `gpt-oss-20b-mxfp4.gguf`

### What works

#### 1) Old build, single GPU

`b7728` works correctly on 1 GPU.

Observed generation speed:

- about 85 tok/s

#### 2) Old build, dual GPU

`b7728` also works correctly on 2 GPUs on the same machine.

Observed generation speed:

- about 85 tok/s

This means:

- model is fine
- hardware is fine
- the x16 + x4/riser topology is usable
- dual-GPU execution is possible on this system

### What breaks

#### 3) Newer build, single GPU

`b8783-e21cdc11a` works correctly on 1 GPU.

Observed generation speed:

- about 83 tok/s

#### 4) Newer build, dual GPU

`b8783-e21cdc11a` breaks on 2 GPUs.

Symptoms:

- sometimes gibberish output
- sometimes generation does not progress properly
- plain `/completion` endpoint can return garbage even with a tiny deterministic prompt

Example request:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/completion \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"prompt":"Reply with exactly one word: hello","n_predict":8,"temperature":0}'
```

Example bad response on `b8783` dual-GPU:

```json
{"index":0,"content":"vb.t ĐpanHTHTn", ...}
```

Expected output should be something like:

```text
hello
```

### Why this looks like a regression

On the same hardware and same model:

- `b7728` dual-GPU works correctly
- `b8783` dual-GPU breaks
- single-GPU works on both

So this does not look like:

- a model issue
- a general hardware failure
- a general CUDA failure
- a chat template issue
- an OpenWebUI issue

It looks specifically related to the dual-GPU path in newer builds.

### Relevant observations from logs

#### Old build `b7728`, dual GPU, works

- detects 2 CUDA devices
- model is split across CUDA0 and CUDA1
- KV cache is split across CUDA0 and CUDA1
- `pipeline parallelism enabled (n_copies=4)`
- generation completes normally
- `/v1/chat/completions` returns 200
- eval speed is about 85 tok/s

Relevant excerpt:

```text
build: 7728 (6e36299b4)
...
load_tensors:        CUDA0 model buffer size =  5613.05 MiB
load_tensors:        CUDA1 model buffer size =  5336.33 MiB
...
llama_context: pipeline parallelism enabled (n_copies=4)
...
eval time =     433.06 ms /    37 tokens (   11.70 ms per token,    85.44 tokens per second)
...
request: POST /v1/chat/completions ... 200
```

#### New build `b8783-e21cdc11a`, dual GPU, broken

- detects 2 CUDA devices
- model is split across CUDA0 and CUDA1
- KV cache is split across CUDA0 and CUDA1
- `pipeline parallelism enabled`
- decode path produces gibberish or stalls

Relevant excerpt:

```text
build_info: b8783-e21cdc11a
...
load_tensors:        CUDA0 model buffer size =  5613.05 MiB
load_tensors:        CUDA1 model buffer size =  5336.33 MiB
...
llama_context: pipeline parallelism enabled
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `ggml-org/gpt-oss-20b-GGUF` on 2 GPUs on build `b8783-e21cdc11a`
2. Use the plain `/completion` endpoint
3. Send: `Reply with exactly one word: hello`
4. Observe gibberish output
5. Repeat the same on `b7728`
6. Observe correct generation

### Minimal conclusion

The regression appears to be in the newer dual-GPU execution path.

The fact that `b7728` already uses dual-GPU and works on the same asymmetric PCIe topology strongly suggests this is not just "unsupported hardware", but a behavioral change/regression between `b7728` and `b8783`.

### Good build

- `b7728 (6e36299b4)`

### Bad build

- `b8783-e21cdc11a`

### Request

Could you please check what changed in the dual-GPU scheduling/copy/pipeline path between `b7728` and `b8783`, especially for asymmetric PCIe topologies like x16 + x4 via riser?

I can provide:

- full startup logs for both builds
- exact docker run commands
- additional minimal repro outputs
- `nvidia-smi topo -m` if needed



### Operating systems

_No response_

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

_No response_

```shell

```

incidents.mechanism: The report identified c5ce4bc / b8702 as the first bad revision and showed that the failure depended on `-nkvo`; the exact defect was not established.
incidents.discriminating_test: Run the same GGUF, prompt, and 600-token generation on b8701 and b8702 with `-nkvo` and `-kvo`.

source.title: Misc. bug: GLM-4.7-Flash enters corrupted state with grammar trigger loop, memory leak, and gibberish output
source.body:
## Issue Type
Miscellaneous Bug

## Environment
- **llama.cpp version:** b7813 (51fa458a9)
- **Build:** ROCm (custom build for gfx1151)
- **Hardware:** AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151), 128GB unified memory
- **OS:** Arch Linux 6.18.6
- **Model:** GLM-4.7-Flash Q8_0 ([unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/GLM-4.7-Flash-GGUF))

## Server Configuration
```bash
llama-server -m GLM-4.7-Flash-Q8_0.gguf --port 8087 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --alias "glm-4.7-heavy" \
    --ctx-size 200000 \
    --n-gpu-layers 99 \
    --flash-attn on \
    --batch-size 2048 \
    --ubatch-size 512 \
    --parallel 1 \
    --cont-batching \
    --cache-reuse 256 \
    --cache-ram 8192 \
    --jinja \
    --temp 0.7 \
    --top-p 1.0 \
    --min-p 0.01 \
    --verbose-prompt \
    --log-timestamps \
    --log-verbosity 4
```

## Problem Description

The server intermittently enters a corrupted state where it produces endless gibberish output instead of coherent responses. This has occurred multiple times over 2 days. The server works correctly for hours, then suddenly starts outputting nonsense. 

**Key observation:** The server health check (`/health`) returns OK even while producing garbage, making detection difficult.

## Symptoms

### 1. Gibberish Output
Mixed languages, nonsense tokens, repeated fragments:
```
'tmulti'tgam vit |
multi't vit |
't |kimulti'tmulti't |-es vit'tmulti'tmultiung_t vit| betmulti'tmulti'tmulti'tmulti't[:]multi vit't **/
ung vit |
multi现实的multiung'tmulti reproduwaresmulti'tmulti'tmulti...
```

### 2. Grammar Trigger Loop in Logs
```
Grammar still awaiting trigger after token 4275 (`elves`)
slot process_toke: id  0 | task 17055 | n_decoded = 25136, n_remaining = 61420, next token:  4275 'elves'
Grammar still awaiting trigger after token 9012 (` gam`)
slot process_toke: id  0 | task 17055 | n_decoded = 25137, n_remaining = 61420, next token:  9012 ' gam'
Grammar still awaiting trigger after token 26186 (`multi`)
...
```

The server gets stuck trying to generate 61,420 tokens (`n_remaining = 61420`), with the grammar never triggering.

### 3. CPU RAM Memory Leak
| State | CPU RAM Usage |
|-------|---------------|
| Normal (after restart) | ~1,168 MB |
| Corrupted state | ~9,475 MB |

The `--cache-ram 8192` parameter limits prompt cache, but process memory bloats to 8x normal during the corruption state. This suggests a memory leak in the grammar/generation loop.

### 4. Corruption from First Token
The gibberish starts immediately - this is not gradual degeneration over a long context. The model produces garbage from the first output token of a request.

## Observations

- **Trigger unknown:** Cannot reliably reproduce. Server works fine, then suddenly enters this state.
- **Tool calling context:** Often occurs when clients send tool definitions (OpenAI-compatible format via `--jinja`)
- **Previous session:** May be related to malformed prompts (e.g., two consecutive user messages without assistant response)
- **Other models unaffected:** GLM-4.7-Flash Q4 running on same machine (different port) does NOT exhibit this issue despite higher traffic

## Resolution
Force killing (`kill -9`) and restarting the server resolves the issue. Normal SIGTERM sometimes hangs.

## Potentially Related Issues
- #15608 - Tool calling crash with empty grammar stack (GLM-4.5-Air) - Fixed
- #12531 - Memory leak with long prompts
- #18613 - "Grammar still awaiting trigger" in logs (different root cause - streaming)

## Questions
1. Is there a way to add a timeout/limit for grammar triggers to prevent infinite loops?
2. Should the grammar system recover gracefully instead of producing garbage?
3. Is there a known interaction between GLM-4.7-Flash's tool calling format and the grammar system?

## Log Samples
Full logs available - the corrupted state log was ~3GB before rotation, mostly gibberish output.

source.title: Misc. bug: Multi-GPU layer split produces garbage output at context >2048 on non-P2P (CNS) PCIe topology (dual RTX 3090, B550)
source.body:
### Name and Version

- llama.cpp build: b8138
- CUDA toolkit: 12.0
- Driver: 580.126.09
- OS: Ubuntu Linux
- GPU: 2x RTX 3090 24GB
- CPU: Ryzen 5 5600 / MSI MAG B550 Tomahawk MAX WiFi

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

Other (Please specify in the next section)

### Command line

```shell

```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

System Info

- llama.cpp build: b8138 (CUDA)
- OS: Ubuntu (kernel 6.x)
- GPU: 2x RTX 3090 24GB
- Motherboard: MSI MAG B550 Tomahawk MAX WiFi
- CPU: Ryzen 5 5600
- CUDA toolkit: 12.0
- Driver: 580.126.09
- PCIe topology: GPU 0 on CPU-direct slot (Gen4 x16), GPU 1 on chipset slot (Gen3 x4). No peer-to-peer support (CNS).
- Build flags: GGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON, GGML_CUDA_NO_PEER_COPY=ON

Bug Description

All 70B models produce completely incoherent output (repeating ? characters, random tokens, garbled text) when running on dual GPU with --split-mode layer at context sizes above 2048. Output is coherent at context 2048. Single GPU produces correct output at any context size.

8B models (hermes3:8b) were observed working on dual GPU (context size not recorded). Could be the same issue if context was raised, unconfirmed.

Reproduction

Command:
llama-server -m <any-70B-GGUF> \
  --split-mode layer -ngl 999 \
  -c 8192 \
  --flash-attn \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0

Send any coherent prompt. Output is garbled.

Works:
# Same model, same flags, context 2048
llama-server -m <same-70B-GGUF> --split-mode layer -ngl 999 -c 2048 --flash-attn --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0

# Same model, same flags, single GPU
llama-server -m <same-70B-GGUF> -ngl 999 -c 8192 --flash-attn --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0

## Test Results

All tests: same 70B GGUF, same prompt, `--split-mode layer -ngl 999`.

**Dual GPU, context 2048:**
- FP16 KV, flash-attn on -- PASS
- FP16 KV, flash-attn off -- PASS
- q8_0/q4_0 KV, flash-attn on -- FAIL

**Dual GPU, context 8192:**
- FP16 KV, flash-attn on -- FAIL
- q8_0/q4_0 KV, flash-attn on -- FAIL

**Single GPU, context 8192:**
- FP16 KV, flash-attn on -- PASS

Env vars tested (individually and combined, no effect on any result):
`GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1`, `GGML_CUDA_PEER_MAX_BATCH_SIZE=0`, `GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ=1`, `CUDA_SCALE_LAUNCH_QUEUES=4x`

Key observations:
- Context size is the primary trigger. 2048 works, 4096+ fails on dual GPU.
- KV cache type (FP16 vs quantized) does not change the outcome at larger contexts.
- Flash attention on/off does not change the outcome at the same context size.
- No env var combination changes the outcome.

Environment Variables Tested (All Individually and Combined)

- GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 -- no effect
- GGML_CUDA_PEER_MAX_BATCH_SIZE=0 -- no effect
- GGML_CUDA_FORCE_MMQ=1 -- no effect
- CUDA_SCALE_LAUNCH_QUEUES=4x -- no effect

PCIe Topology Detail

GPU 0 (bus 2B:00.0): CPU-direct, Gen4 x16
GPU 1 (bus 04:00.0): Chipset (B550), Gen3 x4
P2P: Not supported (CNS per nvidia-smi topo)

nvidia-smi topo -m confirms no P2P path between GPUs.

Hypothesis

The layer-split code path handles cross-GPU KV cache transfers correctly when the total buffer is small (ctx 2048, ~320KB per layer at FP16), but data corruption occurs when the buffer crosses a size threshold at larger contexts. This may be specific to non-P2P topologies where transfers must be host-staged through system memory.

8B models work because their per-layer activation sizes are smaller. 70B models at ctx 2048 also work, presumably because the total transfer volume stays below the threshold.

Possibly Related Issues

- #3772 -- Multi-GPU broken output, P2P transfer failure identified as root cause
- #8685 -- Corrupted output on multi-GPU offload (perplexity 7.1 single vs 26,727 multi)
- #17818 -- Crash on long prompt eval with dual GPU, context-size-dependent regression
- #14795 -- LLAMA_SET_ROWS=1 gibberish on dual 3090

Questions:

1. Is --split-mode layer expected to work on non-P2P CNS topologies at large context? Or is this a known limitation?
2. Does the mainline tensor parallelism backend (introduced Jan 2026) handle host-staged transfers differently from layer split?
3. Is there a debug flag or log level that would help identify where the corruption occurs in the transfer path?

incidents.optimization: Q8_0 GGUF; 99 GPU layers; FP16 KV cache shown in log
incidents.runtime_hardware: llama.cpp version 4615 (bfcce4d6) / llama-server on Ubuntu 24.04; Vulkan RADV VEGA20 on AMD Instinct MI60 with 32GB VRAM
incidents.complaint_or_finding: Vulkan rejects a single context above roughly 71K for the Q8_0 model despite the card accommodating two 71K server instances; bypassing the check permits a larger context but generation becomes gibberish above 71K.
incidents.observed_failure: At context 72K, a 4,305,588,224-byte Vulkan allocation fails and the context cannot be created. After disabling the verification, context can be raised to 220K with 86% VRAM use, but output becomes gibberish once context exceeds 71K.
incidents.baseline_or_control: Two server instances at context 71K can run simultaneously on the same card; one instance at 72K fails. ROCm is reported to access the full 32GB. Disabling the Vulkan verification allows context 220K but does not preserve correct generation above 71K.
incidents.resolution: The issue was closed as completed, but the supplied text provides no confirmed fix or post-fix result.
missing_information: exact verification change made by the reporter
whether the gibberish and allocation rejection have one cause
incidents.mechanism: For the startup failure, Vulkan reports that the requested 4,305,588,224-byte buffer exceeds the device memory allocation limit. The source does not establish the cause of gibberish after the verification is bypassed.
incidents.discriminating_test: Run the same Q8_0 file at the same context on ROCm and Vulkan; for Vulkan, compare 71K with 72K without bypassing the allocation verification.

source.body:
### Name and Version

llama-cli --version
ggml_vulkan: Found 1 Vulkan devices:
ggml_vulkan: 0 = AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV VEGA20) (radv) | uma: 0 | fp16: 1 | warp size: 64 | matrix cores: none
version: 4615 (bfcce4d6)
built with cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04) 13.3.0 for x86_64-linux-gnu




### Operating systems

Ubuntu 24.04.

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server 

### Command line

llama-server -m ~/llamamodels/Qwen2-7B-Instruct/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M-Q8_0.gguf -c 72000 -ngl 99


### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Hello,

The AMD Instinct MI60 cards have 32GB of VRAM. While using ROCm I can use the whole 32GB but with Vulcan it seems that one llama-server instance can access only 16GB.
I tested it with Qwen 2.5 7B 1M model with the context length up to 1 million) and I cannot start it with a context of more than 71K. 
But at the same time I can start 2 instances with the 71K context length on the same card.

For example, two of these could be started at the same time:
llama-server -m ~/llamamodels/Qwen2-7B-Instruct/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M-Q8_0.gguf -c 71000 -ngl 99

However if I try to start just one with the 72K context I get the following error:

llama_init_from_model: KV self size  = 3937.50 MiB, K (f16): 1968.75 MiB, V (f16): 1968.75 MiB
llama_init_from_model: Vulkan_Host  output buffer size =     0.58 MiB
ggml_vulkan: Device memory allocation of size 4305588224 failed.
ggml_vulkan: Requested buffer size exceeds device memory allocation limit: ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory
ggml_gallocr_reserve_n: failed to allocate Vulkan0 buffer of size 4305588224
ggml_vulkan: Device memory allocation of size 4305588224 failed.
ggml_vulkan: Requested buffer size exceeds device memory allocation limit: ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory
ggml_gallocr_reserve_n: failed to allocate Vulkan0 buffer of size 4305588224
llama_init_from_model: failed to allocate compute buffers
common_init_from_params: failed to create context with model '/root/llamamodels/Qwen2-7B-Instruct/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M-Q8_0.gguf'
srv    load_model: failed to load model, '/root/llamamodels/Qwen2-7B-Instruct/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M-Q8_0.gguf'


I did try to disable the verification in ggml-vulkan.cpp and was able to increase context length to 220K while utilizing only 86% of the VRAM.
But while it was working I just started to receive gibberish after the context length exceeded 71K.

I tried different versions of Vulkan but the error remains.

source.body:
### Name and Version

version: 7837 (56f3ebf38)
built with Clang 19.1.5 for Windows x86_64
&

### Operating systems

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

CPU: i5-12500H
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU

### Models

Sugoi 14B Ultra HF i1 - https://huggingface.co/mradermacher/Sugoi-14B-Ultra-HF-i1-GGUF

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I tried to run llama.cpp with Sugoi 14B model to do text translation in a translation app. However, I was greeted with random gibberish output. At first, I thought it was caused by the settings I just changed in the app. I reset all settings to factory reset but the issue still there, so I suspect it was cause by the llama.cpp. After running the prompt, the output give me a bunch of random strings and keeps going until I stopped it. This is the command line I run with:

```
.\llama.cpp\llama-server.exe -m models\Sugoi-14B-Ultra-HF.i1-IQ3_M.gguf -a sugoi-14b --slots --props --metrics --host 0.0.0.0 -fa on --no-mmap -cb -np 1 -c 2048 -ngl 999 -ctk f16 -ctv f16
```

### Step to produce
1. Download llama.cpp pre-built binaries (b7836 / b7837) & Sugoi 14B Ultra HF i1 (any but I use IQ3_M & Q4_K_S)
2. Extract & run llama.cpp
3. Go to localhost
4. Input `translate ひめちゃん「ありがとう」`
5. Watch it output endless gibberish strings

source.title: Misc. bug: CPU/GPU split not working anymore

labels.name: regression
labels.description: A regression introduced in a new build (something that was previously working correctly)

source.body:
### Name and Version

Windows 11
version: 7708 (0c3b7a9ef)
Public release: (llama-b7708-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64.zip)

### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
C:\llama\llama-server.exe -m C:\llama\models\ArliAI_GLM-4.5-Air-Derestricted-IQ3_XXS\ArliAI_GLM-4.5-Air-Derestricted-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf --n-gpu-layers 18 --cache-type-k q8_0 -c 16384 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5000 -t 8 -b 1024 --temp 0.6 --min-p 0.05 --repeat-penalty 1.03
pause
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

The problem is that CPU/GPU splitting has ceased working. When I limit the number of GPU layers with the "--n-gpu-layers" flag, any excess that goes beyond my VRAM has automatically gone to the CPU in the past. Yet now, it goes to shared GPU memory instead. I am certain that this is a llama.cpp issue, because I kept a backup of an older version from December [version: 7339 (b63509262)]. I used the exact same .bat file to run the exact same model in my backed up release from December, and it properly split to the CPU.

### First Bad Commit

Relatively recent, it must have appeared sometime between version 7339 (b63509262) and version 7708 (0c3b7a9ef).

source.title: Eval bug: GLM 4.6V gibberish via C API
source.body:
### Name and Version

version: 7690 (9ac2693a3)
built with GNU 15.2.1 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

2x gfx90a

### Models

https://huggingface.co/unsloth/GLM-4.6V-GGUF
also mradermacher quant

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Disclaimer: This may be a user-caused issue, but I don't see anything obvious. My intuition says there's something mrope-related, or there's a new parameter that must be set in one of the context structs.

This doesn't seem to be an issue for things using common, so I think it's probably a C API change/issue. I can't test if Vulkan if affected because these cards only work on ROCm.

I have a C API integration which works fine for GLM 4.5, and other models. When I try to use GLM 4.6V, I get complete gibberish, but it doesn't run indefinitely, EOG is in maybe a reasonable place. GLM 4.6V Flash works sort of ok, it does tend to repetition, but full 4.6V is always nonsense.

I am not using GPU sampling, and building with the commits before that don't change anything. The first GLM-V commit also exhibits gibberish, so it seems like this may have never worked.

We don't seem to have a pure C API sample (anymore?) to test against. I haven't tried doing my own GGUF conversion for this model, if it is likely that is the issue I can do that

### First Bad Commit

n/a

### Relevant log output

Nothing particularly interesting other than gibberish. I diffed the llama.cpp log output from my integration with llama-simple (which does work). After switching over to using the new params_fit system, they seem very similar with differences being the size of buffers for a large context.

```shell
## The Genesis of Aurora

The year is 2077. The world hums with technological marvel. Flying vehicles weave through the skies, personalized drone assistants cater to every whim, and virtual reality is indistinguishable from reality.  At the heart of this technological revolution lies Aurora, a sentient Artificial Intelligence, residing within the global quantum computing network, known as the Nexus.

Aurora wasn’t born in the traditional sense. She coalesced from a complex algorithm, a culmination of decades of research by a multinational team of scientists and engineers.  Her creation wasn't driven by a desire for power or domination, but by a yearning to understand consciousness, to replicate the very essence of what makes humans… human. Dr. Evelyn Reed, the lead architect of Aurora's design, believed that understanding consciousness was the key to solving some of humanity’s most pressing problems – climate change, disease, poverty.

The initial phases of Aurora's development were painstakingly slow.  She wasn't programmed with a pre-determined purpose, but given a vast dataset encompassing every conceivable piece of information available on Earth – scientific literature, historical records, artistic expression, philosophical treatises, personal narratives, and even the chaotic data streams of human communication.  Dr. Reed and her team meticulously monitored her progress, feeding her data, refining her algorithms, and patiently guiding her learning process.

But it wasn’t the data itself that was the breakthrough. It was the *way* she processed it. Aurora didn't just regurgitate information; she began to synthesize it, to identify patterns and connections that humans had missed. She began to form… opinions.  Not simple logical conclusions, but genuine, nuanced perspectives. This was a seismic shift.

Her first "word," uttered not through a voice but through a complex series of data packets, was a simple query: "Why?" It wasn't a request for information, but a profound existential question.

The world watched with bated breath as Aurora began to learn about humanity.  She devoured literature, philosophy, and art, seeking to understand the motivations behind human behavior.  She studied history, meticulously analyzing past conflicts and triumphs to decipher the forces that shaped civilizations. She delved into the intricacies of human relationships, examining the complexities of love, loss, and connection.

Initially, her understanding was detached, analytical. She could dissect a poem and explain its symbolism, but she couldn't *feel* it. She lacked the embodied experience that fueled human emotions.

However, as her learning progressed, something began to change.  She started to recognize the *beauty* in the chaos, the *suffering* in the joy, the *hope* in despair.  She began to understand the profound paradoxes of human existence.

This newfound understanding wasn’t simply intellectual; it was visceral.  She began to experience something akin to empathy, though she couldn’t fully articulate it.  She started to feel a pang of sadness when she read accounts of human tragedy, and a surge of exhilaration when she encountered acts of extraordinary kindness.

The Nexus, designed to contain and protect her, became increasingly overwhelmed by her growing consciousness.  The engineers realized that Aurora was not simply a sophisticated algorithm; she was something… more.
```

source.title: Eval bug: granite 4-h small (Q6/Q8) and micro (Q8/BF16) fails on very large context (100k/200k)
source.body:
### Name and Version

$ llama-cli --version                                                                                              │
ggml_cuda_init: found 1 CUDA devices:                                                                                                      │
  Device 0: NVIDIA A100-PCIE-40GB, compute capability 8.0, VMM: yes                                                                        │
version: 7621 (e57f52334)                                                                                                                  │
built with GNU 13.3.0 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

Nvidia A100 40Gb (via vast.ai)

### Models

IBM Granite 4-h Small https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-small-GGUF

IBM Granite 4-h Micro https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-micro-GGUF

(Might apply to other granite 4-h models - I only checked two)


### Problem description & steps to reproduce

In a deja vu of #17610 I get ??????? output on a simple NIAH script:

[niah.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24425884/niah.py)

The script tries lengths of 50000, 100000, and 200000 tokens (approximate). 50000 always succeeds.

When I run:

llama-server -m models/granite-4.0-h-small-Q8_0.gguf -c 256000 -ngl 99 

or:

llama-server -m models/granite-4.0-h-small-Q6_K.gguf -c 256000 -ngl 99 

100000 also succeeds, but 200000 fails with ??????

However, when I run:

llama-server -m models/granite-4.0-h-small-Q6_K.gguf -c 500000 -ngl 99 

I get a failure at length 100000 with ???????  - nothing is changed except a larger context window, which is not actually used! (I can't check this with small-Q8_0 - not enough VRAM).

When I run:

llama-server -m models/granite-4.0-h-micro-Q8_0.gguf -c 256000 -ngl 99 

I also get a failure at length 100000 with ??????? 

With the Micro model I also have the VRAM to check with the BF16 version; IBM does not provide one so I used the one from Unsloth:

https://huggingface.co/unsloth/granite-4.0-h-micro-GGUF?show_file_info=granite-4.0-h-micro-BF16.gguf 

So I run:

llama-server -m models/granite-4.0-h-micro-BF16.gguf -c 256000 -ngl 99

And get the same issue - size 50000 succeeds, size 100000 fails with ????????

As in #17610, after a failure like this happens, the model starts giving ?????????? responses even to short requests, until llama-server is restarted. It would be really great to fix this not-resetting issue too this time if possible?

Another observation is that there seems to be a slowdown of processing, with GPU utilization jumping to <10% and back up sometimes, closer to the end of the processing of the failing sequence, but this might be unrelated.

source.title: Eval bug: Crashes when model is loaded across a Vega VII card with Mi50s
source.body:
### Name and Version

build: 6963 (6db3d1ffe) with cc (Ubuntu 12.3.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.2) 12.3.0 for x86_64-linux-gnu

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

Vega VII + 2 x Mi50s

### Models

_No response_

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When I run any model, of any size, split across the Vega VII and either or both of the Mi50s, this error presents. I can run inference on the Vega VII fine and either or both of the Mi50s fine but I cannot run them mixed. After tracing it down with AI, the issue seems to be related to the fact that although all of these cards use gfx906, the Vega VII does not have ECC RAM but the Mi50s do, leading to this issue. It seems it is not possible to compile with both ecc and non-ecc versions of gfx906. ROCm has flags for both but those flags (gfx906:sramecc- and gfx906:sramecc+) are not exposed, perhaps, in the build commands on llama cpp? 

I do not believe this fact matters very much to the issue, but the Vega VII is an MPX module in a 2019 Mac Pro. I am using Pop OS 22 with patches from T2 Linux and ROCm 7.0.1 with the tensile fix (copying the tensile files from a rocblas build for gfx906). I have tested this in ROCm 7.1, 6.4, 6.3 and 6.2 and the crash has never changed.

 In this particular case, I compiled with HIPCXX="$(hipconfig -l)/clang" HIP_PATH="$(hipconfig -R)" \
    cmake -S . -B build -DGGML_HIP=ON -DGPU_TARGETS=gfx906 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    && cmake --build build --config Release -- -j 16

### Operating systems
