source.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4(-Pro) DP-attention (data-parallel-size>1) produces numerically-garbage output when moe_a2a_backend=none and attn_tp_size>1 — dp_gather_partial used where data is already replicated
source.body:
# [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4(-Pro) DP-attention (`data-parallel-size>1`) produces numerically-garbage output when `moe_a2a_backend=none` and `attn_tp_size>1` — `dp_gather_partial` used where data is already replicated

## Affected component

`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py` (`_run_moe_ffn_dp_sync`) and `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_nextn.py` (the NextN/MTP draft
model's own `input_ids` gather).

## Environment

- **sglang revision**: `a9cf5e68e` (as shipped in container tag
  `nightly-dev-cu13-20260715-50d1edaa`, 2026-07-15 nightly build)
- **GPU**: NVIDIA H200 141GB HBM3, 2 nodes (16 GPUs total), also independently reproduced on
  H100 80GB, 2 nodes
- **Model**: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4 (possibly also affecting other DeepSeek-V4-family models —
  this is a serving-topology bug, not model-weight-specific)
- **Backend**: sglang aggregated serving, `moe-runner-backend: marlin`, `fp4-gemm-backend: marlin`
  (the only Hopper-legal NVFP4 MoE runner in this build), `moe-a2a-backend` **unset** (defaults
  to `"none"` — DeepEP is not registered for the Marlin NVFP4 MoE path on Hopper, confirmed
  independently multiple times, out of scope for this issue)
- **Parallelism configs that trigger it**: any DP-attention topology with `attn_tp_size > 1`,
  e.g. `tensor-parallel-size: 16, data-parallel-size: 4` (4 attn-TP subgroups × 4 DP replicas)
  and `tensor-parallel-size: 16, data-parallel-size: 2` (8 attn-TP subgroups × 2 DP replicas).
  **Not** triggered by flat tensor-parallel-only serving (`data-parallel-size: 1`, e.g. flat
  `tensor-parallel-size: 16`), which never exercises this code path at all.

## Summary

With DP-attention enabled (`enable-dp-attention: true`, `data-parallel-size > 1`) and
`moe_a2a_backend` set to `"none"`, the server reaches a genuinely healthy state (health checks
pass, `Server is healthy - starting benchmark`, no crash, no exception) but **every generated
response is well-formed-shape but semantically-meaningless token soup** — not truncated, not
repetitive, not a tokenizer/chat-template artifact, just numerically garbage output. This
reproduces at every `attn_tp_size > 1` DP-attention shape tested (`attn_tp_size=4` with
`data-parallel-size=4`, and independently `attn_tp_size=8` with `data-parallel-size=2`), at
every concurrency level, and is deterministic-per-request-shape (not a race condition — every
request at a given topology is equally garbled).

## Root cause

`_run_moe_ffn_dp_sync` in `deepseek_v4.py` gathers each DP replica's local `hidden_states` into
the global MoE buffer via `dp_gather_partial()` (`is_partial=True`). `dp_gather_partial` assumes
its input is an **un-reduced partial per-attention-TP-rank contribution**, and fuses the attn-TP
reduce into the gather's own `reduce_scatter` — this is a real, intentional optimization pattern
(see the general-purpose sibling implementation in `layers/communicator.py`'s
`_gather_hidden_states_and_residual`, which explicitly coordinates this choice with whether the
attn-TP reduce has already happened via a `use_layer_norm_before_gather`-style flag).

But by the time `_run_moe_ffn_dp_sync` runs, `self.self_attn()` has **already fully all-reduced**
its output across the attn-TP group — via `wo_b`'s own `reduce_results`, or the explicit
`attn_tp_all_reduce(o)` compensator (added in commit `9b10821c8e`, "[NPU] Add Ascend NPU support
for DeepSeek-V4", which runs unconditionally whenever `attn_tp_size>1` in DP-attention mode, on
every backend, not just NPU). So `hidden_states` is **REPLICATED** (bit-identical) across
attn-TP ranks at this point, not partial. Calling the "partial" gather on replicated data makes
its `reduce_scatter`/`all_reduce` **sum** `attn_tp_size` identical copies together, inflating
hidden-state magnitude by exactly `attn_tp_size`× at every layer's MoE-gather step. Result:
well-formed-shape but numerically-garbage output. This is **invisible at `attn_tp_size==1`** — a
reduce over a group of one rank is a no-op, so `dp_gather_partial` vs. `dp_gather_replicate` are
numerically identical there — which is exactly why flat tensor-parallel-only serving (and any
DP-attention config that happens to run with `attn_tp_size==1`) never shows this bug.

**Smoking-gun corroboration**: this exact failure mode was already found and fixed for a
*sibling* call — the `input_ids_global` gather in `DeepseekV4Model.forward` (same file, calling
function one level up) — by the same commit `9b10821c8e`, which switched **that** one call from
`dp_gather_partial` to `dp_gather_replicate`, with the comment:

> "Token ids are replicated within an attention-TP group. Use replicate gather here to avoid
> summing duplicated ids when attention_tp_size > 1."

That fix was never propagated to the 2 other structurally-identical call sites in the same
files:
1. `deepseek_v4.py`, `_run_moe_ffn_dp_sync` — the main `hidden_states` gather.
2. `deepseek_v4_nextn.py` — the NextN/MTP draft model's own `input_ids` gather (same bug as the
   already-fixed sibling, just in the draft-model file instead of the main model file).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Serve DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4 (or any DeepSeek-V4-family checkpoint) with sglang, 2 nodes /
   16 GPUs, DP-attention enabled at `attn_tp_size > 1`. Example server args (aggregated,
   NVFP4/Marlin):
   ```yaml
   tensor-parallel-size: 16
   data-parallel-size: 4
   enable-dp-attention: true
   quantization: modelopt_fp4
   moe-runner-backend: marlin
   fp4-gemm-backend: marlin
   # moe-a2a-backend intentionally omitted -> defaults to "none"
   ```
2. Wait for the server to report healthy (`Server is healthy`, no exceptions in the logs — this
   config reaches a clean health check with no crash).
3. Send a single, simple completion request at `temperature: 0`, e.g.:
   ```
   curl -s http://<worker>:8000/v1/chat/completions -d '{
     "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro",
     "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the capital of France?"}],
     "temperature": 0
   }'
   ```
4. Observe: the response is a well-formed JSON completion (correct envelope, plausible token
   count, no error) but the `content` field is semantically meaningless garbage, e.g. (actual
   captured output from this exact repro):
   ```
   " of1 f# Marcel½ nzt  of of LeslieangcleLet-\nEg, l#)6 Leti)\n\nF  What Morgan io   . imp chees,11 ( /.\n\n 2 -  \n.., reint. lobby st  g (iz copy 4sof2):ct  I - modest3.. Pit ind4ford. | io...Y 1f I/ Liz (] leaves! Kre =).H(System\n       \n.?of ,b19 casc flo.   IE"
   ```
   This is deterministic at `temperature: 0` — every request at this topology returns
   equally-garbled output, not intermittent.
5. Cross-check: fire multiple (e.g. 16) concurrent out-of-band requests directly at the server —
   all independently return equally garbled output, ruling out response mixing/interleaving as
   the explanation.
6. Confirm this is topology-specific, not weight/checkpoint-specific: the identical checkpoint
   and container, served with `data-parallel-size: 1` (flat tensor-parallel, `attn_tp_size==1`),
   returns fully coherent output for the same prompts. Independently reproduced at a *different*
   DP-attention shape (`attn_tp_size=8, data-parallel-size=2`) with the identical garbage-output
   symptom, confirming this is a general property of "DP-attention + `moe_a2a_backend: none`" at
   `attn_tp_size>1`, not specific to one particular TP/DP split.

## Expected behavior

Coherent, correct completions — identical in content to the same server topology's flat
tensor-parallel equivalent (verified: after the fix below, both configs produce byte-identical
answers to test prompts, e.g. `"What is 4 times 5 plus 2?"` → `"22"` on both).

## Actual behavior

Well-formed-shape, syntactically-plausible, but semantically-meaningless garbage output at
every request, at any DP-attention topology with `attn_tp_size > 1` and
`moe_a2a_backend: none`. No exception, no crash, no error status code — the server believes it
is serving correctly.

## Suggested fix

Swap `dp_gather_partial` → `dp_gather_replicate` at the 2 call sites listed above, matching the
pattern already used for the sibling `input_ids_global` gather in `DeepseekV4Model.forward`
(fixed by `9b10821c8e`). This is a one-line-per-site change — no new infrastructure, no behavior
change for existing working configs (mathematically identical to the old behavior at
`attn_tp_size==1`, since a reduce over a group of one rank is a no-op either way).

We have a fix applied and verified locally, currently sitting on branch
[`fix/deepseek-v4-dp-gather-replicate`](https://github.com/mikekg/sglang/tree/fix/deepseek-v4-dp-gather-replicate)
on a fork (not yet opened as a PR against this repo) — happy to open a PR for this once we've
finished validating it against a few more topologies internally.

### Verification performed on our fix (informational — describing what we checked, for context)

1. **Direct curl A/B vs. a confirmed-coherent flat-TP16 baseline**, same prompts,
   `temperature: 0`, run against the patched server while healthy — 3/3 test prompts matched
   the baseline exactly, repeated across 7 independent server launches (4 at one DP-attention
   shape, 2 at 8k context, all never regressing to garbage).
2. **Benchmark harness `generated_texts` samples** across every completed concurrency level of
   two full sweeps (1024 and 8192 token context, concurrency 1 through 512) — all genuinely
   coherent, zero errors on any completed request.
3. **Mathematical/collective-semantics trace** — not just empirical pattern matching, a concrete
   explanation for why the old code path is wrong (backed by the upstream commit that already
   fixed the identical bug for the sibling call site).

## Additional notes

- We did not find an existing open issue matching this specific `dp_gather_partial` /
  `dp_gather_replicate` mismatch as of this writing.
- This is unrelated to the two env-gated performance flags `SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV` and
  `SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER` — both are correctly gated to `attn_tp_size==1`-only for their
  own, separate reasons (an alternate variable-length gather and a post-MoE reduce_scatter
  combine), and enabling either would not fix this bug. We initially suspected they might be
  relevant and ruled them out via direct source inspection before finding the actual root cause.

source.title: [Bug] UnifiedRadixCache prefill crash: TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len() in full_component.commit_hicache_transfer (LOAD_BACK), high concurrency on B200
source.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [ ] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

  ### Checklist
  - [x] Searched existing issues (closest is #24869 / PR #25088, but that fixed the *build* path in `swa_component`, not this one — see below).

  ### Describe the bug

  Under high concurrency, a PD-disaggregated **prefill** scheduler crashes non-deterministically in the
  UnifiedRadixCache HiCache **LOAD_BACK commit** path. `FullComponent.commit_hicache_transfer` reads
  `len(cd.host_value)` for a node in `nodes_to_load` whose `host_value` has raced to `None`, raising
  `TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()`. The exception is uncaught in the scheduler event
  loop, so the whole prefill worker dies and is restarted (a ~5–6 min cold restart in our deployment:
  model reload + RDMA/transfer-engine reinit + PD warmup). During the outage all in-flight KV
  bootstraps/transfers to that prefill fail on the decode side (`Decode handshake/transfer failed`), so
  the decode goes idle and the cluster stops responding.

  Observed twice in a single ~30 min load run, and again ~20 min later — recurs roughly every 15–20 min
  under sustained agentic (long-prefix, cache-hit-heavy) load.

  ### Traceback

  ```
  Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
    File ".../srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 4062, in run_scheduler_process
      scheduler.run_event_loop()
    File ".../srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 1418, in run_event_loop
      dispatch_event_loop(self)
    File ".../srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3934, in dispatch_event_loop
      scheduler.event_loop_overlap_disagg_prefill()
    File ".../torch/utils/_contextlib.py", line 124, in decorate_context
      return func(*args, **kwargs)
    File ".../srt/disaggregation/prefill.py", line 468, in event_loop_overlap_disagg_prefill
      batch = self.get_next_disagg_prefill_batch_to_run()
    File ".../srt/disaggregation/prefill.py", line 407, in get_next_disagg_prefill_batch_to_run
      batch = self.get_new_batch_prefill()
    File ".../srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 2558, in get_new_batch_prefill
      ret = self._get_new_batch_prefill_raw(...)
    File ".../srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 2689, in _get_new_batch_prefill_raw
      res = adder.add_one_req(...)
      new_indices, req.last_node = self.tree_cache.init_load_back(...)
    File ".../srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py", line 2364, in init_load_back
      if self.load_back(best_match_node, mem_quota, req=req):
    File ".../srt/mem_cache/unified_radix_cache.py", line 1657, in load_back
      self.components[BASE_COMPONENT_TYPE].commit_hicache_transfer(...)
    File ".../srt/mem_cache/unified_cache_components/full_component.py", line 326, in commit_hicache_transfer
      n_len = len(cd.host_value)
              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()
  ```

  ### Root cause / analysis

  In `full_component.py`, the `LOAD_BACK` commit loop assigns device slices by re-reading each node's
  `host_value` length:

  ```python
  elif phase == CacheTransferPhase.LOAD_BACK:
      ...
      xfer = transfers[0]
      device_indices = xfer.device_indices
      offset = 0
      for n in xfer.nodes_to_load or []:
          cd = n.component_data[ct]
          n_len = len(cd.host_value)          # <-- cd.host_value is None here
          cd.value = device_indices[offset : offset + n_len].clone()
          offset += n_len
          ...
  ```

  The corresponding **build** phase (`build_hicache_transfers`, LOAD_BACK) walks the evicted path and
  explicitly asserts non-None:

  ```python
  while cur.evicted:
      cd = cur.component_data[ct]
      assert cd.host_value is not None       # build guards...
      backed_up.append(cd.host_value)
      nodes.append(cur)
      cur = cur.parent
  ```

  So `device_indices` is sized as `Σ len(host_value)` over `nodes_to_load` at build time, but between
  build and the commit above, one node's `host_value` is freed to `None` (host eviction / lock race),
  and the **commit path has no matching guard**. This is the same load-back race family as #24869
  (fixed by PR #25088, "Fix HiCache load back start node"), but #25088 addressed the `AssertionError`
  in the SWA component's *build* path — it does **not** cover the Full component's *commit* path, which
  still `len()`s a raced-to-None `host_value`. **Still present on `main`** (verified against the current
  tip: `full_component.py` `commit_hicache_transfer` LOAD_BACK loop is unguarded).

  Note a naive `if cd.host_value is None: continue` is **incorrect**: `device_indices` offsets were
  computed from all nodes' host lengths, so skipping one node desyncs every subsequent slice and
  silently corrupts KV. The fix needs to abort/skip the whole transfer consistently (and free the
  already-allocated `device_indices`), falling back to recompute — or hold the host lock across
  build→commit so `host_value` cannot be freed mid-flight.


### Reproduction

  - PD-disaggregated deployment, `--disaggregation-mode prefill`, `mooncake` transfer backend, TP2, B200.
  - `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, `hicache_write_policy=write_back`, `hicache_ratio=2.0`,
    `hicache_size=64`, `hicache_storage_backend=None` (L2 host tier only, no external L3).
  - Sustained high-concurrency, long-prefix / high-cache-hit workload so evicted prefixes are
    frequently loaded back H→D. Crash appears within ~15–20 min of load.

  ### Suggested fix

  Guard the LOAD_BACK **commit** path in `FullComponent.commit_hicache_transfer` consistently with the
  build-phase invariant: if any `nodes_to_load[i].host_value` is `None`, abort the entire transfer
  (release the allocated `device_indices`, leave the node evicted, fall back to recompute) instead of
  per-node skipping; or ensure the host lock taken in `load_back` covers the nodes across build→commit
  so `host_value` cannot be evicted mid-flight


### Environment

  - sglang `0.0.0.dev13771+gf6c97af5d` (patched v0.5.13)
  - Model: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (NVFP4), 2×B200 per node, TP2, PD-disaggregated, mooncake/IB.

source.title: [Bug] NVFP4 KV cache batched decode (trtllm_mha / SM120 XQA) produces corrupted output
source.body:
## Summary

Batched decode (bs > 1) with `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` + `--decode-attention-backend trtllm_mha` on SM120 (RTX 5090, 32 GB) produces corrupted generations. Single-request traffic is correct. Introduced with #21601; the shipped CI test `test_llama8b_nvfp4_kv_cache_sm120.py` never caught it because its first scheduled execution died earlier with a startup OOM (fixed separately) and the extra-a suite was skipped on the PR itself.

## Repro (RTX 5090 devbox, CI-matching stack)

sglang main @ 67e7f8d13a, sglang-kernel 0.4.5, flashinfer-python/cubin/jit-cache 0.6.15, torch 2.11, model `nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-NVFP4` (snapshot bdb54e24):

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-NVFP4 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 --fp4-gemm-backend auto --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
  --prefill-attention-backend flashinfer --decode-attention-backend trtllm_mha \
  --page-size 64 --cuda-graph-backend-prefill=disabled --enable-multimodal \
  --trust-remote-code --mem-fraction-static 0.8
```

| Condition | Result |
|-----------|--------|
| Sequential requests (bs=1), 5-shot gsm8k subset | **0.75** (8 samples, correct) |
| 32 concurrent gsm8k requests | **0.005** (1/200), garbage output |
| 16 concurrent short unique prompts | 3/16 correct, rest garbage |
| Same, `--disable-overlap-schedule` | still corrupted → not the overlap race |
| Same, `--disable-cuda-graph` | still corrupted → not graph capture |
| `--decode-attention-backend triton` | crashes: `KeyError: 'float4_e2m1fn_x2'` (so trtllm_mha is the only working decode path for KV4 MHA) |

Corrupted output looks like attention over wrong KV pages, e.g. `' A  the     the   7  the 5  the .  the ://://:// ...'`.

## Suspicion

bs=1 being clean while bs>1 corrupts is consistent with the XQA kernel mis-reading paged FP4 data / block scales when a request's pages are non-contiguous (single fresh requests get contiguous pages by luck). Possibly the `permute(0, 2, 1, 3)` non-contiguous views handed to `trtllm_batch_decode` in `trtllm_mha_backend.py`, or a scale-layout (linear vs swizzled) mismatch for `kv_cache_sf`.

## Impact

- `test_llama8b_nvfp4_kv_cache_sm120.py` can never pass its gsm8k accuracy check (num_threads=200) — being disabled pending this fix.

source.title: v0.5.12 DeepGemm regression on B300 (sm_103): CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS in fp8_fp4_gemm_nt TMA descriptor init for shared-experts FP8 GEMM
source.body:
## Human

```
Exception: Capture cuda graph failed: CUDA driver error (/deepgemm/csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/runtime_utils.hpp:143): 700 (CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS, an illegal memory access was encountered)
```

## AI Summary
`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12-cu130` regresses DeepGemm on NVIDIA B300 (Blackwell, sm_120). GLM-5-FP8 inference aborts during CUDA graph capture with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS (error 700)` in DeepGemm's TMA descriptor init. The same workload runs cleanly on `v0.5.11-cu130`.

## Environment
- **Image**: `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12-cu130`
- **Hardware**: 8x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 (Blackwell, **sm_103**)
- **Driver / runtime**: NVIDIA driver 580.126.09, CUDA 13.0
- **Model**: `zai-org/GLM-5-FP8`

## Reproduction

Launch the SGLang server with these flags (this is the recipe that triggers it; same flags work on v0.5.11-cu130):

```bash
docker run --gpus all --shm-size=32g --rm \
  -v $HF_HUB_CACHE:/root/.cache/huggingface \
  lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12-cu130 \
  bash -c "
    pip install --no-deps 'transformers==5.2.0' 'huggingface-hub==1.4.1' && \
    export SGL_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=1 && \
    python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
      --model-path=zai-org/GLM-5-FP8 \
      --host=0.0.0.0 --port=8888 --trust-remote-code \
      --tensor-parallel-size=8 \
      --data-parallel-size 1 --expert-parallel-size 1 \
      --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
      --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --quantization fp8 \
      --attention-backend nsa \
      --nsa-decode-backend trtllm --nsa-prefill-backend trtllm \
      --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
      --cuda-graph-max-bs 128 --max-running-requests 128 \
      --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
      --chunked-prefill-size 32768 --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \
      --enable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion --disable-radix-cache \
      --stream-interval 30 \
      --model-loader-extra-config '{\"enable_multithread_load\": true}'
  "
```

Server loads the model, then aborts at the first CUDA graph capture iteration.

## Failing GitHub Action runs (full logs)
- Run: https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/25984496952
- Failing jobs (identical crash on all TP ranks):
  - https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/25984496952/job/76379310468 (8k1k, conc-128)
  - https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/25984496952/job/76379310585 (1k1k, conc-128)
- Source PR (image bump v0.5.11-cu130 → v0.5.12-cu130): https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/1421

## Symptom
All TP workers crash simultaneously during CUDA graph capture on the **first** batch size processed. No prompt is served.

```
RuntimeError: Error in function 'run' at
/deepgemm/csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/runtime_utils.hpp:143
CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS (700)
```

## Call path
```
cuda_graph_runner.capture()
  → deepseek_v2.forward()
      → MoE layer forward_normal_dual_stream
          → _forward_shared_experts
              → shared_experts.gate_up_proj
                  → fp8_kernel.deep_gemm_fp8_fp8_bf16_nt
                      → deep_gemm_wrapper.gemm_nt_f8f8bf16
                          → deep_gemm.fp8_gemm_nt
                              → native fp8_fp4_gemm_nt
                                  → runtime_utils.hpp:143  ← CRASH
```

`runtime_utils.hpp:143` is the TMA descriptor validation/creation site, suggesting the regression is in how the bundled DeepGemm builds TMA descriptors for Blackwell (sm_120) in the FP8 shared-experts path.

## Working baseline
`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.11-cu130` on the same recipe / hardware / model runs cleanly through CUDA graph capture and full inference.

## Workarounds that unblock the workload
1. `--fp8-gemm-runner-backend cutlass` — bypasses DeepGemm via the CUTLASS FP8 path, runs to completion.
2. `--disable-cuda-graph` — avoids the capture path (large perf hit; smoke-test only).
3. Pin to `v0.5.11-cu130`.

## Suggested next step for maintainers
The diff between v0.5.11 and v0.5.12 in either the bundled DeepGemm vendoring or the shared-experts FP8 GEMM dispatch on Blackwell. Looking at `deep_gemm/csrc/apis/../jit_kernels/impls/runtime_utils.hpp` (TMA descriptor validation) — the addresses or strides passed to the TMA descriptor are likely the regression site.

Happy to provide additional traces or trigger more runs — let me know what's most useful.

source.title: [Bug] GLM-5.2 NVFP4 + EAGLE: CUDA illegal memory access during decode CUDA-graph capture on v0.5.15 and main (works on 2026-07-03 dev-glm52-nvfp4)
source.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but cannot get the expected help (no existing GLM-5.2 + EAGLE CUDA-graph-capture issue found).
- [x] The bug has not been fixed in the latest version (repros on `v0.5.15` release AND `dev` main `b94ac87e`, 2026-07-13).
- [x] Please use English.

### Describe the bug

Serving **GLM-5.2 NVFP4** (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, `--quantization modelopt_fp4`) with **EAGLE speculative decoding** (bundled nextn head, steps=6 topk=1 draft=7) on **8×B200 (TP8)** crashes with an async **CUDA illegal memory access during decode CUDA-graph capture** on both:

- `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.15` (image `06e0aa8359f5`, cu130, 2026-07-10), and
- `lmsysorg/sglang:dev` (image `95bd5fb8e043`, main `b94ac87e`, 2026-07-13).

The same model + flags **work correctly** on the older feature-branch image `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-glm52-nvfp4` (image `4f4216afc5ad`, 2026-07-03, sglang `0.0.0.dev1+g430418e21`, commit `430418e2182606b5296b26c912df8f12ec9b380f` — an ancestor of the v0.5.15 lineage). So this looks like a regression between 2026-07-03 main and v0.5.15.

Symptoms:

- Weight load and prefill/verify graph setup complete fine; the crash happens only during **decode CUDA-graph capture**.
- The async IMA surfaces inside `torch.cuda.random` generator `get_state`/`set_state` under dynamo compile, reported as `InternalTorchDynamoError` → `Capture cuda graph failed` (i.e., the IMA is asynchronous and gets attributed to the RNG-state sync point).
- On `v0.5.15` it fired on TP rank 7 at ~91% of the small-batch-size decode captures; on `dev` (`b94ac87e`) same signature on TP rank 2. Rank/progress varies — consistent with an async IMA.

Note: in all runs (including the working 07-03 image) we disable the multimem all-gather in `logits_processor.py` (`enabled=False` for the `do_tensor_parallel_all_gather` path), because with it enabled even the 07-03 image hits a draft-CUDA-graph IMA on this model. We have not tested mainline without that patch; the capture crash above occurs with it applied.

Untested dodges (can try on request): `--disable-cuda-graph` (not usable for production perf), different speculative shapes, cu12 image flavor.

### Reproduction

```bash
docker run -d --name srv --gpus all --ipc=host --network=host --shm-size 32g \
  -v /models:/models --entrypoint bash lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.15 \
  -c "sed -i \"s/enabled=self.do_tensor_parallel_all_gather and not self.use_attn_tp_group,/enabled=False,/\" /sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/logits_processor.py && python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --served-model-name glm-5.2 --tp 8 --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 6 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 7 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 48 --enable-metrics --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000"
```

Same command with `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-glm52-nvfp4` boots and serves correctly.

### Environment

- 8×NVIDIA B200 (SM100), driver 580.159.04
- Docker images as above (v0.5.15 = cu130 base)
- Model: GLM-5.2 NVFP4 checkpoint (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, `index_topk=2048` DSA), bundled nextn/MTP head used as EAGLE draft

source.title: Bug: DSV4 NVFP4 serving crashes - _DeepseekV4ConfigAlias not registered with HuggingFace CONFIG_MAPPING
source.body:
### Bug: DSV4 NVFP4 serving crashes on SM121 — `_DeepseekV4ConfigAlias` not registered with HuggingFace `CONFIG_MAPPING`

**SGLang**: v0.5.15 (tagged)
**Transformers**: 5.12.1
**Hardware**: NVIDIA GB10 / SM121 / DGX Spark / CUDA 13.2

## Crash

```
[2026-07-13] DeepseekV4ForCausalLM has no SGLang implementation, falling back to Transformers implementation.
[2026-07-13] Using Transformers backend.
[2026-07-13] Scheduler hit an exception:
  File "sglang/srt/models/transformers.py", line 617, in __init__
    self.model: PreTrainedModel = AutoModel.from_config(...)
  File "transformers/models/auto/auto_factory.py", line 252, in from_config
    raise ValueError("Unrecognized configuration class ... _DeepseekV4ConfigAlias ... for this kind of AutoModel")
ValueError: Unrecognized configuration class ...
```

## Root Cause

`sglang/srt/utils/common.py` line 144-148 creates `_DeepseekV4ConfigAlias` and registers it in SGLang's internal `_CONFIG_REGISTRY`:

```python
class _DeepseekV4ConfigAlias(_HFDeepseekV3Config):
    model_type = "deepseek_v4"

_CONFIG_REGISTRY["deepseek_v32"] = _DeepseekV32ConfigAlias
_CONFIG_REGISTRY["deepseek_v4"] = _DeepseekV4ConfigAlias
```

However, `_CONFIG_REGISTRY` is **never synced to HuggingFace's `CONFIG_MAPPING`**. When SGLang falls back to the `Transformers` backend (`sglang/srt/models/transformers.py:617`), it calls `AutoModel.from_config(self.config, ...)`. The config is a `_DeepseekV4ConfigAlias` instance with `model_type="deepseek_v4"`, but transformers 5.12.1's `CONFIG_MAPPING` has no entry for `"deepseek_v4"`.

## Fix

Either:
1. Register `_DeepseekV4ConfigAlias` with `AutoConfig.register("deepseek_v4", _DeepseekV4ConfigAlias)` in addition to `_CONFIG_REGISTRY`
2. Or set `config.model_type = "deepseek_v3"` (which IS in CONFIG_MAPPING) and override defaults in `model_config.py` post-load (as the comment at line 137 already says)

## Reproduction

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all --network host --privileged \
  xomoxcc/dgx-spark-sglang:0.5.15-sm121 \
  sglang serve --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-NVFP4
```

Works on B200/SM100 (upstream-validated) but crashes on GB10/SM121.

source.title: AssertionError: dec_lock_ref on node with node.swa_lock_ref=0 in SWARadixCache under DeepSeek-V4 long-context workload
source.body:
## Title

`AssertionError: dec_lock_ref on node with node.swa_lock_ref=0` in SWARadixCache under DeepSeek-V4 long-context workload

## Summary

Running a DeepSeek-V4-Pro deployment on long-context workloads (prompts in the ~100K–500K token range, with substantial cross-request shared prefix) we intermittently hit an assertion failure inside `SWARadixCache.dec_lock_ref`. The scheduler crashes; all TP ranks hit the same `node.id` simultaneously, suggesting deterministic divergence rather than a races condition.

The crash is **probabilistic** — server runs cleanly for a while (tens of minutes to hours), then fails on a normal `cache_finished_req` path. Once it triggers, every subsequent attempt to release that request crashes the scheduler.

## Stack trace

```
[TP5 EP5] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../managers/scheduler.py", line 3027, in run_scheduler_process
    scheduler.event_loop_overlap()
  File ".../managers/scheduler.py", line 1137, in event_loop_overlap
    pop_and_process()
  File ".../managers/scheduler.py", line 1108, in pop_and_process
    self.process_batch_result(tmp_batch, tmp_result)
  File ".../managers/scheduler.py", line 2472, in process_batch_result
    self.process_batch_result_decode(batch, result)
  File ".../managers/scheduler_output_processor_mixin.py", line 438, in process_batch_result_decode
    release_kv_cache(req, self.tree_cache)
  File ".../mem_cache/common.py", line 469, in release_kv_cache
    tree_cache.cache_finished_req(req, is_insert=is_insert)
  File ".../mem_cache/swa_radix_cache.py", line 517, in cache_finished_req
    self.dec_lock_ref(
  File ".../mem_cache/swa_radix_cache.py", line 807, in dec_lock_ref
    node.swa_lock_ref > 0
AssertionError: dec_lock_ref on node with node.swa_lock_ref=0, node.id=291371
```

The same `node.id` is hit on all TP ranks (TP0..TP7) within the same forward step.

## Environment

- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro` (`num_hidden_layers=61`, `sliding_window=128`, `page_size=256`)
- Hardware: 8× B200, TP=8, EP=8
- Speculative decoding: EAGLE, `--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`
- `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`
- `--max-running-requests 20`
- `--swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1`
- `--context-length 512000`
- `--attention-backend compressed`
- `--mem-fraction-static 0.85`
- `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`
- Hybrid SWA memory enabled (default)
- Radix eviction: `lru` (default)
- Overlap schedule enabled (default)

Env variables left at their defaults:

- `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_RADIX_CACHE_COMPACT` (default `True`)
- `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_RELEASE_LEAF_LOCK_AFTER_WINDOW` (default `False`)

## Workload pattern that triggers it

- Mix of long prompts (≈ 100K–500K tokens) and shorter prompts.
- Multiple long-prompt requests share **very long common prefixes** (e.g. several requests differing only in the last few hundred tokens out of ~485K).
- Stream of requests over time so the SWA prefix-cache is exercised continuously (insert / match / evict / tombstone).
- Some requests generate enough output that `decode_position` advances past `sliding_window` (i.e. workload would exercise the early SWA-leaf release path if `SGLANG_OPT_SWA_RELEASE_LEAF_LOCK_AFTER_WINDOW=True` were enabled, but we leave it at the default `False`).

We have not been able to reduce this to a small standalone reproducer yet — empirically the crash needs the SWA radix tree to grow large (the `node.id` counter at crash time is in the hundreds of thousands, indicating a lot of accumulated insert / split / tombstone activity) and a workload that simultaneously evicts SWA pages and does cross-request prefix matching.

## What the assertion implies

The failure is at `swa_radix_cache.py:807`:

```python
assert (
    node.swa_lock_ref > 0
), f"dec_lock_ref on node with {node.swa_lock_ref=}, {node.id=}"
```

i.e. `dec_lock_ref` walks past the request's `swa_uuid_for_lock` boundary into a node that was never (or is no longer) SWA-locked. So either:

1. `swa_uuid_for_lock` recorded at `inc_lock_ref` time can no longer be found on the dec walk (uuid lost / overwritten by a tree mutation between inc and dec), or
2. `swa_lock_ref` accounting got out of sync with the chain shape due to a tree mutation (split / compact / tombstone) that happened while a request was holding a lock.

We've eyeballed the obvious candidates (`_split_node`, `_compact_single_child_chain`, `_tombstone_internal_node`, `dec_swa_lock_only`) but haven't been able to definitively pin it.

## Reproduction notes

- Repro frequency: roughly every few hours under steady production-like workload. We do **not** have a deterministic minimal repro.
- The crash dump's request list shows ~35 finished + ~15 unfinished requests in flight at crash time, with several long-prompt requests sharing prefixes ≥ 480K tokens.
- All TP ranks fail on identical `node.id`, which suggests the divergent state is in the radix tree itself, not in any per-rank scheduling decision.

Happy to share more dump data or add logging if it helps narrow this down. Let us know what would be most useful.

source.title: [Bug] HunyuanV3 (hy_v3): shared-expert weights silently skipped (`mlp.shared_experts.*` vs model's `shared_mlp`) → NaN on first forward
source.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. (Searched `hunyuan shared_experts`, `HYV3 shared_mlp`, `Hy3 NaN`, `hunyuan_v3 shared` — no existing report. The closest is PR #30331, a sibling fix in `hunyuan_v3_nextn.py` — same silent-name-drop class, different module; see Proposed fix.)
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.

### Describe the bug

HunyuanV3 (`hy_v3` / `HYV3ForCausalLM`) checkpoints name the shared expert
`model.layers.N.mlp.shared_experts.{gate,up,down}_proj.*`, but SGLang's `HYV3ForCausalLM`
model module is named **`shared_mlp`**:

```python
# sglang/srt/models/hunyuan_v3.py, HYV3MoEFused.__init__
if getattr(config, "num_shared_experts", 0) > 0:
    self.shared_mlp = HYV3FeedForward(
        hidden_size=config.hidden_size,
        intermediate_size=config.moe_intermediate_size * config.num_shared_experts,
        hidden_act=config.hidden_act,
        quant_config=quant_config,
        prefix=f"{prefix}.shared_mlp",
        reduce_results=False,
    )
```

`HYV3ForCausalLM.load_weights` has a remap for the router (`router.gate` → `gate`), but
**no remap for the shared expert**:

```python
# sglang/srt/models/hunyuan_v3.py, HYV3ForCausalLM.load_weights
for name, loaded_weight in weights:
    ...
    if "router.gate." in name:
        name = name.replace("router.", "")
    if name not in params_dict:
        continue
    param = params_dict[name]
    weight_loader = getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)
    weight_loader(param, loaded_weight)
```

Because the checkpoint's tensor names contain `.shared_experts.` and the model's parameter
dict only has entries under `.shared_mlp.`, **every shared-expert weight fails
`if name not in params_dict: continue` and is silently skipped** — no warning, no error.
`shared_mlp` stays at its randomly-initialized (effectively zero after a fresh
`nn.Parameter` allocation pattern used here) weights, so:

- `shared_mlp.gate_up_proj` outputs all-zero (or garbage) activations
- `down_proj` then FP4-quantizes a degenerate input (e.g. `amax=0` → the global scale
  `448·6/amax` blows up / degenerates)
- the shared-expert branch produces **NaN**, which propagates into the residual stream

The model **loads without any error** (the routed experts, `mlp.experts.N.*`, match
SGLang's expected names and load fine, so nothing looks wrong at load time), then crashes
on the very first forward pass (warmup or first real request) with:

```
/build/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/TensorCompare.cu:109: _assert_async_cuda_kernel:
Assertion `probability tensor contains either inf, nan or element < 0` failed.
...
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py", line 656, in sampling_from_probs_torch
    sampled_index = torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

This bug is **architecture-independent** — it is a pure weight-name mismatch, not a
kernel/quantization/hardware issue, and should reproduce on any GPU, any quant format,
any TP/PP configuration.

### How we localized it

We used SGLang's own `--debug-tensor-dump-output-folder` per-layer tensor dump to trace
the forward pass op-by-op. The dump showed, in execution order:

```
model.layers.1.mlp.shared_mlp.gate_up_proj   -> output all-zero
model.layers.1.mlp.shared_mlp.act_fn         -> output all-zero
model.layers.1.mlp.shared_mlp.down_proj      -> NaN   (first inf/nan in the whole trace)
model.layers.1.mlp.experts (routed)          -> finite
```

i.e. the routed experts computed correctly; only the shared-expert branch was broken, and
it was broken because it was never fed real weights.

### Reproduction

Serve any HunyuanV3 NVFP4 checkpoint that names the shared expert `shared_experts` (e.g.
`vroomfondel/Hy3-NVFP4-W4A4`, a ModelOpt `modelopt_fp4` export of `tencent/Hy3`):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path vroomfondel/Hy3-NVFP4-W4A4 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 --trust-remote-code \
  --tool-call-parser hunyuan --reasoning-parser hunyuan \
  --tp-size <N> --nnodes <N> --node-rank <r> --nccl-init-addr <head>:<port> \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --attention-backend triton \
  --served-model-name hy3
```

Then send a single request:

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"hy3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}],"max_tokens":8}'
```

The server loads cleanly, then crashes on this first forward with the `multinomial`
device-side assert above.

### Proposed fix

Add a name remap at the very top of the weight-loading loop in `load_weights`, mirroring
the existing `router.gate` remap, so it runs *before* the stacked
`gate_proj`/`up_proj` → `gate_up_proj` mapping (which then applies correctly to the
renamed keys):

```python
# sglang/srt/models/hunyuan_v3.py, HYV3ForCausalLM.load_weights
for name, loaded_weight in weights:
    # HunyuanV3 checkpoints name the shared expert `mlp.shared_experts.*`; this
    # model's module is `shared_mlp` — remap so the weights actually load.
    name = name.replace(".shared_experts.", ".shared_mlp.")
    ...
```

This is a pure name remap — no new logic, no shape changes. The shared-expert weights
are otherwise completely normal (same quantization scheme as the routed experts, which
already load and run correctly).

This is the **same failure class** as PR #30331 ("[Fix] Load HunyuanV3 NextN
final_layernorm into the draft head's output norm"), which fixed a silent name-mismatch
drop in `hunyuan_v3_nextn.py` (checkpoint `...final_layernorm.weight` not remapped to the
model's `shared_head.norm.weight`, dropped by the same `if name not in params_dict:
continue` fallthrough). Same file family, same silent-drop mechanism — a targeted remap
plus a small load-time regression test (assert the shared-expert params are non-null /
actually loaded) would prevent both.

**We verified this fix end-to-end:** after applying it (as a runtime patch, no
checkpoint modification), `vroomfondel/Hy3-NVFP4-W4A4` serves *coherently* — correct
multilingual generation, correct step-by-step reasoning/math, valid code generation —
on a 4× DGX Spark (GB10 / sm121) cluster at TP=4, no NaN, no garbled output. Before the
fix, every configuration that reached a forward pass (various attention/MoE/FP4-GEMM
backend combinations, EP=1 vs EP=4, TP=4 vs PP=4) hit the identical NaN — which in
hindsight makes sense, since it's a weight-loading bug, not a backend/kernel one.

### Environment

- SGLang version: 0.5.14 (custom sm121/GB10 build; the model-loading code path here is
  unmodified upstream code, not one of our patches)
- flashinfer: 0.6.14
- CUDA: 13.x
- GPU: NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark, sm121) — but as noted above, this is not an
  architecture-specific issue; it should reproduce on any GPU that can serve HunyuanV3.
- Checkpoint: `vroomfondel/Hy3-NVFP4-W4A4` (ModelOpt `modelopt_fp4` export of
  `tencent/Hy3`)

source.title: [Bug] MiMo-V2.5 multi-layer EAGLE × triton attention: draft extend step≥1 fails with kv_indices=None triton CompilationError
source.body:
### Summary

`XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` with `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --attention-backend triton` crashes during `MultiLayerEagleMultiStepDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner` capture at step≥1. The triton `extend_attention._fwd_kernel` receives `kv_indices=None` while `SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE>0` (MiMo MTP draft layers reuse the target's SWA attention), and the kernel unconditionally does `tl.load(kv_indices + ...)` in the SWA branch.

This blocks MTP on any hardware where `triton` is the only viable attention backend (e.g. SM120 / RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, where fa3 is excluded by `vision.py:963` / flash-attn #1853, and fa4 paged-KV asserts `"Paged KV not supported on SM 12.0"`).

The same model+EAGLE config works on H200 with `--attention-backend fa3` (#23811 CI, GSM8K=0.925, accept=3.36) because FA kernels use `page_table` instead of `kv_indices`.

### Environment

- Hardware: GCP `g4-standard-384`, 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM 12.0), driver 580.126.20
- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13-mimo-v2.5` (sha `983cd01`, day-0 PR #23811)
- Model: `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` (310.7B, FP8 e4m3 block-scale [128,128], 3× MTP modules with SWA attention)

### Repro

```bash
docker run --rm --runtime=nvidia --ipc=host --shm-size=250g --network=host \
  -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
  -e SGLANG_DISABLE_DEEP_GEMM=1 \
  -v /weights/MiMo-V2.5:/weights:ro \
  lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13-mimo-v2.5 \
  python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path /weights --trust-remote-code --tp 4 \
    --attention-backend triton \
    --mm-attention-backend triton_attn \
    --fp8-gemm-backend triton --ep-size 4 \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --context-length 32768 \
    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
    --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
    --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

Target model load + KV pool + target CUDA graph all succeed. Crash is during draft worker init:

```
[TP0] Capture draft extend cuda graph begin (step 2). avail mem=12.08 GB
[TP0] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../scheduler.py", line 666, in maybe_init_draft_worker
    self.draft_worker = DraftWorkerClass(**draft_worker_kwargs)
  File ".../speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py", line 172, in __init__
    self.init_cuda_graphs()
  File ".../speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py", line 213, in init_cuda_graphs
    MultiLayerEagleMultiStepDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner(self)
  File ".../speculative/multi_layer_eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py", line 426, in run_once
    ret = self.model_runner.model.forward(
  File ".../models/mimo_v2_nextn.py", line 147, in forward
    hidden_states = self.self_attn(
  File ".../models/mimo_v2.py", line 597, in forward
    attn_output = self.attn(q, k, v, forward_batch, sinks=self.attention_sink_bias)
  File ".../layers/attention/triton_backend.py", line 949, in forward_extend
    self.extend_attention_fwd(
  File ".../layers/attention/triton_ops/extend_attention.py", line 617, in extend_attention_fwd
    _fwd_kernel[grid](
triton.compiler.errors.CompilationError: at 142:16:
        if not SKIP_TILE:
            offs_kv_loc = tl.load(
                kv_indices + cur_seq_kv_start_idx + start_n + offs_n,
                ^
AttributeError("'NoneType' object has no attribute 'type'")
```

### Root cause (best understanding)

- `mimo_v2_nextn.py` MTP blocks reuse `MiMoV2Attention` from `mimo_v2.py`, which is a **SWA layer** (`sliding_window=128`, `sinks=attention_sink_bias`).
- `MultiLayerEagleMultiStepDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner` step 1/2 builds a `forward_batch` with `kv_indices=None` (draft KV is in a contiguous temp buffer, not the paged KV pool).
- `triton_ops/extend_attention.py:_fwd_kernel` enters the `SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE > 0` branch and unconditionally `tl.load(kv_indices + ...)` — there is no `kv_indices is None` guard for the "ragged extend without paged prefix" case when SWA is on.
- fa3/fa4 backends pass `page_table` instead and do not hit this codepath.

### Workarounds tried (all fail)

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| Remove `--enable-multi-layer-eagle` | No effect — server auto-sets `enable_multi_layer_eagle=True` for MiMoV2 (`Enable multi-layer EAGLE speculative decoding for MiMoV2 model`) |
| `--speculative-attention-mode decode` | No effect — `MultiLayerEagleMultiStepDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner` still captures via `forward_extend` |
| `--speculative-draft-attention-backend fa4` | Not viable on SM120 (`flash_attn/cute/interface.py:870: Paged KV not supported on SM 12.0`) |

### Cross-check: same config **without** EAGLE works

Same image/hardware/flags minus the `--speculative-*` block: `/health` OK in 150s, GSM8K-style 5/5 correct, multimodal warmup passes with `--mm-attention-backend triton_attn`. So the triton backend itself handles MiMo's diffkv(192/128) + SWA + sink correctly for the target model — the bug is specific to the multi-layer draft extend path.

### Suggested fix direction

Either (a) make `extend_attention._fwd_kernel` skip the `kv_indices` load when it is `None` (no paged prefix to attend over in draft extend step≥1), or (b) have `MultiLayerEagleMultiStepDraftExtendCudaGraphRunner` populate a dummy `kv_indices` tensor for SWA layers when building the draft extend forward batch.

Happy to test a patch on the same SM120 setup.

source.title: [Bug] DeepSeek multithreaded weight loader deadlocks on slow/networked storage (DP-attention, multiple ranks per node): CUDA driver rwlock held across mmap page-fault
source.body:
## Summary

When loading a large DeepSeek-family checkpoint with **DP-attention and multiple ranks per node** from **slow or cold/networked storage** (NFS/Lustre), the multithreaded safetensors weight loader serializes/deadlocks badly enough that one or more ranks miss the initialization barrier and the scheduler dies:

```
RuntimeError: Rank 0 scheduler died during initialization (exit code: -3).
```

On **fast local NVMe (or warm page cache)** the exact same configuration loads fine — which is why this is intermittent and cluster/storage-dependent. This is the same failure class as #7905 (Slow Model Loading on GB200: DeepSeek-R1-FP4, 30+ min, ~50% timeout), and is the load-time manifestation of the DP-attention redundant-mmap behavior that the loader's own `_prefetch_all_checkpoints` docstring already documents.

## Symptoms

- Multi-rank-per-node load (DP-attention + TP, e.g. 4 ranks/node) from networked/cold storage **stalls**; ranks fail to reach the init/NCCL barrier within `watchdog_timeout` (default 300 s) → `scheduler died (exit code -3)`.
- **Warm/local NVMe**: loads fine.
- **Single-threaded** loading: never deadlocks (just slow — and on cold NFS still exceeds the 300 s watchdog).
- `py-spy dump --native` of the stuck ranks shows worker threads blocked in the CUDA driver's `pthread_rwlock_wrlock` inside `cuMemcpyHtoDAsync`, while the source pages are being faulted in (`folio_wait_bit_common`, NFS read) — i.e. the page fault on the pageable mmap'd source happens **while the global driver lock is held**.

## Diagnosis (root cause)

The DeepSeek weight loader (`deepseek_common.do_load_weights`) submits up to 32 concurrent weight copies via `ThreadPoolExecutor()` (`maybe_executor_submit` in `srt/model_loader/utils.py`). Each worker performs an H2D copy from a **pageable, mmap-backed** CPU tensor (`safe_open(...).get_tensor()`, the default since `weight_loader_disable_mmap=False`).

`cuMemcpyHtoDAsync` (libcuda) holds a **global, process-wide driver `rwlock`** for the duration of the staged copy. When the CPU source is a pageable mmap, the copy **page-faults on the source while that lock is held**. On slow storage the fault blocks on I/O (`folio_wait_bit_common`) — so the global driver lock is held across slow I/O, and **every other loader thread (indeed every CUDA driver call in the process) serializes behind it**. With N ranks/node each independently faulting the same shards, contention compounds. Accumulated stalls exceed the init barrier / `watchdog_timeout`, and a rank is declared dead.

Key property: the multithreading provides **no** parallelism in this path — the threads serialize on the driver lock — but it converts slow-storage latency into a hard failure (barrier timeout) instead of merely a slow load.

## Fixes evaluated

| Strategy | Mechanism | Deadlock-safe | Works on NVFP4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Patch: materialize source in worker** | `.clone()` the mmap tensor in the worker → fault happens off the driver lock | **Yes (unconditional)** | Yes |
| `--weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints` | bg thread warms page cache (seq 16 MB reads), shards split across local ranks | Yes, **if prefetch stays ahead** (RAM ≥ model) | Yes |
| `--weight-loader-disable-mmap` | eager `safetensors.torch.load(read())` | (n/a) | **No — `KeyError: 'F8_E8M0'`** |
| single-thread (`max_workers=1`) | no concurrency, no lock contention | Yes | Yes (but slow; >300 s watchdog on cold NFS) |
| stage weights to local NVMe | avoids the slow fault entirely | Yes | Yes |

### Possible patch

Materialize the mmap source resident **inside the worker thread** before the copy, so the page fault happens in the worker (in parallel, **no driver lock held**); the subsequent H2D copy then reads already-resident memory and holds the lock only briefly:

```python
# srt/model_loader/utils.py, inside maybe_executor_submit
def _run_materialized(func, func_args, func_kwargs):
    def _mat(x):
        if isinstance(x, torch.Tensor) and x.device.type == "cpu":
            return x.clone()          # force the page-in here, off the CUDA driver lock
        return x
    return func(*tuple(_mat(a) for a in func_args),
                **{k: _mat(v) for k, v in (func_kwargs or {}).items()})

# replace the submit:
futures.append(executor.submit(_run_materialized, func, func_args, func_kwargs))
```

Cost: a transient per-weight clone, measured at **~1.77 GB/rank peak (~7 GB/node for 4 ranks)**, freed as each copy completes. Eliminates the deadlock unconditionally because the fault is never under the driver lock. (Note: `--weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints` is preferable when node RAM ≥ model size — see below — since it needs no patch and its memory cost is reclaimable page cache; the patch is the unconditional fallback, e.g. when the model does not fit in node RAM.)

### Notes on the existing flags

- **`--weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints`** is the best *existing* mitigation when **node RAM ≥ model size**: it warms page cache ahead of the loader and splits shards across the local ranks so the checkpoint crosses the network **once** (not N×). It neutralizes the slow fault and was fastest on cold NFS in our tests, with only reclaimable page-cache cost. Caveat: it makes the fault *fast* (cache hit) rather than moving it out from under the lock, so it relies on prefetch staying ahead; if `model > node RAM` (or storage is slower than prefetch can read), a cold fault under the lock can still occur.
- **`--weight-loader-disable-mmap`** does **not** work for NVFP4 checkpoints: it routes through `safetensors.torch.load()` which raises `KeyError: 'F8_E8M0'` (the eager deserializer does not know the E8M0 microscaling-scale dtype). It crashes during init regardless of storage.

## Benchmarks

Single GB300 node, TP4 / DP4 / EP4, DP-attention, DeepSeek-V4 NVFP4 (806 GB, 64 shards). Per-rank weight-load time from the loader's own `Load weight end. elapsed=`. Cold NFS = page cache dropped (`POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED`) before each load.

**Load time (per-rank):**

| Strategy | local NVMe (warm) | cold NFS |
|---|---|---|
| baseline multithread (current default) | 71 s | **deadlock → barrier timeout** |
| single-thread | 59 s | 537 s (> 300 s watchdog) |
| **materialize patch** | **43 s** | 264 s |
| `--weight-loader-disable-mmap` | crash (`F8_E8M0`) | crash (`F8_E8M0`) |
| **`--weight-loader-prefetch-checkpoints` (8 thr)** | 46 s | **58 s** |

**Peak host memory:**

| Strategy | anonymous RSS (4 ranks, non-reclaimable) | extra cost |
|---|---|---|
| baseline / single-thread | ~25–32 GB | mmap fault working set |
| materialize patch | ~14–24 GB | **+~1.77 GB/rank** transient clones |
| prefetch | ~23 GB (≈ baseline) | **reclaimable page cache only** |

## Environment

- **GPU system:** NVIDIA GB300 (Grace-Blackwell), 4 GPUs/node, 956 GB system RAM, 144 CPUs/node
- **GPU:** NVIDIA GB300 (~278 GB HBM/GPU), driver 590.48.01, CUDA 13.1
- **SGLang:** `0.0.0.dev1+g54143264b` (nightly cu13; image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260602-98a1b58c`)
- **torch:** 2.11.0+cu130 (cuda 13.0), **safetensors:** 0.7.0, **Python:** 3.12.3, **kernel:** 6.14.0-1013-nvidia-64k
- **Model:** DeepSeek-V4 (NVFP4 / E8M0 scales), 806 GB, 64 safetensors shards (note: model 806 GB < node RAM 956 GB, so prefetch fits fully in page cache here)
- **Storage that triggers it:** NFS-mounted checkpoint (cold). Local NVMe / warm cache does not trigger it.
- **Key server args:** `--tp-size 4 --dp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --moe-a2a-backend megamoe --attention-backend dsv4 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --context-length 4096 --trust-remote-code` (`watchdog_timeout=300`)

## Related

- #7905 — Slow Model Loading on GB200 (DeepSeek-R1-FP4: 30+ min, ~50% timeout, rank reaches monitoredBarrier but rank 0 faulty). Same failure class.
- #12663 — DeepSeek FP8 hang with DP-attention + EP (runtime, related configuration).
- The loader's own `_prefetch_all_checkpoints` docstring already describes the DP-attention redundant-mmap problem that this deadlock is the load-time manifestation of.

source.title: [Bug] compressed-tensors ignore list with .linear submodule suffix is not respected → VLM warmup crashes with mm_fp4 accepts 2d tensors
source.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English.

### Describe the bug

Loading a VLM checkpoint quantized via `compressed-tensors` (e.g., `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-NVFP4`, `cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit`) crashes during warmup, or on the first image-containing request, with:

```
ValueError: mm_fp4 accepts 2d tensors, got torch.Size([1, 2520, 576]) and torch.Size([576, 3456])
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/clippable_linear.py", line 157, in forward
  File ".../sglang/srt/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/schemes/compressed_tensors_w4a4_nvfp4.py", line 160, in apply_weights
  File ".../flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py", line 4367, in _check_mm_fp4_problem_size
```

#### Root cause

These checkpoints follow the standard VLM quantization pattern: the **language model is quantized** while the **vision tower is kept in BF16** and listed in `quantization_config.ignore`. The ignore entries include a `.linear` submodule suffix (this comes from the `CompressedLinear` wrapper that llm-compressor applies), e.g.:

```jsonc
"ignore": [
  "model.vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.linear",
  "model.vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.k_proj.linear",
  "model.vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.v_proj.linear",
  // ... 192 entries total for Gemma-4 / cyankiwi
]
```

But SGLang's Gemma-4 model uses `packed_modules_mapping` to expand a fused `qkv_proj` into shard names without the `.linear` suffix:

```
runtime layer_name:  model.vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj
ignore entry:        model.vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.linear
```

`compressed_tensors/utils.py::_is_equal_or_regex_match(check_contains=True)` only matches `target in value`. Here the target (with `.linear`) is **longer** than the value (without `.linear`), so the substring check fails one direction and the layer is **not** marked as ignored. The fused layer then gets the NVFP4 (or AWQ) quant scheme applied, and during forward the vision tower pushes 3D activations through `fp4_gemm`, which only accepts 2D tensors → crash.

vLLM avoids this entirely because it constructs the Gemma-4 vision tower via `transformers.AutoModel` (which has no awareness of vLLM's quant path); SGLang's native vision tower is the only one that exercises this code path with `.linear`-suffixed ignore entries.

### Reproduction

```bash
# venv: Python 3.12.13 + torch 2.11.0+cu130 + sglang 0.5.11 (source build of v0.5.11 tag)
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-NVFP4 \
  --attention-backend triton \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --context-length 8192 \
  --port 30000 \
  --trust-remote-code
```

The server crashes during warmup with the `mm_fp4 accepts 2d tensors` error above. Adding `--skip-server-warmup` works around the warmup crash but image requests still fail at the same point.

### Fix

The proposed fix (PR linked below) adds a path-extension match in `_is_equal_or_regex_match`: if `target` starts with `value + "."`, treat it as a match. The `.` separator prevents over-match (`q` does not match `q_proj.linear`).

- `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` loads `vision_tower.*` as BF16 (no NVFP4 path).
- Text chat works: a 19-token haiku in ~0.44 s warm on a single RTX 5090.
- Image OCR works: a synthetic invoice PNG (7 lines) round-trips through the vision tower in ~2.3 s for 105 tokens.

source.title: [Bug] Spec v2 + Mamba extra_buffer crash on v0.5.13: NoneType in set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs (H100, TP=1, EAGLE)
source.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Scheduler crashes on the spec-v2 EAGLE verify path for a Hybrid-Mamba model (Qwen3.6-27B-FP8) with:

```
TypeError: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer
```

in `set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs()`. Same function / error / root cause as #27325 (dev build, RTX PRO 6000) and #28312 (Qwen3.5-397B, TP=2), but reproduced here on a **release build + H100 + TP=1 + EAGLE**, which suggests the bug is independent of hardware, TP size, model size, and the NEXTN/EAGLE spelling.

The crash is **request-pattern dependent, not load/memory**: the server starts fine (cuda graph captured), serves normally for ~2 minutes, then crashes on a specific real request (~81k prompt tokens). It is **not an OOM** — the process exits cleanly via the SIGQUIT handler (container exitCode 0), and `nvidia-smi` was only ~75/80 GB at crash time. K8s restarts it, and it crash-loops every ~5.5 min (40 restarts in 7h).

> Note: the log is followed by a cascade of `aclose() / CancelledError / 500` from the parent process reacting to SIGQUIT — those are not the cause. The real cause is the `Scheduler hit an exception` traceback below.

### Reproduction

## Reproduction

Exact launch args (single H100 80GB, TP=1):

```bash
export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
sglang serve \
  --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 \
  --tp-size 1 \
  --max-running-requests 8 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.87 \
  --context-length 262144 \
  --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enable-metrics --log-requests --log-requests-format json
```

Then send real traffic with long prompts (ours peaks ~81k prompt tokens, low concurrency / in-flight ≤ 1). The server serves several requests successfully, then crashes within ~2 minutes.

## Traceback

```
[..] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", in run_batch
    batch_result = self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation(...)
  File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 983, in forward_batch_generation
    batch_output = self.verify(batch)
  File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 1183, in verify
    verify_input.prepare_for_v2_verify(...)
  File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_info_v2.py", line 405, in prepare_for_v2_verify
    set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs(batch)
  File ".../sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py", line 1491, in set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs
    torch.tensor(
TypeError: 'NoneType' object cannot be interpreted as an integer
[..] SIGQUIT received. signum=None, frame=None. It usually means one child failed.
```

## Root cause (matches #27325)

`req.mamba_next_track_idx` is `Optional[int] = None`, initialized to `0` by `_alloc_ping_pong_buffer()` and reset back to `None` by `free_mamba_cache()` (`mem_cache/memory_pool.py`). On the spec-v2 verify path, some reqs reach `set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs()` with the field still `None`, so `torch.tensor([req.mamba_next_track_idx for req in batch.reqs], dtype=torch.int64, ...)` raises.

This code path does **not exist in v0.5.12** — `set_mamba_track_indices_from_reqs` was added in the v0.5.12→v0.5.13 mamba + spec-v2 refactor (e.g. #27463 "topk>1 tree drafting for mamba on spec v2", #26941 "Plug mamba_extra_buffer ping-pong slot leaks", #27118 "extra_buffer lazy"). On current `main` (commit 582bd23f7, 2026-06-14) the function still has no `None` guard.

### Environment

- **SGLang: v0.5.13 (release tag)**, image `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13-cu130`
- **GPU: 1× NVIDIA H100 80GB**, TP=1
- **Model: Qwen3.6-27B-FP8** (Hybrid Mamba, FP8)
- attention_backend fa3, mamba_backend triton, page_size 1

source.title: Qwen3.5 text-only ModelOpt FP4 reaches base AttentionBackend from RadixLinearAttention
source.body:
### What happened

A ModelOpt NVFP4 Qwen3.5 text-only checkpoint loads in SGLang, but the first forward pass crashes in `RadixLinearAttention.forward()` with the base/full attention backend signature:

```text
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/radix_linear_attention.py", line 114, in forward
    return get_attn_backend().forward(
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
TypeError: AttentionBackend.forward() missing 3 required positional arguments: 'q', 'k', and 'v'
```

This looks distinct from the old two-batch-overlap `TboAttnBackend.forward()` issue: my installed source already has the `TboAttnBackend.forward(self, *args, **kwargs): return self.primary.forward(*args, **kwargs)` pass-through, and the repro below disables overlap scheduling.

### Repro command

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path /mnt/ssd2/Models/HF/Ornith-1.0-9B-Heretic-Uncensored-NVFP4-working \
  --served-model-name Ornith-Heretic-NVFP4-SGLang-AltTest \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8000 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --context-length 1024 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.30 \
  --max-running-requests 1 \
  --max-total-tokens 1024 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
  --disable-overlap-schedule \
  --attention-backend triton \
  --decode-attention-backend triton \
  --prefill-attention-backend triton \
  --linear-attn-backend triton \
  --linear-attn-decode-backend triton \
  --linear-attn-prefill-backend triton \
  --sampling-backend pytorch \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune
```

Default backend settings also hit the same `AttentionBackend.forward()` mismatch during warmup.

### Environment

```text
sglang version: 0.5.14
git revision: 58c9408
flashinfer-python: 0.6.12
torch: 2.11.0
transformers: 5.8.1
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 D, 32GB VRAM
CUDA visible device: 0
```

### Model/config details

The checkpoint is a local ModelOpt FP4 export of a Qwen3.5-style text model. The same artifact serves successfully in vLLM with `--quantization modelopt_fp4` after its ModelOpt FP4 loader handles the scale layout.

Transformers config inspection:

```text
config_class transformers.models.qwen3_5.configuration_qwen3_5.Qwen3_5TextConfig
model_type qwen3_5_text
architectures ['Qwen3_5ForCausalLM']
layer_types_first_12 ['linear_attention', 'linear_attention', 'linear_attention', 'full_attention', 'linear_attention', 'linear_attention', 'linear_attention', 'full_attention', 'linear_attention', 'linear_attention', 'linear_attention', 'full_attention']
full_attention_layer_ids None
```

### Likely root cause

`RadixLinearAttention.forward()` calls:

```python
get_attn_backend().forward(
    layer=self,
    forward_batch=forward_batch,
    mixed_qkv=mixed_qkv,
    a=a,
    b=b,
)
```

That only works when the active attention backend is `HybridLinearAttnBackend`, whose `forward()` accepts `mixed_qkv`, `a`, and `b` and dispatches to the linear attention backend.

In this run, the logs never show:

```text
Using hybrid linear attention backend for hybrid GDN models.
```

`model_runner.hybrid_gdn_config` appears to miss the text-only Qwen3.5 config. In both my installed `0.5.14` and current upstream `main` checked today, it imports/checks:

```python
Qwen3_5Config | Qwen3_5MoeConfig
```

but not the text-only classes for `model_type == "qwen3_5_text"` / `"qwen3_5_moe_text"`.

### Local experiment

I tried a minimal local experiment in `model_runner.hybrid_gdn_config`:

```python
if getattr(config, "model_type", None) in ("qwen3_5_text", "qwen3_5_moe_text"):
    return config
```

That changed the failure, which supports the backend-detection hypothesis, but it was not sufficient. The next error was during memory pool setup:

```text
File ".../sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py", line 169, in handle_max_mamba_cache
    assert config.mamba2_cache_params.mamba_cache_per_req > 0
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
AttributeError: 'Qwen3_5TextConfig' object has no attribute 'mamba2_cache_params'
```

So text-only Qwen3.5/GDN likely needs both:

1. detection/routing into `HybridLinearAttnBackend`, and
2. cache sizing/state handling that does not assume `mamba2_cache_params` exists for `Qwen3_5TextConfig`, or derives the equivalent GDN cache params from `layer_types` / Qwen3.5 config.

### Expected behavior

A `qwen3_5_text` config with `linear_attention` layers should install the hybrid linear attention backend and run ModelOpt FP4 inference, or fail early with a clear unsupported-model error instead of reaching base `AttentionBackend.forward()`.

### Additional notes

I searched issues with `qwen3_5_text radix_linear_attention AttentionBackend.forward` and did not find an exact duplicate. This is adjacent to older Qwen3.5 linear attention signature-mismatch reports, but those appear to be fixed in `v0.5.14` for the TBO path.

source.title: GLM-5.2 NVFP4 aggregated DP4 crashes with invalid sampling probabilities under long-context load
source.body:
### Summary

SGLang `main` can crash while serving `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` in aggregated DP4 mode under synthetic long-context load. This does not use disaggregation, external datasets, or any private prompt data.

The failure signature is:

- repeated `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE /workspace/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh 328`
- then `TensorCompare.cu:109 ... Assertion probability tensor contains either inf, nan or element < 0 failed`
- then scheduler crash with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`

### Artifacts

Full logs, repro script, probe JSON summary, local config-load workaround, and base64 tar.gz CUDA coredump are here:

https://gist.github.com/sshleifer/8c19b3465f284ef9cc183360deac42ba

The file to run as the client probe is `glm52_dp4_invalid_prob_probe.py` from the gist. The JSON file is not needed to reproduce; it is the machine-readable result from my run, included to record the exact probe args, success count, wall time, and client-side errors after the server crashed.

The coredump can be restored with:

```bash
base64 -d cuda_coredump_gcp15-gb300-093a-6.66085.1782503960.tar.gz.b64 > cuda_coredump_gcp15-gb300-093a-6.66085.1782503960.tar.gz
tar -xzf cuda_coredump_gcp15-gb300-093a-6.66085.1782503960.tar.gz
file cuda_coredump_gcp15-gb300-093a-6.66085.1782503960
```

`file` reports:

```text
ELF 64-bit LSB core file, NVIDIA CUDA architecture, version 1, no program header
```

### Environment

- SGLang commit: `ee77a7d3307db377682effcfe44e394edbadf0a3`
- Hardware: 4x NVIDIA GB300
- Python: `3.13.13`
- PyTorch: `2.11.0+cu130`
- Transformers: `5.8.1`
- FlashInfer: `0.6.12`
- sgl-kernel: `0.4.4`
- Model: `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4`
- Tokenizer: `zai-org/GLM-5.2`

### Local config-load workaround

On this environment, a clean checkout did not get as far as serving because Transformers rejected the public GLM config's `layer_types=["deepseek_sparse_attention", ...]`. I applied the `config_workaround.diff` in the gist so the model would load. The workaround only maps that layer type to `sparse` before constructing `GlmMoeDsaConfig`; it does not modify scheduling, sampling, attention, or kernels.

The full local workaround was:

<details>
<summary>config_workaround.diff</summary>

```diff
diff --git a/python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/config.py b/python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/config.py
index f66ea9a672..586e326434 100644
--- a/python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/config.py
+++ b/python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/config.py
@@ -60,12 +60,33 @@ class HfModelConfigParser(ModelConfigParserBase):
         revision: Optional[str] = None,
         **kwargs,
     ):
-        config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(
-            model,
-            trust_remote_code=trust_remote_code,
-            revision=revision,
-            **kwargs,
-        )
+        try:
+            config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(
+                model,
+                trust_remote_code=trust_remote_code,
+                revision=revision,
+                **kwargs,
+            )
+        except Exception as exc:
+            if "deepseek_sparse_attention" not in str(exc):
+                raise
+            from transformers import PretrainedConfig
+            from transformers.models.glm_moe_dsa.configuration_glm_moe_dsa import (
+                GlmMoeDsaConfig,
+            )
+
+            raw_config, _ = PretrainedConfig.get_config_dict(
+                model, revision=revision, **kwargs
+            )
+            if raw_config.get("architectures") != ["GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM"]:
+                raise
+            layer_types = raw_config.get("layer_types")
+            if isinstance(layer_types, list):
+                raw_config["layer_types"] = [
+                    "sparse" if x == "deepseek_sparse_attention" else x
+                    for x in layer_types
+                ]
+            config = GlmMoeDsaConfig.from_dict(raw_config)
 
         if (
             config.architectures is not None
```

</details>

### Server command

Run from the SGLang checkout with `PYTHONPATH=python`:

```bash

  --tokenizer-path zai-org/GLM-5.2 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 30000 \
  --served-model-name glm52-nvfp4-dp4-upstream \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --dp-size 4 \
  --enable-dp-attention \
  --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --load-balance-method round_robin \
  --attention-backend dsa \
  --dsa-prefill-backend trtllm \
  --dsa-decode-backend trtllm \
  --sampling-backend pytorch \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --context-length 400000 \
  --max-running-requests 256 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 8192 \
  --chunked-prefill-size -1 \
  --schedule-policy fcfs \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256 \

  --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --log-level info
```

Important parsed args from the log:

```text

### Probe command

The probe uses synthetic text only and calls `/generate`.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/work/sam/sglang_upstream/python \
python repro/glm52_dp4_invalid_prob_probe.py \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \
  --run-id upstream-glm52-dp4-fake-c256-t8-1782504221 \
  --num-examples 128 \

  --followup-words 4000 \
  --output-len 2048 \
  --temperature 1.0 \
  --request-timeout-s 1800 \
  --out-dir repro_artifacts

### Observed result

The client completed `624 / 1024` requests successfully, then the server disconnected after the scheduler crash.

The crash occurred after high KV/token pressure. Just before failure, SGLang reached token usage around `1.00` and started retracting requests:

```text

The server should either complete the requests or reject/retract requests safely under high KV pressure. It should not produce invalid sampling probabilities or crash the scheduler.

### Notes

This repro is intentionally not using disaggregation. It is aggregated DP4 (`disaggregation_mode='null'`) with public model weights and synthetic prompts.

source.title: MiniMax-M3 cookbook recommends MXFP8 on AMD MI300X, but sglang rejects mxfp8 on ROCm
source.body:
## Summary

The official cookbook page for **MiniMax-M3** recommends an **AMD Instinct (MI300X) MXFP8** deployment, but sglang hard-rejects `mxfp8` quantization on ROCm, so the documented MI300X command cannot start the server.

Cookbook: https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/MiniMax/MiniMax-M3 (section "AMD Instinct ROCm" / MI300X cell)

The MI300X cell explicitly generates a launch command with `--quantization mxfp8` and sets `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, model `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8`.

## Reproduction

- GPU: AMD Instinct **MI300X** (gfx942), 8x, `--tp 8`
- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13.post1-rocm700-mi30x` (the latest published ROCm mi30x tag)
- Model: `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` (config `quantization_config.quant_method = "mxfp8"`)

Command (the cookbook MI300X cell, verbatim flags):

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8 \
  --trust-remote-code --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto \
  --tp 8 --quantization mxfp8 --dtype bfloat16 \
  --attention-backend aiter --moe-runner-backend triton \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --watchdog-timeout 3600 --skip-server-warmup \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8300
```

## Actual behavior

Server aborts during argument parsing (before model load / warmup):

```
File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py", line 1266, in _verify_quantization
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: mxfp8 quantization is currently not supported in ROCm.
```

## Root cause

In `python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py`, `_verify_quantization()` rejects any quant not in `rocm_supported_quantization`:

```python
if is_hip() and self.quantization not in rocm_supported_quantization:
    raise ValueError(f"{self.quantization} quantization is currently not supported in ROCm.")
```

On the current `main` branch the list is:

```python
rocm_supported_quantization = [
    "awq", "gptq", "fp8", "compressed_tensors", "compressed-tensors",
    "fbgemm_fp8", "w8a8_fp8", "petit_nvfp4", "quark", "mxfp4",
    "auto-round", "quark_int4fp8_moe", "quark_mxfp4",
]
```

`mxfp8` is **not** present (only `mxfp4` is), so the gate fires unconditionally on ROCm — there is no GPU-arch exception (gfx942/gfx950) and no env-var bypass.

## Expected behavior

One of:
1. `mxfp8` is supported on ROCm (at least MI300X/MI355X) and added to `rocm_supported_quantization`, matching what the MiniMax-M3 cookbook advertises, **or**
2. The cookbook's AMD Instinct MI300X cell is corrected to a quantization that ROCm actually supports today (e.g. `mxfp4`, or the BF16 variant `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3`), so the documented command runs out of the box.

## Notes

- Latest published ROCm images top out at `v0.5.13.post1-rocm{700,720}-mi30x`. The dedicated `dev-minimax-m3` images are **CUDA-only** (`dev-cu12-minimax-m3`, `dev-cu13-minimax-m3`); there is no ROCm MiniMax-M3 dev tag.
- Reproduced with sglang `v0.5.13.post1`; the gate is identical on `main`.

## Environment

- sglang: v0.5.13.post1 (ROCm build, image `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13.post1-rocm700-mi30x`)
- Hardware: 8x AMD Instinct MI300X (gfx942)
- ROCm: 7.0
