source.title: [Performance Regression] ~2x throughput drop in disaggregated PD mode with Wide-EP (DeepSeek-R1 FP4, GB200) between SGLang v0.5.8 and latest nightly
source.body:
## Summary

We observed a significant performance regression in **Wide-EP prefill-decode disaggregated serving** for DeepSeek-R1 (FP4, GB200 NVL72) between SGLang `v0.5.8` (Jan 2026) and the `dev` container (April 1 2026) (The issue should be already existing with sglang-TOT 3.18 according to @nvcastet). At high concurrency (≥2048), throughput drops by ~2x and TTFT increases dramatically. We include detailed worker-level log metrics below for further analysis.

## Environment

- **Hardware**: NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 (partition `gb200`, 12 nodes: 4 prefill + 8 decode, 48 GPUs total)
- **Model**: DeepSeek-R1, FP4 quantization (`modelopt_fp4`), `kv-cache-dtype: fp8_e4m3`, `attention-backend: trtllm_mla`
- **Disaggregation**: Prefill-Decode disagg with NIXL transfer backend
- **Prefill**: TP=4, DP=4, EP=4 per node (4 workers, 1 per node)
- **Decode**: TP=32, DP=32, EP=32 across 8 nodes (1 worker spanning all 8 nodes)
- **Frontend**: Dynamo with 10 frontends (1 + 9 additional), NGINX load balancer
- **Benchmark**: `sa-bench`, ISL=1024, OSL=1024, concurrencies 512/2048/4096/8192

## Baseline Data

@nvcastet  provided two benchmark runs with identical hardware and config, differing only in SGLang/Dynamo version:

### "Good" Run — SGLang v0.5.8 + Dynamo 0.8.1 (2026-03-12)

- Container: `dev-sglang:v0.5.8-cu130.sqsh`
- Dynamo: 0.8.1

| Concurrency | Output Throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean ITL (ms) | Mean E2EL (ms) |
|-------------|--------------------------|----------------|----------------|---------------|-----------------|
| 512         | **33,070**               | **856**        | 13.96          | 680           | 13,720          |
| 2048        | **106,783**              | **1,301**      | 16.99          | 828           | 16,955          |
| 4096        | **151,238**              | **4,560**      | 21.23          | 1,034         | 24,096          |
| 8192        | **138,218**              | **32,847**     | 21.79          | 1,061         | 52,904          |

### "Bad" Run — SGLang `dev-0318` + Dynamo 1.0.0 (2026-03-30)

- Container: `lmsysorg/sglang:dev` (around Mar 18 nightly dev build with a perf fix: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21771)
- Dynamo: 1.0.0 (installed via `dynamo.sh` setup script, `ai_dynamo-1.0.0` and some fixes)

| Concurrency | Output Throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean ITL (ms) | Mean E2EL (ms) |
|-------------|--------------------------|----------------|----------------|---------------|-----------------|
| 512         | 32,458                   | 924            | 14.15          | 689           | 13,962          |
| 2048        | 72,635 (**-32%**)        | 10,215 (**+7.9x**) | 15.69     | 764           | 24,673          |
| 4096        | 74,379 (**-51%**)        | 33,648 (**+7.4x**) | 15.84     | 771           | 48,226          |
| 8192        | 75,507 (**-45%**)        | 80,042 (**+2.4x**) | 16.07     | 783           | 94,839          |

**Key observation**: At concurrency ≥2048, throughput is cut roughly in half and TTFT explodes. At concurrency=512 performance is similar, suggesting the issue is related to scheduling/transfer under load, not raw compute.

## Reproduction Results

We reproduced using the same recipe config on the same hardware.

### Run 1: SGLang `dev-0401` (nightly Apr 1) + Dynamo source `38b9936` (≈1.0.0+)

Our verification run using a more recent nightly container (`dev-0401`, Apr 1). Results closely track Nicolas's "bad" (`dev-0318`) numbers, confirming the regression persists:

| Concurrency | Output Throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) |
|-------------|--------------------------|----------------|----------------|
| 512         | 28,861                   | 1,854          | 14.18          |
| 2048        | 63,699                   | 11,058         | 15.57          |
| 4096        | 69,767                   | 31,161         | 15.95          |
| 8192        | 72,335                   | 73,302         | 15.95          |

### Run 2: SGLang `v0.5.8` + Dynamo `0.8.1` (pip)

Exact version match with Nicolas's "good" setup. **Performance matches the "good" baseline**:

| Concurrency | Output Throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) |
|-------------|--------------------------|----------------|----------------|
| 512         | 29,796                   | 1,873          | 14.03          |
| 2048        | 88,601                   | 2,843          | 17.71          |
| 4096        | 131,592                  | 5,285          | 22.25          |
| 8192        | 154,354                  | 21,687         | 23.58          |

### Run 3: SGLang `dev-0401` + Dynamo source + Mooncake transfer backend

Tried switching `disaggregation-transfer-backend: mooncake` to rule out NIXL-specific issues. Results are similar to Run 1 (NIXL), no improvement:

| Concurrency | Output Throughput (tok/s) | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean ITL (ms) | Mean E2EL (ms) |
|-------------|--------------------------|----------------|----------------|---------------|-----------------|
| 512         | 28,784                   | 1,856          | 14.20          | 692           | 14,945          |
| 2048        | 63,304                   | 11,365         | 15.63          | 761           | 25,763          |
| 4096        | 68,865                   | 31,827         | 15.86          | 772           | 46,435          |
| 8192        | 72,227                   | 73,570         | 16.04          | 781           | 88,338          |

Mooncake prefill logs show even higher `#inflight-req` (27-30) and `token usage` (0.32-0.35) compared to NIXL Run 1 (17-18 and 0.25-0.26). Decode `gen throughput` and `#running-req` are comparable to Run 1 (~2,400-2,550 tok/s, 35-43 running).

## Worker-Level Log Metrics Comparison

We extracted detailed per-worker metrics from our own reproduction runs (Run 1: `dev-0401` and Run 2: `v0.5.8`) during steady-state (concurrency=4096 phase) to compare behavior.

### Prefill Worker Logs

**v0.5.8 (good)**:
```
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 18, #new-token: 16384, token usage: 0.13, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 79,  #inflight-req: 0, input throughput: 12,118 tok/s
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 18, #new-token: 16384, token usage: 0.13, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 61,  #inflight-req: 0, input throughput: 12,428 tok/s
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 18, #new-token: 16384, token usage: 0.13, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 44,  #inflight-req: 0, input throughput: 12,172 tok/s
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 19, #new-token: 16384, token usage: 0.13, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 26,  #inflight-req: 0, input throughput: 12,467 tok/s
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 19, #new-token: 16384, token usage: 0.13, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 6,   #inflight-req: 0, input throughput: 13,203 tok/s
```

**dev-0401 (bad)**:
```
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 18, #new-token: 16384, token usage: 0.26, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 295, #inflight-req: 17, input throughput: 19,508 tok/s
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 18, #new-token: 16384, token usage: 0.25, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 278, #inflight-req: 17, input throughput: 19,605 tok/s
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 18, #new-token: 16384, token usage: 0.25, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 243, #inflight-req: 17, input throughput: 19,691 tok/s
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 19, #new-token: 16384, token usage: 0.26, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 191, #inflight-req: 18, input throughput: 19,750 tok/s
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 18, #new-token: 16384, token usage: 0.25, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 156, #inflight-req: 17, input throughput: 19,739 tok/s
```

| Metric | v0.5.8 (good) | dev-0401 (bad) |
|--------|---------------|----------------|
| `#inflight-req` | **0** (consistently) | **17-18** (consistently) |
| `token usage` | 0.12-0.13 | 0.25-0.26 (2x higher) |
| `input throughput` | 12,100-14,800 tok/s | 19,500-20,100 tok/s |
| `#queue-req` | 0-96 | 35-295 |

Note: The prefill side actually shows *higher* raw input throughput in the bad case, while `#inflight-req` remains persistently at 17-18 (vs 0 in the good case). The `token usage` is also 2x higher in the bad case.

### Decode Worker Logs

**v0.5.8 (good)**:
```
Decode batch, #running-req: 122, #token: 296448, token usage: 0.09, #transfer-req: 132, gen throughput: 5,065 tok/s
Decode batch, #running-req: 143, #token: 308096, token usage: 0.10, #transfer-req: 114, gen throughput: 5,668 tok/s
Decode batch, #running-req: 156, #token: 317248, token usage: 0.10, #transfer-req: 101, gen throughput: 5,772 tok/s
Decode batch, #running-req: 166, #token: 293120, token usage: 0.09, #transfer-req:  61, gen throughput: 5,700 tok/s
Decode batch, #running-req: 153, #token: 244544, token usage: 0.08, #transfer-req:  32, gen throughput: 5,874 tok/s
Decode batch, #running-req:  77, #token: 128320, token usage: 0.04, #transfer-req:   0, gen throughput: 5,680 tok/s
```

**dev-0401 (bad)**:
```
Decode batch, #running-req: 40, #token: 212096, token usage: 0.07, #transfer-req: 165, gen throughput: 2,588 tok/s
Decode batch, #running-req: 38, #token: 210816, token usage: 0.07, #transfer-req: 164, gen throughput: 2,449 tok/s
Decode batch, #running-req: 38, #token: 171264, token usage: 0.05, #transfer-req: 125, gen throughput: 2,390 tok/s
Decode batch, #running-req: 40, #token:  98048, token usage: 0.03, #transfer-req:  43, gen throughput: 2,409 tok/s
Decode batch, #running-req: 36, #token:  51712, token usage: 0.02, #transfer-req:   2, gen throughput: 2,368 tok/s
```

| Metric | v0.5.8 (good) | dev-0401 (bad) |
|--------|---------------|----------------|
| `#running-req` | **77-166** | **36-44** (~3-4x fewer) |
| `gen throughput` (per DP shard) | **4,997-5,874 tok/s** | **2,368-2,588 tok/s** (~2.3x lower) |
| `#transfer-req` (peak) | 132 → drains to 0 | 165 → drains slower |
| `token usage` | 0.04-0.10 | 0.02-0.07 |

## Bisection Attempts

We attempted to bisect the regression window between v0.5.8 (Jan 23) and dev-0401 (Apr 1):

| SGLang Version | Release Date | Dynamo Version | Result |
|----------------|-------------|----------------|--------|
| **v0.5.8**     | Jan 23      | 0.8.1          | ✅ Good performance |
| nightly-0213   | Feb 13      | 0.9.0          | ❌ `Overflow when unpacking long long` in `disaggregation/utils.py:set_buf` |
| nightly-0213   | Feb 13      | 0.9.1          | ❌ Same overflow error |
| nightly-0213   | Feb 13      | 1.0.0          | ❌ `Engine.async_generate() got unexpected keyword argument 'return_routed_experts'` |
| **v0.5.9**     | Feb 24      | 0.8.1          | ❌ NATS routing broken (requests never reach workers) |
| v0.5.9         | Feb 24      | 0.9.0          | ❌ NATS routing broken |
| v0.5.9         | Feb 24      | 0.9.1          | ❌ NATS routing broken |
| v0.5.9         | Feb 24      | **1.0.0**      | ✅ Runs but prefill worker crashed mid-benchmark (TRT-LLM cutlass kernel error) |
| **dev-0401**   | Apr 1       | source (≈1.0.0+) | ✅ Runs but **degraded performance** (≈Nicolas "bad") |

**Findings**:
- SGLang v0.5.9 requires Dynamo ≥1.0.0 to even route requests (NATS protocol change)
- The `nightly-0213` container is incompatible with all available Dynamo versions
- The regression window is between **v0.5.8 (Jan 23)** and **v0.5.9 (Feb 24)**, approximately 1 month

## Discussion

Notable observations from the worker-level metrics:

1. **Prefill `#inflight-req`**: Persistently 17-18 in the bad case vs 0 in the good case. This indicates that in the bad case, completed prefill requests are waiting rather than being immediately handed off.

2. **Prefill `token usage`**: 2x higher in the bad case (0.25-0.26 vs 0.12-0.13), consistent with more KV data being held in prefill worker memory (i.e., completed prefills not yet transferred out).

3. **Prefill `input throughput`**: Actually *higher* in the bad case (19,500-20,100 vs 12,100-14,800 tok/s). The prefill compute itself appears faster or at least comparable.

4. **Decode `#running-req`**: Only 36-44 in the bad case vs 77-166 in the good case. The decode worker has far fewer active requests generating tokens.

5. **Decode `gen throughput`**: ~2,400-2,600 tok/s in the bad case vs ~5,000-5,800 tok/s in the good case (per-DP-shard). The lower running request count directly reduces decode throughput.

6. **Transfer backend**: Switching from NIXL to Mooncake did not improve the situation, suggesting the bottleneck is not specific to the transfer backend implementation.

7. **Concurrency dependence**: At concurrency=512, performance is similar between good and bad. The degradation appears at concurrency ≥2048, suggesting the issue is related to behavior under high load rather than per-request overhead.

These metrics point to a change somewhere in the disaggregation data path between SGLang v0.5.8 (Jan 23) and v0.5.9 (Feb 24). The exact root cause has not been identified. Possible areas to investigate:
- Changes to `sglang/srt/disaggregation/` between Jan 23 and Feb 24
- KV transfer scheduling or queuing logic
- Prefill-to-decode handoff mechanism
- Connection management under high concurrency

<!-- ## Additional Issue: `sa-bench` Tokenizer Bug (Separate, Fixed)

During initial debugging, we discovered that `sa-bench` (the benchmark client) was generating inflated token counts for DeepSeek-R1 due to a `transformers` v5 bug: `LlamaTokenizerFast` overwrites the true `ByteLevel` pre_tokenizer for DeepSeek-R1, causing ~6x token inflation (6116 tokens for a 1024-token prompt). This was fixed by porting SGLang's `_fix_v5_tokenizer_components()` to `sa-bench`. **This is a client-side bug only and does not affect the performance regression.** -->

## Setup Details

### Recipe Config (YAML)

```yaml
model:
  path: dsfp4                    # DeepSeek-R1 FP4 checkpoint
  precision: fp4

resources:
  gpu_type: gb200
  prefill_nodes: 4
  decode_nodes: 8
  prefill_workers: 4             # 1 per prefill node
  decode_workers: 1              # 1 spanning all 8 decode nodes
  gpus_per_node: 4

frontend:
  type: dynamo
  enable_multiple_frontends: true
  num_additional_frontends: 9    # 10 total frontends
  nginx_container: nginx

backend:
  sglang_config:
    prefill:
      tp-size: 4
      dp-size: 4
      ep-size: 4
      attention-backend: trtllm_mla
      quantization: modelopt_fp4
      kv-cache-dtype: fp8_e4m3
      disaggregation-mode: prefill
      disaggregation-transfer-backend: nixl
      mem-fraction-static: 0.84
      max-total-tokens: 131072
      max-prefill-tokens: 32768
      chunked-prefill-size: 65536
      disable-cuda-graph: true
      enable-dp-attention: true
      enable-single-batch-overlap: true
      disable-radix-cache: true

    decode:
      tp-size: 32
      dp-size: 32
      ep-size: 32
      attention-backend: trtllm_mla
      quantization: modelopt_fp4
      kv-cache-dtype: fp8_e4m3
      disaggregation-mode: decode
      disaggregation-transfer-backend: nixl
      mem-fraction-static: 0.83
      max-total-tokens: 3122380
      max-running-requests: 67584
      moe-a2a-backend: deepep
      deepep-mode: low_latency
      ep-dispatch-algorithm: static
      ep-num-redundant-experts: 32
      enable-dp-attention: true
      enable-dp-lm-head: true

benchmark:
  type: sa-bench
  isl: 1024
  osl: 1024
  concurrencies: 512x2048x4096x8192
  req_rate: inf
```

### Key Environment Variables

```
SGLANG_NVFP4_CKPT_FP8_GEMM_IN_ATTN=1
SGLANG_PER_TOKEN_GROUP_QUANT_8BIT_V2=1
SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_HEARTBEAT_MAX_FAILURE=100000
SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=100000
SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT=100000
SGLANG_MOONCAKE_CUSTOM_MEM_POOL=True
SGLANG_USE_MESSAGE_QUEUE_BROADCASTER=0
SGLANG_DISABLE_TP_MEMORY_INBALANCE_CHECK=1
# Decode-only:
SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024
SGLANG_MOE_NVFP4_DISPATCH=1
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use the recipe config above with SGLang `v0.5.8` container + Dynamo `0.8.1` → observe good performance
2. Use the same config with SGLang `dev-0401` (or any recent nightly) + latest Dynamo → observe ~2x throughput drop at concurrency ≥2048
3. Check decode worker logs for `#transfer-req` — it will be high (15-20+) in the bad case vs 0-1 in the good case

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected**: Performance should be at least as good as v0.5.8 (or better with optimizations)
- **Actual**: ~2x throughput regression at high concurrency, ~8x TTFT increase at concurrency=2048

source.title: Quality regression (LLM-as-judge scores) after upgrading from 0.5.9 to 0.5.10rc0 with Qwen3.5-27B-FP8 on Blackwell SM120
source.body:
After upgrading from sglang 0.5.9 to 0.5.10rc0, I'm observing a significant quality regression when serving Qwen3.5-27B-FP8. My internal LLM-as-judge evaluation pipeline (which runs independently of sglang and Qwen3.5-27B-FP8) shows roughly a 20% relative drop in scores. The issue is reproducible: rolling back to 0.5.9 with identical configuration restores previous quality levels. All sampling parameters, model weights, and evaluation prompts remain unchanged between versions.

GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, Driver Version: 575.64.03, CUDA Version: 12.9.

source.title: [flackci] Intermittent segfault in Triton MoE kernel during piecewise CUDA graph warmup on B200
source.body:
## Description

During piecewise CUDA graph warmup compilation for `lmsys/gpt-oss-120b-bf16` (4-GPU) on B200, a segmentation fault occurs in the Triton NVIDIA driver backend while executing the fused MoE experts kernel.

The crash happens at ~93% of the "Compiling num tokens" phase (69/74 iterations).

## Error Stack Trace

```
Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault

Current thread (most recent call first):
  File "triton/backends/nvidia/driver.py", line 668 in inner
  File "triton/backends/nvidia/driver.py", line 712 in __call__
  File "triton/runtime/jit.py", line 757 in run
  File "triton_kernels/matmul_ogs.py", line 467 in matmul_ogs
  File "sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/triton_kernels_moe.py", line 306 in triton_kernel_fused_experts_with_bias
  File "sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_kernels.py", line 115 in run
  File "sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/runner.py", line 117 in run
  File "sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py", line 423 in forward_cuda
  File "sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1034 in run_moe_core
  File "sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1013 in forward_impl
  File "sglang/srt/models/gpt_oss.py", line 269 in moe_impl
  ...
  File "sglang/srt/model_executor/piecewise_cuda_graph_runner.py", line 406 in warmup_compile
  File "sglang/srt/model_executor/piecewise_cuda_graph_runner.py", line 309 in __init__
  File "sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 2450 in init_piecewise_cuda_graphs
```

## Environment

- **GPU**: NVIDIA B200
- **Model**: `lmsys/gpt-oss-120b-bf16` (TP=4)
- **Attention backend**: `trtllm_mha`
- **CI job**: `stage-c-test-4-gpu-b200 (0)` in [PR Test run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/23680918199/attempts/7?pr=19915)

## Analysis

The segfault originates in the Triton NVIDIA driver backend (`triton/backends/nvidia/driver.py:668`) during JIT compilation/execution of the MoE `matmul_ogs` kernel. This appears to be a Triton + B200 (SM100) driver-level issue during CUDA graph warmup.

source.title: [Bug] Eagle V2 speculative decoding crashes with NaN in logits when radix cache prefix hit occurs (SM120 / 8 * RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell)
source.body:
## Environment

| Component | Version |
|-----------|---------|
| Container | `lmsysorg/sglang:glm5-blackwell` (sha256:968b8bc5f67c) |
| Model | [festr2/GLM-5-NVFP4-MTP](https://huggingface.co/festr2/GLM-5-NVFP4-MTP) |
| GPU | 8× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96GB (SM120, TP=8) |
| CUDA | 12.9.1 |
| Quantization | modelopt_fp4 |
| KV cache dtype | bfloat16 (auto-set by server_args.py for DSA on SM12) |
| Speculative algorithm | NEXTN (mapped to EAGLE / eagle_worker_v2) |

## Launch command
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /model \
  --served-model-name GLM-5 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype auto \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --attention-backend flashinfer \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --enable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \
  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN \
  --speculative-num-steps 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 1 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.92 \
  --max-running-requests 8 \
  --enable-nan-detection \
  --watchdog-timeout 600
```
(env: `SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=True`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=0`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_DEEP_GEMM=0`)

## Bug description

Server starts successfully, CUDA graphs captured, speculative decoding works fine on the **first requests** (accept rate ~0.85–0.94, ~50 tok/s).

Crash occurs **consistently** when a subsequent request hits the **radix cache prefix** (`#cached-token > 0`). On the first such request, `eagle_worker_v2.py` raises `NaN in the logits` and all TP workers crash simultaneously.

## Crash traceback
```
[2026-03-03 18:14:33 TP1] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 3076, in run_scheduler_process
    scheduler.event_loop_overlap()
  File ".../scheduler.py", line 1123, in event_loop_overlap
    batch_result = self.run_batch(batch)
  File ".../scheduler.py", line 2279, in run_batch
    batch_result = self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation(...)
  File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 675, in forward_batch_generation
    batch_output = self.verify(model_worker_batch)
  File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py", line 765, in verify
    detect_nan(logits_output)
  File ".../sglang/srt/speculative/spec_utils.py", line 713, in detect_nan
    raise ValueError("Detected errors during sampling! NaN in the logits.")
ValueError: Detected errors during sampling! NaN in the logits.
```
(all 8 TP workers crash at the same timestamp)

## Reproduction pattern

The crash is **100% reproducible** with this sequence:

1. Send request A (input ~200 tokens) → completes normally, accept_rate ~0.9
2. Send request B (input ~3000 tokens, no cache overlap) → completes normally
3. Send request C (input ~4400 tokens, **overlaps with previous context → `#cached-token=2688`**) → **crash on step 2 of decode**

Log line immediately before crash:
```
Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 1792, #cached-token: 2688, ...
Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #token: 4480, accept len: 1.82, accept rate: 0.91, ...
Decode batch, #running-req: 1, #token: 4544, accept len: 1.75, accept rate: 0.88, ...
→ CRASH
```

## Key observation

**Without speculative decoding** (same hardware, same model, same NSA patches) the server is fully stable:
- Handled 15,000+ token contexts without issues
- No NaN, no crashes across dozens of requests

This strongly suggests the bug is in **Eagle V2 verify path when processing a batch where KV cache was partially populated from radix cache prefix**, not in the base model or attention backend.

## Additional context

- SM120 (Blackwell) requires several patches to run GLM-5-NVFP4-MTP:
  - KV cache dtype forced to bfloat16 (fp8_e4m3 unsupported for DSA on SM12)
  - NSA backends patched from `flashmla_sparse`/`trtllm` → `flashinfer` (SM90/SM100-only backends produce NaN on SM120)
  - DeepGemm disabled (`SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=0`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_DEEP_GEMM=0`) — separate numerical instability issue on Blackwell
- `speculative_algorithm` is set to `NEXTN` in CLI but gets mapped to `EAGLE` internally with `draft_model_path = target_model_path` (MTP heads reused)
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=True` is required, otherwise NEXTN falls back silently to non-v2 Eagle and loads the full model twice → OOM

## Workaround

Disabling speculative decoding entirely resolves the crash. Running without MTP: **~33 tok/s**. With MTP (before crash): **~50 tok/s**, accept_rate 0.80–0.94.

Would be happy to provide full logs or test patches. This hardware (SM120) is fully available for testing.

source.body:

### Describe the bug

Running NVFP4 quantized models (e.g., `vincentzed-hf/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`) on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) produces NaN outputs and garbage generation.

### Reproduction

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path vincentzed-hf/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --port 8000 \
  --attention-backend triton \
  --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass
```
```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "qwen3.5", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}], "max_tokens": 50}'
```

**Result:** NaN in logits, model outputs garbage

### Environment

| Component | Version |

| GPU | NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (8x, 96GB each) |
| Compute Capability | SM 12.0 |
| SGLang | 0.4.7+ (vz/qwen3-5 branch) |

### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.

- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

There are multiple issues in the same ticket, but they all relate to speculative decoding not working or causing crash. The test script includes 4 variants in total: json_object and json_schema both with reasoning disabled and enabled. 

There are several relevant issues about spec v2/overlap and structured outputs: #11762 #15623 

Hardware: 8xH200 nodes
SGLang versions tested 0.5.6.post2 and 0.5.7

First issue
- DeepSeek V3.1 PD disaggregated serving decode node crashing almost instantly under high load. This crash does not appear with the test script, only under production workload (long context, varying use of structured outputs)
- DeepSeek V3.1 single node (TP8) deployment - works as expected and does not crash under production workload

source.title: NaN in hidden states with modelopt_fp4 quantization under concurrent load (GLM-5-NVFP4-MTP on Blackwell)
source.body:
## Summary

GLM-5-NVFP4-MTP with `--quantization modelopt_fp4` produces **NaN values in model hidden states** under concurrent request load, causing `torch.multinomial` to crash with `probability tensor contains either inf, nan or element < 0`. 

This is **not** related to speculative decoding, radix cache, or any specific attention backend — the NaN originates directly from the model's transformer layers.

## Environment

- **Hardware**: 8× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, 96GB each)
- **Model**: GLM-5-NVFP4-MTP (`--quantization modelopt_fp4`)
- **SGLang**: Built from `main` (commit `346a4131cfbac5`)
- **PyTorch**: 2.7+ (nightly, Blackwell support)
- **Docker**: Custom image based on `nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:25.03-py3`
- **CUDA**: 12.8+

## Launch command

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /mnt/GLM-5-NVFP4-MTP \
  --tp 8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --attention-backend flashinfer \
  --moe-runner-backend cutlass \
  --kv-cache-dtype bf16 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --enable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.88 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5000 \
  --served-model-name glm-5 \
  --max-running-requests 64 \
  --enable-metrics
```

## Reproducer

The bug requires **concurrent requests** — serial requests don't trigger it. Save this as `test_nan_concurrent.py`:

```python
"""
Concurrent reproducer for NaN crash with modelopt_fp4 quantization.

Sends bursts of 64 concurrent requests with a shared prefix.
Typically crashes within 2-5 rounds without --enable-nan-detection.

Usage:
    python3 test_nan_concurrent.py --url http://localhost:5000 --concurrency 64
"""

import argparse, json, sys, time, requests
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed

def send(base, prefix, suffix, model, i):
    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prefix + suffix}],
        "max_tokens": 64,
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }
    try:
        r = requests.post(f"{base}/v1/chat/completions", json=payload, timeout=180)
        r.raise_for_status()
        return i, True, ""
    except Exception as e:
        return i, False, str(e)[:200]

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--url", default="http://localhost:5000")
    parser.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=64)
    parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=0, help="0=infinite")
    parser.add_argument("--model", default="glm-5")
    parser.add_argument("--prefix-repeat", type=int, default=60)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    prefix = (
        "You are an expert assistant specializing in science, technology, "
        "and history. You provide detailed, accurate, and well-structured "
        "answers. Always cite relevant facts and provide context. "
    ) * args.prefix_repeat

    suffixes = [
        "Explain the theory of general relativity in simple terms.",
        "What caused the fall of the Roman Empire?",
        "How do mRNA vaccines work?",
        "Describe the process of nuclear fusion in stars.",
        "What are the main differences between TCP and UDP?",
        "Explain quantum entanglement to a 10-year-old.",
        "What is the significance of the Turing test?",
        "How does photosynthesis work at the molecular level?",
    ]

    # Flush cache and seed
    try:
        requests.post(f"{args.url}/flush_cache", timeout=30)
    except:
        pass
    time.sleep(0.5)
    send(args.url, prefix, "Say hello.", args.model, 0)
    print(f"Running bursts of {args.concurrency} concurrent requests...")

    rnd = 0
    max_rounds = args.rounds if args.rounds > 0 else float("inf")
    t0 = time.monotonic()

    while rnd < max_rounds:
        rnd += 1
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.concurrency) as pool:
            futs = [
                pool.submit(send, args.url, prefix, suffixes[i % len(suffixes)], args.model, i)
                for i in range(args.concurrency)
            ]
            fails = sum(1 for f in as_completed(futs) if not f.result()[1])
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
        if fails:
            print(f"Round {rnd}: {fails}/{args.concurrency} FAILED after {elapsed:.0f}s")
            print("Check server logs for NaN tracebacks.")
            sys.exit(1)
        if rnd % 10 == 0:
            print(f"Round {rnd}: OK ({elapsed:.0f}s)")

    print(f"Completed {rnd} rounds without crash in {time.monotonic()-t0:.0f}s")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## Crash traceback

```
/pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/TensorCompare.cu:109: _assert_async_cuda_kernel: block: [0,0,0], thread: [0,0,0]
Assertion `probability tensor contains either `inf`, `nan` or element < 0` failed.

    batch_result = self.run_batch(batch)
  File "scheduler.py", line 2370, in run_batch
    batch_result = self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation(...)
  File "tp_worker.py", line 500, in forward_batch_generation
    batch_result.next_token_ids = self.model_runner.sample(...)
  File "model_runner.py", line 2570, in sample
    next_token_ids = self.sampler(...)
  File "sampler.py", line 161, in forward
    batch_next_token_ids = self._sample_from_probs(...)
  File "sampler.py", line 202, in _sample_from_probs
    batch_next_token_ids = sampling_from_probs_torch(...)
  File "sampler.py", line 600, in sampling_from_probs_torch
    sampled_index = torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
```

## Root cause analysis

We instrumented the code with synchronous NaN checks at multiple stages to trace exactly where NaN originates:

### 1. NaN comes from model hidden_states, NOT from sampling/softmax

We added a NaN check in `DeepseekV2ForCausalLM.forward()` (which `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` inherits) before `logits_processor`:

```
!!! DS_MODEL hidden_states NaN before logits_processor: 1007616/7403520 elements, shape=torch.Size([1205, 6144])
```

**~13.6% of hidden state elements are NaN** in affected batches. This is not a single-token numerical edge case — entire sequences within the batch have NaN hidden states.

### 2. NaN propagates through the pipeline

```
hidden_states (NaN) → lm_head matmul → logits (NaN) → softmax → probs (NaN) → multinomial → CRASH
```

### 3. It's NOT related to speculative decoding

Crash reproduces identically **without** any speculative decoding args (`--speculative-eagle-model` etc. removed).

### 4. It's NOT related to radix cache

Crash reproduces with `--disable-radix-cache`.

### 5. High concurrency is required

- **Serial requests**: 50+ rounds, no crash
- **8 concurrent**: Crashes after ~5 runs of the reproducer
- **64 concurrent**: Crashes within 2-5 rounds consistently

This suggests the NaN may be related to batch size / memory access patterns rather than a cache race condition.

### 6. `--enable-nan-detection` is an effective workaround

With `--enable-nan-detection`, the sampler replaces NaN logits with `-1e5` (effectively zero probability after softmax). The affected tokens are simply not selected.

**Stress test result with `--enable-nan-detection`:**
- 200 rounds × 64 concurrent requests = **12,800 requests over 21 minutes — ZERO crashes**
- 3,136 NaN detections were logged during this run (NaN still occurs but is handled gracefully)

## What we investigated (not the cause)

| Hypothesis | Result |
|---|---|
| Speculative decoding (EAGLE-v2) | ❌ Crashes without spec decoding |
| Radix cache prefix hit race | ❌ Crashes with `--disable-radix-cache` |
| Softmax numerical instability | ❌ NaN already present before softmax |
| Temperature division by zero | ❌ Temperature is 0.7 (valid) |
| top_k/top_p renormalization | ❌ NaN present before these are called |
| `SGLANG_SPEC_NAN_DETECTION=1` | ⚠️ Uses `torch._assert_async` — same generic CUDA assert message, doesn't help isolate the source |

## Likely root cause

The NaN originates in the **transformer layers** of the model with `modelopt_fp4` quantization. With 13.6% of hidden state elements being NaN in affected batches, this points to:

1. **FP4 dequantization numerical instability** under specific input patterns that only manifest with larger batch sizes
2. **Possible race condition in quantized weight access** when multiple sequences are processed concurrently
3. **Kernel-level issue** in the cutlass MoE runner or attention computation with FP4 weights

## Workaround

Add `--enable-nan-detection` to the launch command. This replaces NaN logits with `-1e5` before sampling, preventing the crash. Quality impact appears minimal since the NaN tokens receive ~0 probability and valid tokens are selected instead.

## Related

- #19796 — Similar NaN crash report (initially attributed to radix cache + EAGLE-v2, but root cause is deeper)
- PR #19897 — Zero-fill draft KV for cached prefix (does not fix this issue)

source.title: [Feature] Auto-fallback from DeepGemm when checkpoint scale_fmt is not ue8m0
source.body:
### Checklist
- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

When SGLang auto-enables DeepGemm on Blackwell and detects that the checkpoint's scale format is not `ue8m0`, it logs a warning but proceeds anyway:

```
WARNING model_config.py: DeepGemm is enabled but the scale_fmt of checkpoint is not ue8m0.
This might cause accuracy degradation on Blackwell.
```

The "accuracy degradation" described in the warning is severe enough to cause **CUDA crashes under load** — `device-side assert triggered` (NaN/Inf in probability tensor) or `illegal instruction` at concurrency ≥ 64.

**Suggested fix:** When `fp4_gemm_runner_backend == 'auto'` and the checkpoint's `scale_fmt != ue8m0`, SGLang should automatically fall back to a non-DeepGemm backend (e.g., `flashinfer_cutlass`) instead of enabling DeepGemm with an incompatible checkpoint. The current warning should be upgraded to an automatic fallback with an info-level log message explaining why DeepGemm was not used.

This class of bug affects multiple models on Blackwell — see #16816, #16595, #20375. In each case users had to manually discover and set `--fp4-gemm-backend` or `--fp8-gemm-backend` as a workaround (which currently doesn't even work for FP4 — see #20775).

### Reproduction

```bash
# Any NVFP4 checkpoint with non-ue8m0 scale format on any Blackwell GPU
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000

# Run benchmark at concurrency >= 64 to trigger crash
```

source.title: [Bug] --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass does not disable DeepGemm on Blackwell
source.body:
### Checklist
- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Setting `--fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass` does not prevent DeepGemm from being enabled on Blackwell GPUs. The flag is correctly parsed (`fp4_gemm_runner_backend='flashinfer_cutlass'` in server args), but DeepGemm is still activated — the following warning appears 4 times during startup:

```
WARNING model_config.py: DeepGemm is enabled but the scale_fmt of checkpoint is not ue8m0.
This might cause accuracy degradation on Blackwell.
```

Adding `--fp8-gemm-backend triton` also does not suppress DeepGemm.

This means there is **no way to disable DeepGemm via CLI flags** when serving NVFP4 checkpoints on Blackwell, which leads to CUDA crashes at concurrency ≥ 64 when the checkpoint's scale format is not `ue8m0`.

### Reproduction

```bash
# Model: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4 (NVFP4, non-ue8m0 scale format)
# GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (CC 12.0)

# Expected: DeepGemm should NOT be used when --fp4-gemm-backend is set explicitly
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --fp8-gemm-backend triton \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000

# Actual: DeepGemm warning still fires 4 times during startup.
# At concurrency >= 64, server crashes with:
#   CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered
# or:
#   Assertion `probability tensor contains either `inf`, `nan` or element < 0` failed.
```

Concurrency 1 and 16 complete successfully. The crash is triggered at concurrency 64+ due to accumulated numerical errors from the DeepGemm/scale_fmt mismatch.

source.title: Triton attention + CUDA graphs crashes on GB10/sm_121a — illegal memory access on first warmup inference
source.body:
**GPU:** NVIDIA GB10 (sm_121a, CUDA cap 12.1)
**Image:** lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260303-145ae518
**Model:** Qwen3.5-122B-A10B NVFP4

**Symptoms:** Weights load fine, CUDA graph capture succeeds (~21s), server reports ready, first warmup POST crashes:
- Default (flashinfer sampling): `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`
- With `--sampling-backend pytorch`: `asyncio.CancelledError` + 500 on first POST

**Workaround:** `--disable-cuda-graph` works correctly.

**Other notes:**
- `--attention-backend trtllm_mha` raises ValueError: check only matches SM100, not sm_121a (also Blackwell)
- Same setup on RTX 5090 (Ampere) works fine with CUDA graphs — sm_121a specific
- Crash is post-capture during warmup forward pass (triton kernel correctness on sm_121a?)

**Launch cmd:**
```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /models/qwen3-5-122b-nvfp4 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --attention-backend triton --reasoning-parser qwen3 --context-length 16384
```

incidents.complaint_or_finding: Deepseek 3.2 NVFP4 crashes or hangs with SpecV2 on the cited SGLang nightly, while the reporter did not observe it with SpecV1.
incidents.observed_failure: A prefill/generation run raises a scheduler exception in the SpecV2 draft path and reaches NSA backend FlashMLA KV attention; the report characterizes the outcome as a crash/hang.
incidents.baseline_or_control: SpecV1 did not appear to fail in local testing; SpecV2 also crashed after applying the linked patch and after downgrading FlashInfer versions.
incidents.resolution: Issue metadata is closed with state reason completed; the supplied text does not identify the fix.
incidents.mechanism: The issue title attributes the failure to a seqlens_k shape requirement: it must have shape batch_size; the supplied traceback is truncated before confirming that error.
incidents.discriminating_test: Run the same NVFP4 checkpoint and prompt with SpecV1 and SpecV2 under the same nightly and attention backend; failure only with SpecV2 points to runtime/config interaction rather than checkpoint damage.

### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary We are serving the **official DeepSeek-V4-Pro** checkpoint (downloaded from DeepSeek's HuggingFace repository, unmodified) with vLLM `v0.24.0`. The engine starts cleanly, loads all weights, and answers every request with HTTP 200 and **no NaN, no error, no warning** in the logs. **Key finding:** Under **tensor parallelism (TP16, also TP8+PP2)** the generated text is **completely garbled** — it collapses into repeating fragments such as `#`, `0.0`, and random character noise for every prompt. **After switching to the other official parallelism, DP16 + expert parallelism (EP), the exact same weights produce fully correct output** (`12+12=?`→`24`, `中国的首都是`→`北京`, `1+1=`→`2`). So the model weights and the DP+EP path are fine; the failure is specific to the **TP execution path** for DeepSeek-V4 (FP4 MoE / `ue8m0`) in vLLM `0.24.0`, and it is **silent** (no numerical error surfaced). We would like guidance on (a) whether the TP path for `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` (FP4 MoE / `ue8m0`) is correctly supported in `0.24.0`, and (b) how vLLM could surface a clearer diagnostic when the model forward silently produces garbage. ## The garbled output (core issue) Greedy decoding (`temperature=0`) via the raw `/v1/completions` endpoint: | Prompt | Generated output | | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | | `中国的首都是` (The capital of China is) | `0.0,0.0,0.0...` | | `The capital of France is` | `ias Judas, # \n\n#...` | | `1+1=` | `u4A.us # \n\n#...` | | `def add(a,b):` | `labor P1K6e # \n\n#...` | Characteristics: - **Every** prompt degenerates (natural language, math, code alike). - The output collapses into repeating tokens / character noise (`#`, `0.0`). - Occasionally the first few tokens look plausible before collapsing — this is consistent with a forward pass that is numerically wrong but not NaN. - The engine reports the request as a normal success (HTTP 200); nothing in the logs indicates a problem. ## Environment | Item | Value | | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | vLLM version | `0.24.0` | | Model | DeepSeek-V4 (`DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`), FP8 weights, `scale_fmt=ue8m0` | | GPU | NVIDIA H20D (Hopper), 8 GPUs per node | | Cluster | 2 nodes, Ray distributed executor (`--distributed-executor-backend ray`) | | Parallelism | TP16 (and TP8 + PP2 also tested) | | torch NCCL | `nccl==2.28.9` | | Filesystem | JDUFS (checkpoint 805.33 GiB, 64 safetensors shards) | ## Reproduction ```bash export VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=0 vllm serve /path/to/deepseek-v4 \ --served-model-name deepseek-v4 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \ --trust-remote-code \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --block-size 256 \ --enable-expert-parallel \ -cc.pass_config.fuse_allreduce_rms=False \ --tensor-parallel-size 16 \ --distributed-executor-backend ray \ --max-model-len 80000 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \ --max-num-seqs 512 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \ --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \ --compilation-config '{"mode": 0, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice \ --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 ``` Test the served model with a raw greedy completion: ```bash curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"deepseek-v4","prompt":"1+1=","max_tokens":32,"temperature":0}' ``` ## Concrete example with `logprobs` (the model is confidently wrong) To confirm this is the model forward and not sampling, we requested `logprobs`. For the prompt `12+12=?` the model outputs nonsense, and — crucially — each garbled token **is** the argmax (`top_logprobs[0] == chosen token`), so this is not a sampling artifact; the model's own distribution ranks garbage first. Request: ```bash curl http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "deepseek-v4-pro", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "12+12=?"}], "max_tokens": 5, "logprobs": true, "top_logprobs": 1 }' ``` Response (abridged): `finish_reason: length`, `system_fingerprint: vllm-0.24.0-tp16-ep-...` ```jsonc "content": ".Skip vad , 00", // expected: "24" "logprobs": [ { "token": ".Skip", "logprob": -11.09, "top_logprobs": [{ "token": ".Skip", "logprob": -11.09 }] }, { "token": " vad", "logprob": -11.36, "top_logprobs": [{ "token": " vad", "logprob": -11.36 }] }, { "token": " ,", "logprob": -3.60, "top_logprobs": [{ "token": " ,", "logprob": -3.60 }] }, { "token": " ", "logprob": -2.96, "top_logprobs": [{ "token": " ", "logprob": -2.96 }] }, { "token": "00", "logprob": -2.01, "top_logprobs": [{ "token": "00", "logprob": -2.01 }] } ] ``` Note the very low logprobs (e.g. `.Skip` at `-11.09`, `vad` at `-11.36`) yet these are still the top-ranked tokens — the entire output distribution is degenerate, which points at wrong forward-pass numerics rather than a tokenizer, template, or sampling issue. ## What we tried (none fixed the garbled output) We systematically ruled out several suspects; the garbled output was **identical** in every case: | Change | Purpose (what it rules out) | Result | | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | TP16 → TP8 + PP2 | cross-node TP16 communication | still garbled | | Switched to a DeepGEMM-enabled image with custom components installed (log confirms `enabling UE8M0 for DeepGEMM`) | missing DeepGEMM kernels | still garbled, identical | | Raw `/v1/completions`, `temperature=0` (greedy) | chat template / tool / reasoning parsers | still garbled | | Varied `--gpu-memory-utilization` | OOM / memory pressure | still garbled | | Switched from TP16 to DP16 + EP (`--data-parallel-size 16 --data-parallel-size-local 8 --data-parallel-hybrid-lb --enable-expert-parallel`), the other official parallelism recommended by DeepSeek | whether the issue is specific to the TP execution path vs. the model implementation in general | **✅ FIXED — output is correct** (`12+12=?`→`24`, `中国的首都是`→`北京`, `1+1=`→`2`), no garbling | **This is the key finding.** All TP-based configurations (TP16, TP8+PP2, with/without DeepGEMM, greedy, any `--gpu-memory-utilization`) produce identical garbled output, **but switching to DP16 + EP makes the output completely correct.** The model weights, the model implementation, and the DP+EP path are all fine — the garbling is specific to the **TP (tensor-parallel) execution path** for DeepSeek-V4 in vLLM `0.24.0`. ## Relevant model details (official DeepSeek-V4-Pro architecture) **Important:** this checkpoint is the **stock DeepSeek-V4-Pro** downloaded from DeepSeek's official HuggingFace repository, **with no modifications**. The fields below are **native DeepSeek-V4 architecture features** (CSA/HCA hash-compression attention + Sinkhorn routing + FP4 MoE + `ue8m0` FP8 scale), **not** a private/custom variant. `config.json` (quantization + V4 architecture fields): ```jsonc "quantization_config": { "activation_scheme": "dynamic", "fmt": "e4m3", "quant_method": "fp8", "scale_fmt": "ue8m0", // -> log: "enabling UE8M0 for DeepGEMM" "weight_block_size": [128, 128] }, "expert_dtype": "fp4", // DeepSeek-V4 architecture fields: "num_hash_layers": 3, "hc_sinkhorn_iters": 20, // plus hc_eps / hc_mult / compress_rope_theta / compress_ratios / // o_lora_rank / o_groups / index_* / swiglu_limit ... ``` Weight tensors include the V4-specific modules (hash-compression attention, Lightning Indexer, etc.): - `hc_attn_base` / `hc_attn_fn` / `hc_attn_scale` - `hc_ffn_*` - `attn.attn_sink` - `index_*` (Lightning Indexer / hash-compression) The checkpoint ships **no `modeling_*.py`** and `auto_map` is `null`, so the model relies entirely on vLLM's **built-in** `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` implementation. Our working hypothesis is that vLLM `0.24.0`'s built-in support for official DeepSeek-V4 — specifically the FP4 MoE / `ue8m0` quantized forward path — is **incomplete or buggy**, producing numerically wrong (but not NaN) activations → garbled tokens. During load, vLLM does resolve and use custom paths, e.g.: ``` [quant_config.py:75] DeepSeek V4 expert_dtype resolved to 'fp4' [attention.py:87] Using DeepSeek's fp8_ds_mla KV cache format. [attention.py:689] Using FP8 indexer cache for Lightning Indexer. [mxfp4.py:623] Using 'MARLIN' Mxfp4 MoE backend. # custom TileLang kernels compile successfully: TileLang ... compile kernel `hc_prenorm_gemm_tilelang` TileLang ... compile kernel `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` ``` So the code paths *are* being exercised, but the final output is still garbage. ## Secondary observation: cannot disable DeepGEMM to cross-check To sanity-check whether DeepGEMM was involved, we tried `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`. It does **not** run — instead of falling back, it crashes during `profile_run`, because `scale_fmt=ue8m0` appears hard-coupled to DeepGEMM and CUTLASS has no matching dispatch: ``` [config.py:741] Detected quantization_config.scale_fmt=ue8m0; enabling UE8M0 for DeepGEMM. ... File ".../vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py", line 413, in fused_wqa_wkv File ".../vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/scaled_mm/cutlass.py", line 320, in apply_block_scaled_mm return ops.cutlass_scaled_mm(...) RuntimeError: dispatch_scaled_mm, /workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/c3x/scaled_mm_helper.hpp:17 [core.py:1231] EngineCore failed to start. ``` This is a minor side finding (it would be nice to reject `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0` at config-validation time with a clear message instead of crashing after loading ~800 GiB of weights), but it is **not** our main concern — it just prevented us from ruling out DeepGEMM as a cause of the garbled output. ## Questions for maintainers 1. **Is the TP-path garbled output a known issue** when serving the official DeepSeek-V4-Pro weights (FP4 MoE / `ue8m0` / hash-compression attention + Sinkhorn) on vLLM `0.24.0`? We confirmed that **DP16 + EP produces correct output with the same weights**, so the model implementation itself works — the problem is isolated to the **tensor-parallel execution path**. Is TP for `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM` officially expected to work in `0.24.0`, or is it only supported in a later version / specific recommended image? 2. What in the **TP path** could break the FP4 MoE / `ue8m0` forward while DP+EP stays correct — e.g. block-quantization scale alignment when a single FP4 expert weight is sharded across TP ranks? Are config fields (`num_hash_layers`, `hc_*`, `index_*`, `expert_dtype=fp4`, `scale_fmt=ue8m0`) handled correctly under TP? If a path is not fully implemented, could vLLM **warn or refuse** instead of silently emitting garbage? 3. Is there a recommended way to debug a "no error but wrong output" case like this (e.g. logits dump, reference forward comparison)? ## Anything else We are happy to provide full startup logs, the complete `config.json`, and the list of weight tensor keys on request. ## transformers vs vLLM Per the vLLM template, please note this is a **model-implementation** question, not a serving-layer bug. This is the **official DeepSeek-V4-Pro** checkpoint, but it ships **no `modeling_*.py`** and `auto_map` is `null`, so it cannot be loaded via `transformers` with `trust_remote_code`; there is no reference `transformers` forward to compare against. The output therefore depends entirely on vLLM's built-in `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`. If a matching upstream `transformers` (or reference) implementation exists, a side-by-side logits comparison would confirm whether the mismatch is in vLLM's port. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

source.title: [Bug] MiMoV2 load_weights: fused qkv_proj path uses naive chunk(tp,dim=0)[rank], misplaces Q values into K/V slots
source.body:
## Summary

`vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py:load_weights` has a code path for fused-`qkv_proj` checkpoints (MiMo-V2 Pro variants) that does

```python
if "qkv_proj" in name:
    if name in params_dict:
        param = params_dict[name]
        loaded_weight = loaded_weight.chunk(tp_size, dim=0)[tp_rank]
        default_weight_loader(param, loaded_weight)
    continue
```

For a checkpoint where the fused tensor is laid out `[Q | K | V]` along dim 0 — which is the case for at least `festr2/MiMo-V2.5-Pro-NVFP4-MXFP8-attn-TP8` — a naive `chunk(tp_size, dim=0)[tp_rank]` gives 7 of 8 ranks (at TP=8) rows that fall entirely inside the Q region. Those ranks' `QKVParallelLinear` parameter slots for K and V end up filled with Q values; only the last rank gets any real K/V data. Attention is therefore severely broken on 7 of 8 ranks.

The proper loader (`QKVParallelLinear.weight_loader` with `shard_id="q"/"k"/"v"`) handles the TP split per-section correctly. It's already used by the `stacked_params_mapping` path for checkpoints that store Q/K/V as separate tensors; the fused path just doesn't reach it.

## Repro

Model: `festr2/MiMo-V2.5-Pro-NVFP4-MXFP8-attn-TP8` (the only Pro-format quant I'm aware of that hits the fused branch; the Flash variant stores split q_proj/k_proj/v_proj and goes through `stacked_params_mapping`, which is correct).

Cluster: 8-node DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), TP=8, Ray distributed executor. With other patches in place (MXFP8 dispatch wired into `modelopt_mixed`, `weight_scale_inv` -> `weight_scale` rename for the modelopt MXFP8 scale parameter), the model reaches Application startup and serves requests, but inference returns degenerate token loops (`*\0` / `Müslü` / `the` style — varies with prompt but never coherent).

## Empirical evidence the layout is `Q→K→V` (not per-rank pre-sharded)

For layer 0 `model.layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight_scale_inv` (shape `[27136, 192]`, uint8 E8M0):

| Region (dim-0 slice) | Rows | Mean byte | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q section `[0:24576]` | 24576 | **114.55** | 24576 = 128 Q heads × 192 head_dim |
| K section `[24576:26112]` | 1536 | **115.99** | 1536 = 8 KV heads × 192 head_dim |
| V section `[26112:27136]` | 1024 | **113.27** | 1024 = 8 KV heads × 128 v_head_dim |

The three sections have distinguishable scale-byte distributions (note V is systematically smaller-magnitude, consistent with `attention_value_scale=0.612` applied to V before attention). If the tensor were per-rank pre-sharded (8 chunks of `[Q|K|V]` concatenated), every chunk would have the same internal structure and the per-rank means would be identical; instead they're flat ~114 for the first 7 chunks (all-Q) and a weighted mix for chunk 7 (which spans the Q/K/V boundaries).

## Fix

Split the fused tensor by `(q_size, k_size, v_size)` using config dims (distinguishing full vs. SWA layers via `hybrid_layer_pattern`), then call the existing `QKVParallelLinear.weight_loader` three times with `shard_id` `"q"`, `"k"`, `"v"`. Each call lets the proper loader take this rank's TP-slice of that section, identical to the existing stacked path.

Proposed patch against `vllm/model_executor/models/mimo_v2.py` (replacing the `if "qkv_proj" in name:` block):

```python
if "qkv_proj" in name:
    if name in params_dict:
        param = params_dict[name]
        try:
            _li = int(name.split(".layers.")[1].split(".")[0])
        except (IndexError, ValueError):
            _li = -1
        _is_swa = (
            _li >= 0
            and hasattr(self.config, "hybrid_layer_pattern")
            and self.config.hybrid_layer_pattern[_li] == 1
        )
        if _is_swa:
            _nh = self.config.swa_num_attention_heads
            _nkv = self.config.swa_num_key_value_heads
            _hd = self.config.swa_head_dim
            _vhd = getattr(self.config, "swa_v_head_dim", _hd)
        else:
            _nh = self.config.num_attention_heads
            _nkv = self.config.num_key_value_heads
            _hd = self.config.head_dim
            _vhd = getattr(self.config, "v_head_dim", _hd)
        _qs = _nh * _hd
        _ks = _nkv * _hd
        _vs = _nkv * _vhd
        if loaded_weight.shape[0] == _qs + _ks + _vs:
            _q = loaded_weight[:_qs]
            _k = loaded_weight[_qs : _qs + _ks]
            _v = loaded_weight[_qs + _ks : _qs + _ks + _vs]
            _wl = getattr(param, "weight_loader", default_weight_loader)
            _wl(param, _q, "q")
            _wl(param, _k, "k")
            _wl(param, _v, "v")
            loaded_params.add(name)
        else:
            # Unexpected shape — keep old behavior.
            loaded_weight = loaded_weight.chunk(tp_size, dim=0)[tp_rank]
            default_weight_loader(param, loaded_weight)
    continue
```

I have this running on a TP=8 cluster; with the patch, the same model produces coherent output for chat and completion prompts (`12 × 7` → `84`, `def fibonacci(n):` → proper Python recursion, etc.). Without the patch, the same configuration produces the degenerate token loops described above.

The patch handles both full and SWA layers (MiMo-V2 has full attention layers at positions where `hybrid_layer_pattern[layer] == 0` and SWA layers elsewhere). It applies to both the FP8 weight tensor and the uint8 E8M0 scale tensor (`weight_scale_inv`) because both share the `qkv_proj` name prefix.

## Why this also affects users who don't see the symptom

The Flash-format MiMo-V2 checkpoints (separate `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj`) go through the `stacked_params_mapping` path before hitting this branch, so they're fine. Only fused-`qkv_proj` Pro checkpoints reach the buggy path. To my knowledge today that's `festr2/MiMo-V2.5-Pro-NVFP4-MXFP8-attn-TP8` and the BF16 source `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5-Pro` (if anyone tries to serve it directly).

## Related

- vllm#41797 (DiffKV Triton attention for MiMo) — gets the model past the attention-backend selection blocker; the load-path bug is independent.
- NVIDIA/cutlass#3096, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2776 — the wider sm_121/NVFP4 conversation. For this specific checkpoint the garbage signature `あるい/Müslü` was *not* a CUTLASS Sm120 ArchTag symptom; the same garbage class shows up across MXFP8 attention kernels (Marlin / Emulation / FlashInferCutlass) and NVFP4 MoE backends (Marlin / CUTLASS / Emulation) — only the load-side fix above clears it.

Happy to open a PR with the patch + a small test. Wanted to file the diagnosis first so the analysis isn't buried.

Working repo with patches + recipe: https://github.com/idonati/spark-vllm-docker-festr2

source.title: Eval bug: Gemma 3 on ARM64 CPU (Cortex-A76) produces wrong logits; Qwen unaffected — b8816
source.body:
### Name and Version

```
version: b8816 (also reproduced on b8708)
built: ubuntu-24.04-arm runner, cmake -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH=armv8-a
host: Raspberry Pi 5 (Cortex-A76, ARMv8.2-A, features: fphp asimdhp asimddp asimdrdm)
```

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CPU

### Hardware

Raspberry Pi 5 (Broadcom BCM2712), 4× Cortex-A76 @ 2.4 GHz, 8 GB RAM. ARMv8.2-A with half-precision + dot product. No SVE.

### Models

Primary repro: Gemma 3 270M fine-tune (base: `unsloth/functiongemma-270m-it`), quantized to Q8_0.

Also reproduced to a lesser degree on: `unsloth/gemma-3-1b-it-GGUF` (Q8_0), which segfaults on b8708 and produces numerically wrong (but non-crashing) output on b8816.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

Same GGUF on Mac CPU produces correct output; on the Pi ARM64 CPU build the forward pass silently produces a wrong probability distribution.

Reproduction via llama-cpp-python API (or llama-cli directly — the result is the same):

```python
from llama_cpp import Llama
llm = Llama(model_path="/path/model.Q8_0.gguf", n_ctx=512, n_gpu_layers=0, logits_all=True)
out = llm.create_completion("The capital of France is", max_tokens=1, temperature=0, logprobs=10)
```

**Mac CPU (llama-cpp-python 0.3.20, bundled ggml 0.9.11):**
```
top tokens:
  ' Paris': -0.003
  ' **':    -6.139
  ' Bast':  -8.627
  ...
```

**Pi ARM64 CPU (b8816 built from GitHub workflow with `-DGGML_NATIVE=OFF -DGGML_CPU_ARM_ARCH=armv8-a`, ggml 0.9.11):**
```
top tokens:
  ' bel':   -0.602
  ' el':    -1.468
  ' where': -2.533
  ' bal':   -2.695
  ' the':   -3.475
  ...  (" Paris" not in top 10)
```

Identical garbage with quantization = Q8_0 and bf16 (different garbage between quants, but still no "Paris" on Pi). Identical across `n_threads=1/2/4`. Same behavior with `flash_attn` on/off.

Isolated the bug to Gemma 3 architecture specifically:
- Qwen 2.5 0.5B Q8_0 on same Pi/binary: `" Paris"` at -0.918 ✓ (matches Mac to within expected precision)
- Gemma 3 1B base Q8_0: segfaults on b8708; produces wrong-but-not-crashing output on b8816 (`" France"` top instead of `" Paris"`)
- Our 270M Gemma 3 fine-tune: byte-identical garbage logits between b8708 and b8816

The binary strings show standard Gemma 3 ISWA implementation symbols (`llm_build_gemma3`, `llama_kv_cache_iswa`). Qwen uses standard GQA and is unaffected. This strongly points at the ARM64 CPU kernel path for Gemma 3's interleaved sliding window attention or an upstream fp16 accumulation issue specific to this architecture/shape.

### First Bad Commit

Bisection not performed yet — b8708 and b8816 both show the symptom. The 1B segfault does get fixed somewhere in that range, but the 270M numerics bug is present across the full range tested.

### Relevant log output

```
llama_context: n_ctx         = 4096
llama_context: n_ctx_seq     = 4096
llama_context: n_batch       = 2048
llama_context: n_ubatch      = 2048
llama_context: causal_attn   = 1
llama_context: flash_attn    = enabled
llama_context: kv_unified    = false
llama_kv_cache_iswa: using full-size SWA cache
llama_kv_cache_iswa: creating non-SWA KV cache, size = 4096 cells
llama_kv_cache_iswa: creating     SWA KV cache, size = 4096 cells
llama_kv_cache: K (f16): 6.00 MiB, V (f16): 6.00 MiB
llama_kv_cache: K (f16): 30.00 MiB, V (f16): 30.00 MiB
sched_reserve:        CPU compute buffer size =  2058.01 MiB
Warmup completed in 49.2ms
```

No errors at load time. The model loads cleanly, reports the expected graph layout, and warmup completes. The divergence appears in the forward pass logits directly.

I'm happy to bisect the range and try additional reproductions if useful. Also happy to share the fine-tuned GGUFs privately if helpful.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CUDA

### Hardware

rtx 5060ti 16GB + rtx4060ti 16GB

### Models

Qwen_Qwen3-30B-A3B-Q6_K.gguf by bartowski.
sha256sum: d511d02955714b08ff1b4354d6eae8ea513179a83fa5498466db2731528074dd

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

I'm using a grammar to simulate the nothink qwen prompt format. Sometimes the output is generated correctly, sometimes the model outputs the wrong token while still aligned with the grammar.

The command I'm using to test:
```
curl http://localhost:8080/completion -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "prompt": "<|im_start|>system\n<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\nhi<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n",
  "grammar": "root ::= \"<think>\\n\\n</think>\\n\\n\" .*",
  "temperature": 0.001,
  "n_predict": 6,
  "seed": 42
}'
```

Correct output: `[151667 198 198 151668 ...]  <think>\n\n</think>...`
Wrong output: `[151667 198 198 27 14 ...]    <think>\n\n</...`

Sometimes the model outputs the correct output, sometimes it outputs the wrong output and the following output breaks since the model cannot see the `</think>` token. I'm not restarting llama-server between tests and not changing the seed. I expect the model to always output the token 151668

Command line used to launch llama-server: `/llama-server -ngl 175 -t 6 -c 32768 --host 0.0.0.0 -fa -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --slots -a current --temp 0.6`

### First Bad Commit

_No response_

```shell
`{"index":0,"content":"<think>\n\n</think"...`
```

source.body:
### What happened?

The quantized version of gemma 27b (Q8_0) still gets the answer wrong to even simple problems.
The version of gemma on ai studio answers correctly all my questions.

Example problem that quantized gemma consistently fails while the ai studio gemma answers correctly.
```
Matteo has 20 apples, he buys 20 oranges. Then he discards half of his fruits equally.
Then he discards a quarter of his fruits equally between apples and oranges. How many apples remain?
```
The correct answer is 7 or 8.

I also tried asking the model to repeat the question by prepending "Repeat the question and then answer it: ".
The model in llama.cpp fails this simple task while the model in ai studio repeats the question word by word.

I noticed that the ai studio response starts with
`Here's how to solve the...`
while the response when run in llama.cpp starts with
`Here's how to solve this...`

So I printed the probabilities from llama.cpp and this is the output. I would have expected a much higher probabilities for "the" with respect to "this" even after quantization:
```
<bos><start_of_turn>user
Matteo has 20 apples, he buys 20 oranges. Then he discards half of his fruits equally.
Then he discards a quarter of his fruits equally between apples and oranges. How many apples remain?<end_of_turn>
<start_of_turn>model
[('Here', 1.0), ('This', 0.0), ('1', 0.0), ('**', 0.0), ('It', 0.0)]
[("'", 1.0), (' is', 0.0), (' are', 0.0), (' how', 0.0), (' we', 0.0)]
[('s', 1.0), ('d', 0.0), ('st', 0.0), ('ss', 0.0), ('re', 0.0)]
[(' how', 1.0), (' a', 0.0), (' the', 0.0), (' why', 0.0), (' step', 0.0)]
[(' to', 1.0), (' we', 0.0), (' this', 0.0), (' the', 0.0), (' you', 0.0)]
[(' solve', 1.0), (' break', 0.0), (' figure', 0.0), (' work', 0.0), (' breakdown', 0.0)]
[(' this', 1.0), (' the', 0.0), (' problem', 0.0), (' that', 0.0), (' these', 0.0)]
[(' problem', 1.0), (' word', 0.0), (':', 0.0), (' riddle', 0.0), (' puzzle', 0.0)]
```

Here is the setup:
model version: bartowski gemma-27b-it at Q8_0 after tokenizer fix
llama-server: 3264 (upstream version after merge)
inference parameters:  temperature = 0.01, seed = 0


### Name and Version

$ ./llama-cli --version
version: 3264 (09a5534f)
built with cc (Debian 12.2.0-14) 12.2.0 for x86_64-linux-gnu


### What operating system are you seeing the problem on?

Linux

### Relevant log output

```shell
<bos><start_of_turn>user
Repeat the question and then answer it: Matteo has 20 apples, he buys 20 oranges. Then he discards half of his fruits equally. Then he discards a quarter of his fruits equally between apples and oranges. How many apples remain?<end_of_turn>
<start_of_turn>model
**Question:** Matteo has 20 apples. He buys 20 oranges. Then he discards a quarter of his fruits equally between apples and oranges. How many oranges remain?

**Answer:** Here's how to solve this problem:

* **Step 1: Understand the Problem**

The problem states that Matteo discards a quarter of his total fruit, not just a quarter of the oranges.

* **Step 2: Calculate Total Fruit**

Matteo starts with 20 apples.

* **Step 3: Calculate the Split**

After buying 20 oranges, he has 20 + 20 = 40 fruits total.

* **Step 4: Calculate the Discard**

Half of his total fruit is 40 / 2 = 20 fruits.

* **Step 5: Calculate the Remaining Fruit**

Since he discards a quarter of his fruit, he has 40 / 4 = 10 fruits discarded.

* **Step 6: Calculate the Remaining Apples**

He discards 10 fruits / 2 = 5 apples.

* **Answer:**  Therefore, 5 apples are discarded.

Let me know if you'd like to know how many apples and oranges Matteo has left! 🍎🍊
```

For politically sensitive questions, security and privacy issues, and other non-computer science questions, you will refuse to answer."$'\n''### Instruction: <<function>>[{"name":"get_current_weather","description":"Get the current weather in a given location","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"location":{"type":"string","description":"The city and state, e.g. San Francisco, CA",},"unit":{"type":"string","enum":["celsius","fahrenheit"]},},"required":["location"]}}]'$'\n'"<<question>>What's the weather like in Oslo?"$'\n'"### Response: "

source.title: [Bug]: ByteDance-Seed/BAGEL-7B-MoT int4 quantization: only partial layer quantization achievable without significant accuracy degradation
source.body:
### Problem Description

[Intel/BAGEL-7B-MoT-int4-AutoRound](https://huggingface.co/Intel/BAGEL-7B-MoT-int4-AutoRound) is an int4 quantized version of [ByteDance-Seed/BAGEL-7B-MoT](https://huggingface.co/ByteDance-Seed/BAGEL-7B-MoT), produced with AutoRound. During quantization experiments, we found that applying int4 to all transformer layers leads to unacceptable accuracy loss. Only a subset of layers can be safely quantized at int4, while sensitive layers must remain at higher precision.

source.title: [Bug]: GLM-5 Generates Nonsensical Output with RTN Quantized Version
source.body:
### Problem Description

I am encountering an issue with a quantized version of the [Model Name] model. The model frequently generates nonsense sequences (e.g., 人事, 出生 etc.) these two words should be '(.*?).
img_v3_02vc_320011c2-ec27-4870-a91d-75cbf6ee8f3g

**need to check if it's a code issue or RTN issue**



---
base_model:
- zai-org/GLM-5
tags:
- text-generation-inference
---
## Model Details

This model is a mixed int4 model with group_size 128 and asymmetric quantization of [zai-org/GLM-5](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5/) generated by [intel/auto-round](https://github.com/intel/auto-round). Please follow the license of the original model.

**The model is quantized with pure RTN mode**

## vllm inference

**Setup**
~~~bash
pip install git+https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git@main


pip install git+https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git
~~~



**MTP has not been supported, we will try to fix it later.**

~~~bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,2,3,4 vllm serve  Intel/GLM-5-int4-mixed-AutoRound  \
     --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
     --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \
     --tool-call-parser glm47 \
     --reasoning-parser glm45 \
     --enable-auto-tool-choice \
     --served-model-name glm-5
~~~





~~~bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d ' {
    "model": "glm-5",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
      {"role": "user", "content": "Summarize GLM-5 in one sentence."}
    ],
    "temperature": 1,
    "max_tokens": 4096
  } '
~~~



## Generate the Model

this pr is required https://github.com/intel/auto-round/pull/1466

~~~bash
auto-round zai-org/GLM-5 --ignore_layers layers.0,layers.1,layers.2,self_attn,shared_experts --iters 0 --disable_opt_rtn --output_dir ./glm5_int4 --format auto_round:auto_awq --asym
~~~



## Ethical Considerations and Limitations

The model can produce factually incorrect output, and should not be relied on to produce factually accurate information. Because of the limitations of the pretrained model and the finetuning datasets, it is possible that this model could generate lewd, biased or otherwise offensive outputs.

source.title: [Bug]:Llama 3.1 8B Instruct W2A16 Quantization leads to Model Collapse (repeating "!") despite using "Best" settings
source.body:
### Problem Description

> I am encountering severe model collapse when quantifying the `Llama 3.1 8B Instruct` model to **2-bit (W2A16)** using AutoRound.
> Despite using the "Best" configuration (iters=1000, nsamples=512, enable_alg_ext), the resulting model loses all language capabilities and outputs repeating exclamation marks (e.g., `!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!`) when loaded in vLLM.
> **Expected Behavior:**
> Since Llama 2 (7B/13B) retains some reasoning capabilities under 2-bit quantization in previous benchmarks, I expected Llama 3.1 8B to at least generate coherent text.
> **Current Behavior:**
> * The model outputs repeating characters (garbage).
> * GSM8K score is exactly 0.
> * **However, the same setup works perfectly for 4-bit (W4A16), achieving 76.6% on GSM8K.** This confirms my environment and basic workflow are correct.


### Reproduction Steps


> Run the AutoRound quantization with the following "Best" settings for 2-bit:
> 
> 

> ```bash
> auto_round \
>   --model_name "./llama3.1-8B-Instruct" \
>   --bits 2 \
>   --group_size 128 \
>   --format "auto_round" \
>   --iters 1000 \
>   --nsamples 512 \
>   --seqlen 2048 \
>   --batch_size 8 \
>   --minmax_lr 2e-3 \
>   --enable_alg_ext \
>   --output_dir "./llama3.1-8B-Instruct-W2A16-Best"
> 
> ```

### Environment Information

> * **Model:** Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
> * **AutoRound Version:** 0.9.4
> * **Inference Engine:** vLLM 
> * **GPU:** RTX 6000Ada
> * **CUDA Version:** 12.8

Hi, I'm trying to quantize on several GPUs: Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking
I have four GPUs with 24GB of VRAM each, but I don't know how to create the device_map for the model.

I saw a configuration you used for Deepseek 3.1, but I don't know how to adapt it for Qwen3. Could you please explain how to do it for Qwen3 Next? No matter how many times I've tried, I always get an error with HIP Allocator.


```
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import transformers

model_name = "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1"

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name, trust_remote_code=False, torch_dtype="auto")

block = model.model.layers
device_map = {}

for n, m in block.named_modules():
    if isinstance(m, (torch.nn.Linear, transformers.modeling_utils.Conv1D)):
        if "experts" in n and ("shared_experts" not in n) and int(n.split('.')[-2]) < 63:
            device = "cuda:1"
        elif "experts" in n and ("shared_experts" not in n) and int(n.split('.')[-2]) >= 63 and int(
                n.split('.')[-2]) < 128:
            device = "cuda:2"
        elif "experts" in n and ("shared_experts" not in n) and int(n.split('.')[-2]) >= 128 and int(
                n.split('.')[-2]) < 192:
            device = "cuda:3"
        elif "experts" in n and ("shared_experts" not in n) and int(
                n.split('.')[-2]) >= 192:
            device = "cuda:4"
        else:
            device = "cuda:0"
        n = n[2:]

        device_map.update({n: device})


from auto_round import AutoRound

autoround = AutoRound(model=model, tokenizer=tokenizer, device_map=device_map, nsamples=512,
                      batch_size=4, low_gpu_mem_usage=True, seqlen=2048,
                      )
autoround.quantize_and_save(format="auto_round", output_dir="tmp_autoround")

```

source.title: Auto-round pulls in wrong Triton wheel and breaks Intel XPU environment
source.body:
### Issue Summary

Most models like qwen from transformers requires **`auto-round`**, which in turn installs the **default `triton` wheel** (CPU build) instead of the Intel XPU–specific one.
This breaks the XPU environment.

---

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run:

   ```bash
   pip install 'auto-round>=0.5'
   ```
2. Observe that it downloads:

   ```
   triton-3.4.0-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_27_x86_64.manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl
   ```
3. Check the installed packages:

   ```bash
   pip list | grep -i triton
   ```

   Output:

   ```
   pytorch-triton-xpu 3.4.0
   triton             3.4.0
   ```

---

### Actual Behavior

* When running PyTorch with XPU:

  ```
  torch._dynamo.exc.BackendCompilerFailed: backend='inductor' raised:
  ImportError: cannot import name 'intel' from 'triton._C.libtriton'
  ```
* Even after uninstalling `triton`, errors persist:

  ```
  ImportError: cannot import name 'Config' from 'triton' (unknown location)
  ```

  because `torch/_inductor/runtime/triton_compat.py` still expects the correct XPU build.

---

### Workaround

Force-reinstall the Intel XPU–specific Triton wheel:

```bash
pip3 install --pre pytorch-triton-xpu==3.4.0 \
  --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/xpu \
  --force-reinstall
pip uninstall triton   # ensure the default wheel is removed
```

---

### Root Cause

`auto-round` depends on `triton`, which resolves to the **standard PyPI Triton wheel**.
This conflicts with the **XPU-compatible `pytorch-triton-xpu`** package required by Intel GPUs.

---

### Recommendation

* Package maintainers (e.g. `auto-round`) may need to make the dependency conditional or document the correct installation steps.
* Ensure dependencies explicitly require the **`pytorch-triton-xpu`** package instead of the default `triton` build.

source.title: Multi-GPU Quantization Always OOM
source.body:
## Background
Successfully quantized Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on a single GPU following your suggestion last week. Issues arise only when the model is too large to fit on a single GPU and multi-GPU quantization is required.
## Reproduction Cases
Tested on two different setups, both failed with OOM. When quantizing Qwen2.5-72B-A10B on 8x H20 and Qwen3-27B on 8x RTX 4090, both resulted in OOM errors. As a reference, quantizing Qwen3-27B on a single H20 succeeded with ~60GB VRAM usage.
### Single GPU Observation
When quantizing Qwen3-27B on a single H20, VRAM usage increases progressively per layer and stabilizes at ~60GB, which exceeds the 24GB limit of a single RTX 4090.
### Multi-GPU Observation
When quantizing on 8x RTX 4090, abnormal VRAM distribution is observed:
GPU 0 remains nearly idle with very low VRAM usage about 30GB
GPU 1~7 all show continuously increasing VRAM usage simultaneously, as if each GPU is independently quantizing the full model rather than handling only its assigned shards
Eventually all non-primary GPUs run OOM
It seems like each GPU appears to be loading a full model copy instead of only its assigned portion.
### Environment
GPTQModel: 6.1.0.dev0 (main branch)
Transformers: 5.5.4
PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu129
Triton: 3.6.0
Python: 3.12.13
